I thought I had it all planned, but then I got distracted by this ridiculous YouTube video about Pokémon and now I’m scrambling.      Aww, but you know what? I don’t know if I’m ready to go out again after that time last week when I accidentally walked into a room full of people and just stood there like a complete idiot.      Oh, come on, you’re not still thinking about that! You were just shy. It’s not like you said anything, you just looked at the floor the whole time.      Yeah, and then I ended up talking to a guy who thought I was a barista. He asked me if I took orders. I was like, “Excuse me, I’m a student from the Philippines.” And he just stared at me like I was from Mars.      That’s hilarious! You should’ve told him you were from the Philippines and not a café. Maybe he’d have found it more interesting.      Oh, you’re not helping! I still get flashbacks of that moment. I mean, it’s not every day you have to explain your accent to a guy who’s from the same country, but not the same part.      You know, I think that’s just part of being in university. You meet all sorts of people, some of them surprising.      True, but sometimes I feel like I’m just waiting for someone to ask me why I’m not from the Philippines. It’s like people assume I’m a Brit because of my accent, but I actually grew up in the Philippines.      That’s so weird. I get that sometimes, like when I’m at home in London, people always say “where are you from?” but I’m British. It’s confusing.      Exactly! It’s like we’re two halves of the same person. You’re from London, I’m from the Midlands, but we both have English roots. It’s a weird mix.      Yeah, and it’s kind of cool.

So, I’ve been thinking about our holiday plans again. I know it’s still early, but I’m really starting to miss the beach. I mean, I know we’re not going anywhere fancy, but even a quick trip to somewhere like Scarborough would be nice.      I can see that. I’ve been thinking about that too. Though I’m a bit nervous about the weather. If it’s too wet, it might not be worth it. But if it’s nice, we could just hit the beach, maybe rent a bike or something.      Yeah, I’d love that. I mean, I haven’t been to the coast in ages. I’m actually thinking about taking a solo trip later this year, just to clear my head. But I’d rather go with you two. It’s more fun that way.      Well, if you’re thinking about a solo trip, maybe we can team up. You take the first half, and I take the second? I’ll do the beaches, you can do the cities.      Oh, I’d rather do the cities. I mean, I’m a civil engineer, not a beach bum. I prefer culture over sand.      Yeah, but you don’t have to be a beach bum to enjoy the sea. You can still walk along the shore, take photos, have a picnic. It’s not like you have to lay on a towel the whole time.      Exactly. And I think the best part is that it doesn’t have to be far. Just a quick drive from here, and we can have our own little getaway.      I suppose. But I still worry about the weather. I’ve been reading up on the forecast. It looks like there might be some rain in the next couple of weeks.      Well, if the weather doesn’t cooperate, we can always switch to indoor plans. Maybe we can catch up on some TV shows we’ve been meaning to watch.      Oh, that’s a great idea! I’ve been meaning to finish  Stranger Things  and  Fargo  again. Maybe we can do a movie night after we come back from the beach.      I think I’m more of a football fan than a TV fan, but I’ll admit, I’ve been binge-watching  Peaky Blinders  again. It’s so good.      Yeah, I’ve been rewatching that too. But I also got into  The Crown .

You know, I was talkin’ to my cousin the other day, and he said he’s thinkin’ of takin’ a trip to London. A proper trip, not just a day out. He’s got a bit of money saved up now, thanks to eBay and all that.      Yeah, I heard that. He’s been sellin’ stuff on there for ages. I used to do that too, back when I was still workin’ part-time. I got rid of that old caravan, and it paid for a couple of months of childminding.      That’s not bad. I’ve been thinkin’ about sellin’ my old car. It’s a bit of a relic, but it still runs, and I’d rather get some cash in than keep it in the garage collectin’ dust.      I’d say that’s a good idea. I sold my old teaching car last year when I retired. It was a Land Rover, and it had more miles on it than a lot of people have in their lives. But it made a decent amount on eBay.      You know, I’ve been thinkin’ about sellin’ my house too. It’s been empty for a while now, and I’ve been stuck in the same place, not doin’ much. I’d rather move somewhere with more space, maybe in the country.      I’d say that’s a wise move. I’ve been thinkin’ the same. My place is too small, and I’ve been feelin’ like I’m stuck in a rut. I’m thinkin’ of buyin’ a smaller place in Cornwall. Maybe a house with a garden.      Cornwall sounds nice. I went there once with a group of friends. We stayed in a youth hostel near Penzance. It was peaceful, and the views were amazing. You could see the sea from the room.      That sounds idyllic. I’ve always wanted to go there. I’ve heard the beaches are amazing, and the horses are plentiful too. I’ve got this idea of goin’ horseback ridin’ one day. I’ve always had a soft spot for horses.      That’s a good one. I’ve been thinkin’ about takin’ up riding too. I’ve got a bit of money saved now, and I’m not as young as I used to be. But I’d love to be able to ride again.      It’s never too late, really. I’ve seen people my age get into all sorts of things.

So, I just got an email from the midwife about the feeding schedule for the baby. She said it’s important to start with breast milk, but if there are any issues, we can use formula. I was just thinking… how are we going to manage this?      Oh, don’t worry, I’ve been doing some research on this. I know it’s not easy, especially with both of us being new parents. I remember when my sister first had her baby, she used formula because she couldn’t produce enough milk initially. It was a bit of a mess, but she got through it.      That sounds tough. I’ve been reading a lot about the importance of breastfeeding for the baby’s immune system, but I also know that every situation is different. I just hope I’m not being too pushy about this. I mean, the baby’s health is the priority, right?      Absolutely. But I think it’s also important for us to be flexible. I’ve heard some moms talk about how they have to pump and store milk, and it can take up a lot of time. We need to make sure we’re not burning out. What about you? Are you planning on breastfeeding?      I’m hoping to, but I’m also aware that it might not work out. I’ve heard some people say that it’s not always possible, especially with certain health conditions or if you’re not getting enough support. I just want to make sure we’re prepared for any scenario.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I think it’s also good to talk to other new parents or join some support groups. I joined a Facebook group for new moms in our area, and it’s been really helpful. They share tips, advice, and even some funny stories.      That sounds great. I should really look into that. Maybe I’ll start browsing some of those groups. I’ve also been thinking about the baby’s sleep patterns. I read somewhere that babies often sleep a lot in the first few weeks, but then they start getting more active. Is that right?      Yeah, I think that’s true. My little brother was such a sleepy baby. He would sleep for hours, but then suddenly he’d wake up in the middle of the night and be impossible to calm down.

Good morning, everyone. I’ve had a bit of a busy morning with the patients. I’m still catching up on my notes, but I thought I’d come down for breakfast with you all. What’s the plan for the day?      Well, I was thinking we could all go to the market this afternoon. I’ve got some errands to run, and I thought we could pick up some fresh produce. Oh, and maybe a few new books for the house. It’s been a while since we’ve done that.      That sounds good. I’ve been meaning to get some new plants for the garden. The ones I bought last week didn’t survive the frost, and I’m not sure if I’m doing something wrong. I’m getting a bit frustrated, to be honest.      I can relate. I’ve been trying to grow some herbs in my small balcony garden, and I keep watering them too much. My mum says it’s like giving them a bath instead of a drink, but I don’t know—maybe I’m just not getting it right.      Oh, I’ve been there. I remember when I first started gardening, I tried to grow tomatoes in a pot, and I ended up killing them all. I’m not sure if it was overwatering or not enough sunlight. Anyway, enough about that. Let’s talk about what we’re going to do today. I think it’d be good to have some fresh veggies on the table.      Exactly. And I was also thinking about inviting the kids over for dinner this weekend. They’ve been so busy with work lately, and I’d love to have them all together again. Maybe we can make some of the traditional dishes—like Sunday roast or something.      That sounds great. I could help with the cooking. I’ve been practicing my recipes lately, and I think I’ve gotten a bit better. I’m even trying to write some of them down for future reference.      That’s a good idea. I’d love to learn more about cooking, especially since I go to nursing school. I think it’s a great way to unwind and also help out in the house. Plus, it’s a skill that’s always useful.      You’re all right, then. I think it’s important to have a bit of structure in life, especially when you’re juggling work and family.

Hey, have you seen the latest Ed Sheeran album? I’ve been listening to it non-stop. It’s so good, especially that track about Cambridge. I feel like it’s like a love letter to the city.      Oh, I know! I’ve been waiting for it too. I think the lyrics about the River Cam and the colleges really hit home. I mean, we both grew up in Cambridge, right? It’s like he’s writing about our hometown.      Yeah, it’s crazy how he can put so much into just a few lines. I almost feel like I can picture the campus in my head just from listening. I wish we could go back and visit sometime. It’s been ages since we last went to the botanical gardens.      I know, I miss the plants too. We used to go there every weekend during the holidays. You remember that one tree we used to climb? The one with the big branches that blocked out the sun?      Oh, you mean the one that was actually a bit dangerous? I still remember that one time when you fell and scraped your knee. You were so mad at me for pushing you!      Yeah, and you were so smug about it. I still have the scar. It’s like a badge of honor, right? Anyway, I was thinking about school today. I’m getting really stressed about the upcoming Science and Maths tests. I’m already dreading the physics one.      I know, I feel the same. I just don’t get how we’re supposed to memorize all these formulas. It’s like trying to remember the entire periodic table in one go. I think I’m going to ask the teacher for extra help next week.      Maybe you should. I’ve been using this app that helps you practice problems step by step. It’s not perfect, but it’s better than nothing. Oh, and did you know they’re starting the Art class next month? I’m thinking of doing a project about Christmas.      That sounds cool. I was going to do something with plants, like a mini greenhouse. I’ve been collecting seeds and trying to grow them. My mum says I’m a natural gardener.      You are! I think you’re going to be great at it. Speaking of Christmas, are we still doing the annual family tree thing?

I’ve been trying to get that rat puppet out of my granddaughter’s room for weeks, but she’s too attached to it. It’s not even real, it’s just a toy! But she talks to it like it’s the most important thing in the world.      Oh, I know the feeling. My niece had a stuffed elephant that she named "Benny." I swear, she used to take it to school and leave it on her desk. I once saw her trying to teach it to count!      Yeah, I remember when my brother used to play with a puppet like that. He’d make it sing and dance. My mum used to get so upset. She’d say, “You’re turning the house into a theatre!” But he was just being playful.      I remember when I was a kid, I used to make a puppet out of a sock and a stick. I thought it was the greatest thing. My mother thought I was being too theatrical. Eventually, I grew out of it, but I still remember the way it moved.      I think we all had our little creative phases. I remember when I was younger, I used to ring handbells in church, and I thought it was the most amazing thing. I used to imagine that the bells were speaking to me.      Oh, I remember when I was a kid, my uncle used to play the handbells at the local church. He used to say the bells had a soul. I used to think he was mad, but now I kind of believe him.      I think it’s just the way some people are wired. I used to love the sound of the bells. I still do, actually. I’ve been thinking about getting my eyes tested. I’ve been having trouble seeing the finer details on the bus.      That’s not good. I had that problem a few years ago. It was really scary. I ended up having to go to the optician, and it turned out I had a bit of a cataract. It was fine once they fixed it.      I’m not sure I want to go through that. I’ve always been a bit scared of the doctor. But I suppose it’s better to know than to be blind.      Exactly. I think we should all get our eyes checked. I’ve been meaning to for a while now.

You know, I've been meaning to ask you, what’s your favorite thing about Venice? I mean, apart from the canals and the architecture, which are obviously amazing. But I feel like there’s more to it than just the tourist traps.      Oh, there’s so much more! I grew up here, you know. Venice used to be a much quieter place. I mean, back in the 80s, you could walk through the streets and hear the sounds of the people, the fishermen, the traders. It wasn’t all about the tourists who just come for the photo ops. It was a real city with a real rhythm.      That’s what I’ve always heard from the locals. It’s sad to think of it as just a tourist spot now, isn’t it? I guess when you grow up there, you see it differently.      Absolutely. I remember as a child, the markets were so lively. You could walk through the Rialto and see the fish being sold, the spices, the fruits. The food was different too. You didn’t just go to a café for coffee and a slice of lemon cake. You went to the trattorias, where the food was real, the ingredients fresh, and the people friendly.      I wish I could go back and experience that. When I first came here, I was just overwhelmed by the crowds. But I’ve been trying to explore the smaller places, the hidden gems. I went to this little family-run café yesterday and had the most amazing espresso. I think it’s called La Bottega, isn’t it?      Yes! That’s the one. The owner, Maria, is from the old school. She treats her customers like family. You can tell she loves what she does. I always go there when I can.      I’ll have to check it out next time. I was also thinking about what we could do today. I know it’s a bit late, but maybe we can take a walk along the Grand Canal? I want to see it at sunset. It’s supposed to be magical.      That sounds wonderful. I’d love that. I’ll even bring my camera. You know, I’ve been meaning to take some photos of the old buildings at dusk. The light is so soft and golden.      Perfect. It’ll be like a little escape from the tourists.

So, I heard you mentioned you're going to the gym more often now? I mean, I know you've been trying to get back into shape, but how are you doing with it?      Honestly, it's been a bit of a rollercoaster. I started off really motivated, like, every single day, but then I got so busy with work at Bupa and then my friend group started hanging out more, and I just... lost my rhythm.      I know what you mean. It's so easy to fall back into old habits, especially with nights out and all that. But I’ve been trying to be more consistent lately, even if it’s only two or three times a week.      That’s actually really inspiring. I think I need to set some kind of goal, like maybe hitting a certain number of sessions a month, or even tracking my progress. I’ve heard people talk about apps that help with that.      Oh, I use one of those. It's called  Fitbit . It tracks your workouts, steps, even your heart rate. It’s not the most glamorous thing, but it keeps me accountable. And honestly, it helps me feel like I’m on track with my fitness goals.      Yeah, I might have to try that. I’ve been thinking about trying something like that, but I don’t know if I can afford the subscription.      Oh, no worries. There’s a free version, and it's pretty basic. I just upgraded to the premium one because I wanted more features, like tracking my nutrition. It’s not perfect, but it’s a start.      I’m definitely going to look into it. Speaking of which, have you thought about what you’re going to do after university? I mean, you’re a project co-ordinator now, but I know you’ve been thinking about your future.      Honestly, I’m still a bit stuck. I love my job, but I’m not sure if I want to stay in project coordination forever. I’ve been talking to some people about maybe moving into management or even starting my own business.      That’s exciting. I think it’s good to have those conversations early on. It’s not like you have to have everything figured out, but it’s good to have a direction.      Yeah, I guess that’s the thing. I don’t want to just be coasting through life like I’ve been doing.

Well, I just got a card from my daughter, and it’s all about her new grandbaby. She’s got the most adorable little face—like a tiny version of me, I swear! It’s so exciting, isn’t it? I’ve been meaning to call you about it.      Oh, that’s wonderful! I remember when my son was born, I thought I’d never get used to the idea of being a grandpa. But now, it’s like time has slowed down a bit. Still, I can’t help but think about how different things are now compared to when I was your age. You know, back in the day, people talked about the world in a different way.      Definitely. I’ve been thinking about how much the world has changed, especially with the way people move around. I’ve been meaning to visit France again, actually. How do you think things are there now? I’ve heard stories about property prices and the bureaucracy.      Oh, France, France. I’ve always had a soft spot for it, even though I’ve never truly lived there. I’ve been to Paris a few times, but I’ve always found the bureaucracy frustrating. The way people go on about property and land—it’s like a different language. You ever try buying a house in France? I’ve heard it’s a nightmare.      Oh, I did try once. It’s all about the paperwork and the taxes. And the land? I mean, it’s beautiful, but the system is so different. It’s like they’re always waiting for you to make a mistake.      Exactly! And don’t even get me started on the anarchists and the bureaucrats. It’s like they’re the same thing. I once had a friend who tried to visit London from France, and he barely made it through customs.      That’s for sure. I’ve heard about Chichester Cathedral’s spire collapsing. Are you aware of that? It’s tragic.      Yes, I read about it. The architect was called Porden. I’ve always been interested in architecture. I’ve been writing a book about the history of English cathedrals, actually. It’s a bit of a gothic obsession on my part.      That sounds fascinating. I’ve been to the British Library a few times—what’s your take on it?      It’s a treasure trove, but I’ve always felt there’s something missing.

So, I just got my results back from the mock exams. I’m pretty happy with them, but honestly, I’m so tired of all the revision. It’s like every day is just studying, studying, and more studying. Do you guys feel the same?      Honestly, I feel like I'm going to collapse. I’ve been up all night studying for history, and I still couldn’t remember the dates. I mean, how do you even focus on that stuff when you’re so exhausted?      Yeah, I feel the same. I mean, it’s not even exams yet, and I’m already burned out. I think we all just need a break, even if it’s just for an hour. Like, maybe go out somewhere or just relax for a bit. But I guess the teachers won’t let us.      I know, man. I was thinking about going to the park with my mates this weekend to just clear my head. But my mum said I need to study for that science test next week. Ugh, I feel like I’m wasting my time.      Speaking of waste, I saw this comic yesterday that was so funny. It was about a kid who tried to skip school and ended up getting caught by his principal, who turned out to be a giant robot. It was wild. I still laugh about it.      Oh man, I love comics like that. You know what I just read? This one about a superhero who is just a normal kid who accidentally gains powers. Like, it's so relatable. I mean, what if I had powers? I’d probably just use it to throw paper at the teacher.      I’d use it to walk through the walls. No more getting stuck in the hallway. But seriously, you know what I miss the most? My family dinners. We used to have these big meals every weekend, like the whole family would come over, and we’d all just talk and eat. It was like a real event.      Yeah, I miss that too. We don’t even have time for that now. My parents are always busy with work, and I’m always with my friends. I mean, I’m not complaining, but it’s kind of sad. I go home and it’s just me and my sister, and she’s always on her phone.      I get that.

Well, I do hope Jonathan doesn't get too excited about his birthday. He's already got the whole house in a muddle because he's been trying to clear out the old stuff from the attic. I don't know how he's going to fit all this stuff in the new house we’re thinking about moving to.      I know, it's a bit of a nightmare. I've been helping him this week, and honestly, it's like trying to sort through a museum. You'd think after all these years, people would just get rid of things they don’t use. But no, they've got this bizarre attachment to every little trinket.      Mum! Can I have the old TV? It still works, I swear!      Oh, not the TV again! You’re eleven, for goodness’ sake! That thing’s been in the attic since the ’90s. You can’t even use it properly now. And besides, we’ve got a new one coming, and it’s got all the latest tech.      You know, maybe there's something to be said for nostalgia. I mean, I left my old office – that’s been cleared out, and I actually miss the way things used to be. But maybe it's just me. I always thought branding meant something more than just a logo. It’s kind of funny, though. I wrote a book about it, and now I'm trying to clear out my own things.      I still remember the day your colleague, Neil, tried to sell his old university sweatshirt as a “branding piece.” He claimed it was a collectible. I almost fell out of my chair.      Oh, I remember that. You were still in high school back then. You were more into planning your holidays than branding. Although, I did have a few good ideas about how to market our garden. It was a bit of a mess, but I thought it could be a holiday rental.      Yes, you did. You thought you could turn the garden into a luxury resort. You even got a brochure printed. I still have it somewhere in the attic, between the old photo albums and the dusty pots.      Maybe we can do that! We could turn the garden into a garden party place. I’ve been thinking about putting up posters for the school fairs. We could sell lemonade and cupcakes.

Hey, have you thought about your GCSE options yet? I mean, I know it’s only the beginning of the year, but I feel like I’m already overwhelmed. I’ve got to choose between maths, English, sciences… and then there’s the arts. I’m really torn between doing drama and clarinet. Do you think I should pick one or the other?      Honestly, I don’t know. I’m still trying to figure out what I want to do. I think I’m leaning towards doing history and English, but I’m also really into YouTube. I mean, I’ve been watching these YouTubers like MrBeast and PewDiePie, and it’s crazy how they’ve made such a name for themselves. I wonder if you could even get a job doing that? I mean, I know it’s not a real job in the traditional sense, but you can make a lot of money.      Yeah, I mean, some people do. But I don’t know if I’m cut out for that. I think I’d rather do something more stable, like maybe a tech job or a teacher. I’ve always loved learning, and I think teaching would let me help others. Although, I still might go for something like graphic design or something creative. It’s just so hard to know what to do.      I know, it’s really stressful. I’ve been trying to talk to my dad about it, and he said that he thinks I should do what I’m passionate about. But then again, he’s not exactly sure what that is. He’s always said he wanted to be a famous person, like a rock star or something. I don’t know, it’s so confusing.      I think you’re not the only one. I remember my brother talking about wanting to be a YouTuber too. He even started a channel, but it never took off. He tried to do videos about bogs and bloggers, which was so weird. I mean, it was a funny idea, but he didn’t have the right audience or anything. It’s like, how do you even get people to watch your videos?      I tried to do a few videos about PE, like trying to do a push-up or something, but I can’t even do one properly. I think I’m just too lazy. I mean, I love PE, but I always end up being the last one to finish.

You know, I’ve been watching these birds all morning. They’ve been flitting around the garden like they’re trying to find something. I’ve seen a sparrow, a magpie, even a crow. I don’t know what’s got into them.      I think they’re just trying to get some food. Winter’s been a bit harsh, hasn’t it? I’ve noticed the birds are acting more skittish than usual. Even the squirrels are more cautious these days.      It’s not just the wildlife, is it? I’ve been thinking about the history of this area too. My gran used to talk about how the village used to be much more lively, with more people around. Now it’s just us old folks hanging around.      Yeah, I remember when this place was buzzing with activity. The farmers used to come in and out all the time, and the shops were always open. Now, it’s just a ghost town with a few lads from the youth club and occasional tourists like ANON.      You know, I’ve been reading about the history of Norfolk lately – it’s fascinating how the county has changed over the years. There used to be a lot of industry here, especially in the textile sector. I think my great-grandmother worked in a factory in Norwich.      That’s interesting. I’ve always thought the textile trade was the backbone of Norfolk. My father used to talk about the mills all the time. He said it was a booming industry back in the day.      I suppose things have changed. I remember when we used to have more jobs around here. I was a childminder for years, and there were always people needing help. Now, with the economic downturn, it’s hard to find work, even for someone like me with a little bit of education.      It’s sad to see the area decline so much. I used to work as a civil engineer, so I saw a lot of development projects back in the day. But now, it’s like everything’s been left to rot.      I’ve been researching some environmental software lately. It’s amazing how we can track wildlife patterns and even predict changes in local ecosystems. It’s a bit of a different world from the way things used to be, but it’s a step forward.      I suppose we all have to adapt in our own way.

So, I was just thinking about schools. I was in a secondary school in Costessey, and it was nothing like now. We had to walk five miles to get there, and the teachers used to beat us with sticks if we didn’t do our sums. But it was a good school, I suppose, and we all got on well. I reckon it was better than today’s schools. They’ve gone all soft on the kids, don’t you think?      Oh, I agree. I went to a school in Harrow, and it was a different story altogether. We had all these rules, and the teachers were strict but fair. But I do miss the days when kids had to earn their place. Now, they’re all given things on a plate. I mean, I can’t even remember the last time I saw a child actually work for something.      Well, I suppose that’s part of the social change. I was a teacher, so I saw both sides. Young people now have more opportunities, but they also lack discipline. I used to have to discipline them in the classroom, but now it’s all about sensitivity and not making anyone feel bad. It’s a bit of a paradox, isn’t it?      I don’t know, mate. I’ve seen the system change so much. Back then, you couldn’t even wear the wrong color shirt to school. Now they’re allowing all sorts of clothing. I remember once I had a friend whose dad used to hang around the school with a paintbrush and a ladder, just to make sure no one was wearing the right uniform. He used to say, “If you don’t dress the part, you don’t belong.”      Oh, that’s a classic. I had a cousin who used to do that. He’d hang around the gates with a clipboard and a marker. He used to say, “If you’re not in the right uniform, I’ll write you up.” I think he actually did write people up.      I remember a joke about that. “Why did the school inspector get kicked out of the school? Because he tried to check the uniforms, and the headteacher said, ‘We don’t allow inspections in this school!’”      That’s a gem. I’m going to have to remember that one. I think it’s about time we start writing some of these old jokes down.

So, I was just thinking about that snow we had last week. I mean, it was  massive , wasn’t it? I woke up to a world covered in white, and it felt like we were living in a fairytale—except the motorway was a complete mess. I swear, if I had to drive anywhere, I would’ve just stayed in bed all day.      Yeah, I remember. The whole town was stuck. I tried to get to the university, but the roads were like a warzone. I ended up staying at my flat with my mates, watching  The Office  and eating takeaway. It was pretty ridiculous, honestly. I think the snow was a good excuse to do something different though.      I totally agree. You know, I was thinking about starting a garden in the back of the house. With all the snow we’re getting, maybe it’s finally time. I’ve been looking into some plants that can survive the cold, and I even found this app that helps you plan your garden based on your climate.      That sounds great. I’ve been meaning to do the same. I’ve got a few raised beds I want to build, and maybe some fruit trees. I was actually thinking about doing a  Come Dine With Me  event with my friends. You know, like a cooking competition. We could all bring our best dishes and judge each other. It might be fun.      Oh, that sounds like a solid idea! I could do a vegetable-based menu—grilled courgette, roasted carrots, and a herb-infused quiche. You could do something more traditional, like a Sunday roast. It would be nice to have a proper meal without the hassle of going out.      Yeah, I like that. I’ve got a few recipes up my sleeve that I’ve been perfecting. Maybe we could guestimate the scores and have some prizes. I could even get my mates to join in as judges. It could be a really fun night.      Definitely. Speaking of events, I was also thinking about the stag and hen parties. I hear the wedding is coming up in a few months, and I’ve been trying to figure out what to go for. I think a weekend getaway would be perfect—maybe somewhere with a beach and a few activities.      That sounds like a good plan. I was actually going to suggest a place in the Lake District.

Aye, these are nice. Proper home-cooked. I remember when I was a lad, my mum used to make these every Sunday.      Aye, and she would always say they were the best in the whole of Norfolk. I’ve tried a few places, but nothing beats the real thing.      I have to say, I’m quite fond of roast dinners. There’s something comforting about the smell of roast meat and Yorkshire pudding. Although, I prefer it with some green beans on the side.      Well, I can see why you’d say that. I’ve always been partial to a bit of variety. But I must admit, the roast beef here is quite good. A little bit of garlic in the sauce, and it’s almost like it’s been made by a chef.      Aye, well, it’s not like the restaurants in London where they serve you overcooked meat and a plate of cold vegetables.      I remember when I was a childminder, I used to bring little ones to the village hall for Sunday dinners – all the local farmers would bring their best meat and vegetables. It was a proper community thing.      That sounds lovely. I’ve been to a few village events, but I always feel a bit out of place. I suppose because I come from a city, you know?      Aye, it’s a different vibe. I’ve been to a couple of events in Norwich, and the sense of community is really strong there. It’s not just about the food, it’s about the people.      Well, food brings people together, no matter where you come from. I think that’s why I always say, if you want to know a person, just sit down and have a meal with them.      To good food, and good company.      And to life, and the joy of sharing it.      To the simple things in life.      And to the fact that even though we’ve had different lives, we still find our way back to the same table.      Aye, and that’s the real treasure.      It’s amazing, really. I used to think that being a lecturer was the most important thing in life, but now I see that the people around you are what really matters.      Exactly. The food, the conversation, the warmth of the room – it all adds up to something special.      Well, if that’s the case, we should be having dinner every night.

So, Dad, I’ve been meaning to ask you—why do you always make that weird tomato and cheese soup? It’s like a cross between a soup and a sandwich!      Oh, that’s your mum’s recipe. She learned it from her grandma, who used to say it was the only way to keep the family healthy. Though honestly, I think it was just a way to get more cheese out of the fridge.      I remember that. You used to chase your mum around the kitchen trying to get her to stop making it. I mean, I still remember the time the soup spilled on the carpet and we had to clean it up with the dog!      Oh, yes, that was a disaster. The dog turned into a soup monster for a while. But you know, I still think that soup has a kind of comfort food magic. It’s like the smell of home.      I guess it  does  have that comfort thing. But I still can’t figure out why you never make it now. It’s like you’ve forgotten how to cook.      Oh, I’ve just been too busy with work and all. But I think it’s because I’ve been cooking more for myself lately. You know, when you’re on your own, you don’t want to mess up the food.      That’s true, love. I remember when I was younger, I used to cook for my wife and kids. But after she passed away, I found it hard to cook for just one. I think I just stopped trying.      That’s sad. But you know, even if it’s just for yourself, cooking is a way to stay connected to the past. It’s like a recipe is a memory.      Yeah, that makes sense. You know, I’ve been thinking about moving back home for a while. I always used to joke about it, but now I think it might be a good idea.      Yeah, I’d really like that. I’ve been working so much lately, and I just feel like I’m missing out on the real life that happens when you’re at home.      Just don’t forget to bring your own cheese, then. I’ll be there to make sure you don’t end up with another soup disaster.      And I’ll be there to make sure you remember how to use the stove.

So, I was just thinking about how we could integrate more interactive elements into online learning. I've seen a few viral videos on TikTok where students are using gamified learning platforms—like Duolingo or even some AI-driven tutors. It's pretty cool how they're making education more engaging.      That's interesting, I've seen some of those videos too. I think the key is making learning less about passive absorption and more about active participation. But I wonder, how do you actually implement that in a university setting? Especially with the rigid structures they have.      That's a good question. I've been thinking about starting a small venture—something like an edtech startup that provides tools for universities to track student engagement through interactive modules and real-time feedback. The idea is to help professors see how students are interacting with the material and adjust their teaching accordingly.      That sounds really promising. I mean, I've been working in education for years, and I've seen how difficult it is to keep students engaged, especially in remote or hybrid learning. What do you think the biggest challenge would be?      Well, one of the main challenges is getting universities to adopt new tools. They often have a lot of bureaucracy and are hesitant to change their traditional methods. Also, there's the cost—investing in new platforms can be a big financial hurdle for smaller institutions.      I can see that. But maybe if we can show them the ROI—like higher retention rates, better student outcomes, and more personalized learning experiences—it could make a difference. I know some of the students I work with are really eager for more interactive and flexible learning options.      Exactly. And with the current shift towards remote and hybrid learning, it's more important than ever. I've been looking into some case studies where universities that implemented gamified learning saw a significant increase in student participation and satisfaction.      That’s really encouraging. I'd love to help out if you're open to it. My knowledge of education systems and student behavior could be useful. Plus, I can help you navigate the university bureaucracy a bit.      That would be great. I think collaboration between entrepreneurs and educators is key for meaningful change. I'd love to have you on board as a consultant or even as a partner in some capacity.

Hey, thanks for coming over! I’ve been dying to catch up. It’s been ages since we last saw each other. How have you been?      I’ve been good, thanks! Just got back from a weekend shift at the clinic. It was a bit hectic, but I managed. How about you? Work okay?      Yeah, it was pretty busy too. We had a last-minute project deadline, and I had to pull double shifts. But it’s all done now, so I’m just trying to relax. I’ve been thinking about what to do this weekend. You know those Halloween parties that happen around here?      Oh, I know! There’s one in the village on Saturday. I was actually thinking about going. The one at the community centre. It’s always a good time, and I think the food is decent. But I was wondering if you’d like to come with me?      Honestly, I’d love to! I’ve been meaning to go to one of these for a while now. I’ve been too busy with work and everything. But maybe we can go together? I’ll ask if the others are free too. It might be fun to have a group.      That sounds great. I think the others are okay with it. I was also thinking about my 5-year plan. I’ve been considering moving to the countryside for a bit. I want to get back to nature and maybe start my own nursing practice. Do you have any thoughts on that?      That’s actually something I’ve thought about too. I’d love to live in the countryside and be closer to the land. I’ve been reading a lot about different English counties lately. Do you know much about the English countryside?      I do! I’ve always been fascinated by the different regions. I think the Cotswolds are amazing. The rolling hills and the little villages. I’d love to live somewhere like that. Have you ever been?      Not really, but I’ve always wanted to. I think I’ll start looking into that after this year. I’ve been thinking about taking a little trip to the South of England next month. Maybe visit some of the historic places and get a feel for the area.      That sounds like a great idea. I could come with you, if that’s okay. I’ve been meaning to see more of the UK.

Oh, I just had the most ridiculous idea about the garden, and I had to tell someone. You’ll think I’m mad, but it’s actually quite clever.      You always have the strangest ideas, but I’m all ears. What’s on your mind?      So, I was out there this morning, minding my own business, when I noticed this huge patch of weeds in the corner. And I thought, what if I just let it grow? Not cut it, not weed it, just let it be. You know, like a wild garden?      A wild garden? You’re talking about turning your front yard into a jungle?      Not exactly a jungle, but something more natural. I thought, what if I just let the wildflowers take over? Maybe even plant some native ones, and then let them run wild. It’d be like a little bit of nature, not just a garden.      That does sound interesting. But wouldn’t it take forever to get going? I mean, you’d have to plant something first.      Oh, I know, but I thought maybe I could start with some seeds. And then just… let it happen. I mean, I’ve seen these wildflower meadows in the countryside. They’re so beautiful. Maybe it could be a bit of a project.      It could be. But you know, I’ve always thought that gardens are meant to be tamed, not left to their own devices. Still, I can see the appeal. You’re not the only one with a green thumb, you know.      I know, but I think it’s time to try something different. You know, I’ve been doing the same thing for years—cutting, trimming, killing weeds. It’s all so… controlled. I’d like to see what happens if I let it go.      Well, I suppose if you’re going to do it, I might as well help. I’ve got some time on my hands, and I’d love to see the results. What do you think the neighbors will say?      I don’t think they’ll mind. They might even be impressed. Though I’m sure some will have a few words to say. But I think it’s worth the risk.      Alright, then. Let’s start with the seeds. I’ll go get my old gardening books and see what we can find. Maybe we can make it look like something special.

Right, so I was just telling my mates about the football match last night. The way that team played was just ridiculous. I mean, they had a chance in the first half, and they didn’t even try to score. It was like they were playing for the other team! I don’t know, I thought they had some good moves. But yeah, I guess that’s just how it goes sometimes. Did you see that player from Cambridge? He was on fire, wasn’t he? Oh yeah, he was, but the rest of the team just didn’t back him up. It’s so frustrating. I mean, I’ve only been to France for like a week, but I already miss the vibe of the games back home. You know, the real passion, the way the fans get behind their teams. I get that. I think it’s just different here. I mean, everyone here is so chill, and the games are more about enjoying the atmosphere rather than the actual competition. But hey, I guess it’s a good way to relax. Yeah, but I can’t help but think about uni. Did you get your results yet? I’ve been so stressed about the exams. I’m dreading the next one. I just hope I don’t fail again, like I did with that essay on scientific methods. You always said you were bad at essays. I remember you writing that one about the difference between qualitative and quantitative data. I still can’t believe you got a pass. Oh, don’t remind me. I thought I was going to fail that one. I spent three days writing it, and I still didn’t know what I was talking about. But I guess I’m just not the academic type. I’d rather be out playing football or listening to some new bands. Yeah, I get you. I’m more into bands than I am into science. I mean, I was thinking about going to a gig this weekend. There’s this local band here that’s been getting some good reviews. Do you want to come? Honestly, I’d love to. I haven’t been to a live gig in ages. I think it’s time I shook up my routine a bit. Plus, it might give me some inspiration for my translation assignment. You know, the one where I have to translate a poem from French to English.

So, I was just thinking about how weird it is that we have spiders and mice in our houses, but never birds. I mean, I’ve never seen a bird in my flat, even though there are plenty of birds outside. Do you ever see them coming in?      Honestly, I haven’t seen a single bird in my house since I moved in. I mean, I’ve had mice, a few spiders, even a cockroach once—scared the life out of me. But birds? I think it’s just the way the windows are set up. Maybe they don’t like the view or the noise from the street. Or maybe they just don’t want to get too close to humans.      My neighbor said something similar. She mentioned that birds are more skittish than they used to be, maybe because of all the litter and the way we mess with their habitats. I’ve noticed that even when I open the window, they just fly away or keep their distance. It’s like they’re not trusting us anymore.      That’s actually kind of sad, isn’t it? I mean, we’re surrounded by nature, but we don’t really interact with it. I think it’s funny how we’ve got these little creatures in our homes, but we don’t even really acknowledge them. I mean, I’ve caught mice in the kitchen, and I’ve seen spiders in the corners of the bathroom, but I never really think about them as living beings.      I guess that’s the problem. We sort of treat them like pests rather than part of the ecosystem. I’ve had to deal with a few spiders in my office too. One time, I saw one on my desk and I about jumped out of my chair. I couldn’t even tell if it was a spider or a fly.      Oh, I’ve had that experience too! Maybe we’re just not used to seeing them up close. I remember once I saw a mouse in the hallway, and I was so startled I dropped my cleaning supplies. I ended up shouting for my husband, and he just laughed at me.      That’s probably the best reaction. I mean, we’re not going to let them run free, but maybe we could be a little more understanding. I go out walking my dog sometimes, and I see all sorts of birds and small animals in the park.

So, this is where you live, then? It's... quite cozy. I've heard a lot about Stevenage, but I haven't been here before.      Yes, it's a lovely town. I moved here from Bristol years ago, actually. It's not what I expected, but I've grown to love the quietness and the community feel. You're from Dorchester, aren't you? I remember hearing that place mentioned when I was teaching.      Yes, that's right. Dorchester is a small town in the south of England, near Bournemouth. It’s a bit of a mix—there's a lot of history there, and the sea is never far away. I grew up there, and it shaped a lot of my views, even though I ended up teaching in London.      That must have been a big move. I remember when I first started teaching, I felt like I was leaving behind everything I knew. It took me a while to settle in. Speaking of settling in, I've been meaning to ask—how did you end up teaching? I still can't believe I managed to stay in education for thirty years. I left last year, and it's been... different.      It was a natural progression, honestly. I wanted to work with children, and I've always been passionate about education. I even did a postgraduate course in teaching methodology. It gave me a deeper understanding of how students learn, which I think made me a better teacher.      That’s impressive. I only had a secondary school education, and I did everything I could to keep up. I taught English for most of my career. It was hard work, but I loved it. Speaking of which, have you heard any stories about my family? I’ve been meaning to tell you about my mother's illness.      I’ve heard a bit. I think it was something like Alzheimer’s? I’m sorry to hear that. It must have been hard on the whole family.      Yes, it was. She had it for a number of years, and it got worse and worse. I remember the last time I saw her, she didn’t even recognize me. It was heartbreaking. She was a strong woman, but the disease took everything from her.      That sounds really difficult. I’ve been through a lot in my life, but I never had to deal with something like that.

So, I was just thinking about that hot air balloon festival we saw last summer. Do you remember when we got stuck in the field because of the wind? It was  absurd .      Oh, I remember! I was so worried we’d end up spending the night in a field with a balloon and a dog. But then we met this guy who had his own balloon and offered us a ride. It was wild.      I know, right? And then we ended up camping that night. We had to pitch the tent and set up the fire, and the dog was just running around like it was the most exciting thing ever. I swear, he thought he was the star of the show.      Oh, he  was  the star. He had this look of triumph whenever he chased a squirrel and came back with the little guy in his mouth. You’ve got to admit, he’s a pretty good hunter.      He is. And I think the wildlife here is just so much more active than in the city. I mean, in London, you’d be lucky to see a bird, let alone a fox or a deer.      Yeah, and it’s not just the animals—it’s the whole vibe. The countryside just gives you so much more space to breathe. Plus, you can still see the power lines, but they’re like part of the scenery now.      I know, and honestly, I’d rather have the power lines than the noise and pollution of the city. It’s a bit of a trade-off, but I think we’d rather have a quiet walk through the fields with a dog and a few birds than a packed train and a million people.      Exactly. And the money thing? It’s funny how much you spend on stuff in the city, but out here, it’s more about experience than possessions. Like, we could afford that camping trip, but we wouldn’t have been able to do it in London without a budget of at least three times as much.      Yeah, and you know what’s cool? Even though we’re both lecturers, we don’t have to worry about the money as much as people in other jobs. It’s not like we’re struggling to make ends meet or anything.      True. But I still think we’d love to see some of those hot air balloon festivals in different places.

So, I was thinking about how the weather has changed so quickly this year. It's been like one thing after another—sunny one day, then pouring rain the next. It’s almost like the seasons are fighting over the calendar.      I know what you mean. I’ve been coaching people at the gym, and it’s been tough keeping a consistent schedule. One week we’re doing outdoor classes, and the next, it’s all indoors because of the weather. It’s like the seasons are playing a prank on us, isn’t it?      Yeah, and I’ve been teaching language classes online, so I’ve noticed that people are more willing to learn when the weather is nice. I guess when it’s rainy, they’re more inclined to stay home and binge-watch shows instead of coming to class.      True. I always thought that people with a bit more education would be more likely to commit to learning, but I’ve seen the opposite. Some of the most dedicated students are the ones who just have a passion for it, not necessarily the highest qualifications.      That’s interesting. I was thinking about how books can be such a great resource. I’ve been reading a lot lately about teaching methodologies, especially in language learning. It’s amazing how much you can learn from just a few well-chosen books.      I’ve always been someone who prefers practical knowledge over theoretical. That’s why I ended up in management. I like being able to see results quickly. But I have to say, I’ve been reading more about personal development lately because it’s about time I stopped taking things for granted.      I hear you. I think it’s important to keep learning, even if it’s not in your job. It keeps your mind sharp. Speaking of which, have you ever thought about taking up a language? I’ve been helping some of my students with their English, and it’s been a real eye-opener for me.      I’ve thought about it, but I’ve always been too busy. Although, after a couple of years in management, I think I’ve reached that point where I need to do something for myself. Maybe I could even start coaching language classes, you know? Who knows, maybe I’ll be your partner in crime one day.      Only if you promise not to make it too difficult.

Right, I've got the list here. We need to make sure we don't forget anything for the weekend. I know it's a bit of a long list, but with the grandkids coming over, we need to be prepared.      Yeah, I reckon it's going to be a bit of a party. Both grandmas and grandpas are coming, and then there's the kids. I think someone should bring the snacks. You know how they get when they're excited about the weekend.      Oh, the snacks are always a bit of a problem. My son used to bring these giant bags of crisps and sweets. They never lasted the day. I suppose it's better to have a bit of variety—maybe some fruit, some cheese, some chocolate. Something for everyone.      You know, I remember when I was a kid, we had to make do with what we had. A bit of bread and cheese, maybe some tinned beans. Now, with the grandkids, it's like hosting a dinner party every weekend. I reckon we should set up a little table in the garden for them. Bring out the picnic blanket and some music.      That's a good idea. The weather's been nice lately, so it's a shame to keep them all indoors. I'll check the forecast again before we decide. Besides, we can always move things around if the weather turns.      Speaking of the forecast, I heard there's supposed to be some rain tomorrow. I'll bring an umbrella just in case. You know how the grandkids get when it starts to drizzle. They all run inside like it's the end of the world.      Oh, I remember that all too well. I tried to calm them down once, but they just said, “Mum, it’s not raining, it’s just falling.” I didn’t know what to say.      That’s the spirit of the go. They’re just kids, you know. They don’t see the world the way we do. I think we should make sure they feel at home. Maybe we could tell them some old stories from when we were young. The kind that made us all laugh and remember the old days.      That sounds lovely. It’s a shame we don’t get to see them as often as we’d like. With work and responsibilities, it’s easy to let things slip.

Hmm, I'm not sure about this route. It says it's the shortest, but I've been driving past this road for years and never seen this turn-off. Are you sure we're heading the right way?      Yeah, it says it’s the fastest route, but I’ll be honest, I’m a bit skeptical. I’ve been down this road once before, and it turned out to be a dead end. Maybe it’s updated since then?      That’s the problem with satnavs these days, isn’t it? They think they know everything, but sometimes they’re just wrong. I remember my dad always used a paper map, and he never got lost. Though, to be fair, he also never dared to take the A-roads unless he had to.      True. But I guess we all have our quirks. Speaking of quirks, I remember that time you got us both stuck in a field because the satnav said there was a petrol station, but it turned out to be a duck pond.      That was a classic. I was so embarrassed. I remember pacing around that field like a madman, shouting at the sky, thinking I was in some kind of survival show. I even tried to hitchhike, but no one stopped.      I was the one who said, “At least the ducks are happy.” That’s the kind of thing that keeps me going in this job. I write about the absurd and the mundane, and I need to find the poetry in it all.      I can see that. You have a way of making the ordinary feel special. I used to think I was just a teacher, but now I think I’m a storyteller too. My students often say I make history come alive.      That’s the magic of it, isn’t it? Whether you’re teaching or writing, it’s about connecting people to something bigger than themselves. Speaking of connecting, do you think we’re going to make it to the gig on time? This weather’s not helping.      I hope so. I don’t want to miss that gig. It’s a big one, and the band’s been on the rise. I’ve been to a few of their shows, and they’re really something special.      Yeah, I’ve heard they’re amazing. I’m just hoping my car doesn’t break down again.

So, I just got back from the site visit, and it was a bit of a mess. The client had some last-minute changes to the brief, and the contractor was already halfway through the foundation work. I was tempted to just walk away and say, “This is a disaster,” but I kept my cool. I mean, it’s not like I haven’t seen this before.      Yeah, I remember that. You always have that kind of client who thinks they’re the only one who can see the big picture. But you know what? They’re not the only ones who get stressed about it. I had a friend of mine at the office—let’s call him Dave—who’s been struggling with his project brief for the university. He’s been going through the motions for months, and it’s starting to show.      Oh, Dave? Yeah, he’s been in a rut. I saw him last week, and he was just sitting in his office, staring at his laptop like it was the enemy. I told him to take a break and go for a walk, but he said he couldn’t even get up. He’s got this idea that if he puts in more hours, he’ll get the brief right. But honestly, he needs to take a step back and figure out what he actually wants from the project.      I agree. It’s one thing to be passionate about architecture, but it’s another thing to have a clear vision. And honestly, I think he’s just trying too hard. He’s got this image of being the next big thing, but he’s not even on the right track.      I know. Anyway, I was thinking about talking girls the other day. I was at the university cafeteria, and there was this girl who looked like she had a degree in architecture. She was sketching something on her tablet, and it was really cool. I asked her what she was working on, and she said it was a proposal for a community housing project. I almost asked her out, but I was too nervous.      You’re still a nervous wreck, aren’t you? I’ve seen you flinch at the sight of a girl with a sketchpad. But you know, you could do worse. You’ve got that quiet intensity that people go for. I mean, if you ever do get into a relationship, I’d suggest you don’t talk about architecture the first time you meet.

You know, I was just thinking about how different driving habits are these days. I mean, I grew up in Boston, and I remember how people were always polite on the road. You’d signal, you’d give way, and you’d never cut someone off. It felt like a kind of unspoken code of respect.      Oh, I’ve noticed that too. I think it’s just because so many people are rushing now. I mean, it’s not just about getting somewhere quickly—it’s about being in a hurry to get somewhere  else . I’ve even had people who just zoom past me at traffic lights and then double back when they see someone’s going the same way. It’s like a game of chicken, but on the road.      Exactly! And I think it’s worse now with all these cyclists and pedestrians. I was almost hit last week by a car that just decided to park in the middle of the road. I mean, that’s not even driving—it’s just reckless. I had to wave my phone in the air like I was trying to communicate with aliens.      I remember when I first started driving in Grantham—it was like a whole new world. I got pulled over once for not using my indicator, and I was so embarrassed. I thought, “This is a small town, how hard can it be?” But I soon learned that people don’t just drive, they  perform .      Yes, and it’s not just the drivers. I think there’s a general lack of patience these days. I was at the supermarket the other day, and someone cut me off at a junction. I just gave them the finger, and they just looked at me like I was a complete stranger. It’s like we’re all barely speaking the same language anymore.      I’ve noticed that. I think part of it is the way we’re all so busy. If you’re always stressed, it’s easy to forget that people are just trying to get somewhere as well. Maybe we should all try to be a little more considerate. I mean, it’s not like it’s hard—just a little bit of patience.      You’re right. I think sometimes we forget that driving is a shared space. I was going to ask you if you wanted to go out for a walk later.

So, I just read through the job ad for the media position ANON is applying for, and I think it’s a really good opportunity. It’s at a local broadcaster, right? They’re looking for someone with experience in radio and media production. That’s kind of what ANON does, so it’s a good fit.      Yeah, I think it’s a solid move. They’ve got a good reputation in the area. But I have to say, I’m a bit nervous for them. ANON’s never applied for a job like this before. They’ve always worked independently.      That’s true, but they’ve got the skills. They’ve done a lot of work for local radio stations and even produced a couple of podcasts. The key is how they present their experience in the application. You know, they need to highlight the right things.      Exactly. And they’re going to need to write a strong cover letter. I’ve been helping them draft a few versions. It’s tricky, though. They want to make sure they don’t come off as too ambitious or too uncertain.      I get that. You don’t want to overstate your achievements, but you also don’t want to understate them. So, I was just telling my partner about the 40s party last week... It was a disaster. You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about that referendum we had last year. It was so divisive, wasn’t it? I still remember the arguments we had in the kitchen about it. Yeah, you used to play it too, remember? You were always the one who’d try to make up songs on it.

So, I've been thinking about social media a lot lately. I know it's such a big part of our lives, both at work and for fun. I just can’t get used to this new car. It’s got all these fancy gadgets, but I’m more used to the old one. You know, the one that didn’t break down every three months. Oh, I’ve been trying to learn Spanish for years, but it’s like trying to teach a cat to bark! Maybe you should look into language exchange groups? I heard there are some online platforms where you can chat with native speakers. So, Dad, I've been thinking about sorting all this paperwork. I know it's going to take a while, but I thought maybe we could scan everything and then put it into a digital folder. You know, I’ve never been to this place before. It’s a bit out of the way, isn’t it?      Yeah, I know. I passed it on the way to the motorway junction. It’s been one of those stretches where we were just pulling through, no time to actually stop. I used to go to one near my old flat in Nottingham. It had this weird little pastry counter and the guy there always had this strange habit of making up stories about the customers. I still remember that one time he said he’d once met a biker who’d ridden from London to Edinburgh on a single tank of fuel.      That’s a story. I’ve always heard about the occasional biker who’s got that kind of experience. But do you think they’re still around? I mean, with electric cars and all.      Mate, they’re still around, and they’re still having a laugh. I saw one of them the other week at the pub. He was telling everyone about his road trip across Europe and how he managed to scare off a couple of suspicious locals with his motorcycle. It was hilarious.      That’s a different type of adventure. I mean, I like driving, but I’ve never been the biker type. I’m more the "let’s just get to the next town and get a takeaway" kind of person.      Yeah, I get that. But you know, there’s something about the open road. Even if it’s just for a weekend. I think it’s a chance to see things you wouldn’t normally see.      I guess. I just feel like every time we drive somewhere, it’s like a little journey with its own challenges. Like, who knew you could get stuck in traffic for an hour just trying to get a coffee?      And yet, here we are, stuck in a petrol station between two exits, with a questionable choice of snacks.      You know what they say – every journey begins with a single step, and in this case, it’s a single petrol pump.

Right, I was just thinking, do you know who you'd rather play tennis with—Federer or Djokovic? I mean, they're both legends, but I can't decide.      Ugh, I don’t really know. I mean, Federer’s just so graceful. I watched him play when I was younger, and it was like watching art. But Djokovic is so intense, you know? He just doesn’t stop.      I think it's the skill, really. You can't argue with what they've achieved. But you know, I actually played a bit when I was younger. My mum used to take me to the local club every weekend. It was a way to keep me out of trouble, honestly.      Oh, that’s sweet. I remember when I was your age, I was a total tomcat. I’d rather have been out riding my bike than going to tennis practice. I hated it at first, but now I can’t imagine not playing. It’s just… it’s like a second language. You don’t think about it, you just do it.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? It becomes part of you. I remember when I started, I was terrible. I’d hit the ball into the net every time. But after a few months, it just… clicked. You learn to trust your instinct.      I think that’s what makes the difference. You’ve got to believe in yourself. Even when you’re not hitting the ball right, you have to keep going. My brother used to tell me, “You can’t win if you don’t play.”      Yeah, he’d say that a lot. But honestly, I think he was just trying to get me to stop whining about missing a serve.      You know, I’ve been thinking about taking up coaching. I mean, I’ve got the experience, and I’d love to help someone else find their passion. Maybe you could start coaching, Dad? You’ve got a natural way of explaining things.      That’s an interesting idea. I mean, I haven’t thought about it, but I do enjoy teaching. Maybe there’s something in it. I just hope I don’t turn into one of those people who yells at kids all the time.

So, I was just telling my mates about the napkins we had at the family dinner last night. They looked like underpants! I swear, they were the same color and had the same shape. I thought we were having a joke, but then my mum said, “Don’t worry, they’re just  bodacious  napkins.” I didn’t know what she meant at first.      Oh, I remember that. It was one of those  very  British moments where you’re like, “Is this a joke or is it just… weird?” But honestly, I couldn’t stop laughing. I think we all thought it was a prank, but no one said anything. It was like we were all in on it.      I was so confused. I thought maybe it was a new trend or something. I almost asked, “Is this a religious symbol?” But I didn’t want to ruin the moment. I just thought, “What’s happening here?”      Yeah, I remember being like, “Is this part of the Christmas dinner tradition now?” I mean, I thought we were safe with the turkey and the mince pies. But those napkins? I still don’t know what they were.      Oh, those napkins! I remember them too. You know what I think? They were just the wrong size. Like, someone got the wrong pack from the kitchen. But it was so funny. I had to tell everyone about it the next day.      Right, and then there was the Christmas music. I nearly cried when I heard “All I Want for Christmas Is You.” I mean, it’s a good song, but I was like, “Wait, why is it so  emotionally powerful ?”      I know, right? I thought, “I can handle this. I can handle the emotional weight of a Christmas song.” But then I started thinking about how my son got a new toy, and it all just… clicked.      I think that’s the thing with Christmas. It’s all about memories. Even if it’s just about napkins that look like underpants and a really loud song.      And your dad was telling us all about how he and your mum first met during Christmas. He said it was like a  Downton Abbey  moment.      I’m not sure if that’s a compliment or not, but I’m sure it’s true. He kissed her on the cheek in the middle of the park, and they swore it was fate.

So, I’ve been thinking about that dinner we had last week with the Browns. I still can’t believe how much money we spent on that fancy restaurant. So, I just got an email from my boss about the appraisal. I was supposed to be doing a presentation on the new project, but I think I’m more ready to talk about the new Marks and Spencer food line. Alright, I’m not sure if I’m ready for this night out. I was just trying on these new heels, and I’m already slipping in the shop. Oh, come on, you’re doing it again.
