You know, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about soul mates. I mean, I don’t believe in them in the romantic sense, but I do believe in people who just  get  you. Like, you know the one person who can look at you and understand your quirks without asking a single question.      I know what you mean. I’ve always thought about it in terms of spiritual journeys. Like, maybe we’re all on a path, and sometimes we meet someone who helps us reach a part of ourselves we didn’t even know we had. I think that’s what I felt with you—like you were someone I didn’t have to explain to.      That’s sweet. But I think I’m more of the practical type. I’d rather say, “I like you because you make me laugh when I’m exhausted,” than talk about soul mates and spiritual journeys. Although... Maybe I’m just not ready to talk about that yet.      Fair enough. I do like the idea of imaginary parties, though. I mean, what if we hosted a party in the 1920s? Or maybe even the 18th century? I’d love to see how people dressed, what they talked about, and how they interacted.      You’d be the one trying to convince everyone to wear bowler hats and speak in measured tones. I’d be the one in a flapper dress, dancing with the first guy who asked me to.      Exactly. I’d be the  disapproving  uncle. But I’d still be there, cheering you on from the corner.      You’re impossible. But I love it. You know, I’ve been thinking about visiting some historical sites. Maybe we could do a road trip. The Tower of London, the Roman Baths... something like that.      That sounds amazing. I’d love to take a break from work and just wander around. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck lately, and maybe a change of scenery would help.      It’s on the agenda. We’ll plan it for next month. I just need to check with the director about my schedule.      I’ll take care of the itinerary. You just relax and think about the historical figures we might meet along the way.      I’ll be thinking about the ones who were probably more interesting than us. But I’m sure you’ll be the one who ends up telling the best stories.

It’s so good to catch up, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking about how much I’ve missed our chats, especially since I’ve been so busy with the new project at work. How are you all doing?      I’ve been good, thank you. Work has been a bit hectic lately too, but it’s not as overwhelming as it used to be. I actually got promoted recently! I’m now a senior civil servant, so I guess I should be more confident. Although, I still feel like I’m not quite there.      You’ve made it, love. I remember when you were still working on that project that took you six months to finish! You were like a one-woman team, and now you’re running the show. I’m proud of you.      Thank you. I couldn’t have done it without everyone’s help. Speaking of which, I heard you’re running that little business in Peterborough. How’s that going?      It’s going well, honestly. I’ve been trying to keep it small and community-focused. It’s not as big as I’d hoped, but it’s something I’m proud of. I’m even thinking about expanding a bit next year, maybe opening a second location in Grantham.      That’s great! I’ve always admired your tenacity, even when you were starting out. I remember when you used to knit in the evenings just to pass the time. Have you still got that habit?      Oh, I’ve never stopped. I even make little gifts for the kids at the local nursery. It’s a great way to keep my hands busy and remind me that not everything has to be about work. Though I have to say, I’ve realized that the language I use in my business is a bit more formal than what I use at home. It’s quite a shift.      I know what you mean. I sometimes feel like I’m speaking two different languages when I’m at work versus when I’m with my family. It’s a bit strange.      Yeah, I’ve noticed that too. I think it’s just part of the job, but it’s interesting how our language changes depending on the context. I’ve always found it fascinating how people have different dialects and ways of speaking based on where they’re from, even within the same country.

So, I was just telling my mates about the flat we saw on Airbnb last week... It was in some weird part of the city, and I swear the toilet was louder than the shower. I don’t know how anyone lives there.      Yeah, I remember when we were looking for somewhere to stay. I think we all had a bit of a breakdown. I mean, I still can’t believe we managed to get a place that wasn’t a single room with a shared bathroom.      Oh, I know what you mean. I was in a house with six other people, and we had to share the fridge. It was like a MySpace group chat for food.      That sounds like a nightmare. I’ve been thinking about how much we’re spending on rent. I mean, we’re all students, right? How do people afford this?      I know, it’s insane. I’ve got a part-time job, but I still can’t cover the bills. I’ve been thinking about moving back home, but my parents live in the South, and I’d hate to move so far.      I can’t even afford to buy a sandwich every day, let alone pay rent. I mean, I’m trying to save up for the phone bill. I’m already in debt with that.      I’ve been trying to figure out how to manage my money. I’ve had to cancel a few subscriptions and cut back on shopping. I used to buy a new outfit every month, but now I just wear the same jeans every day.      Yeah, I’ve done that too. I’ve even started cooking more. Maybe I’ll start a cooking blog for the uni newsletter. It’s not like I have anything better to do.      You could start with a blog about how your pasta is burning every time. I swear, I once watched a video where someone cooked a pasta dish and it looked like it had been in a fire.      I tried that once. My flatmate thought I was trying to make a brûlée. It was a complete disaster.      So, have you heard about the football match this weekend? I think it’s against Leeds.      Yeah, I’ve been waiting for this all week. I’m so tired of watching boring games. This one’s gonna be a real match.      I’m going to be there.

So, I was just telling my mum about the time I tried to ride a moped in Bolton and ended up in the hospital because I hit a kerb. It was  not  pretty.      Oh, you had  that  incident? I remember hearing about it from your dad. You were so young, and you thought you were being so brave.      Yeah, I remember hearing about that. You were like, "I can do it, I can do it!" and then, boom, you were in the ER. It was like a mini  Mission: Impossible .      Yeah, well, I still have the scar on my knee to prove it. And I was so proud of myself, thinking I was cool and independent. Silly me.      You were just trying to grow up, that’s all. I remember when I was your age, I thought I was the greatest at everything. I used to ride my bike all over town and never looked back.      Speaking of growing up, did you ever think about going to university? I mean, I know it’s not for everyone, but I’ve been thinking about it. I want to study something like business or maybe even something related to the environment.      Oh, I think that’s a great idea. You’re smart, and you have a good head on your shoulders. I went to university, and it opened up so many doors for me. It wasn’t always easy, but I’d say it was worth it.      Yeah, I was thinking the same thing. I’m currently looking at a few courses and trying to figure out what I want to do. It’s kind of overwhelming, but I think I’m on the right track.      Well, as someone who works in management consulting, I can tell you that having a degree opens up a lot of opportunities. It’s not just about the job— it’s about the confidence and the skills you gain.      Exactly. And it’s not just about the money. It’s about being able to make a difference, to have a voice in the world, and to be able to support your family.      I guess I just want to be able to live on my own one day. Not like, completely on my own, but have my own space and not have to rely on my parents as much.      That’s so true. I think that’s part of growing up.

So, I’ve just come back from Cornwall, and I can’t stop talking about it. You should’ve seen the YHA volunteer work we did! It was like a proper holiday, but we were also helping out with the community.      Oh, I heard about that! I thought you were going to be on a cycle race or something. I’ve been thinking about joining one myself. I mean, I’ve got this old bike in the garage that’s been collecting dust for years.      That sounds like a good plan, but you’d better not start without me. I’ve got a friend who’s a cyclist, and he’s been talking about a "Yorkshire in a day" race. It’s a bit of a challenge, but I’m thinking of signing up.      A Yorkshire in a day? Sounds like a mad idea. I’ve done the lighthouse walk up in Cornwall, though. That was something else. I remember the sea was so rough, and the wind was howling like a pack of wolves.      You always loved the sea, didn’t you? Even when you were a kid, you used to go crabbing with your dad. I still have that photo of you, all covered in sand, holding a crab like it was a trophy.      Oh, yes, that was the day. I think I got that crab stuck in my shoe for hours. But it was worth it. I still remember the way the sun was setting over the water.      I think the lighthouse and the crabs were both part of your favorite things. You always said about how the sea was a kind of living thing. I mean, you used to talk about it like it had a soul.      Well, it does in a way. It’s got the tides, the waves, the crabs, the birds. All that stuff. It’s something you can’t really explain, but you feel it when you’re out there.      I’ve been thinking about taking some photos of the lighthouse while I’m still in the area. You know, maybe something for the wall. I’ve been looking through my old photos, and it’s like a time machine.      That’s a brilliant idea. You could even frame it with the one from when you were a kid. I’ll help you with the setup. We could even try to get some of the local kids to come over and see it.

So, I’ve been thinking about that date I had last week. He said he’d got a big promotion, but when I saw him, he was still wearing the same old clothes as before. What a bloke!      Oh, I knew someone like that. My cousin had a guy who was all about the big words and the “I’m a man of culture” stuff, but he couldn’t even cook a proper egg. You know what I mean?      Yeah, I’ve had that too. The guy I went out with once was always talking about his “career aspirations” and how he was “working hard to make it.” But the last time I saw him, he was hanging out with his mates at the pub, eating chips and shouting about the football.      Oh, you’re not telling me you actually went out with someone like that? I mean, I wouldn’t be surprised if he thought he was the next Tony Blair or something!      Oh, he was definitely a contender for the “Most Overqualified for a Pub Quiz” award. He once tried to explain the meaning of “moral relativism” in a bar. You know what happened? The barman got bored and walked out.      Honestly, sometimes I think people use their professions as a way to impress people. Like, “I’m in finance, so I must be smart.” But I’ve seen a lot of people in finance who can’t even manage their own budget.      I guess it’s all about what people think they need to prove. I used to work in events, and I saw so many people trying to be “the one with the cool connections.” But it’s all just a facade.      Yeah, I can relate. I’m just a labourer, but I’ve got more common sense than a lot of people I know. I mean, I know how to fix a broken tap and how to cook a decent meal. That’s more than a lot of “professionals” I’ve met.      Exactly. I think it’s funny how people think that having a certain job makes you a better person. I mean, I’ve got a postgrad degree, but if I had to choose between that and knowing how to make a proper roast dinner, I’d go with the roast dinner every time.      That’s the spirit! I think I’ve been trying to make a point here.

Hey, I’m back! I can’t believe how long I was away. I’ve been in Barcelona for the weekend and it was absolutely amazing. I’m so glad I got to see the city, even though it was just for a few days.      Oh, you were in Barcelona? That’s great! I’ve been wanting to go there for ages. How was it? Did you get to do all the things you wanted to?      It was absolutely incredible. I stayed in a place right near the beach, and I got to walk along the Rambla every day. I even went to the Sagrada Familia. I’ve always loved architecture, and that place is just stunning. You know that one scene from  No Country for Old Men  where they’re walking through the streets? It felt like that, but way more alive.      Sounds like you had a great time. I still haven’t gone to Barcelona, but I’ve been thinking about planning a trip. Do you think it’s worth the hassle? I mean, the flight is expensive and I don’t want to just end up being stuck in a hotel the whole time.      It totally is worth it, especially if you go in the summer. I met a few people from the local bar where I was – they were all super friendly. I even tried some really good tapas. You know, the ones with fried potatoes and all that. I ate so much that I almost couldn’t move the next day.      Oh no! That sounds like a good problem to have. I’m actually thinking about doing something similar with a friend. Maybe we could go to Paris next? We’ve been talking about it for ages. I mean, I’ve always wanted to see the Eiffel Tower and the Louvre.      Paris is amazing too. I actually saw  La La Land  there, but that was just the movies. The real thing is even more beautiful. I think we should plan something soon. Maybe you can come with me next time I go to Barcelona – or maybe we can even go together?      That sounds like a plan! I’ve been meaning to go somewhere for a while, and this would be a nice way to do it. I can go talk to my boss and see if I can get some time off.      Perfect. I could use a trip too – I’ve been working way too much lately.

Good morning! This is a lovely spot, isn’t it? I’ve been meaning to come here for a while. The sea view is absolutely perfect for a Sunday morning.      It’s a real gem, isn’t it? I’ve been coming here off and on for years. I actually met my wife the first time I brought her here for a coffee. She loved the ambiance.      Oh, that’s romantic! I’ve always been a bit of a bookworm, though. I think I’d have ended up in a library or something. I’ve worked as a teacher for the past ten years, mostly in secondary school. I’ve had a pretty steady career, but it’s not without its challenges.      That’s impressive. I’ve always admired people who can make a difference in the lives of others. I’m an entrepreneur, actually. I run a small business importing handmade goods from various countries. It’s been a rollercoaster, but I love the freedom and the creativity it brings.      That sounds fascinating. I’ve always been more of a planner, though. I like knowing what’s coming next. I suppose that’s why I ended up in teaching. It gives me a sense of structure and purpose. I even did a postgrad in education, which helped me move into a more senior role.      That’s really admirable. I’ve got a graduate degree too, in business management. It helped me get started, but the real learning has come from just diving in and making mistakes. I often tell people that the best way to learn is to fail and then try again.      I can see that. I’ve had my share of failures too, especially when I first started teaching. I remember the first time I had to deal with a disruptive class. I thought I was going to lose my mind. But over time, I learned to adapt and found my rhythm.      That sounds like a classic growth moment. I used to be really hesitant to take risks, but once I started experimenting with my business model, things really took off. It’s funny how being out of your comfort zone can lead to the best opportunities.      Absolutely. I think we both have different paths, but they’ve led us to similar places of growth and satisfaction. It’s always nice to meet someone who’s been through similar experiences, even if we come from different backgrounds.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever miss living with your old flatmates? Like, I know we’re not exactly in the same situation, but I've been thinking about how much I used to enjoy the chaos of the flat.      Honestly, I do. I mean, it’s been a while since we had that kind of…  chaos . Remember when we used to just throw everything on the floor and call it a ‘designer look’? It was madness, but it was also kind of fun.      Oh, I remember! And when you tried to cook and the whole kitchen ended up burning down? You said it was a ‘smoky ambiance’ and left it for hours. I was so terrified I’d get a fine from the council.      Yeah, I almost got called out for that. I mean, I did get a warning from the landlord, and it was a bit of a wake-up call. But I think I would’ve kept doing it if it wasn’t for the smell of smoke creeping up the stairs.      It was such a mix of good and bad. I miss the rhythm of it all. You know, the noise, the mess, the weird hours. And the fact that we could just come home and not have to worry about anything else.      I guess it’s kind of like that now, in a way. We’re not exactly a chaotic bunch, but we do manage to make each other laugh a lot. I mean, it’s not the same as having a bunch of people around all the time, but there’s a different kind of comfort in just having someone to come home to.      Yeah, I know. It’s not the same. But I do think we’ve got a nice balance now. I mean, sometimes I wish we had a roommate to bounce ideas off, or someone to cook with, you know? Like, just to make things more interesting.      Maybe we can find someone? I mean, if we’re not too busy trying to survive on takeaway and takeaway.      Oh, don’t get me wrong, I love takeaway. But I do miss the days when we’d have proper meals. Maybe we could try to at least take turns cooking once a week? Just to get back into the rhythm?      I’m in. As long as you don’t try to burn the kitchen again.

Well, I've done it, old girl. I got the shopping done without even having to go to the supermarket. Just a few local shops, and I managed to save a few quid.      You did? That’s a surprise. I thought you'd be stuck in the same old routine. A few local shops? That’s a lot more than I can manage, honestly.      Oh, it wasn’t that hard. Just slow and steady. I went to the corner shop first, then the butcher, then the baker, and then grabbed a few bits from the greengrocer. I even got the bread and milk from the same place. It all added up.      I suppose it’s about staying active, isn’t it? You never know when you’ll need to move around. Though I do miss being able to take the bus, even if it's just to the post office.      Yeah, I know. It’s one of those things. I used to take the bus all the time when I was working. Now it feels like a big effort just to get out the door. But I suppose it’s better than sitting in the house all day.      I suppose so. You’ve always been the more active one, even when you were still working. I used to follow you like a puppy, just to make sure you didn’t get lost.      That’s what you are, you old dog. Always close behind. But I’ve got to say, I feel a bit more useful now. Maybe I’ll start going to the library or the community center. I heard they’re doing some activities for retired folks.      The community center? Are they still running that? I thought it had shut down a few years back.      I’m not sure. But I saw a notice on the door the other day. It said they were reopening. Maybe it’s something to do with the council's new initiative. I’m hoping it’ll give me something to do.      Well, if it’s something you enjoy, I say go for it. You’ve always been the one with the energy to do things. I just hope you don’t overdo it.      Don’t worry, I’ll take it easy. I’ve got a long time to go. I’m not ready to retire from living yet.      That’s the spirit, old man.

Right, I've got the list here. We need to make sure we don't forget anything for the weekend. I know it's a bit of a long list, but with the grandkids coming over, we need to be prepared.      Yeah, I reckon it's going to be a bit of a party. Both grandmas and grandpas are coming, and then there's the kids. I think someone should bring a few games to keep the younger ones occupied during the day.      I've got the games, actually. I found an old set of Scrabble and some cards in the attic last week. I brought them down to the shed, but I can pick them up in the morning if you need them.      That sounds good. I remember playing Scrabble with my dad when I was a kid. He was pretty good. I think he once beat me at that game. I still can't get over it.      He must've had a real knack for words. I remember him watching the news and trotting out all these fancy words. It was a bit intimidating at first, but I learned a few myself.      Yeah, he was always trying to teach us how to play. Though I think he did it more to show off than to actually teach. Anyway, I'm just glad he was around. He was a real character, wasn't he?      He was. And you know, I still miss him. It's funny how the years go by, and suddenly you're not just talking about him—you're remembering all the things he did and the stories he told.      It's part of what makes family so important. Even though he's not here, he's still part of our lives in so many ways. I think the kids are really good at keeping that connection alive. They always ask questions about him, and I try to tell them as many stories as I can.      That's one of the best things about them. They're so curious and eager to learn. I think that's what makes this family so strong—we're all connected through these shared stories and memories.      Exactly. And that's what makes the visit so special. It's not just about the food or the games, it's about bringing everyone together and sharing those moments. I think we're all looking forward to it.

Right, so I’ve been thinking about these health supplements I saw online. They’re all over the place—vitamin D, probiotics, even something called “dragon fruit extract.” You know, the ones that claim to boost your immunity and improve your skin.      Honestly, I don’t trust any of that stuff. I mean, I’ve tried a few things from the shop, like those protein bars and energy drinks, and I feel like I’m just paying for a placebo.      Yeah, I’ve seen that trend too. It’s like everyone’s suddenly obsessed with “natural” stuff. I mean, I’m a student, so I’m always trying to balance school and fitness. I’ve been working out more, and I’ve started taking some sort of multivitamin just in case.      That’s what I did too, but then I realized I was actually paying for a pill that’s mostly sugar and filler. I’m going to switch to eating more real food instead.      I did that too. I’ve started cooking more, which is probably why I’ve lost a bit of weight. But I still feel like I need that “extra boost” sometimes, like before exams or when I’ve been studying all night. It’s weird how much we trust these products, even when we don’t know if they work.      Exactly. I’ve been trying to use some of the apps that track your health, like the ones that monitor your heart rate and sleep patterns. It’s all very high-tech, but I’m not sure how accurate they are.      I’ve used one of those apps too. It told me I wasn’t getting enough sleep and even suggested a new pillow. I bought it, and now I’m like, “Oh, I just sleep better on my old one.”      That’s what I thought too. My brother told me about a time he followed a fitness program for three months and then stopped. He ended up gaining all the weight back, but he still thought he was “on the right track.”      I remember my cousin doing the same thing. He started running every day and ate all sorts of weird stuff—like kale smoothies and whatnot—and then one day he just stopped. He said he was “burning out,” and now he’s back to his old habits.      Yeah, it’s funny how everything trends.

Okay, I think I’ve finally got everything sorted for tomorrow’s shopping. Let me just check the list again—milk, bread, eggs, and maybe some fruit. Did we mention the apples?      Yeah, you did. And I think we need to pick up some toilet paper while we’re out. I reckon we’re running low. Also, I saw that new brand of coffee on the shelf—do you think we should try it?      Can I just say, I don’t even know what’s on the list anymore. I’ve been scrolling through TikTok for the last hour, and now I’m like, “What’s a milk carton even look like?”      Oh, come on, Sam. I think you’re just being dramatic. You’ve got a list right there. You just need to actually look at it. Although... Maybe I should double-check it. I’m not sure I got the fruit down. Did we say apples or bananas?      I think it was apples. But as long as we get something for fruit, that’s fine. Speaking of fruit, have you seen those little bugs crawling around the kitchen? I swear they multiply every time I turn my back.      Yeah, they’re everywhere. I was trying to kill one earlier with a piece of paper, and it just ran away. What’s the deal with these things? Are they like, immune or something?      I don’t know, but I heard from my mum that if you squish them with your bare hands, it stops them from spreading. Although, I’m not sure if that’s true. I mean, I’ve only ever seen a wasp once, and that was in a tree. I didn’t even try to kill it.      You know, I once had a bite from a horsefly. It was terrifying. It didn’t really hurt, but it swelled up like a balloon. I think the best thing was to put some ice on it and take an antihistamine. But the worst part was the itching—it lasted for days.      Yeah, I got bitten by a mosquito last week. It was like someone had stuck a hot needle into my arm. I’ve been using this cream my dad gave me, and it’s helping, but I still can’t stop scratching.      I’m not sure I’d ever want to be bitten by anything. I mean, football’s the only thing I really care about.

Hey, have you seen that new YouTube channel by that guy who does science experiments? I think his name is James, or maybe it's Jake? Anyway, he did this one experiment where he put a whole bunch of balloons in a box and then heated it up, and the balloons all exploded. It was so cool!      Oh yeah, I saw that! I tried to find the video again, but I couldn’t remember the exact link. I guess I should check my Instagram feed again. I follow a few science YouTubers, like the one who does physics with everyday objects.      Yeah, I follow him too. He’s pretty good, but the real star is that guy who does like, the science with food videos. He made a vinegar and baking soda volcano that actually erupted and covered the whole table! My science teacher was so impressed, she even said she was going to try it in class next week.      Seriously? That’s amazing! I mean, I’ve seen a lot of videos like that, but it’s still cool to see real people doing it. I guess you have to be really creative to make it look that good.      Totally. I think it’s because they’re using so many different materials. Like, they use baking soda, vinegar, red food coloring, and even some glitter. It looks like a real volcano. I’m glad my teacher is going to try it. Maybe I can help her set it up.      You’d be perfect for that. You’re always the one who picks up all the supplies and brings them to class. I mean, science class is the only time I actually pay attention, and it’s mostly because of those videos.      Yeah, I know, right? I used to hate science. But after watching all those YouTube videos, I started to like it a little. I mean, I still don’t like the actual experiments, but the videos are so fun. And honestly, I think it’s helping me get better grades.      That’s so true. I mean, if you can make learning fun, then why not? I’ve started following more educational YouTubers, and it’s helping me remember things better. Plus, some of the teachers even recommend them in class.      I wonder if our science teacher is on Instagram? I think she might be. Maybe I can follow her and see what she’s up to.

Ugh, I feel like a walking glue factory. I think I’ve got a cold. I’ve been sneezing all morning, and my throat feels like it’s been sandpapered. How are you holding up?      Honestly, I’m not far behind. I’ve been battling this for three days now. My nose is so congested I can barely breathe through it. I think I might be starting to get food poisoning too. Last night, I ate something questionable at that new café near the campus. Now I’m feeling like I’ve been hit by a bus.      Oh no, that sounds rough. Did you go to the clinic or something? I’ve been meaning to get my flu shot. It’s been a while since I had one, and I heard the new one’s actually effective this year.      I was going to, but I’ve been too run-down. I’ve been thinking about the whole vaccination thing lately. I mean, I’m not anti-vax, but I do worry about the long-term effects. I’ve heard some people say they’ve had weird reactions, even after one shot. It’s a bit of a dilemma.      I get that. I was pretty nervous about it too, but my doctor said it’s pretty safe and that it’s important to protect yourself, especially with the hospital system being as busy as it is. I’ve been to the hospital a couple of times for check-ups lately, and it’s been so stressful. The waiting rooms are always packed, and the staff are overworked.      Yeah, it’s been wild. I had to wait over two hours just to get a consultation last week. And you know the thing that’s really tripping me out? The new cameras everywhere. They’re using body language recognition tech to monitor patients, like to detect pain or anxiety. It feels a bit intrusive, even if it’s supposed to help.      That’s something I’ve heard about too. I mean, it’s supposed to be a way to improve patient care, but I can’t help but feel like it’s a step too far. I’m also thinking about watching that old Lloyd Grossman show again. I remember the guy was a go-to guy on TV for food reviews. He had this weird charm, even if he was a bit of a slob.

Oh, I just can’t believe I’ve got this word in my rack.  Scrabble —I mean, is that even a real word? I thought it was a type of board game. Not sure if I should even use it.      Oh, it  is  a real word, but I think it’s more of a verb than a noun. Like, when you’re  scrabbled  in a game. Though, honestly, I think it’s just a way to describe the chaos when you're trying to get the last letters.      I think you’re both overthinking it. Scrabble is a game that’s been around for decades, and it’s got a rich vocabulary. I’ve had to look up words for hours in my head just to win a game with the kids. They’ve even started calling me "Scrabble Queen."      And I remember when I was a schoolmaster, we used to play Scrabble in the staff room. Sometimes it would go on for hours. I’d say it was one of the most competitive games I’ve ever played—except for the chess matches we had on Fridays.      Well, I got “quibbling” on the board, and I’m still not sure if that’s a valid word. But I don’t want to be the one who ruins the game by being too strict.      Quibbling? I think that’s a word, but I’d definitely put it in the “questionable” category. I’d be surprised if it’s even in the dictionary. Maybe it’s a regional thing? Dad, do you remember when we used to study English in school? I mean, we used to argue about whether "colour" or "color" was correct. I think we even had a spelling bee once. You know, I still can’t get over how that old Ford got to be so quiet. It’s like it’s been given a new lease of life, isn’t it? I think the real benefit is the mental clarity it brings. When you’re out in the wilderness, there’s no Wi-Fi, no emails, no deadlines. It just forces you to slow down and be present. I’ve found it really helps with my stress levels.      I can see the appeal, but I’d still be too nervous. You don’t know what’s around the corner. One minute it’s fine, the next—it’s freezing, and you’re lost. I mean, I remember reading about a guy who got stuck in a blizzard for three days. No one knew where he was. That’s not something I’d want to risk.      That’s a scary story, but I think it’s a matter of preparation. If you know what you’re doing, it’s not as dangerous as people think. You carry the right gear, you know the weather forecast, you plan your route. And you’re not alone, you’re with people who understand the risks.      Yeah, and there’s something powerful about pushing yourself out of your comfort zone. It’s not about being reckless. It’s about understanding your limits and respecting nature. I think it’s a skill that takes time to develop.      I guess I just don’t see the point. I’ve got my garden, my books, my cup of tea. I don’t need to go out into the cold. But I can see how it could help some people. Maybe if you’re feeling down, or overwhelmed by work.      It’s not just about escape. It’s about grounding yourself. When you’re out there, you’re not just surviving—you’re living.

So, I was just thinking about that film we watched last night,  The Banshees of Inisherin . You remember how that ending just...  popped ? I mean, it was so unexpected, right?      Yeah, I couldn’t believe it when Martin left Colm. I was like, “Wait, what? Is this a metaphor for something?” But then I realized, no, it was just... well,  him . He’s just that kind of man. You know, the type who’s always walking away.      Exactly! I mean, I get it, but it felt like they were trying to make us feel the weight of his decision, you know? Like, he’s not just leaving because he’s upset, he’s leaving because he’s  friended  with someone else now. It’s so sad, but also kinda poetic.      It’s interesting how they treated the relationship, isn’t it? Like, it’s not just about the man himself, it’s about the  idea  of friendship. I mean, the whole film is about how people change and how relationships can fade, even if you don’t realize it. It’s kind of like how we all grow up and start to see the world differently.      Yeah, I thought that was one of the best parts. And then the whole ending with the chicken and the coffee... that was just...  perfect . I mean, it’s so simple, but it captures the whole essence of the film.      Definitely. I was thinking about how it all ties back to the themes of  literature  too. Like, it’s almost like a modern-day  Wuthering Heights , but with a more grounded, real-life kind of drama.      Oh, really? I mean, I’ve read  Wuthering Heights , but I never really thought about how it compares to modern films. I guess both are about passion, obsession, and the passage of time. Except in the film, it’s more about the  internal  conflict, not the external.      Yeah, I think that’s right. And you know, I was just thinking about food the other day. I had this really amazing meal last weekend – pulled pork with some of that southern-style BBQ sauce. It was so good, I almost cried.      Is that the kind of food you get when you’re a consultant engineer? Or is that just your secret passion for cooking?      No, it’s not that. I just love good food, and I think it’s one of the things that makes life worth living.

Alright, let's see... I've been thinking about those stories we used to tell when we were kids. I remember one about the time we tried to build a treehouse with Lego and ended up knocking down half the garden.      Oh, I remember that! You were so determined to make it a castle. I think you even used the plastic bricks to make a moat. Mom was so mad when she came out and saw the mess.      I thought it was cool. I wanted to be a knight in the castle. My sword was a ruler, you know.      You were a terrible knight. I think you even screamed when the Lego tower fell. What happened to the treehouse, anyway?      I don’t know. I think we gave it up after a week. We got bored, and then we started playing with the PlayStation instead. You remember that?      Oh yes! We tried to play  Grand Theft Auto , but I think we got stuck in a loop where we just kept running into walls. It was hilarious. I think we still have that disc somewhere.      Did you ever play  Mario Kart ? I think I got the red shell every time.      You did. It was amazing. I think you even raced against the cat once. Or was that the dog?      No, that was the cat. I think he thought the game was real and tried to chase you.      I remember that. You were so scared you were going to get squashed. But you still won the race.      Yeah, and I think I got a medal for it too. You know, the one that said “Hero of the Kart.”      That was just a paperclip and some paint. You were a natural.      Wait, what about the typewriter? I think it was in the hallway. You said it was from your granddad.      Yeah. It was old, but it worked. You remember how we used to write stories on it? It was so clunky, but it felt like magic.      I miss that. I think we could have written a whole book if we had more time.      We could have. But I think it was just the way we used to talk, you know? Like, the Brownie Promise evening, when we promised to be good and help each other.      Yeah, that was real. I think we still remember it.      Maybe we should do it again. Just for fun.

You know, I’ve been meaning to ask you, have you noticed how some people in Bradford just wear these scruffy clothes all the time? I mean, not that there's anything wrong with that, but sometimes it's like they've picked up their outfit from a charity shop and left it there overnight.      Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve seen some serious fashion statements out there. But then again, I’ve also seen some of the finest breakfasts in the city. You know, the ones that come with a side of fresh fruit from the local farm. I’ve been meaning to visit one of the fruit farms near Wakefield, but I keep putting it off. I’ve got this theory that the best apples come from the ones that grow in the fields, not the ones in the supermarkets.      I agree. I’ve been growing herbs in my garden for a while now, and it’s amazing how much better they taste when you’ve picked them yourself. I even tried making some jam with them—though I’m not sure I’d say it’s up to the standard of the ones from the shop.      You’ve got to be careful with jam. I once tried making some with black currants and ended up with something that tasted more like a cough syrup than a jam. But that’s what you get for experimenting, I suppose.      Well, I still think it’s worth trying. And I’ve noticed that the locals are more open about talking about their gardens than the ones in London. Still, I can’t get over the sheer number of roadworks about the place. It’s like the city’s trying to build something new every day.      Yeah, I’ve been stuck in more traffic than I can count. I even had to stop for a coffee once—just to see if I could remember where the café was. But I think I did. I tried to make a joke about it, though. Said I was just checking if the place was still there.      That’s the spirit. Still, I’ve got to say, I think the best thing about living in Bradford is the community. Despite all the roadworks and the junk mail that keeps piling up on our doorsteps, there’s something about these people. They don’t just live here—they  belong  here.

Hey, I’ve been meaning to ask you, what’s your take on these new health guidelines about eating more chocolate? I mean, sure, it’s a treat, but I don’t know if it’s really as good for you as they say.      Oh, I’ve heard that one before. It’s like the government trying to monetize your sweet tooth. But honestly, I’ve started eating a couple of squares a day as part of my routine. My doctor said it might help with the stress of work. You know how it is, being a head of department—constant pressure.      That’s interesting. I read somewhere that dark chocolate can actually improve mood and concentration, which is good for someone in my line of work. I’ve been trying to incorporate it into my daily routine too. But I still feel guilty if I have more than a small piece in the evening.      Guilty? I’ve been there. I used to think of chocolate as a vice, but now I see it as a way to keep my spirits up. Though I’ve also started using it as a reward for good days. Like, if I finish a difficult shift, I’ll treat myself to a square or two. It’s kind of like self-care, isn’t it?      Exactly. And don’t forget the tea. I mean, it’s not just about the chocolate—proper tea and a bit of time to relax is essential. You can’t ignore the importance of body care and mental health these days.      I agree about tea. I’ve been trying to make the most of my mornings with a proper cup. But sometimes I get distracted by work and end up skipping it. It’s a habit I need to be more consistent with.      Speaking of habits, have you heard about the new mobile phone app that helps with meditation and mindfulness? I’ve been meaning to try it, but I’m not sure if it’s worth the subscription. I keep thinking about the time I spend on Facebook, but I tell myself I need to be more present.      I’ve heard of it. I tried one for a while, but I’m not really into the whole ‘mindfulness’ thing. Though I do try to take regular breaks during the day. I’ve started using the ‘focus mode’ on my phone to block out distractions.

So, I've been thinking about what I want to do next. I've got this idea for a project—like, a creative campaign for a small brand. I’d love to take it further, but honestly, I’m not sure if I’m ready to step out of my current job just yet.      I get that. It’s so easy to feel like you’re not “ready,” but sometimes the best opportunities come from taking a leap. You know, I was in a similar place last year. I was working part-time as a survey programmer, and I thought I needed to make more money before I could even consider doing anything creative.      Oh, I remember when I was in university. I had this massive fear of failure, and I couldn’t even apply for a single job because I was terrified of saying no. It’s funny how that changes as you grow.      Absolutely. I think part of it is just looking at the bigger picture. Like, you don’t have to be perfect to start. You just have to start. I mean, I did a few side projects while I was studying, and they ended up leading to some freelance work. It was a little scary at first, but it paid off.      That does sound encouraging. I’ve been thinking about applying for a few freelance writing gigs, but I’m not sure if I’m qualified enough. I mean, I have a graduate degree, but I don’t know if that’s enough.      It  is  enough. Don’t underestimate yourself. I was in a similar position—working on a postgraduate degree while trying to make ends meet. I had this job as a survey programmer, and I used it to learn data analysis, which actually helped me in my side projects. My boss even said I was the best at what I did.      That’s great. I think I need to start applying for those gigs. Maybe I can talk to my old college friends to see if they know of any opportunities.      That’s a good idea. And remember, even if you don’t get the job, it’s still a learning experience. I mean, I got rejected a few times, but eventually, I landed something. And it was all because I stopped waiting for the perfect moment.      You’re right. I think I’ll take that advice to heart.

So, I've been thinking about getting back into exercise. I've been feeling a bit sluggish lately. I used to go to the gym a few times a week, but with work and everything, it's been hard to keep up.      That makes sense. I’ve been meaning to start again too, but I’m still recovering from that little illness I had last month. Still, I’ve been walking more, which is a start. I think it’s easier to build up to something like that.      I totally agree. I’ve been trying to fit in some yoga sessions three times a week, and it’s been a great way to unwind. Plus, it helps with my posture—being a writer, I sit for so long. It’s easy to get stiff.      That’s a good point. I’ve been sitting at my desk for hours transcribing, and I’ve started to notice some aches in my back. Maybe I should try something like that. Do you think it's worth investing in a yoga mat or just doing it at home?      I think it’s definitely worth it. I bought one and it’s been a lifesaver. It’s not too expensive, and it gives you a good grip. Plus, there are plenty of free online classes, so you don’t even need to spend much.      I couldn’t agree more. There’s a ton of resources now—especially for people starting out. I’ve also started making my own smoothies instead of buying them. It’s a bit of a commitment, but it’s way healthier and cheaper in the long run.      Oh, I’m always interested in cooking. I’ve been trying to cut down on processed food, but it’s tricky. I love cooking, but I don’t have a lot of time. My sister’s always telling me to cook more, but I just end up grabbing something quick.      I can relate. I tried to make a meal once a week, but it got overwhelming. I think the key is to plan ahead. Maybe prep some meals on the weekend and freeze them? That way, you don’t have to think about it during the week.      Exactly! I’ve started doing that too. I batch cook on Sundays and freeze individual portions. It’s so much easier. Plus, it’s good for the wallet.

So, how's the work been lately? I heard you were working on a big project with the council?      It's been pretty busy, yeah. The civil engineering department’s been pushing a lot of new developments around the city. I've been working on a bridge project near the river. It’s a bit of a challenge, but the team’s great.      That sounds intense. I was just thinking about the recent Budget announcement. I mean, with the cost of living rising so much, how are you managing?      Honestly, it’s tough. I’m self-employed, so I’m not getting the benefits or the salary hikes that others are. I’ve had to cut back on a lot of things, like going out to restaurants or buying new clothes. But I guess that’s just how it is these days.      I know. I’ve been working at the university, and even with the graduate salary, it’s not enough. I’m thinking of maybe doing a part-time job on the side to make ends meet.      That’s a good idea. I’ve actually been thinking of taking on some freelance work, but the market’s pretty saturated. You know, it’s not just about the money anymore—it’s about the stress and the hours. I mean, even if someone is in a higher position, they’re not necessarily better off.      Yeah, I guess the cost of living crisis is affecting everyone, regardless of your job. It’s just sad to see how far we’ve come from the stability we had a few years back.      For sure. I was thinking, maybe we should both go to that musical at the Cambridge Theatre next week. You know, something to take our minds off work for a bit.      That sounds perfect. I’ve been wanting to see  Les Misérables  again. I always love the way the music and the story come together. It’s like a whole world in a couple of hours.      Don’t tell me you’re a real fan of musicals? I mean, I like them, but I’m not sure I could sing along without embarrassing myself.      Well, you’re not the only one. I’ve been trying to get better at singing, mostly for the sake of my own confidence. You never know when you might need to belt out a number.      Okay, okay.

So, I was thinking, do you ever get tired of the same old scenery in Liverpool? I mean, it’s got its charm, but with all the new developments going on, it’s starting to feel like a bit of a maze.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been driving around the city for years, and I swear, every time I think I know the streets, something new pops up—new roads, new buildings, sometimes even new traffic lights. It’s like the city’s got a life of its own.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? I’ve always been fascinated by urban development. It’s like a giant experiment in sociology and architecture. You’ve got these old buildings, some of them centuries old, and then all of a sudden, there’s this new glass tower next to them. It’s a bit like a play in two acts.      I think it’s the same with people, too. Some of us are like the old buildings—solid, dependable, and sometimes a bit stubborn. Others are like the new developments—flashy, modern, but sometimes a bit too much for the rhythm of the town.      Exactly. I often tell my students that understanding urban development is like understanding a living organism. You don’t just build something and leave it. It grows, it changes, and sometimes, it even sheds skin.      That’s a good analogy. I’ve got a few friends who used to live in the city and moved out when all the new buildings started popping up. They said it was like being in a film set. One day it’s a quiet street, and the next day, it’s a construction zone.      And you know, I’ve been thinking about acting for a while. I mean, I’ve always been interested in the way people express themselves. It’s something I try to unpack in my lectures. I think acting is like a form of urban development—people change, they adapt, and they often do it without even realizing it.      I’d say that’s a fair comparison. From what I’ve seen, people in the city are often more adaptable than those in the country. You’ve got to be. If you’re a taxi driver, you can’t afford to be stuck in your ways.      That’s true. And I think that’s part of what makes the city so dynamic.

So, I just saw this really weird sign off the motorway. It said something like,  “Watch out for the cow with a hat.”  I had to stop the van just to check it out. You’d think they’d at least make the sign a bit more...  normal .      That’s not weird—it’s just Polish. You know how they like to be…  creative  with their signs. I once saw one that said  “No parking, or you’ll be fined.”  Literally. It was in red, and it looked like a warning from the devil. You don’t even need to read it, you just feel it.      That’s true. But seriously, what’s the cost of living here? I mean, we’re already over budget on the fuel and the food, and now I’m thinking about how much we’ll need for accommodation once we get to Tarnow. I’m starting to feel like we’re on a budget treadmill.      I know, I know. But think about it—we’re not going to be stuck in a hotel, right? We can just stay with people or find a hostel. I’ve got a few contacts in Tarnow, some friends from my teaching days. We could even have a few local meals. It’s not like we’re planning to stay in luxury.      Yeah, but I don’t want to be the one who accidentally overspends and then has to explain it to the others. You know how some people get when they think they’re being economical but end up costing the group more.      That’s exactly why I’m keeping track of everything. We’ve got a spreadsheet. I even added a column for “unexpected expenses.” I’m not sure what I’m going to do with that column, but it’s better to be safe than sorry.      I’m not sure if I trust you with that. You might fill it with things like “hitchhikers’ snacks” or “last-minute coffee.”      Hey, I’ve been good! I only added “unexpected expenses” once. It was for the extra fuel we used when the van took a wrong turn and we had to backtrack for three miles. I told myself it was for the  experience .      You’re a disaster. But in a good way. Honestly, I’ve missed this kind of banter. It’s funny how something as simple as a trip can bring people together.

So, are we really going all the way to Preston just to buy a loaf of bread? I mean, I thought we were going to the Hay Festival, not the shop.      Well, we’ve got to get things for the weekend. The Hay Festival is a  big  event, you know. And if we don’t get groceries now, we’ll be stuck with whatever’s in the fridge.      Yeah, it’s not like we’re going to be running out of supplies, but the last time I went to the shop without a list, I ended up buying a whole cow.      That must have been a  real  haul. I remember you talking about it like you were on a shopping spree.      It was a shopping spree, all right. I bought a bag of chips for the road trip, a loaf of bread for the festival, and a spare tire just in case.      You were in a panic because your car broke down on the way to the beach. It was  so  dramatic.      I was dramatic. I remember trying to fix it myself, and I ended up getting covered in oil.      You were  literally  covered in oil? That’s the stuff of legends.      Yeah, and you ended up having to take the bus back.      I had to. I couldn’t afford a tow truck.      Speaking of stuff, have you thought about the Queen’s birthday? I mean, it’s  huge —and I think it’s coming up soon.      Yeah, the whole country’s probably going to be watching. I wonder if we’ll be able to get a cake from the shop.      I think the shops are closing early today because of the train strikes.      Train strikes? That’s not fair! I was going to go to the library for my exams, but now I might be stuck.      It’s not the best timing. I was going to take my son to the Hay Festival, but now I might have to cancel.      Well, I’ve been trying to get my act together. I’m moving house next week, and it’s going to be a  mess .      That sounds tough. I hope it works out.      Yeah, it’s a big change. But I mean, it’s also a fresh start.      It is. I just hope I don’t end up like the last time I moved. That was  so  stressful.      I can only imagine.

Oh, I just saw a post on Facebook about a man who tried to fix his Wi-Fi and ended up turning his house into a spaceship. I couldn’t stop laughing! It’s like he thought he was building a Star Trek model, not just connecting to the internet.      I remember something similar. My nephew tried to set up a smart home system a few years back and ended up with a bunch of blinking lights and no idea how to turn the lights off. He looked like he’d just been dragged into a sci-fi movie.      Yeah, my dad tried to get a smart TV and accidentally turned on the "cinema mode" and then couldn’t find the button to turn it off. He spent an hour watching the same scene over and over and just kept saying, “It’s not working, it’s not working!” Like he was in a horror movie!      I remember the time my sister tried to clear out her attic and ended up discovering a whole box of old letters from the 1930s. She was so shocked she nearly cried. It was like stepping back in time, except the only thing that changed was the dust.      I can’t imagine that. I’ve got a cousin who tried to clear out her mum’s flat and found a box of old diaries. She spent weeks reading them, and it made her really think about her own life. It’s strange how things you read in the past can affect the present.      I wonder if that’s what mental illness is like—like seeing things in the past that you didn’t notice before? Or maybe it’s just the way your brain processes things. I’ve heard some people say it’s like you’re stuck in a loop, repeating the same thoughts over and over.      I think it can be. I used to know someone who was struggling with it. They’d repeat the same phrases all day, like they were stuck in a loop. It’s heartbreaking to see someone you care about like that.      Yeah, and it’s so hard to understand if you haven’t been through it. I think it’s important to be patient and not judge. I remember my brother once said, “You can’t fix it by just talking about it,” but I think talking about it is the first step.

Right, I think I've got this laptop set up now. Let me just check if it's connecting to the Wi-Fi. Hmm, no signal. Not sure what's going on.      Oh, you didn't plug in the Ethernet cable, did you? I thought you were going to use the wired connection.      Oh no, I forgot! I thought this Wi-Fi was super reliable. I mean, it’s supposed to be one of the best in the area. Didn’t even need a password, right?      Yeah, but sometimes the router’s still a bit dodgy. Remember the time when you tried to stream a movie and it just froze mid-fight scene?      Oh man, I still remember that. I was halfway through watching  The Matrix  when the screen just went black. I thought it was the movie ending.      That was gold. You were so convinced it was the real Matrix, you even tried to hack the laptop.      Yeah, and you ended up downloading a bunch of pirated software. I was like, “Mate, you just upgraded your laptop with a virus.”      Yeah, but I learned my lesson. Now I use a firewall. Although, honestly, I still don’t trust Wi-Fi. I think it’s too easy to get hacked.      I’d say it’s safer to use Ethernet. Even if it’s a bit of a hassle. You can’t beat the stability.      I still prefer my old desktop. It’s slow, but it’s reliable. Doesn’t need updating every week.      I guess that’s the thing with technology. It keeps changing. I remember when we had to use floppy disks. Can you even believe that?      I can. I once had a friend who still uses a floppy disk to back up his photos. Says it’s “safer” than the cloud.      I’d say that’s a bit of a stretch. But hey, if it works for him, I’m not arguing.      Alright, I think I’ve got the Ethernet cable sorted. Let me try that now.      Good idea. And maybe check the settings again just to be sure.      If it still doesn’t work, we can always try the old-school way—just use your phone’s hotspot.      I’d rather not. But I suppose it’s an option.      Yeah, just don’t let it become your new main computer. You’ll end up missing all your old stuff.

So, I just wanted to say, this bistro is  amazing . I mean, it's like... a real gem in the middle of Tarnow. I can already tell it's going to be a hit. The decor is so cozy, and the menu seems really well thought out. I’ve never been to a place like this before in Poland, and I feel like it’s exactly what this town needs.      Yeah, I agree. I’ve been here a couple of times already, and it’s always packed. The owner is really passionate about the place, and the food is just... different. It’s like a fusion of British and Polish, which is such a cool concept.      It really is. I love how it’s not just about the food, though – the whole vibe is so welcoming. I think it’s going to be a great spot for people to gather. Wait, does it have a bar?      Yes, it’s open from morning till night, and the bar has a great selection of local beers and wines. I mean, it’s not just for tourists, right? It’s for locals too.      Of course, and that’s what makes it special. I sometimes feel like in places like this, the locals are the ones who really make the difference. But, honestly, I’ve been feeling a bit... lost lately. You know, after everything that’s happened.      I hear you. I’ve been thinking about my own life a lot lately too. It’s funny, because I’m out here teaching English, and I feel like I’m still chasing some kind of dream I don’t even fully understand. I mean, I’m not sure if I’m the right person for this job or if I just keep doing it because I don’t know what else to do.      That’s a tough place to be. I’ve had my share of addiction – not just to substances, but to things like work, or even just staying busy. It’s like when you’re unemployed, you lose your identity. I feel like I’ve become a different person since I stopped working.      Yeah, that’s exactly it. I’ve been trying to get back into fitness, actually. I think it’s one of the few things that gives me a sense of control. I’ve started going to the gym again, and it’s helping me feel more grounded.

So, I’ve been thinking about going to the Dorset Steam Fair next week. I got the ticket online, but I’m not sure if I’ve got everything sorted. You know, like, what do I need to bring?      I remember when I went to that fair last year. It was a bit of a trek, but the atmosphere was amazing. You should take a picnic. The food stalls are okay, but nothing beats a proper meal.      Oh, and don’t forget to check the facilities for the disabled. I’ve heard it’s pretty good—there’s a ramp at the entrance, and they’ve got some accessible toilets. But I’d still recommend bringing a mobility aid if you’re going to be around for the whole day.      Yeah, I was thinking about that too. My cousin has a wheelchair, and I want to make sure she can enjoy it. I’ve also been looking at property prices in the area. They’re going up so fast, it’s almost impossible to buy anything.      I know, it’s heartbreaking. I used to work as a mechanic, and I always thought I’d be able to save up. But with inflation and all… I’ve just been sitting at home, watching the prices rise. Maybe I should move back to London? But I don’t know if I could handle the city anymore.      I understand. I’ve been working as a care assistant for years, and I’d love to move somewhere with better access to healthcare. But the prices here are just as bad as anywhere else. I’ve been thinking about getting a cat to keep me company, though. They’re great for the soul.      Yeah, I’ve been toying with the idea of getting a cat. I’ve got a spare room, and I’m not sure if I’m ready for a dog. Plus, I’ve heard they’re easier to take care of. Although, moving furniture can be a nightmare. I’ve been trying to figure out how to rearrange the living room without breaking anything.      That’s the thing about moving furniture—it’s like a game of Jenga. You never know what’s going to fall. I tried to move my old sofa once, and it ended up cracking the wall. I still haven’t fixed it.      It’s all part of the process, though.

It’s been a bit of a beast today, hasn’t it? The wind’s got the house rattling like it’s trying to find its way out. I think I’ll be glad to see the back of this weather, even if it’s just for a few more hours.      Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I was out this morning, and I swear the sky was as grey as my old teaching uniform. But the sun did come out for a bit, and the garden was nice to sit in. I think I’ll take the dog for a walk later.      My granddad said the same thing. He said the weather’s like a drama queen – always moody. But he also said the lights are going to be on in the village hall tonight for the comedy night. Maybe we could go? I’ve been dying to see some live comedy, even if it’s just local acts.      That sounds like a good plan, if you can get your granddad to agree. I’ve been meaning to go to one of those events, but I’m always too busy writing. You know, I was just thinking about Ashaad’s birthday last week. It was so chaotic with all the kids. I don’t know how he manages to have a proper party with so many siblings. So, I was just thinking about that time we tried to cook lasagna for the whole block and ended up burning it. Remember?      Oh, how could I forget? Speaking of nightmares, have you been feeling okay lately? You’ve been a bit quiet.      Honestly, I’ve been tired. I’ve been working crazy hours at the clinic – you know, with the pandemic, and then the new funding, and all the patients coming in.      You’ve been working non-stop. You need to take a break. Maybe we could go on a weekend trip together. You know, just to get out of the house for a bit.      That sounds nice. I’ve been meaning to get away for a while. Well, I just thought of something. You know when I was a kid, my dad would take us on these long cycle rides around the countryside. Oh, I remember hearing about that. It was quite a benefit, wasn’t it? I think I read somewhere that some dentists even got free vacations. I agree, and I had the same perk. I remember one time, I took a sailing trip through the south of England. It was beautiful, and the lectures they gave were just someone sitting in a cabin and talking about oral health while the ship was rocking. It was an interesting contrast. I was told to check online for last-minute tickets, but I just couldn’t be bothered.      I know what you mean. Even trying to get into a museum or an exhibition now is a hassle. I think it’s a shame. Back in the day, it was so much easier.

So, I’ve been thinking about this education business idea we were talking about earlier. We need something that’s not just another tutoring service or online course platform. I like that. And it could even tie into the learning materials we were talking about earlier. Plus, it would be a great way to show how communication strategies evolve over time.      That’s a solid plan. It could appeal to a wide audience—students, working professionals, even older adults who want to improve their digital literacy.      Exactly. Now, they’re more connected online but less confident in real-world interactions. It’s a paradox.      It is. And maybe that’s the gap we can fill. We can create a learning environment that bridges the gap between digital and in-person communication. It could be a small business that offers both online and in-person workshops.

So, I was just thinking about how we used to go to the seaside every summer when we were kids. It feels like forever ago, doesn’t it?      Yeah, it really does. I guess we both have that deep-seated connection, even if we don’t always admit it. I think it’s why we both ended up studying marine biology. It’s not just a hobby, it’s almost like we’re being called to it.      I love that. I think it’s funny how our childhoods shaped our careers. It’s like the sea has been guiding us in different ways, even if we didn’t know it at the time.

So, I just saw this outfit on the TV show  Fashion Police  — like, this woman wore a neon pink tracksuit with a sequined jacket. I was like, “Is this real life? But even then, there are boundaries. I mean, I’m a teacher, so I have to set an example for the kids. I can’t just show up in a crop top and a tank top.      Yeah, I get that. So, I was just looking through my old photos from last summer, and I couldn’t believe how different everything looked. I mean, I thought I remembered it all so clearly, but there are these moments where I can’t even tell what’s going on in the pictures.      That’s normal, love. I remember when I was your age, I used to take photos all the time, but I never really got the hang of it. It was like trying to catch a ghost. I’ve been trying to capture the everyday things—like the way the light hits the windows in the morning or the way the trees look when the wind is blowing.      That’s so thoughtful. I think that’s what makes a good photographer, isn’t it? Not just the technical stuff, but the ability to see beauty in the ordinary. You know, I used to take photos for a living, back in the day. I even did some work for a local magazine.      Oh, really? That’s so cool! What kind of photos did you take?      Mostly portraits and street photography. I loved capturing people in their natural environment. I remember one time I was photographing a group of kids in the park and one of them was so nervous, he kept turning his head. I ended up taking a photo of him just as he looked up at me. It turned out to be one of my favorite shots.      That sounds like the kind of thing that could be really scary if you’re not careful. But sometimes, I still wonder what people think when they see my pictures.      That’s the beauty of it. You can’t control how people feel about your work. Right, I’ve just come round! Sorry if I’m a bit early, but I thought I’d pop in before the weather turns bad. I've been walking round the village, and the sky’s looking pretty grey.      Oh, don’t worry, we were just about to start the tea. Come on in, sit down. You’ve been out all morning?      Aye, I was checking on the chickens. That cockerel’s been getting a bit feisty lately. I’ve always said that a good cockerel should know when it’s time to wake up and when it’s time to rest.      I agree. It’s like the world is full of problems, isn’t it?      It is, but life goes on. I was thinking about my birthday next month. I’ve been meaning to plan something, but I just haven’t found the time.

So, I've been thinking a lot lately, and I think I need to talk to you about something... Well, not something too big, but it's on my mind. Well, she’s been working in Canada for the past few years, and it’s been tough. She's been feeling pretty isolated, even though she’s doing well professionally. I’ve been thinking about how she’s never really had a strong support system here, and I feel like I could offer her a more stable environment. Plus, I miss her a lot. She’s my only child, you know.      That’s understandable. I can see why you’d feel that way, especially if she’s been feeling lonely. But have you talked to her about it yet?      Not really in detail. I’ve just mentioned it a few times, more as a thought than a plan. I’m not sure how she’d feel about moving back. I know it’s a concern, and I’ve been thinking about that too. I’m not sure yet, but I’m trying to see it through. I’ve got some savings, and I’m sure she could help me with the daily chores.

So, I've been meaning to ask you, how did you find the job interview for that new teaching position? I heard it was a bit of a tough call. You’ve always been a great mentor to her, and she’s really taken your advice to heart. I think you’re the kind of person who really makes a difference in people's lives.      Thanks, that means a lot. I just hope she doesn’t forget where she came from. Sometimes young people get too caught up in their own ambitions.      I know what you mean. I really enjoy talking to her. It’s always good to have someone who really understands you. Speaking of understanding, have you caught up on the news lately?      Not really. I’ve been quite busy with the interview and all.

So, I was just telling my nephew about the time I tried to put together a mousetrap game with my brother-in-law. It was a complete disaster. I think we ended up with more glue than mice!      Oh, I remember that! I think we ended up with more wires than we could use. You were so determined to make it look like a real board game, but it just ended up looking like a science experiment gone wrong.      Yeah, I remember that. It was hilarious. But I think the real lesson was that mousetrap games are more complicated than they seem. I mean, I still can’t figure out how the trap actually works. I’ve been thinking about going to the States for a few months, but I’m not sure yet.      Oh, that was a while back. I went to New York for a few months in the early 90s. I was working as a translator for a publishing company. It was amazing – the culture, the energy, everything. But it was also a huge culture shock.      Really? I've always wanted to work in the States, but I've been too busy with my job here. I mean, I've been to a few cities, but never for an extended period.      I’ve been to the US twice, once in college and once for a summer program. I loved it, especially the cities. But I think what surprised me the most was how different the kids were. I mean, they were so outgoing, so confident. It made me wonder if that’s just how American kids are, or if it’s the culture.      Yeah, I remember that. My cousin went to school in Texas and came back with a different attitude. He was like a new person – more confident, more bold. I think it’s a combination of the environment and the way they’re raised. But I have to say, I miss the American kids. They’re so full of energy.      I’ve always found it fascinating. I’ve never been to the US, but I’ve read a lot about it. I’m planning to go to a conference in Chicago next year, so maybe I’ll get a chance to see some of it firsthand.

Okay, I'm back! I had such a great time shopping in the market. Well, I think that was one of the best rugby matches I've seen all season. That try from Oisin was just brilliant, wasn’t it?      Yeah, honestly, he played like a pro tonight. So, I was just telling my mates about the time I tried to order a latte in that café in Cambridge. You know, the one with the  really  posh accent? A latte with a dash of  accent ?” I swear, I thought I was in a comedy sketch.      That’s the thing with accents, mate. You can’t really fake it. I mean, I’ve been teaching English for years, and I still get caught out when I’m in a place where people are all different.
