I reckon it’s something like a Cockney or a Scouse, but somehow worse. Anyway, I’ve tried to learn some local slang, but the only thing I picked up was “cheeky” and “lorry driver.”      Oh, I remember when I first moved to London. I thought I was doing great with my “posh” accent, but I ended up sounding like a  knight from the Crusades . I tried to say “I’m going to the shops,” and the guy I was talking to said, “Wait, are you going to the  horse  shops?” And I was like, “No, the  general  shops.” He just laughed so hard he nearly knocked over his pint.      It’s funny, isn’t it? I think accents are like personality markers. You can’t really  fake  them. I’ve taught students from all over the world, and the ones who try to sound like the locals end up sounding like they’re trying too hard. It’s like trying to act like a Frenchman at a café in Paris. You just stand out.      I think I’d rather just be me. I mean, I’ve got my own way of speaking, and I think it’s kind of cool. It’s like, why pretend to be someone else when you can just be yourself?

Hey, I just finished making the pasta. It’s ready to go. You want some?      Yeah, that sounds great. I’ve been staring at this bowl of cereal for the past hour. I need something more substantial.      You’re lucky I was in the mood to cook. I’ve been thinking about this all week.      You always say that. But I’m glad you did. Honestly, I’ve been so busy with work lately, I haven’t had time to even think about cooking.      I know. You’ve been commuting to that new project co-ordinator gig, right? How’s it going?      It’s okay, I guess. The commute is brutal, though. I wake up at five every morning just to get there on time. I’m starting to think I need a better car.      You need a car that can handle the long distances. Maybe something with better fuel efficiency?      Yeah, that’s what I was thinking. I’ve been saving up for a used car, but I’m not sure yet. Between the rent and the groceries, it’s hard to set aside money for something like that.      I get that. My job as an administrator has me working late sometimes, and I’ve been trying to save up for a car too. But it’s hard to balance it all.      I know what you mean. I’ve also been trying to cut back on my expenses. I’ve started meal prepping and cooking at home more. It’s helped a bit.      That’s smart. I’ve been thinking about doing the same. I mean, the cost of living is going up, and you really have to be careful with your money these days.      Definitely. I’ve realized that saving isn’t just about earning more—it’s about spending less. I used to think if I made more, I’d have more to spend, but that’s not the case.      Right. It’s all about prioritizing. I’ve been trying to do more with less, and it’s been a learning curve. Plus, I’ve been looking into car insurance and maintenance costs. I don’t want to end up in a situation where I’m paying more than I can afford.      Yeah, that’s exactly what I’m trying to avoid. I’ve been putting money into a savings account just for that. I’ve got a bit saved up now, so maybe I can start looking for a car soon.

Right, I've got the list here. We need to make sure we get all the essentials for the next few days. I've got the eggs, milk, and bread, but I think we might need some more fruit.      Yeah, I was just thinking the same. We’ve been eating a lot of pasta lately, so maybe we should get some fresh vegetables to mix things up. Also, I saw that there’s a sale on apples at the market. Should we pick those up?      I don’t know about the apples, love. You know how they get squashed when you carry them too long. I’d rather spend a bit more on the quality ones, even if they’re a bit pricier. You know, for the grandkids.      Oh, alright, I’ll give you that. But I’m telling you, the apples are the best in the whole market. I’ve bought them for years, and they always come out of the bag perfect. You don’t get that with the cheaper ones.      Well, if you say so. But I think we should also check the bread aisle. I saw a new kind of whole grain bread that the local baker makes. It’s got a bit of a tang, but it’s quite good.      That sounds interesting. I’d like to try it. But we should also make sure we get the toiletries. I think we’re running low on shampoo and toothpaste.      Ah, yes. I picked up some of that green tea from the shop a week ago, but I think that’s gone now. Maybe we should get a new jar to have on hand. And don’t forget the toilet paper — I know we’ve been using it up.      I’ll take care of that. I was going to run to the shop later anyway. But I also need to take the dog for a walk first. He’s been extra restless since the weather turned.      That’s the dog for you. I think he’s just trying to get out and about. Maybe we could go for a walk together later? You know, to get some fresh air and burn off some energy.      I’d like that. I’ve been feeling a bit sluggish lately, so a bit of exercise wouldn’t hurt. But I’ll go with you to the shop. I’ve got a soft spot for the baker.

So, I was just telling the kids about the pirate ship—the one that sailed all the way to the New World. You know, Captain Flint and all that. It’s such a classic tale, isn’t it?      Yeah, it’s so cool! I mean,  pirates —they’re like the ultimate adventurers. I wish I could be a pirate. I’d sail the seas, hoist the Jolly Roger, and maybe even find some treasure!      Yeah! I think pirates are the best. You don’t have to go to school, you just get to go on big ships and fight with swords. I’d like to have a sword, too. Like, a real one.      A real sword would be dangerous, though. But if you’re careful, maybe you could have something like that. Though, I think you’d have to be in a  circus  to have a sword, or maybe even a  magic  show. Did you hear that there’s a magic workshop coming up?      A magic workshop? Like,  real  magic? Like turning things into something else?      Exactly! They said it’s a real circus workshop, and they’re going to show you how to do tricks and magic. You know, like making things disappear or making fireflies appear! It’s part of the Shakespeare week activities at the town center.      Really? I love magic! I’d like to make a rabbit disappear and then bring it back. Or make a horse appear out of nowhere.      That sounds like something a real magician would do. Maybe even like the ones that perform at Stratford. You know, the ones that come to do Shakespeare plays for the whole week?      Stratford? Isn’t that where Shakespeare was born?      Yes! That’s where the Royal Shakespeare Company is based. It’s always full of people who love the plays, and they have all sorts of workshops, like stop motion animation. You know, that’s where you make your own movies with clay figures.      Oh, like the ones with the box and the films? I saw some on TV. It was so much fun!      Exactly! And I think they’re even doing some Easter pictures this year—like the ones where you can paint your own eggs or something like that. It’s all part of the celebrations.      I want to make a stop motion movie about pirates! I can make a little ship and a pirate captain, and then he can find treasure!

Well, I’ve been meaning to tell you all about that time I got arrested in Jeddah when I tried to sail my boat from there to Cyprus. It was a bit of an adventure, really. I was doing a bit of sailing in the Gulf, and I thought,  why not try to get out of the country ? I had a small boat, just me and a few supplies. I figured it’d be easier than trying to get a visa or anything.      Arrested? That’s something! What happened exactly?      Well, I was sailing out of Jeddah, just heading towards the open sea. I didn’t have a proper permit, and I didn’t know the local rules. I was pretty confident I could get away with it, you know? I had a small boat, and I thought I could make it to Cyprus. But apparently, the coast guard caught me. They must have seen the boat on radar or something. I was in the water for a few hours, and then they came to get me. I was pretty flustered.      That sounds like a real problem. I remember when I was teaching in Saudi Arabia, I had to be real careful with everything. One wrong move and you could find yourself in a situation like that.      Exactly. I was trying to be independent, but I didn’t realize the legal stuff was so strict. It was a bit of a wake-up call.      I suppose in many countries, especially in the Middle East, you can’t just sail around doing whatever you want. Even in places like the UK, there are rules and regulations you have to follow.      Yeah, I’ve heard about people trying to fly or travel without proper documentation. It’s not just about boats. It’s about respecting the laws of the country you’re in. I remember when I was teaching in Saudi Arabia, I had to be careful even with alcohol. There are strict rules about that.      Oh, I know. I tried to bring a little bottle of whiskey with me to celebrate my first month there. I didn’t even open it. I was just being cautious. But I remember the look on the guy’s face when he caught me with it. That was one of the more memorable moments.      That must have been intense. I was in Manchester when I first started, and I had to be careful about what I said or did.

So, I was just telling my sister about the mess in the bathroom again. It’s like a war zone in there. I’m so tired of cleaning up after the boys. I think it’s time we had a family meeting about rules and responsibilities.      I know what you mean. My son’s always leaving his stuff around. I caught him trying to hide a soda can in the shower last week. Honestly, I’m not sure if he’s trying to be sneaky or just doesn’t care anymore. But when you're a parent, you learn to not take things too seriously.      Yeah, I don’t do that. I’m not a kid anymore. I’m 15 and I know how to be responsible. I mean, I do my homework, I help out around the house, and I even do some babysitting for my cousin. I’m not a total waste of space.      That’s great to hear. You’ve got the right attitude, Sam. I was just thinking about the summer holidays. I’ve got a few opportunities lined up. Maybe some work experience at a local company, and I might even try something new. I’ve always wanted to write a book, so I’m thinking about doing some freelance proofreading, like I do for other people.      You always were the creative type. I don’t know if I could ever write a book. I just stick to selling things and managing the lunchtime crew at the school. It’s not glamorous, but it keeps the lights on and the kids fed.      I guess. I’m just trying to figure out what I want to do when I’m older. I’m thinking maybe something with technology or maybe even a bit of travel. I’ve always loved the idea of exploring new places. I mean, I’ve already been to London, and I want to go further. Maybe even to Europe.      That sounds amazing. You should definitely take that chance. I remember when I was your age, I thought I knew everything. Now I realize there’s so much more to the world than what you see on your screen or in your neighborhood.      True. I think it’s important to keep an open mind, especially when you're young. You never know what could come from a simple decision. Like, I never thought I’d end up working in education, but here I am, doing what I can to make a difference, even if it’s small.

So, I just tried the truffle oil they had in the restaurant in Pula, and it was  so  good. I mean, I’ve had truffle before, but this was like,  truffle  in the best way. It just elevated everything.      I’m not surprised. Croatia has some amazing culinary traditions. And not just the truffles—they’ve got this whole vibe of  slow food , you know? It’s not just about eating; it’s about enjoying the moment.      Wait, did you guys know that truffles are actually a type of fungus? I just learned that in my biology class. It’s wild, right? Like, they grow underground and you have to dig them up?      Yeah, I remember reading something like that. But honestly, I’m still not sure if I’d want to dig for them. I’d rather just eat the ones they serve at restaurants.      I think that’s the point—there’s a difference between the work and the experience. You can do the work, but the real magic happens when you’re served it.      You know, I actually studied truffle farming in grad school. It’s a bit niche, but it’s fascinating. You have to use trained dogs to find them, and it’s not just about the food. It’s about the environment, the tradition, the whole ecosystem.      Wait, really? You worked with truffles? That’s wild! So, are they common in Britain? I mean, I know the UK doesn’t have the same truffle scene as Italy or France, but I’ve heard people talk about black truffles and white truffles.      Yeah, they do have some truffle farms up in the Scottish Highlands. But it's not as widespread. In England, it’s more of a luxury item. People talk about it, but they don’t really cook with it as much.      So, how do you even grow truffles? I mean, is it like planting them in the ground?      It’s a bit more complicated. You have to plant the truffle bulbs in a specific type of soil, and then you wait—like, years—before you can harvest them. And then you need trained dogs to sniff them out. It’s not like a regular crop.      So, it’s like a treasure hunt, but with food?      Exactly. It’s like a combination of farming, science, and a bit of luck.      I’d love to try that one day.

So, this place—the Printing House. I’d never been here before. It’s got that old-world charm, doesn’t it? A bit like stepping back in time with all these books and the smell of paper.      Yeah, it’s got that dusty, academic vibe. Though I’ve been here a few times for meetings. The view from the window is actually pretty good. You can see the whole river and the city from here.      I’ve only been here once, actually. It was for a project deadline. Honestly, I was more focused on finishing my work than taking in the atmosphere. But I did notice how quiet it is compared to the rest of the campus.      Quiet is good for thinking, I suppose. I’ve been working on a research project lately about regional dialects and how they influence language policy in education. It’s a bit of a niche topic, but I find it fascinating.      That sounds interesting. I’ve always been curious about how dialects are perceived in professional settings. I mean, we all grew up with our own accents, right? But do people actually notice them in the workplace?      It depends on the environment. I’ve noticed that in some offices, people might make assumptions based on how someone speaks. But then again, I work in a more laid-back department, so it’s not something we talk about much.      That’s a bit of a problem, isn’t it? I mean, if you’re from a different region, you might feel like you have to “soften” your accent to fit in. But is that really fair? Language is part of identity, after all.      I guess it’s a balance. You want to be understood, sure, but you also don’t want to lose your sense of self. I’ve definitely had moments where I’ve thought, “Should I speak more like the people around me?” But I usually don’t. I think it’s better to be authentic.      I agree. I mean, I’ve always spoken with a Cambridge accent, but I’m from Cambridge. So it’s not like I’m hiding anything. But I can see how it might be different if you’re from somewhere else. Like, if you’re from a more rural area, or a different part of the country—people might judge you for that.      That’s exactly what I’m trying to study.

So, I just wanted to check – do you think we should stop off at that petrol station on the way? I’m starting to get a bit worried about the fuel level, and I don’t want to be stuck somewhere with no signal or anything.      Honestly, I haven’t noticed anything wrong with the gauge, but I guess it’s better to be safe than sorry. I mean, it’s only a short drive to Tarnow, right? I’m sure we’ll make it without any issues.      Yeah, I know, but when you’ve been driving for a few hours, you start to get that  feeling . I remember once I was driving across the country with my mum and the car broke down in the middle of nowhere. It was terrifying.      Oh no, that sounds awful. I hope we don’t have anything like that. But honestly, I think we’re in good hands. The car has been running fine, and the fuel’s been holding up.      Well, I just want to make sure we’re not getting into any trouble. I’d rather stop and check it out than risk anything. Plus, I remember the last time we drove to a friend’s house, we got lost for ages.      Oh, come on, that was because we were trying to take the scenic route. I think the shortest way is actually quite straightforward. You know, the one that goes through that little village with the old gas station.      That’s the one. I thought we had a map, but somehow it ended up in the back of the van. I still don’t know how it got there.      Maybe it was the wind. I swear, sometimes the van seems to have a mind of its own. But seriously, I think we’re okay. Let’s just keep an eye on the fuel and the road, and we’ll be fine.      Okay, fine. But I’m still going to stop at that petrol station just to be on the safe side. I don’t want to be stranded in Poland without a phone signal or anything.      Fair enough. I’m not going to argue with you on this one. Besides, it’s not like we’re going anywhere else. Just a quick stop, and then we’re almost there.      Exactly. And after that, we can have a proper meal and catch up like we used to.

So, I just saw this ad for McDonald's on the TV, even though it was muted. You could tell it was a football ad by the way they showed the logo over and over again. It’s like they’re trying to make the brand as iconic as the football club itself.      Yeah, I saw that too. I mean, it’s not a bad idea—they’re using the same kind of visual language as the football clubs. The red and white, the crest. It’s pretty clever, actually. But I wonder if it’s just another way for them to piggyback on the hype of the season.      Definitely. I think it’s about capturing the energy of the game, you know? Football’s a huge part of British culture, and McDonald's knows how to tap into that. They’ve done it with the strips too, haven’t they? I mean, those new designs they introduced last year—bold, bright, and really modern.      Oh, those were a bit controversial, weren’t they? I remember people saying the new kit didn’t look like the club’s traditional colors. Like, it was too flashy and didn’t respect the heritage. But then again, football kits are always evolving. Clubs want to stay relevant, especially with the younger audiences.      Yeah, but there’s a balance to be struck. I mean, if you look at some of the sponsorship deals, it’s not just about the logo. It’s about how the brand integrates with the team’s identity. Like, when a club like Manchester City had that massive deal with Emirates, it wasn’t just about the logo on the kit—it was about the whole image, the branding, the marketing.      Exactly. I think part of it is also about the fanbase. You know, the fans have a huge say in what kind of design they like. I mean, if you’re a fan of a club, you want the kit to represent your team. It’s not just about the sponsor; it’s about the pride you feel when you wear it.      That’s true. I remember a couple of years ago when a club changed their kit colors for a sponsor, and it caused a lot of backlash. Fans didn’t want their identity diluted. It’s a fine line between innovation and tradition.      And then there’s the element of sports sponsorship itself.

I’ve had enough of this. I’ve been trying to get my eBay orders sorted for weeks, and it’s just a mess. I don’t know how people do it. I mean, I’m not even sure if they’re real or not. Some of them look like they were sent by a ghost.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to get my job seekers allowance too. I’ve had to fill out so many forms, and it’s just so frustrating. I keep getting called back for more information, and it’s like they’re not actually helping me. I mean, I’m not even sure if I qualify anymore.      My brother, you’re not even qualified? You’re unemployed, haven’t worked in years, and you’re trying to claim benefits? I mean, I get that it’s hard, but you have to do it right. You need to be organized, or else you’ll just end up in the same place as me, stuck in this endless loop of paperwork and no real help.      Yeah, I know. I’m not even sure if I should be doing it. But what else am I going to do? I can’t just sit around all day. I’m not a child anymore. I need to be able to afford to live, you know?      I know, I know. I just wish there was a better way. I mean, I’ve been looking at day trips with the kids. You know, the ones that don’t cost too much. Just a walk in the woods, or a visit to the local museum. I don’t want them growing up in a world where everything is too expensive. I mean, the gas and electricity costs are just ridiculous now.      Yeah, I’m not even sure if I can afford to cook. I’ve been trying to use the George Foreman grill, but it’s not even worth it. It just takes forever, and the food tastes like cardboard. I don’t know how people even bother.      I tried it once, and I was so disappointed. I thought it would be like a miracle, but no. It just ended up being a disappointment. I think I’ll stick to the old ways. Just boiling things and hoping for the best.      That’s probably the only way. I’m just so tired of feeling like I’m stuck in this rut.

Well, I've been thinking about how different people approach food these days. I mean, I've always preferred cooking from scratch, but lately I've been seeing so many people relying on convenience stores for everything. It's a bit sad, really.      Yeah, I can't say I disagree. I mean, if you're working all day and don’t have time to cook, it’s understandable. But I do miss the old days when you’d go to the local market and pick out fresh vegetables. You could tell the quality just by looking at them.      Oh, I remember those days. When I was younger, I used to go to the market every Saturday with my mum. She’d always say, “Don’t buy the ones that look too perfect, they’re probably been in the fridge for days.” And she was right. You could tell the difference between a good apple and a bad one in a heartbeat.      I bet that was the kind of wisdom that comes with age, isn’t it? I’ve been thinking about my own mother’s advice lately. She always said, “Don’t rush through life, take your time.” But I’m not sure I’ve ever really listened.      I think we all have our own versions of that. I mean, I did listen to my mum’s advice when it came to driving. She always told me never to use the sat nav in the car. “You can’t trust it,” she said. And honestly, I still don’t. I mean, I’ve been through some wild detours because of it, but I’ve never had an actual accident.      I remember when I used to drive. I was always telling people I’d never have a car crash, but then one day, I got into an accident. It was nothing major, just a scrape. But it reminded me how dangerous driving can be, especially when you’re tired or you’re waiting for the sat nav to give you the right directions.      I think we all have our own stories about that. I remember once I was flying with my kids and the plane had to go down because of some kind of mechanical failure. It was terrifying, but I think it’s made me more aware of the importance of safety in everything we do.      Yeah, and I think that’s what makes us all human, isn’t it?

Hey, have you seen the latest science project we have to do for the end of term? I’m  so  stressed about it. I don’t even know where to start.      Oh no, I feel you. I’ve been trying to figure out what we’re supposed to do. I think it’s something about renewable energy, right? But I’m not sure if it’s a model or a presentation.      Yeah, I think that’s it. It’s supposed to be something you can actually build, like a mini wind turbine or something. But how are we supposed to do that in a school lab? I mean, I don’t even have the right tools.      I know, I’ve been asking my brother for help, but he’s a trainee teacher, so he’s basically just trying to survive his own projects. He said he’s got one about photosynthesis, and he’s already stuck on the same thing.      That’s not fair! He’s supposed to be helping us. I mean, isn’t that part of the job? I hope he doesn’t get too overwhelmed. Anyway, what about you? Are you doing anything creative with it?      I was thinking of making a diorama of a solar farm – like, a miniature version with lights and fake panels. It’s not exactly the most scientific, but I’m not great with engineering.      That sounds fun, but I’m just panicking. I think I’m going to ask Miss Walker if we can do something a bit more artsy, like a poster or a video. I’m not sure if that’s allowed, though.      Maybe you could combine both? Like, make a video explaining your model and then add some creative elements to it. I bet the teachers would like that.      Yeah, that’s an idea. I was also thinking about doing something related to art, like a mural or a sculpture. Do you think they’d accept that?      Definitely! Art and science can go hand in hand. Plus, with your talent, you could make something amazing. I bet you could even get extra credit for creativity.      Thanks, that’s nice to hear. I just need to stop overthinking and get started.      Yeah, I know the feeling. But if we keep talking about it, we’ll never get anything done. Let’s go start working on our projects – I’ll help you with the layout, and you can help me with the design.

So, what do you think about all this talk about religion lately? I mean, I’ve been reading some stuff about the Matrix and Scientology, and it’s like, where do you even start?      Honestly, I think it’s all pretty confusing. I mean, I used to think religion was about love and helping people, but then I heard about all these groups that act like they know everything. I mean, what’s the point of believing in something if it’s just another way to control people?      I don’t know. I just like watching the Matrix movies. They’re cool. But I don’t think I believe in anything, really. I think it’s all just stories.      I get that. I mean, I used to go to church with my mum when I was younger. But then I started thinking about all these other things—like, why is everything so complicated? Why do we have to believe in something to be good?      I think it’s about finding meaning. Like, if you don’t believe in anything, what’s the point of living? But then again, I also think people use religion to justify all sorts of bad things. I mean, I’ve heard about nuns who are amazing, but I’ve also heard about them being strict and even mean.      Yeah, I guess that’s true. I mean, I read this book about a nun who started a school for poor kids, and it was amazing. But then I also saw a documentary where some nuns were really harsh and made people feel guilty for things they didn’t even do.      It’s like, how do you know which ones are real? I mean, I don’t even know what to believe anymore. I mean, I used to think the Matrix was just a movie, but then I started thinking, what if it’s real? I mean, what if we’re just living in a simulation?      I think it’s just a movie, but it’s cool. I like the idea that we’re in a dream. Then I can do anything I want if I wake up.      I think that’s the thing, though. You can believe in whatever you want. Like, I think religion is just a way to connect with something bigger, but I’m not sure what that is. I mean, maybe it’s the Matrix, or maybe it’s something else entirely.

So, I was just thinking about those dancing lessons I signed up for last week. You know, the ones that promised to make me a total dancer in three weeks. I’ve had one class so far, and honestly, I feel like I’m more likely to fall over than actually dance.      Oh, I remember you saying that. You were really excited about it, though. I think you thought you’d be able to impress your cousin at the family gathering next month.      Yeah, I did! But now I’m starting to question everything. I mean, how do people even do that? I’ve seen videos of people doing the tango and the waltz, and I’m like, “How are they not falling apart?”      Maybe it’s the same as learning any new skill. I mean, I had to take an engineering course at uni and it was brutal. But you get the hang of it. Maybe you should just keep at it. And maybe pick a style that you actually like.      I was thinking about that. I’ve been trying to figure out if I want to do classical or modern. I’ve seen some videos of people doing street dance, and it looks so much fun. But I’m worried about the ageism angle. Like, do people even want to learn dance later in life?      Honestly, I don’t think age matters. If you’re passionate about it, that’s what counts. Plus, someone like me, who’s in engineering, can barely walk without tripping over my own feet, so I’d say it’s fair game for anyone.      True. But I do feel a bit out of place. I mean, I know it’s all about having fun, but I keep thinking about the old English that I studied at uni. You know, the one that’s so tricky, like the 'th' and 't' sounds.      Oh, I remember you getting stuck on that. You were trying to read some medieval texts, and you kept saying “thorn” instead of “thorn”!      Yeah, and I took it so seriously. Still do, honestly. I think it’s the kind of thing that you really need to love, otherwise it’s just work.      I get it. I mean, I’m in engineering, and sometimes I feel like I’m just doing the same thing day in, day out. But I know I’ll never be able to say “thorn” without overthinking it.

So, I just saw this massive olive tree outside the town, and it looked like it had been there for centuries. You know, I thought about how much of a part olive oil plays in Croatian cuisine. Do you think we should try to find a local olive oil shop?      That’s a great idea. I’ve read that the olive oil here is actually some of the best in the world. I think we should stop at a market tomorrow. Oh, and maybe pick up a bottle to bring back home. My aunt used to make her own olive oil when she was younger.      Can I go with you? I’ve always wanted to see how they make it. I mean, I’ve watched a few videos, but I never thought I’d actually be able to see it in person. And the wine too—my mom always says the wine here is better than anything in the UK.      Of course you can, love. You’re not too young to get a little hands-on with culture, are you? Just don’t get too excited and knock over the bottles.      I’d say that’s a risk worth taking. I mean, it’s not like we’re in the UK anymore. So, I've been thinking about social networking a lot lately. I mean, it's everywhere now. It's like you can't go anywhere without seeing someone scrolling on their phone or posting something. So, John, I’ve been thinking about what we need to do with the tape. I know we’re planning to use it for the local health service consultation, but I’m not sure if we’ve got all the details right. Oh, look at this! I still remember the day we took this photo. It was the summer after uni, and we were all staying at my parents’ place in Kemsing. I don't think I've ever been that scared in my life, but that last scene with the shadowy figure in the hallway? It was  so  real, I nearly jumped out of my skin! Yeah, I know, it was pretty intense. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting an iPad for work. It would make my lessons so much easier, especially with all the resources and apps I can use. So, I've been meaning to ask you, have you read that new book by David Mitchell?  The Glass Hotel —it’s supposed to be brilliant. So, I've got this job application I need to send off by tomorrow, and I was wondering if you could help me look it over. I feel like I’m missing something important.      Of course, love. I know, I know. But I feel like I can handle it.

Well, I've been meaning to talk about this place for ages. You know, how it's changed since we were kids. Back in the day, this was a proper village, not just a collection of houses with no real community. It's all been taken over by these new developments and all that. They want to modernize things, but I don’t think it's done it properly.      It's like everyone's chasing the latest thing, but they forget what’s important. So, I was just thinking about that time we tried to get a takeaway in Sunderland when we were kids. I think it was like 2008 or something. So, I heard you mentioned your mum was in the hospital again. Are they doing anything about it? So, I’ve been thinking about our holiday plans again. We’ve got that cabin in the Alps, right? I was just talking to my sister about how we should take the kids skiing this year. He’s got this thing about being the “expert,” but he’s really just a beginner who’s proud of himself.      You know what’s funny? I remember when I was a kid, we’d go to the ski resort in the Lake District. My dad would take me and my brother, and we’d spend all day just looking at the mountains. I think the first time I actually skied was when I was twelve. It was about as exciting as watching a puddle freeze.      I think that’s part of the charm. It’s not about the snow or the slopes; it’s about the memories. I’ve been thinking about taking the boys to the ski resort near me. Maybe it’s a chance to give them a taste of something new.      Yeah, I’d love to go. I’ve been saving up for a new pair of skis. My dad said I can get a discount if I buy the whole set. I’m really excited about it. It’s not just about the skiing, though—it’s the whole experience. The food, the chalets, the views.      I’ve heard the food in the Alps is amazing. I mean, I’ve seen pictures of those mountain restaurants with the views and the food that looks like it’s from a Michelin restaurant.

Hey, I just found this old photo album in the attic. It looks like it's from the early 2000s. You remember when we first started taking photos together? It feels like forever ago.      Oh, I remember! We were still living in London, right? I think it was after that trip to Kyoto. You were obsessed with the temples and the way the light hit the paper lanterns. I still have that old camera you got me for my birthday.      Yeah, and you were the one who insisted on taking photos of everything—trees, street signs, even the ducks in the park. I still can't believe we managed to get a decent shot of them without getting soaked by the rain. You were so determined.      I was! I told you it was the only way to capture the true essence of Japan. You were more interested in the food and the onsen. But I think that’s why we clicked—complementary hobbies, you know?      Definitely. You always had that knack for finding beauty in the everyday. Remember when we were in Osaka and you took that picture of the street vendor with the neon sign flickering in the background? It’s one of my favorites.      Oh, yes! I still keep that one on my phone. I even tried to recreate the lighting in my studio once. It didn’t quite work, but it was fun trying.      Speaking of which, have you ever thought about taking a photography course? I heard there’s a workshop in Norfolk next month. You’d probably love it. And it could be a good way to reconnect with the craft.      That sounds like a great idea. I’ve been wanting to get back into it. It’s been a while since I’ve gone anywhere that required a camera. I’ve been too busy with teaching and the kids.      Yeah, I can see that. But maybe we could take a weekend trip to a place with nice lighting. I’ve always wanted to go to the Lake District again. There’s something magical about the way the light falls there in the early morning.      I’d love that. You know, I’ve been thinking about badgers too. I saw a documentary about them the other day. They’re so clever. I swear they have their own little society.      Oh, I’ve always thought they were fascinating.

So, I was telling my mates about that time I got lost in Ireland and ended up in a cow field at midnight. I’m telling you, it was like something out of a horror movie. I swear, the cows were like,  “What are you doing here, mate?”  and then I had to ask for directions from an old lady who looked like she’d stepped out of a 1950s sitcom.      Oh, I’ve got a story about that too. My aunt went to Ireland once and literally skinny-dipped in a lake because she thought it was a  “trick”  to get rid of bad luck. She came back with a sunburn and a cold, and she still says it’s the best thing she ever did.      Oh, skinny dipping? I was at a café in Birmingham once when a guy walked in and started stripping. I didn’t know what to do, so I just stared at him, and he said,  “You’re not gonna tell anyone, are you?”  I said,  “No, I’m not.”  Then he left. I didn’t tell anyone, and I still don’t know if it was a joke or a conspiracy.      You’re all missing out. I’ve been to Australia, and I’ve seen the real deal. You know what’s better than skinny-dipping? Smashing a coconut on the head and watching it explode. It’s like a party in your own backyard.      That sounds like a nightmare. I’d be scared of coconuts after that.      Wait, I’ve heard stories about Australia and zombies. I think it’s a thing where they have zombie apocalypse parties and you’re supposed to dress up like a zombie and eat burgers. It’s like the only way to survive.      You’re mixing up your stories. I once had a snoring roommate who would wake me up every night with the sound of a chainsaw. I thought I was dreaming until I realized it was just him.      Yeah, I’ve had that too. I used to work in a café and had a guy who would snore so loud, the customers would start asking if we were doing a live performance.      Speaking of work, have you guys seen the new photo app that filters your photos to look like they were taken in the 80s? It’s so fake, but somehow it’s trending.

So, I was just telling my mates about the peanuts I ate at the theme park last weekend. I thought they were normal salted peanuts, but they turned out to be  chips ! Like, £2.50 for a bag of salted crisps. I almost choked on the first one.      Oh man, that’s a classic. I remember when I was a kid, my dad used to bring me a bag of peanuts from the snack bar at Alton Towers, and I’d eat them all in one go. But now, I can’t even remember the last time I saw a bag of peanuts in the park. They’ve all gone digital.      Yeah, I guess it’s all about the nostalgia. I mean, I still love them, but I’ve started eating more of the actual nuts in the last few months. Maybe it’s the postgrad lifestyle? I mean, I’m trying to be healthier. I even bought a bag of roasted peanuts the other day and ate them with my laptop while working on my research project.      I can relate. I’ve been doing the same thing. I’m trying to cut down on the sugary snacks, especially since I’m doing my PhD. I remember my advisor once told me that if you’re not eating properly, your brain won’t function as well. So, I started bringing my own snacks to the library.      That’s smart. I think I need to start doing that. I’ve been relying too much on vending machines. Although, I’d rather have a bag of peanuts than a chocolate bar any day. Speaking of snacks, do you remember that film  The Iron Giant ? I just watched it the other night, and it reminded me of the theme parks I used to go to as a kid.      Oh, that’s a classic. I watched it when I was about 10. I used to go to the theme parks with my family all the time. My dad used to work at a tour operator, so we’d go to places like Thorpe Park and Alton Towers every summer. It was like the highlight of the year.      That’s awesome. I wish I had that kind of access. I’ve only been to one theme park in my life, and it was in Manchester. It wasn’t even that great. I think I’m still waiting for the day I can afford to go to a proper one.

So, I was just telling my sister about how I decided to take up rowing last month. It was a complete whim, really. I thought, "Why not? I’ve always been interested in water sports, and it’s a way to stay fit and meet people." But honestly, it’s more challenging than I expected.      Oh, I can imagine. I tried kayaking last summer, and I nearly capsized three times in the first hour. I thought I was a total disaster. But then I started to get the hang of it. It's just about balance, isn't it?      Yes, it does take some practice. I've been to a local club, and the coach is really patient. Although, I must say, the weather’s been terrible lately. I’m constantly trying to find the right gear for wet weather. I bought a waterproof jacket, but it’s still uncomfortable. I need something more durable.      Haha, I know what you mean. I remember once I tried to go kayaking in a sudden downpour, and I ended up with a puddle of water everywhere. I had to borrow a towel from another paddler to dry off. It was a bit of a comedy of errors.      Oh, I’d love to try kayaking. Maybe next summer. I’ve also been thinking about how much my mum used to talk about her first time meeting my dad. She was so nervous, and they met at a family gathering. It was just a simple conversation, but it turned into something meaningful. It always makes me smile when I think about it.      That’s sweet. I remember when I met my husband, it was at a French language class. We both had the same teacher, and we started talking during a break. We ended up going out for coffee and then... well, it all snowballed from there. My sister always jokes that I should’ve been a matchmaker.      That’s funny. Speaking of family, my aunt passed away last year. It was unexpected. I was so shocked, and it really made me think about how quickly life can change. I’ve been trying to stay in touch with the family more, just in case something happens again.      That’s so sad. I’m sorry to hear that. My brother is currently unwell, and it’s been a tough time for our family. It’s one of those things that makes you realize how fragile life can be.

Okay, Dad, I was thinking about Morse code today. I mean, it's so old-fashioned, right? But it's kind of cool how people used to communicate without phones or texts. I was trying to remember how to send a message in Morse, you know, just for fun.      Yeah, I remember learning it in school. It was part of the basic communication skills we had to learn. You know, back when people actually used telegraphs and things like that. It's funny how things have changed. Now, we just text and send emojis instead of dots and dashes.      I know, and I love emojis, but sometimes I feel like they’re just shorthand for real emotions. Like, if you’re sad and you send a 😢, it doesn’t really mean the same thing as if you explain it in words. But I guess it’s easier to use. Also, I’ve been getting so many Amazon deliveries lately. My room is full of boxes. I even got these new shoes from eBay. They were supposed to be cheap, but they were a bit expensive in the end.      Oh, I know what you mean. I tried buying some stationery online once, and I ended up with a whole bunch of pens that didn’t even work. You know, the ones that look like they’re made in China. But I guess it’s all part of the experience.      Yeah, and I still use my Vodafone phone, but sometimes I feel like it’s better to just write things down. Like, when I’m trying to remember something, I can’t just text myself. I know that’s not the same as using an app, but I like the idea of having a notebook and a pen. Although I can’t find my pen. I think it’s in the drawer. Or maybe it’s in the kitchen. I can’t remember.      You know, you should’ve written it down when you thought of it. We’re all forgetting things these days. I remember when I was your age, I didn’t have a phone, so I had to remember everything. But now, even my memory is getting worse. I can’t even remember where I put your glasses.      You’re not helping. But seriously, I was thinking about university today. I’ve got the results day coming up, and I’m a bit nervous.

Hey man, it’s been ages! I’ve been meaning to catch up with you, but life has been a bit of a whirlwind. How have you been?      Same old, same old. You know how it is—uni, exams, trying to keep up with all the work. But I’ve been keeping busy, actually. I reckon I’ve got a few plans for the future that I’m really excited about.      Oh, really? What’s on the horizon? You’ve been so secretive lately. Didn’t you say something about wanting to travel?      Yeah, I did. I’ve been thinking a lot about Japan lately. Tokyo specifically. I’ve been watching some documentaries and reading up on the culture. I’m pretty sure I’m gonna go there this summer.      That’s awesome! I’d love to go, but I’ve been stuck in London for a while now. I’ve got this part-time job that’s keeping me pretty busy. Also, I’ve been trying to finish up some coding projects for my computer science degree.      Oh, that’s cool. I’ve been working on my own stuff too—mainly machine learning. It’s pretty intense, but it’s fun. You know, I’ve been thinking about how the internet has changed the way we learn and work.      Absolutely. I mean, universities are starting to integrate online learning more than ever. It’s a bit of a headache, but it’s also opened up so many opportunities. I mean, who knew you could study Japanese from a computer in London?      Exactly! I’ve actually been taking an online course in Japanese. It’s not the same as being there in person, but it’s been helping me get a better handle on the language. I think I might even go to Japan for a few weeks next year.      That’s a bold move. I think I’d need a few months of practice before I’d feel ready. But hey, I’ve been to some good restaurants here in London recently. I think I tried this amazing sushi place near King’s Cross.      Oh man, I’ve been dying to try that. I’ve been going to this ramen place in Islington, but I’ve heard mixed reviews. I’m not sure what to think.      You should totally check it out. It’s one of those places where the food is so good it’s almost like you’re in Tokyo.

So, I was scrolling through my Facebook feed the other day, and I came across this photo from our trip to Buckfast Abbey last summer. I couldn’t believe how much time had passed since we were all there, and I thought, “Oh, I wish we could go back!”      Yeah, I remember that trip. It was so nice, wasn’t it? I still have that photo of us all sitting on the stone steps, laughing like mad. You were the one who kept trying to take selfies with the whole group, and the monks were watching you like you were crazy!      Oh, I was trying to be the photographer, but I think I only got one decent photo. The rest were blurry or had the monks in them! I was so proud of myself for managing to take a picture at all.      I still remember the way you all looked, covered in mud from that little trail we took near the abbey. I was the one who almost fell over the edge, and you all just laughed at me. I still don’t know how you managed to get up that hill with such a heavy bag!      It was ridiculous. I swear, we all looked like we were in some sort of adventure film. I think the monks thought we were a group of tourists on a budget.      Speaking of trips, have you two thought about going on a cruise? I’ve been meaning to suggest it for ages. I heard a really nice one is leaving from Plymouth next summer. It’s a few days, and I think it’s within our budget.      I’ve always wanted to go on a cruise. I’ve never been on one, and I think it would be nice to see the sea again. Although, I might have to take my walking stick with me.      Oh, you’ll need your stick for the ship as much as for the land!      Well, if we can get the insurance sorted, maybe we can all go together. I’ve been meaning to talk to my son about it. It’s about time we all took a proper holiday, you know.      Yeah, you’re right. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck in my routine lately. It’s nice to hear someone else wants to break the monotony.      We’ll have to plan it properly. Maybe we could do a few things in Devon first, like visit some of those quaint villages we’ve heard so much about.

So, how was your trip to Belgium, Mum? I mean, I know you said it was amazing, but I’ve been dying to hear all the details.      Oh, it was absolutely fantastic! We went to Brussels, Bruges, and Antwerp. The food was incredible—especially the waffles. I’ve never had anything that good before.      I’ve heard about the waffles, but I’ve never actually tried them. Is it like the ones you get in the UK or are they different?      Oh, they’re different. They’re super thick, and they come with all sorts of toppings—like chocolate, sugar, and even fruits. It’s like a dessert, but you eat it with a bit of syrup. I had one with chocolate, and it was divine.      Wow, I’d love to try that. Wait, did you have any trouble with the GPS? I remember you mentioned something about the Sat Nav not working properly.      Oh, that was a bit of a struggle. We downloaded the map before we left, but when we got there, the Sat Nav didn’t work at all. We ended up getting lost in Bruges for about 30 minutes. It was so frustrating. I remember my daughter was trying to help me, and I was just shouting at the phone.      Yeah, and the phone’s a new one, right? You got the latest model from the shop. I think it’s the one with the fancy camera and everything.      Yeah, I got it for my birthday. I thought it would be great for taking pictures of the scenery. But it seems like it’s more trouble than it’s worth. I still haven’t figured out how to use all the features.      I think you just need to take it slow. I found a couple of YouTube videos that helped me. Maybe you can borrow mine for a while. I’ve got a couple of old ones that still work.      That would be great. I’d rather not end up being the one who’s trying to navigate with a broken Sat Nav again. I remember the last time I tried to drive in France with a faulty GPS, I ended up in the middle of nowhere.      You’re not the only one. I think that’s a common problem with driving abroad. You’ve got to be careful with the road signs, too. They’re all in French, and I kept thinking I was in Paris instead of Brussels.

So, I’ve been thinking about what we’re going to cook for dinner tonight. I was going to make that stir-fry with the chicken and veggies we bought last week, but I’m not sure if I want to go through with it. It’s been a while since I’ve cooked anything substantial, and I’m beginning to feel a bit out of practice.      Hey, don’t worry about it. I think it’s actually a good idea to cook something familiar. You know, it’s easier to get it right and you’ll be more confident. Plus, I’ve been craving some good Chinese food lately. If you’re nervous, I can help you through it.      That would be nice. But what if I burn the noodles again? I remember last week I tried making pad thai and the noodles turned into a sad, sad mess. I’m not even sure if it was the noodles or the oil.      Oh, everyone has a story like that. I used to make soufflés, and I once managed to set the kitchen on fire. It was a combination of overconfidence and underestimating the heat. I think we’re both just as guilty of that.      You’re not wrong. But I think we should also consider adding some flowers to the table – you know, to make it feel a bit more special. I’ve been meaning to try some of those new scented candles you mentioned. I think they might match the perfume we got from the boutique last month.      Yeah, that sounds like a great idea. I love the way that perfume smells – it’s a bit floral and a little spicy, like a warm hug in the middle of winter. I was actually going to buy a bottle for myself, but I thought maybe we could share it. It’s not like we’re not used to spending time together, after all.      You’re absolutely right. And I was thinking about the fireplace – maybe we could light it up. It’s been a bit chilly lately, and I think it would make the evening feel cozier. I remember when we first moved in, we had a fire going all night and it felt like we were in a cabin in the woods.      That’s the spirit. I’ve also been thinking about our friends on Facebook. I saw one of them posted a photo of their garden, and it looked absolutely beautiful.

Well, I've always thought Australia was a fascinating place. I've never been, but I've heard so much about it from my friends. I’m more of a person who likes to stay in the UK, though. I mean, I’ve lived in Bristol most of my life. But I’ve heard so many stories about Australians, especially the ones from Queensland. Do you think it's true that they all have a kind of laid-back attitude?      Oh, absolutely. I was in Queensland a few years back for a family wedding. It's such a different vibe compared to the North of England. I mean, the people there are so friendly. I remember someone at the reception said, "You're not from around here, are you?" and I said, "No, I'm from Manchester." And their eyes just lit up. I think Aussies have this way of looking at people from other parts of the world, like they’re always curious about where you're from.      And that's part of the charm, isn't it? I've always thought that the Australians do have that unique sense of identity. I’ve never been there, but I’ve heard a lot about the accent, the culture, the way they dress. I mean, I remember reading that business men in Australia wear a lot of suits, but they’re not as formal as in London. It's like they're trying to be professional but still have that casual edge.      That’s interesting. I think in the UK, especially in places like Bristol or Manchester, people are more formal when it comes to dressing for work. Or at least, they used to be. I remember when I was teaching, we had to wear smart clothes every day. I can't imagine that being the case in Australia. I suppose it's a reflection of their lifestyle.      Exactly. I think part of it is the climate. If you’re in a place where it's always hot, you don’t want to be over-dressed. Plus, Australia is such a big country, with so many different regions. I mean, I’ve heard that in some parts of Queensland, the dress code is more relaxed than in Sydney.      I suppose that's true. But I have to say, I would love to visit Queensland one day. I’ve always been curious about the dialect.

So, I just saw this article on social media about how people are starting to take podcasts more seriously. Like, some influencers are even using them as a way to build their brand. I mean, I listen to a few podcasts myself, but I never thought they'd become such a big deal.      Yeah, I guess that’s true. I actually started a podcast last year about English teaching and language learning. It’s not too big, but it helps me connect with other teachers and learners. Plus, it's a great way to keep my skills sharp and stay up to date with the latest trends in the field.      That’s awesome. I used to think podcasts were just for people who wanted to fall asleep while driving, but now I see how they can be so much more. I’ve even started listening to some educational podcasts and I find them really helpful. It’s like having a tutor in my ear while I commute.      Exactly! And I think part of the reason they’re so popular is because of social media. People can share their favorite podcasts, recommend them to friends, and even get a following just from consistent content. I mean, some of the biggest podcasts out there started off as something casual, like a blog or a YouTube channel.      That’s interesting. I remember when I was in school, we had to watch a lot of TV shows and movies as part of our English class. Now, it seems like podcasts are stepping in as a more interactive and personal alternative. I think people are looking for more authentic ways to engage with language, especially when it comes to learning.      Absolutely. I’ve noticed that in my classes too. A lot of students prefer listening to podcasts rather than watching TV because it’s less distracting and more focused. Plus, it’s a great way to hear how people actually speak in different contexts. It’s not just scripted dialogue; it’s real conversations.      I can see that. It’s also surprising how much the TV landscape has changed too. I mean, I still watch some shows, but I feel like the content is more niche now. There are so many streaming platforms with their own original content, and people have more control over what they watch.      Yeah, it's all about personal preference these days.

So, I just got a text from ANON saying her Travelling Circus is coming to Norwich next week, and she wants us to come and see it. I told her I’d be happy to, but I need to check the schedule.      That sounds awesome! I’ve always wanted to see a circus. Do you think we can go?      Yeah, I’d love to see it. It’ll be like a real-life adventure!      Definitely. But first, I need to sort out some things. I’ve been meaning to get the photograph for ANON’s Blue Peter Badge. My postgrad degree is going to be useful for that, right?      Wait, what’s the Blue Peter Badge?      Oh, it’s this badge you get if you do something cool, like planting a tree or collecting something, and then you get a photo for it. ANON wants to collect one for her, and she needs a photo of her doing something interesting.      So, like, a photo of her performing?      Not exactly. It’s just a photo of her doing something she loves, like swimming. I think she’s been practicing a lot.      Can I come swimming with her?      Of course! I’d love that. But before that, I need to get her passport. I remembered she mentioned she had one, but I haven’t seen it yet.      What’s a passport?      It’s a special document that lets you travel to other countries. ANON wants to visit her aunt in China, and she needs a passport.      China? I’ve heard stories about the Chinese eating old eggs.      Oh, that’s an old wives’ tale. I think it’s a myth. But it’s funny that she mentioned it.      Why would they eat old eggs?      I think it might be something related to tradition or something. I’m not sure. But I think it’s just a story.      What if we go to China and see if it’s true?      Well, we’d need a passport for that. ANON’s birthday is coming up, and I think it would be a great idea to get her one.      Yeah, and maybe we can get her a Blue Peter Badge while we’re at it.      That’s a great idea. I’ll start working on that. And I’ll also check the dates for the circus.      I can’t wait!      I’ll bring my swimming goggles!

Right, so I was just thinking about that thing I heard about—the whole erectile dysfunction thing. It's weird, isn't it? I mean, I know it's a real thing, but it's like… how do people even deal with it? Yeah, I mean, I’ve heard about it, but I haven’t really had to deal with it myself. I guess it’s one of those things that people don’t really talk about, you know? Like, you don’t just go up to someone and say, “Hey, do you ever get anxious about performance?” Exactly. I mean, I think it's more common than people like to admit. I’ve heard some of my mates mention it, but they’re always like, “Oh, don’t worry, I’ll get it sorted.” Like, it’s not a big deal. But I don’t know, I feel like it’s a bit of a taboo subject, especially for guys. I guess because it’s so tied up with masculinity, right? Like, if you can’t perform, you’re not a real man. But isn’t that kind of ridiculous? I mean, sex is supposed to be about connection, not just about “getting it done.” Yeah, I agree. I mean, I’ve been in relationships where it wasn’t always about the physical stuff. Sometimes it’s more about the emotional stuff. But I don’t know, sometimes the pressure gets to you. It’s like, you’re not just trying to have sex, you’re trying to make it look easy, like it’s not a struggle or anything. Oh, right, because that’s what people want to see—this perfect, effortless sex. But I think the reality is a lot more complicated than that. And honestly, I think it’s more about how people are feeling than how they’re performing. Yeah, I mean, I’ve been there. I had this one guy who was like, “I just don’t get it, I’m not even aroused.” And I was like, “You’re not even trying?!” But it’s not that simple. It’s not just about wanting it or not wanting it. There’s a whole bunch of stuff that goes into it. Exactly. So I think it’s important to talk about it, you know? Because if you don’t, it just festers. And I think a lot of people avoid it because they don’t want to feel like they’re failing or something.

Okay, I just checked the fridge, and I think we have everything we need for the cauliflower cheese. But honestly, I’m not sure how we’re going to make it without a few ingredients. Did you remember to pick up the spice mix?      No, I didn’t. I was so busy running errands and trying to remember to buy the double peas for the freezer. I actually left the shop with a bag of Quorn and a veg box, but I forgot the spice mix. I’ll go get it now. You want me to bring it back or do you want me to pick it up on my way to the market?      No, no, I’ll go with you. I’m already at the fridge, and I might as well grab the spice mix and check if the frylight is still in the cupboard. I think I remember seeing it in there last week.      Yeah, that’s right. I mean, it’s not like we’re using it for anything else. I’ve been trying to use the 0-calorie syrup more instead. I mean, it’s not exactly pleasant, but it’s better than using sugar, right?      It’s not terrible, but I still prefer the artificial flavor. I mean, when you’re cooking for someone else – like for our ‘treat day’ on Saturday – you want the food to taste good. It’s not just about the syns or the calories anymore.      True. I was just thinking about that. I’m trying not to be too strict with myself, but I do feel like I need to weigh myself again this week. The scales have been so unreliable lately. I’ve lost a few pounds, then I gain them back the next day. It’s frustrating.      I know. I’ve been meaning to talk about that. I think the problem is that I’m not eating enough protein. Maybe I should start tracking my meals better. I’ve been using Siri to set reminders for when to eat, but it’s not always accurate.      That’s a good idea. I use the calendar app to plan my meals and plan my ‘treat day’ as well. I want to make sure I’m not overdoing it on Saturday. I even go to the supermarket to check if the Quorn range is still the best option. I’ve been trying to save money on groceries, especially with the tax increase.

So, I was just thinking about our holiday plans for next year. I know it's still a bit early, but I've been meaning to ask—do you still want to go to Spain? Or maybe we could try somewhere different this time?      Honestly, I’d love to go somewhere different. Spain is great, but I’ve been feeling like I need a bit of a change of scenery. Maybe somewhere with more nature? Like the Lake District? Or even a beach in Cornwall?      Oh, Cornwall sounds lovely. I’ve always wanted to go there. The beaches are amazing, and the scenery is so picturesque. I mean, imagine waking up to the sound of waves and having a perfect day like that.      Exactly! And I heard there are some really cool writers who live there, too. I was thinking about writing a little something—maybe a short story or even a poem. I’ve been feeling inspired lately, especially after that book I read about rural life and the connection to nature.      That’s a great idea. I’ve actually been thinking about writing more, too. I’ve got this idea for a short story about a woman who finds a tattoo that changes her life. It’s kind of a fantasy thing, but it’s been sitting in my head for a while.      Oh, that sounds interesting. I’ve always had a fascination with tattoos. I’ve never gotten one, but I’ve always admired the symbolism behind them. There’s this one guy at work who has a dragon on his arm—literally, a full dragon. It’s massive.      Wow, that’s impressive. I used to think tattoos were too permanent, but I’ve been thinking about it more. Maybe something meaningful—like a quote or a symbol from my past. But I need to be careful. I don’t want to regret it later.      Yeah, I get that. I think it’s about what resonates with you personally. I’d love to have something that represents my journey or something I’ve learned. But honestly, I’m still not sure. Maybe I’ll wait until I’m older and more settled.      That makes sense. I think we both need to be in a place where we feel more grounded before making such a permanent decision. Speaking of grounded, have you thought about the domestic sphere lately? I feel like the house is getting a bit cluttered, and I’m wondering if we should do a cleaning day or something.

Well, I’ve just got a postcard from the Isle of Skye. It’s beautiful, really. I got it from a friend who went there last month. I can’t wait to see it properly, but it’s a bit crumpled, and the postmark is a bit unclear. Do you want to see it when I get it out?      Of course, I’d love to. You’ve always had a soft spot for the Highlands, haven’t you? I remember when we went to Glencoe a few years back. It was breathtaking. Yes, it’s a complicated topic, isn’t it? I suppose it’s not just about politics—it’s about identity, culture, and history. I think it’s important to respect both sides of the argument, though I personally think Scotland should remain part of the UK. But then again, I’ve never been to Scotland, so I can’t speak from personal experience, can I?      I suppose that’s a fair point. I’ve only been once, and even then, I was more taken by the rhythm of the countryside than the political debates. Still, it’s hard not to notice how people take sides. I’ve seen friends and colleagues argue about it passionately, even when they’re sitting down to dinner.      True. And I think that’s one of the reasons I’m looking forward to the coming weekend. We’ve got some friends coming over, and I was thinking we could take them to a local museum or something. Maybe even a nice walk in the countryside. It would be a good way to get out and enjoy the change of scenery.      That sounds like a great idea. The weather has been quite mild lately, so it should be pleasant. I was actually thinking about making a few arrangements myself. I’ve got a few people coming over too, and I wanted to make sure we all have a good time. Maybe we could combine our gatherings? That way we don’t have to do too much individually.      That’s a good move. I think it would be more enjoyable for everyone if we coordinate a bit. I’ll get in touch with the other hosts and see if we can work out a schedule.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about the Syrian refugees. I mean, it’s such a huge issue, isn’t it? I keep wondering how we can even begin to help them.      I know, I’ve been drawing about it too. I drew a chair for them, like the one in the picture book. Is that okay?      Yeah, I drew a chair too. I think it’s the best way to make them feel safe. Chair is important.      That’s a lovely idea. I mean, a chair is something simple, right? It gives you a place to sit and feel comfortable. I remember when I was in school, we had to draw chairs for our art project. It was a bit boring, but I think it helped me understand the different types of chairs.      Yeah, I like drawing chairs. My teacher said we need to think about the legs and the back. She said some chairs have four legs, and some have three. I think the ones at home have four legs, like the one by the window.      No, mine has three legs. It’s like the chair in the library. I think it’s called a stool. Teacher said stools are different from chairs.      That’s right. Stools are usually smaller and don’t have a back. I used to sit on a stool in the classroom when we had our tests. It was really uncomfortable, but I guess the teachers thought it would keep us focused.      So, if we draw chairs for the Syrians, maybe we can make them feel like they belong. Like, they can sit and rest. I think it would help them feel safe.      I think the chair should be red. Red is a strong color. It makes you feel brave.      That’s an interesting idea. Maybe we can make a red chair for the refugees. It would go well with the room. I could even put it by the window.      I think I’ll put a picture of a smiley face on the chair. So the Syrian people can smile when they sit down.      And I’ll put a flower on the back. Flowers make things happy.      I think that’s a beautiful way to think about it. Just a simple chair, but full of meaning. I can’t wait to see what we come up with. Maybe we can even make a whole room for them, with chairs, a table, and a picture of the sun.

I just got a message from Lucy. She mentioned she’s thinking of starting a baby shower for Hannah. You know, the one who’s been trying for a year now? Oh, right! I remember she was talking about it last week. I think she’s really excited. But I was wondering—do you think she’s ready for the next step? I mean, it’s not just about the baby, is it? Definitely not. I think she’s emotionally ready, but I wonder if she’s physically and financially prepared. I mean, Hannah’s working full-time and still studying for her PhD. She’s got a lot on her plate. Yeah, I guess that’s true. But then again, she’s got that support system. Her parents are helping out, and she’s got her sister living nearby. It’s not like she’s doing it alone. True. And I think she’s been working on her finances too. I remember she mentioned she’s been setting up a savings account, even though it’s slow going.
