I think we’re all kind of at that stage in life now—whether we’re starting families or helping others. It’s a different kind of responsibility, but it’s rewarding. I couldn’t agree more. I’ve been thinking about teaching about this too. Maybe I should start a module on the different phases of life and the emotional and social changes that come with it. It could be really insightful. That’s a great idea. You know, I was thinking about that too. Parents, friends, relationships—those are all interconnected. It’s not just about the academic side; it’s about understanding the lived experiences of people as they navigate these changes. Exactly. And I think it’s important to highlight the role of friends in all of this. I mean, we’ve all been there for each other—whether it’s celebrating a new job, or just offering a listening ear when things get tough.

So, I was just thinking about that time I was in university and we had this lecturer who was absolutely obsessed with superstitions. He used to tell us that if you walked under a ladder, you’d bring bad luck, and he even made us all recite a rhyme about it before we entered the lecture hall. I don’t know if he was just trying to be funny or if he actually believed it.      Aww, that’s adorable. I remember something similar from my time at university too. There was this guy in my history class who always refused to sit in the front row because he said it was bad luck. He even had a little talisman he kept in his pocket. I don’t think he ever got a good grade, though. Maybe he was just too distracted by his rituals.      Ha! I think he just wanted to be unique. Or maybe he was trying to impress the professor. I mean, universities are full of eccentric people, aren’t they? It’s like you’re always surrounded by people who think they have the answers to the universe, even if they’re just lecturers.      Absolutely. I sometimes wonder if we’re not just lecturers, but also part-time magicians. We tell stories, we sprinkle a bit of mystery, and we’re somehow expected to be trusted with the minds of students. It’s kind of a comedy of errors, really.      You know, I was thinking the other day about how even the police have their own superstitions. My sister told me that when she was in a rush to get to a meeting once, she had to cross the street three times because she remembered reading somewhere that it brings luck. I laughed at her, but I couldn’t help but think about how much of our lives are influenced by things we can’t quite explain.      That’s true. I think it’s part of human nature to look for meaning in the chaos. Even in the countryside, where it feels so peaceful, there’s something about the land that makes you feel like it has its own stories waiting to be told. I’ve had that feeling walking through the fields here—like there’s something watching or listening.      Yeah, it’s like the countryside has a way of creeping into your thoughts. I go out walking on weekends and I start wondering about all sorts of things—like why the police are always so worried about the public, or why we still have all these old superstitions.

You know Dad, I’ve been thinking about getting a new phone. My current one’s been acting up—battery dies in the middle of a text, and it’s really slow. I’ve been reading up on the latest models, and I think maybe the new iPhone 15 would be a good upgrade. What do you think?      You’ve only had your old one for a couple of years, and now you’re already looking for a new one. I remember when I first got a mobile phone back in the 90s—it was a brick, bigger than my head, and it cost me a fortune to make a single call. These days, you can’t even keep up with the technology, can you?      I know, I know! But seriously, I’m in the market for something reliable. And I’ve heard that the new models have better cameras and faster processing. Maybe even some AI features?      AI? That’s the buzzword these days, isn’t it? I heard about some of the smart home gadgets that use AI. They can even remember your coffee order. I tried one of those once, and it ordered me a cappuccino instead of tea. Baptiste was furious!      Oh, I can imagine! You know, I was thinking about hiring a van for a few months. I’ve got this idea to visit the Great Dorset Steam Fair next summer. I’ve always wanted to see those old steam engines up close. I think it’d be a great way to spend a weekend with some family.      That sounds like a plan! I remember when I used to go to those fairs when I was younger. There were so many things to see—antiques, vintage cars, even horse-drawn carriages. It’s a shame they don’t have them more often around here. You could probably take the van and drive down to Bournemouth for the fair. Would you need help with that?      Yeah, I was wondering if you could help me figure out the best way to hire a van. I’m not too experienced with that stuff. And I need to figure out the cost, insurance, and maybe even a route. I’m not sure if I should go alone or bring some family along.      You could bring your aunt and uncle. They’ve always had a soft spot for steam engines. And if you’re worried about the cost, I can talk to a few friends of mine who used to run a van rental business.

So, I was just thinking about the local library again. I mean, it's been such a staple of the community for so long. You know, I remember when I was a kid, we’d go there every weekend to borrow books or just sit in the quiet corner with a coffee. But now, the council has said they're considering demolishing it to make space for a new development. It just feels like a huge loss.      That’s terrible. I heard about it too. It's one of those places that just… feels like home. You know, even when it's not perfect, it has that kind of character. I mean, the old buildings, the way the walls are still cracked from decades of use, the smell of old paper… There's something about it that you just can't replicate with a new building.      Exactly. I mean, sure, the library is old, but it's still functional. The council keeps saying they need to modernize, but what’s the point of replacing something that works? I mean, the budget could be used to upgrade the existing facilities instead of tearing them down. I can’t believe they’re even considering it.      I know, and it's so ironic. The same council that's pushing for modernization is also trying to preserve the old town hall facade, right? It’s like they’re splitting themselves. I mean, they want to keep the old look for the town hall, but destroy the library? That doesn't make sense.      It doesn’t. I read an article the other day about how the library’s community space is used for everything—classes, meetings, even music events. If they tear it down, all of that will be gone. And I don’t even know what the new development would be. Maybe a shopping center? That would be a shame.      I was going to say the same thing. And I was just thinking about how we passed that old building on the way here. You know, I was looking at those upholstery fabrics I saw online earlier. You know, those deep, rich tones—maybe something like the deep green of the library’s walls? I think it would be amazing to have that kind of color in our living room.      That’s a good point. I mean, if we ever decide to change the upholstery, maybe we can go for that green.

You know, I’ve been meaning to ask you, what do you think of this new indie-folk band? Their album has been getting a lot of buzz.      Honestly, I like their vibe. The lyrics are raw and real, and the guitar work is solid. But I’m not sure I’d call it  indie —more like  acoustic  with a modern twist.      I agree. I think they’ve got a unique sound, but it’s still rooted in the traditional folk style. I like how they blend storytelling with contemporary production.      You two are more into music than I am, aren’t you? I mean, I know the basics, but I can’t pick out the nuances. Though I do enjoy a good rock band every now and then.      You’d be surprised. When I was younger, I used to play guitar in a band. But that was before I got into business analysis and started prioritizing spreadsheets over songs.      You’re not the only one. I used to dye hair for fun, but now I do it for a living. It’s a weird mix of art and routine.      I can relate. I started as a writer, then moved into editing. It’s been a journey, but I love the creative side of it. I think my hobby of reading poetry actually helps with my job—keeps my mind sharp.      I used to be into TV a lot. I used to watch a lot of drama series. But now, I’m more into cooking shows. There’s something comforting about learning how to cook.      You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a new TV. I’ve been trying to watch more shows, but I can’t seem to find anything that interests me.      Maybe you should try some British drama.  Sherlock  is amazing. Or  Fleabag  if you’re into comedy. I think you’d enjoy it.      Yeah, and if you’re into history,  Sherlock  has some pretty cool references. Though I’m not sure how much you’d get if you’re not into the mystery genre.      I tried  Sherlock  once, and I was like, “This is so over the top.” But I did enjoy the way it mixed sci-fi with real-world detective work.      I guess I’m more of a classic movie guy. I still enjoy old Westerns and British comedies. But I’ve been trying to branch out a bit.

Alright, lass, I’ve been thinkin’ about the car insurance again. Y’know, after I got that fine for parkin’ in the wrong place. Not that I’m proud of it, but it’s gotten me thinkin’ about how much we’re payin’ for this old banger of ours.      Yeah, I’ve noticed. Mum’s been complainin’ about the monthly bill for weeks. I mean, the car’s not even that old, but the insurance is like a tax on top of everything else. I’ve been tryin’ to figure out what’s goin’ on with it.      Aye, and I was sayin’ to myself, if you’re in a car, you’re in a car—why pay more than you have to? I’ve been readin’ up on it a bit, you know, spare time, doin’ some research. It’s all about the risk, lass. The more you drive, the higher the risk.      So, what’s the deal with the risk? I mean, I’ve heard about things like no-claims bonuses, but I don’t really get how that works. And why do some people pay less than others?      Well, it’s all about the insurer’s calculations. They look at your driving record, your age, where you live, how much you drive, and even your job. The fewer claims you’ve had, the lower your premium. But if you’re young and a bit of a risk-taker, like you, then they might charge you more.      That’s me! I’m not exactly the safest driver. I mean, I passed my test, but I still remember that time I hit a kerb on my first day.      You’re not alone. I’ve seen young drivers get charged double what a more experienced one would. But if you’re in college, sometimes they offer discounts. You know, student rates. That might be worth lookin’ into.      That could work. I mean, I’m not even sure what the current rate is. I just pay whatever the company says. Maybe I should compare a few options.      Exactly. You could even look into a telematics policy. You know, one that tracks your driving. If you’re careful, you might save money. Some companies even offer lower rates for safe driving.      Hmm, that’s an idea. I’ve heard about those, but I never really got into it. Maybe I should start lookin’ into that.

So, I’ve been thinking—did you know that the real reason Irish people got the right to vote on the equality marriage thing was because of a few years of stress at work? I mean, it seemed like a lot of us were at our breaking point.      Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I mean, I’ve been stressed with school lately. A lot of work, exams, and stuff. But I don’t think it was enough to get that vote. Although, I do remember seeing a lot of people talking about it on social media. It felt like everyone had an opinion.      That’s true. And if you think about it, the stress levels were high. It was like the whole country was holding its breath. But I think the real turning point was the way people started using words like “equality” and “marriage.” You know, the language changed a lot in those years.      Exactly, and the way people used their faces too. I remember seeing that one video where a guy got emotional on a bus and people just looked at him like he was crazy. But now, when people talk about emotions, they’re much more open about it. It’s like we got better at reading each other?      Maybe. But I still think the stress of work is something that affects people in different ways. I mean, you can’t just say “this is too much” and then everything changes. I’ve read some stuff about how stress is measured through heart rate and something called “perceived stress.” But I still don’t know if that’s enough.      I heard about that. They use these apps to check your stress levels. It’s like a little test you take on your phone. But I think the real way to tell if you’re stressed is how you talk. Like, if you’re using more words like “can’t” or “don’t” a lot, that’s a sign.      I think you’re right. And speaking of that, have you seen the new podcast about how people use words in different accents? It’s wild. I mean, some accents are so different from others that you can’t even understand them. I remember someone from Cork trying to talk like a Londoner, and it was like a joke. But it was funny.      Yeah, I heard about that. Although, I think the real fun is when people try to pronounce words like “curry” wrong.

So, I was just thinking about that time we drove up to the hilltop village last summer and got stuck in a traffic jam because of the wildlife crossing. I swear, there were more sheep than cars on that road!      Oh, don’t get me started. I remember you were so excited about the birds you saw flying over the hills. You even said something like, “Look at those wings! They’re like a Boeing 747!”      Yeah, I was being dramatic, but the view was amazing. I still can’t believe we managed to find that little café at the top. I think it was called “The Hilltop Hoot.”      You guys are obsessed with the hills, aren’t you? I just want to get to the next town and find a better burger. I heard there’s a place in Manchester with a drive-thru that’s like, five stars.      Oh, you’re still thinking about that? You’ve been talking about it for weeks. I told you, the only thing that counts is the food, not the location.      Yeah, and I told you, the food was amazing. But I still think the way they cook the chicken there is the best I’ve ever had.      You two are acting like you’re in a documentary. Let’s get back to the topic. I was just thinking about the weather. It’s hotter than the summer before last, and I still can’t believe we’re all stuck in this car for hours. I swear, I’m about to start hallucinating from the heat.      Don’t worry, love. I’ve got a fan blowing from the back of the car, and I’ve already opened the window. You can’t even feel the heat now.      Yeah, I tried to open the window, but it’s stuck. I think it’s a safety feature or something. Mom, can we stop and get ice cream?      Ice cream? We haven’t even reached the next town yet. But I’m up for it. Just don’t expect me to eat the whole thing.      Okay, but you two are going to have to settle on one flavor. I don’t want to hear anyone arguing like you did last time we tried to split a cone.      Oh, come on, we didn’t argue. We just had different opinions.      Oh, I know, we used to have a contest to see who could eat the most without getting a brain freeze.

Okay, I just can't get over the whole shmeat thing. It's like, if it's grown in a lab, is it even real food? I mean, how do you feel about that?      Honestly, I'm not sure. It's kind of exciting, but also weird. Like, if we can make meat without animals, why would we even need to eat animals anymore? I mean, I love meat, but I also don't want to be part of the system that causes so much harm. Especially with how bad the environment is right now.      Yeah, I get that. I think it's a big step towards sustainability, but the idea of eating something that's not from a living creature still unsettles me. I mean, I’m not vegan, but I do try to eat less meat. It’s not just the environment for me—it's also about animal welfare.      I agree. I mean, I’ve been vegetarian for a few years now, and I have to say, it’s been a huge shift. I used to love steak, but now I feel guilty every time I think about the cows that were killed for it. But still, I wonder if something like shmeat would make it easier for people like me to enjoy the taste without the guilt.      I think it could, but I don’t know if I’m ready to switch to that yet. I mean, I’m not a huge fan of lab-made anything. I prefer food that’s grown in nature, even if it means supporting a system that's not perfect. Plus, I still love the idea of cooking with real ingredients. There’s something about the process of cooking that feels more meaningful.      I can see that. I still cook a lot, and I think there's a kind of art to it. But I also have to be honest—I’ve started taking vitamin tablets just to make sure I’m not missing out on nutrients. It’s not that I don’t like eating vegetables, but I’m not always eating enough, you know?      Yeah, I’ve thought about that too. I always feel like I’m not getting enough protein, even though I eat a lot of legumes and tofu. But then again, I don’t really go out of my way to eat meat anymore. I guess I just don’t have the appetite for it.

So, I just got this massive delivery of stuff from Amazon, and it’s like a pyramid scheme of boxes. I’m not even sure what half of it is.      You’re not the only one. My mum sent me a box of “Christmas essentials” and it’s like a shopping mall in a cardboard box. I still don’t know what half the stuff is for.      I swear, if you could get a refund for the number of things you buy online and then never use, you’d be rich. I just bought a new game, and I’ve only played like two hours of it. I’m still trying to figure out the plot.      Yeah, I feel you. I bought this game called  The Last of Us Part II  and I’ve barely made it past the tutorial. My cousin says it’s a masterpiece, but I’m just trying to not get shot in every level.      I tried to play it once, and I was like, “This is not a game, this is a war movie with short attention spans.” I’ve moved on to  Minecraft —which is basically a free version of  Fortnite , but with dirt blocks.      At least you’re getting something out of it. I’ve been trying to get into  Elden Ring  but it’s like a nightmare. I keep dying in the first boss. I still haven’t gotten around to buying a proper gaming chair. I know that sounds like a big deal, but I’m not even sure if I’ll ever use it.      You’re not even a student yet, and you’re already trying to invest in gaming chairs. You’re getting ahead of yourself, mate.      I think it’s called “preparing for the future.” I mean, you never know when you’ll be a pro gamer or something. Though I doubt it.      Yeah, I’m just trying to survive the next few years. I’ve got exams coming up, and I’m already stressed about that. Although, I did just start watching  Stranger Things  again. It’s been a while.      I’m still waiting for the season to come out.

So, I just got back from my holiday in Spain, and I have to say, it was absolutely  mad ! I mean, I went to Seville and I got lost three times, but that's probably just because I don't speak Spanish well enough. But the food—oh my goodness, the tapas! I tried this incredible dish called  tortilla de patatas , which is like a Spanish omelette, and it was just  delicious . I even tried to eat it with my hands, like the locals do, and I looked like a complete idiot, but it was fun.      Wow, that sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to go to Spain, but I’ve never managed to get the time. I’m actually thinking about taking a gap year after uni to travel Europe. I’ve been planning it for ages, but I keep getting distracted with work.      Oh, that’s a great idea! I mean, with the way the world is now, you can’t really afford to stay in one place forever. But I think I would’ve gone to Portugal instead, just because I love the beaches and the vibe. I even thought about taking a trip to Lisbon and the Algarvian coast, but I ended up going to Seville because it was cheaper and I wanted to see the culture first.      Yeah, I think I’d like that too. It’s just hard to balance everything. I work part-time as an admin for the language research department, and I’m in the middle of a big project. I’m really not sure I can take time off right now.      I get it—work can be so demanding. But you know, it’s about planning. I worked for a few months to save up for my trip, and it was worth every penny. I even met some amazing people along the way. There was this guy from Barcelona who spoke English and Spanish, and he showed me around the city. It was like a real-life language exchange!      That sounds incredible. I’ve always wanted to practice my language skills while traveling, but I’m scared of being too awkward. Do you think people are generally friendly there?      Definitively yes! I mean, in Seville, even if you don’t speak the language, people are  very  friendly. You just have to smile and show you’re trying. I got into some great conversations with people at the market, and I even bought a small bag of olives from a local woman who taught me how to say “thank you” in Spanish.

So, I was just thinking about uni days – you remember when we used to get up at 7 in the morning for lectures, and then we’d end up falling asleep in the library by 3? It’s crazy how fast time flies.      I remember that! I swear, the only reason I survived those lectures was because I had a friend who’d bring me coffee and a bag of crisps every single day. I’d eat the crisps while studying, and the coffee would keep me awake just long enough to survive the next class.      Yeah, but now I’m just grateful that I don’t have to do that anymore. I mean, I’m at sixth form, so I’m still studying, but it’s not the same. I miss the chaos of university, honestly.      I get it. You’ve got to admit, there’s something about that period of life. You’re trying to figure out what you want to do with your life, and you’re constantly surrounded by people who are just like you—vibrant, full of energy, and a bit too caught up in their own drama. But still, I think it was the best time of my life.      Definitely. Although, I have to say – I would have given anything for a massage during that time. I used to come home from lectures so sore, I couldn’t even move. I’d just lie on the couch and wish someone would come in and rub my shoulders for an hour.      I remember you complaining about that all the time. You’d even try to convince me that we should start a massage business, just so we could make money while doing something you love. You said it was “the most lucrative and relaxing career path ever.”      I was serious, too! Maybe I still am. I mean, I do love giving massages. It’s just that I’m not sure I can afford to start a business right now. Plus, I’ve got this project due next week, and I’m so stressed.      You always say that. But I think you’re just trying to avoid the lectures. You know, I’ve got this idea – maybe you could get a part-time job doing massages while you study. If you’re good at it, you could even do it from home. Who knows, maybe it’ll lead to something bigger.

You know, I’ve been thinking about this migrant crisis in Calais. It's been on the news a lot lately, and I can't help but feel uneasy about it. I mean, it's one thing to have people seeking asylum, but the way it's being handled... it's just not right.      I know, it's a real mess. I've been reading about it too. I think the main issue is that there's not enough support or infrastructure to help these people properly. It's not just about the boats or the camps — it's about the human aspect. These are people who are desperate, and they’re not getting the help they need.      I agree. I think the government is being too slow. But I also think there’s a lot of fear involved. People are worried about their own safety, about jobs, about the economy. It's a bit of a Catch-22 situation.      Yeah, that’s exactly it. My dad used to say that when things get tough, people don’t think about the bigger picture — they just think about what’s in front of them. I sometimes wonder if that’s what’s happening here. People are just looking at the immediate problem, not the long-term solution.      You know, I was thinking the other day about how our generation, or at least mine, had to work harder for everything. So, I was telling my wife earlier that I think I’ve finally found the perfect way to enjoy a curry without having to cook it. You could always try to do something like that for the park event. They’re having a night deposit box thing. I think it’s a way for people to give money to charity anonymously. So, you know, I was just thinking about Halloween. I remember when I was a kid, we used to have the most terrifying costumes. You know, I didn’t even know what Halloween was until I was like ten. My parents just said it was a night when witches and ghosts come out. I was so terrified, I actually had a nightmare about a witch coming to my bedroom. But when I started going to school, I learned it was just a holiday. I dressed up as a vampire once, and my friends laughed at me because I wasn’t scary enough.      You know, I think being scared is part of the fun. I remember when I was a kid, I used to dress up as a ghost and walk around the house with a sheet over my head. My sister would be the witch and throw fake spiders at me. It was like a little play. And the best part? We didn’t have to go out. We just stayed in the house and told spooky stories all night.      We did something like that too. My mum used to read us all the best horror stories. She told one about a haunted house with a ghost who loved to play pranks. I think the ghost was named Mr. Whiskers or something like that. Anyhow, it made us all so scared we couldn’t sleep for weeks.      I think the key to Halloween is the imagination.

I don’t know how people manage to get to places like this without getting stuck in traffic. It’s like the whole country’s stuck in one giant jam.      I know, it’s been like that for years. It’s the only thing that makes me feel like we’re not completely stuck in this mess.

Right, so I was just thinking, do you remember that time we tried to plan that secret weekend trip to York? So, I was just thinking about that film we watched last night,  The Midnight Adventure . You remember, the one with the robot that actually  feels  emotions? Still, I couldn’t stop laughing when it shouted “I’m not a machine!” at the end.      Yeah, it was like they were trying too hard to be profound. I mean, it’s not every day you see a robot sitting in a bar drinking a pint of beer and having a real conversation with a human. It was kind of… surreal. So, I was just telling my mum about the washing machine—the one we got last week. She’s like, “Oh, you’ve got a washing machine now? I thought you were still using that old thing from your flat in Sunderland!”      I can imagine. You’ve always been the one who puts everything in the washing machine—shirts, sheets, even your dog’s muddy paws. I remember one time you tried to wash your cat in there too. Ended up with a massive mess in the bathroom.      Oh, that was  bad . I swear, I thought I was doing a good thing. I mean, it’s not like cats are supposed to get clean in the washing machine, right? But I thought, “Well, this way I can get the cat off my hands and into the laundry!” It was a disaster, honestly.      Yeah, and then you had to call the plumber, right? I think the machine was still running for like an hour after that.      I still don’t know how it didn’t explode. It’s all a bit ridiculous. But I have to say, the new machine does a decent job. I think it’s the one from the shop in Cambridge. The one that’s been recommended by all the friends who moved here.      Yeah, I heard that one’s good. I go to the shop sometimes to pick up some food. You know, the kind that actually lasts more than a day. I’ve been trying to get into a better habit of cooking at home. I’ve even been experimenting with some recipes from my mum—like proper English Sunday roasts.      Oh, I’d love to try that! You know I love a proper roast. I mean, it’s not like I can just order takeaway every night.

So, I've been thinking about moving house again. I mean, it's not like I have much money, but I've been meaning to get out of this place for a while.      Oh, really? I thought you were happy enough in Hunsonby. I mean, it's a quiet place, and the countryside is lovely. But if you're thinking of moving, why?      Yeah, I'm curious. Is it because of the house prices? I heard they've gone up again, even here. Didn’t you say the area's a bit isolated?      Well, it's not just the prices, though they’ve gone up like everyone else’s. It's more about the future. I’m not sure if I’m going to be able to afford a place that’s more accessible, especially with my health now.      That sounds tough. I mean, with the state of the economy and everything, it’s hard to know where to move. Have you considered the south?      I thought about it, but I don’t know. I’ve heard the cost of living is way higher there, even more so than in the north. I mean, I remember when I was in London, it was just ridiculous. But I guess people still think it's worth it.      Right, and the whole idea of the south versus the north—it's always been a thing, hasn’t it? Like, the south is all about money and status, and the north is more working-class. But is that really true anymore?      I think it’s more about perception than reality. I mean, I live in the north now, and I can’t afford to live in the south even if I wanted to. But I know people who do, and they’re not necessarily richer. It's just the cost of rent and property here is so much higher.      Exactly. I mean, I was in the oil industry, and I remember the days when you could get a house in the south for a decent price. Now, it's like the same as the north, but you’re paying more for the same thing.      And then there's the whole VW scandal. I think it had an impact on people’s trust in the economy, didn’t it? People were all worried about the future, about jobs, about the state of the country.      Definitely. It made people feel like the system was broken.

Well, I've been thinking about all this pension stuff again. I know it's supposed to be a safety net, but I can't help but feel like it's not enough these days. You know, with the cost of living going up and the housing developments being built on the outskirts of town, it’s hard to see how anyone can make ends meet.      I hear you, mate. I’ve been in the same boat for years. I mean, I've got the pension, but it's just not keeping up. And with the way the government’s handling things, I don’t know what’s going to happen when we get older. I keep telling myself I’ll just stay in a bed and breakfast like you said, but I’m not sure how easy that’s going to be.      You know, I’ve been thinking the same thing. It’s not just the pensions, it’s everything. The way the world has changed, with all these new technologies and computers, you think it would make things easier, but it's the opposite. I had to learn how to use one just to manage my emails, and even then, I’m still confused half the time.      Yeah, I’ve got a computer now, but honestly, it feels like a language I can’t speak. I remember when I was working, I had to use these huge mainframes, and now it's all just tiny screens and buttons. I don’t know what the younger generation goes through.      And don’t get me started on the family stuff. I had a cousin who moved to the States a few years back, and he told me about all these new housing developments there. He said people are just building more and more, but it's not the same as here. There’s a real lack of community now. I used to know everyone in the village, but now it’s all just strangers in flats and houses that look the same.      I remember when the village used to have that nice little inn. I used to stop there when I was doing my childminding. It was a real place, you know? Now it’s been turned into a bungalow block, and the only thing you can get there is a takeaway. I sometimes think about how things have changed, and it worries me.

So, I just got an A in my biology exam, which is basically a miracle because I failed the first one. I mean, I studied for like three days straight, and it paid off.      Yeah, I heard you were pulling an all-nighter before the test. I tried to get you to study with me, but you were too busy on your phone.      I know, I know. I was just scrolling through social media, trying to find something to laugh at. It’s one of those days where the internet doesn’t help when you’re stressed.      I get it. I spent the whole weekend binge-watching a YouTube series about evolution, and now I’m like, “Wait, did humans really evolve from primates?”      Duh, of course they did. But I mean, some people still think we’re descended from apes, and that’s just… wrong. It’s like, if you don’t believe science, what do you believe?      That’s what I was thinking. I mean, if someone told me that, I’d be like, “Are you serious?” But then again, I’ve seen some insane stuff on the internet. Like that whole “men are better at math” thing.      Oh, I saw that meme about men being better at STEM and women being more emotional. It’s so gross. Like, who even came up with that?      Oh, I remember when my sister got into a fight with her biology teacher about that. She said, “If men are better at science, why do we have so few women in STEM fields?”      Exactly! And then the teacher said, “Maybe because women are just not as interested.” That’s when my sister walked out. She was so unimpressed.      I mean, if that’s the case, then why did I get an A in biology? I was the one who was talking about evolution all weekend.      You had a  lot  of help from the internet. And honestly, I think it’s funny how people get so worked up about things like gender and science. Like, it’s not even a real debate.      I think part of it is just the way society is set up. Like, women are told they can’t be scientists, and then they don’t even get to try.      And then there’s racism, too. Like, some people think certain races are smarter than others, which is just… nonsense. I mean, how do you even measure that?

Well, I've been thinking about that thing with the hospital appointment. I was just wondering, have you had yours yet? I hear the MOT is going to be more expensive this year, and I need new tyres too.      I hear you. I’ve been meaning to get my car checked, but I just haven’t had the time. Well, you two know I’ve been thinking a lot lately about history—especially about the things that shaped our world. I was telling my sister about this book I read about the transatlantic slave trade, and it made me wonder how much we really understand about the past.      What’s the transatlantic slave trade? Is it like a big boat?      It’s like a big boat, but not just any boat—it was a system that lasted for hundreds of years. People were taken from their homes, forced to go to faraway places like the Americas, and treated very badly. It was cruel, and it caused a lot of suffering.      Why did they do that? Why would they take people?      Well, there’s a lot to unpack there. Some people believed that the people they were taking were not human, or that they were less important than others. This idea helped them justify the suffering. But the reality is that it was a human rights violation on a massive scale.      But why would they want to take people?      It was all about money and power. The people who owned the ships and the land made a lot of money by forcing people to work for them. They didn’t pay them, and they treated them like animals. It was a system built on exploitation.      That’s not fair. Why didn’t they stop it?      That’s the tricky part. It took a long time for people to realize how wrong it was. There were activists, writers, and even children who spoke out. But it took many years of struggle before change happened.      So, was it like a war?      It was part of a larger struggle. There were wars, rebellions, and movements for freedom. People like Frederick Douglass and Harriet Tubman fought for the rights of those who were enslaved. The North wanted to end it, and the South wanted to keep it. It was a very big war that changed the course of history.      So, all of this happened a long time ago?      Yes, but it still affects us today. We’re still learning from the past, and we need to understand it so we can build a better future.      I think I get it now.

So, I was watching this new drama on the box last night,  The Halcyon Days , and I just couldn’t stop thinking about it! It's such a strange mix of nostalgia and modern problems. You’ll be a train engineer one day, I can tell. But go on, get your toys from the shelf. We still have to finish unloading the dishwasher. I think there’s a box of sugar on the bottom.      Yeah, and there’s some milk in the fridge, too. I’ll go get it. Wait, do you think George Stephenson had to clean the dishes after he built the train?

So, how’s your lunch going? You’ve been staring at your sandwich for ages.      Oh, it’s fine, thanks. I just hadn’t decided what to eat. I’m still trying to figure out what’s on the menu today. Honestly, I’ve never had proper fish and chips. I grew up in Russia, and even then, it was like a Russian version of it. I mean, I’ve had the real thing once, but it was like a token visit to a British restaurant.      Oh, I see. I had a friend from Moscow once who brought me some of that—like, it was a mix of fish and borscht. It was… interesting.      That’s not the worst thing I’ve ever eaten. It’s a bit of a culture shock, honestly.      You must miss your family. How are they managing?      They’re great. I miss them, but the school here is actually really good. The kids are friendly, and the teachers are very supportive.      That’s good to hear. I have a nephew who started in the same school. He’s a bit of a troublemaker, but he’s getting better.      Sounds like you’ve got a busy life. How do you manage work and family?      It’s a struggle, but I’m lucky I have a good team.

So, I just got a massive bag of blankets from that shop in Preston. Hey, do you know what this is made of? It’s got a nice sheen, but it’s not silver or gold. I think it might be copper, but I’m not sure.      I don’t know, but I think it’s something like brass? Hey guys, did you hear about the Montenegro trip? I think the school is organizing it for next year. It’s supposed to be a gap year kind of thing, right?      Yeah, I heard about that too. You know, I even tried to build that shed in the garden. It took me weeks, and the result was a mess.      Oh, I remember that shed! You managed to make it look like a fortress. I remember coming home one day and seeing that thing. I barely recognized it. You were so proud, too. I think you thought you were building a guest house.      Oh, I was! I was going to call it 'The Grand Manor'. I even painted the door gold and put up a sign. It looked grand, didn’t it?      It did. It was a sight. I still remember the look on your face when you finally got it open. It was like you’d just made history.      You two are a real pair of eccentrics. I sometimes wonder if you ever think about what you could have done with all that time and energy. But I suppose it’s part of the charm.      I suppose so. I mean, we’ve had a lot of adventures, haven’t we?

You know, I’ve been thinking about Christmas plans again. I was just telling Sue the other day how I really want to make it a bit more special this year.      I hear you. I’ve been considering it too. We’re all busy at work, so it’s important to make time for the family. But have you thought about where we’re all going to meet?      I’ve got an idea. We could all meet at my place. It’s a bit of a mess, but I’ve been redecorating, and it’s actually quite nice now. Plus, I’ve got a few decorations up that Myra helped me with.      Oh, you’ve got to be joking. If Myra’s involved, you’re in for a real show! I remember last year when she tried to put up fairy lights and accidentally set the whole thing on fire.      Oh, yes, that was a sight. But you know, we all have our little quirks. Speaking of quirks, I’ve been meaning to ask—have you all got your Christmas shopping done yet?      Not at all. I still have a few things to pick up. I’ve been trying to find the perfect gift for my sister, but everything seems to be priced way too high these days.      I know what you mean. I’ve been browsing online, but honestly, it’s just too tempting to buy everything. I’ve ended up spending more than I intended.      I’m still waiting for my paycheck. I’m not even sure I’ll be able to afford the basics, let alone gifts. I’m just trying to budget properly.      I know, it’s tough. I was thinking about money the other day. It’s funny how even with our jobs, it’s not always easy. I’ve been trying to cut back on food shopping and cook more at home.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been trying to do the same. It’s not just about saving money—it’s about being more mindful of what we spend.      I’ve been planning a trip to the coast for the weekend. It’s just a short drive from here, and I thought it might be a good chance to relax and get my head together.      That sounds nice. I’d love to go with you. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck at home lately.

Good morning, John. It's lovely to be here. I've never been to Northern Cyprus before, and I must say, it's quite a different place from England. I was just wondering, how long have you lived here?      Oh, I've been here for about ten years now. I retired from my job in the UK and came over with my wife. We thought it would be a nice change of scenery, and the weather's so much better than back home. Although, I must admit, it's a bit of a culture shock at first.      That's understandable. I can imagine. I've heard that the pace of life here is slower, which I guess is a good thing. But what’s it like living here? Are there many people like you, retired or from the UK?      Well, there are quite a few expats, especially from the UK. A lot of people come here for the climate and the cost of living. But the locals, the Cypriots, are very friendly. They’re not as overbearing as some people I’ve met back home. Although, I’ve noticed that sometimes they can be quite insistent on their way of doing things.      That must be interesting. I’ve been teaching for years, so I’ve always been used to dealing with different people and cultures. But I imagine adapting to a new place can be quite challenging, especially when you're retired and not working anymore.      Yes, it can be. At first, I felt a bit lost, not having a routine. But now I've settled in. I take up gardening, and I go to the local market every morning. It’s a nice way to meet people and get to know the community.      That sounds lovely. I wish I had more time to explore. I've only been here a few days, and I’m already beginning to like it. I was wondering, have you ever had any funny experiences here?      Oh, there have been a few! One time, I tried to order a coffee at a local café and the barista looked at me like I was speaking another language. I was just trying to say “latte,” and she kept repeating it back to me. I finally had to show her on my phone how to pronounce it.      Oh, that’s a classic! I’ve had similar experiences when I first came here.

So, I just got back from work, and honestly, I was so glad to get out of that lecture hall. I mean, I love teaching, but after three hours of going through the same material with a group of students who don’t seem to care, it’s exhausting. How about you?      I know exactly how you feel. I had that same lecture this morning about postcolonial literature. I’ve been trying to get them to engage with the texts, but honestly, half of them just zone out. I can’t even remember the last time I had a class that actually paid attention. It’s like the whole thing is just a formality.      I feel you. But on the flip side, I still get a bit of a rush when someone actually asks a good question or has an original insight. It makes it all worth it. Although, I did have one student today who asked if we could discuss the environmental impact of colonialism. I had to stop myself from jumping up and down. I thought,  this is the first time I’ve heard that angle on it.       That’s brilliant, isn’t it? I think that’s the kind of thinking we should be encouraging. It shows that they’re not just regurgitating facts—they’re making connections. I had a student last week who wrote a paper about how pollution in postcolonial cities is a direct result of colonial-era industrialization. It was really insightful. I actually got a bit emotional reading it.      That sounds amazing. I’m glad you’re getting some good work out of it. Speaking of which, have you seen the air quality here? I mean, it’s not  that  bad, but it’s definitely not like back home. I miss the clear skies of Norwich. I had to bring a mask with me today because it felt like the air was really heavy. You’d think in a city like this, with all the traffic, it would be worse.      Yeah, the pollution is a real issue. I mean, I’ve been here for a few months now, and it’s gotten worse every week. I keep telling myself it’s temporary, but I’m starting to think it’s just going to be part of life here. I’ve even started reading up on ways to combat it on a personal level—like using public transport more, reducing waste, that kind of thing.

Well, I think I’ve got everything we need for dinner. Chicken, potatoes, some veggies. I’m thinking of making a simple roast chicken with roast potatoes and green beans. It's not fancy, but it's filling and easy enough to make on a weekday.      Sounds good. I’ve been craving something hearty. Though I’ve been working late a lot lately, so I’ve been skipping lunch. Maybe I should start bringing a packed lunch to work instead of relying on takeout.      Yeah, I’ve been doing that too. I’ve got a lunchbox that I fill with a sandwich, some fruit, and a yogurt. It’s more healthy than the greasy takeaways I used to get. Plus, I save money and feel better about what I’m eating.      I know what you mean. I used to live on takeaway, but now I try to cook more. I’ve even started taking photos of my meals. It’s kind of a thing—people post their food on social media these days. I’ve got a folder on my phone called “Dinner Photos” with like 200 pictures. Maybe I should start putting them on Instagram.      That’s a bit much. I’ve got a few photos of my meals, but I’m not one for sharing every single one. Though I did just post a photo of my lunch yesterday—just a simple salad with some olives and a lemon wedge. People seemed to like it. It’s strange how people get so excited about food.      I love it. I think food is such a big part of life, and sharing it with others is special. I’ve been doing a little food blog on my website. It’s not very popular yet, but I’m trying to build up a following. I did a post about my favorite lunch recipes. It was mostly just my gran’s recipes, though. I think she’s the best cook I’ve ever known.      That’s sweet. I think I’ve got a few recipes from my mum. She used to make the best Sunday roasts. I wish I could cook as well as her. Maybe I should start writing down my own recipes too. It would be a nice way to remember the good old days.      Oh, I think we should start putting the chicken in the oven. I don’t want it to go cold.

So, I just got an email about the new bus route they’re planning to open in the city. It’s supposed to go from King’s College to the bus station near the railway station, right? I think it’s meant to help students and commuters who don’t want to walk all the way from the campus. Has anyone heard anything about it?      Yeah, I heard about it too. I think it’s going to start running next month. From what I’ve read, it’s going to be a bit of a game-changer, especially for people who live outside the city but still want to get to the university quickly. But I also heard some people are worried about the route—like, is it going to be frequent enough? I mean, I’m an engineer, so I guess I can see the challenges of getting the timing right.      I can imagine. I was thinking the other day about how much it would help if there was a better connection between the city centre and the colleges. I mean, walking from King’s to the train station isn’t exactly a walk in the park. I know a few people who’ve been caught in the rain or late for lectures because of it. It’s a real pain.      Exactly. I remember when I was a student here, I used to take the bus from Royal Mile to the main campus. It was a long ride, and sometimes the bus would get delayed because of traffic. I think the new route is going to be a bit shorter, which is a big plus. Although I do wonder how it’ll compare to the current services. You ever go to the Cambridge University Press bookshop? It’s got some great used books, and I’ve found a few rare editions there over the years.      Oh yeah, I love going there. I’ve found some really cool books that you can’t get anywhere else. But I can’t help but think about the student protesters who’ve been out there lately. There was that one demonstration about tuition fees. It was pretty intense, I heard. I tried to go, but I got distracted by the bookshop and ended up buying a few books instead.      That was one of the bigger ones. I think it was a couple of months ago.

So, I've been thinking about our old days in Dublin. Remember when we used to cook up a storm every weekend? I swear, we could make a stew out of a few ingredients and turn it into a feast. I can still remember the smell of that lamb shank with red wine sauce — it was like a holiday every time.      Oh, I still miss that. You always had a way of making even the simplest meal feel like a celebration. I remember you used to say, “If it’s not fresh, it’s not for dinner.” And when it was fresh, it was  amazing . I guess I’ve lost that touch since moving to Birkenhead. I can barely make toast without burning it.      You’re not the only one! I’ve had to learn how to cook properly since I started working in HR. I used to think about the old days when we all just gathered for Sunday dinners. Now, I’m lucky if I can get a meal out of a microwave without setting the kitchen on fire.      Well, I think it’s because we had time. These days, people are always rushing. You know, I’ve been thinking about getting back into cooking. Maybe I can start with something simple — like a good old Irish stew. I remember how much my kids used to love that. It was one of the few things I could do that didn’t involve them crying.      You should! And maybe you could even share it with our group. I’m always trying to find a good meal to bring to the office — you know, to impress my colleagues. If you can make a stew that brings back memories, it’s bound to win over even the most cynical of them.      I’d be happy to help. I could even research some recipes. I’ve been reading up a lot on traditional British and Irish cuisine. It’s funny — I always thought I knew what was traditional, but now I realize there’s so much more to explore. I’ve even tried some of the regional dishes from the North West, and they’re quite different from what I grew up with.      That’s interesting. I’ve always considered myself more of a Dubliner, but I think there’s a lot to learn from the North West. I mean, you can’t deny the charm of a good Sunday roast.

So, I was just thinking about how we used to walk along the Thames when we first moved to London. It feels like forever ago, doesn’t it?      Yeah, it does. I remember we used to stop at that bridge near Woolwich—do you remember the one with the big clock on it? I swear I used to think it was broken half the time.      Oh yes! I used to get so frustrated when we'd be walking and you’d stop to check the time. I’d just say, “It’s not broken, it’s just slow!” But you’d ignore me like I was talking to a wall.      You know, I still think it’s broken. My watch says it’s 3:47 PM, but that clock says 3:23. I’d say I’m late for something, then check again, and it’s still the same. What’s the point?      I don’t know. It’s the same clock that’s been there since the 1800s, right? I mean, it’s got character. But I still can’t believe that people don’t just walk to the O2 Arena instead of taking the Tube. It’s only a short walk from here, isn’t it?      Oh, I know, but I still don’t own a car. And my partner’s parents are coming to visit next week, and I’m already dreading it. What am I going to do? Let them drive us around in a taxi? That’ll cost a fortune.      I’d rather have a taxi than try and explain to them how the London underground works. You know, most people don’t even know what a Bank station is, let alone where the City is.      Exactly! And that’s why I think we should plan a holiday with the family. Maybe go somewhere with a car. I was thinking about the Lake District. The views are beautiful, and it’s a chance to get away from all the city noise.      That sounds perfect. Though I’ll admit, I’d rather not have to deal with American cup measurements while cooking. I mean, who even  uses  a cup anymore? It’s like the 19th century!      I know, right? I swear, if I had to measure something with a cup, I’d just use the tablespoon and forget about it. It’s not like we’re in the US, is it?

Oh, I can't believe it's raining again! I was just about to go for a walk in the garden with the kids. It’s been so dry all summer, and now it's suddenly thrown a tantrum.      I was just thinking the same thing. I’ve been trying to get the kids to help me clean the kitchen, but with the rain coming down like a waterfall, I don’t think they’re going to be rushing into the house any time soon.      Ugh, the worst. I was hoping the weather would finally break and let us take the kids to the park for their sports day. I’ve been trying to get them all dressed up and ready for the event, but now I’m worried the rain might delay everything.      Oh no, that’s not great. But you know, I actually have a plan. I found this "build a bear" at the shop last week, and I thought maybe the kids could have a cuddly toy to keep them entertained if the weather doesn’t clear up.      You did that? Did you tell them it’s a "build a bear" or just let them think it was a regular stuffed animal?      I let them think it was just a regular one. They were all excited about it, and when I finally told them what it was, they were like, “Oh, is this someone’s friend?”      I can imagine. My eldest had a phase where they thought all the cuddly toys were sentient and had feelings. I spent weeks trying to get them to stop talking to their teddy bear.      Oh, I remember that. My sister used to do that too. She even had a little ritual where she would “feed” her teddy bear toast and milk every morning.      That was before she was potty trained, I suppose. You know, I still remember my own potty training. It was a mess. I’d have to keep the door open so the parents could hear if I needed help.      I still have nightmares about it. I think I was so scared of messing up that I just held it in for days.      I’m sure you’re not the only one. I had a friend who cried for weeks because she was so embarrassed about it.      At least we’re all growing up. I think I need to make a list of things I still want to do before I retire, like swimming in England.

So, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about what I want to achieve in the next few years. With the house-sitting here in Australia, I’m feeling like I have a bit of a blank canvas to work with. I mean, I’ve always wanted to start a new project—maybe something more sustainable, you know? I’ve been reading a lot about eco-friendly businesses and how they’re shaping the future.      That sounds really interesting. I’ve always admired people who can turn their passions into a successful business. But I have to say, I’m a bit nervous about the whole idea. I’ve been teaching for over a decade, and I’ve always found comfort in the routine, you know? But I do feel like I’m stagnating a little. I think I need to start thinking about my own goals.      I totally get that. I was in a similar place a few years back. I was working in a corporate job, and while it paid well, it didn’t make me feel fulfilled. I remember the day I decided to take the leap and start my own business. It was scary, but it was also one of the best decisions I’ve ever made. You don’t have to be fearless, just willing to take a step.      That’s reassuring to hear. I’ve been thinking about maybe taking some courses in digital education or something related to my field. I’m not sure if I want to leave teaching entirely, but I’d like to expand my horizons. Maybe even work part-time and still have time for my family.      That’s a great idea. Also, have you thought about joining up with some of the friends we’ve been in touch with? I know about this group of entrepreneurs who meet up every few months to share ideas and support each other. It might be a good way to network and get some fresh perspectives.      I haven’t considered that. Maybe I should look into it. I’ve been feeling a bit isolated lately, especially since I’m away from home. It’s good to have a community to lean on. Speaking of which, have you thought about family planning? I mean, I know we both have our own goals, but I think it’s important to talk about how we want to balance work and family in the long term.

So, I was just telling my mates about the time I tried to order a latte at Costa and the barista thought I was ordering a  latt  for a  latt  for a  latte ... like I was being sarcastic or something. I was just trying to say "latte" properly. It was ridiculous.      I remember that too. I once tried to say "how do you do?" in a posh accent to a guy at the pub, and he just stared at me like I was speaking another language. I think he thought I was trying to be a posh posh.      Yeah, that’s the thing, isn’t it? I think it’s funny when people go to the trouble of changing their accent, especially when they’re just trying to sound "better." But then again, I guess when you grow up in Warrington, you don’t really think about accents that much.      I mean, I grew up in Warrington too, and I still don’t think about my accent much. But sometimes, like when I go to Leeds, and I hear that Yorkshire drawl—it’s like, "Oh, that’s different." I feel like I’m in a different country.      Yeah, I don’t know if it’s the accent or the vibe, but when I’m in Leeds, I just feel like I’m in a different part of the world. I can’t even tell you the last time I had a conversation with someone from Warrington. Anyway, I used to think that people from Manchester had the worst accent, but I’ve heard the Leeds ones are worse.      That’s because they’re trying too hard. I mean, we all have our own ways, but for the love of God, don’t overdo it.      I remember when I was at university, there was this guy from York who tried to speak like a posh posh. He said things like "I shall take a pint of lager" and "I do not wish to be exposed to such a level of tedium." It was so fake.      I think I once tried that in a group project. I tried to sound like a professor, and all my mates just stared at me like I was a foreigner.      I’ve been trying to sound posh for years, but I can’t even pronounce "biscuit" right. I say "biscit" and my mum just laughs.      Maybe you should just stick to your natural accent.

Well, I’ve been thinking about that game we had last Saturday, when the kids were all out in the garden playing football. It was chaos, really. I was trying to keep an eye on them, and the next thing I know, one of them’s running through the garden with a ball, and the other’s chasing after him, and I’m just sitting there on the bench thinking, “What have I done with my life?”      Oh, don’t start on that. You know how they are. I remember when I was their age, I used to play football every day like it was my job. Now I can barely walk to the shops without getting out of breath. But you know what’s funny? I’ve been telling my niece that if she ever wants to learn how to play, I can teach her. She’s the one who’s always saying, “Grandma, why aren’t you active?”      That’s typical of you, Speaker_2. You always say the most ridiculous things. But I have to say, it’s nice to hear you’re still up for something. You know, I’ve been thinking about organising a family gathering for the summer. Maybe something like a barbecue or a picnic in the park. It’s been too long since we all got together.      Yeah, I agree. I was actually talking to my mum about it the other day. She said she’d love to see everyone again. But someone has to take charge of the food. You know, the kind of food that makes people happy and not the kind that makes them sick.      Oh, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to make the best of my time now that I’m retired. Maybe I should start a little garden. I’ve always wanted to grow vegetables, but I’m not sure I’m up to it.      You’ve got to give it a go. You never know, you might end up being the best gardener in the neighborhood. I’ve got a few seeds I’ve been saving for just this kind of thing. Maybe we can start a little garden together.      That’s a great idea. And if you go for it, maybe we can all help. I mean, it’s not like we don’t have the time. We’ve got the whole summer to make it work.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever miss those days when we used to stay up all night with our mates, just talking about everything? I mean, sure, we were total chaos, but there was something about those nights that felt like you were living your life to the fullest.      Yeah, I know what you mean. It’s like, once you’ve left that stage, you start thinking about all the times you could’ve done things differently. But honestly, do you think we’re doing the right thing by staying in uni? I mean, I’ve been thinking about dropping out. I’m so tired of all this work and not seeing any real progress.      I get it. It’s exhausting. I mean, I’m not even sure why I’m still here. I keep thinking about how much time I’ve wasted, and I just feel like I’m not getting anywhere. But I don’t know, I keep telling myself I’ll just push through. Maybe I’ll get that job I’ve been applying for.      I wish I had that kind of confidence. I feel like I’m just going through the motions. I mean, I love my courses, but it’s just… so much pressure. I feel like I’m not even in control of my own life anymore. Sometimes I think maybe I should just take a break and figure things out later.      You know, when I was a kid, my mum always said, “If you’re not enjoying what you’re doing, you’re doing the wrong thing.” I used to think she was just being dramatic, but now I’m starting to see what she meant. I mean, I’m not saying dropping out is the answer, but maybe you should take some time to think about it. You don’t have to do everything all at once.      Yeah, I guess that’s something to consider. I mean, I’ve always loved stories about people who dropped out and then found their path later. I just feel like I’m always trying to catch up with everyone else.      Speaking of stories, have you ever told the one about how your dad used to call you “Lily the Lizard”? I swear, you were like a tiny green monster back in the day.      Oh, that was  so  embarrassing. I was like three, and I used to walk around like a little dragon, and he just couldn’t resist.

Hey, it's so good to see you again! I’ve been trying to get in touch for ages, but I’ve been so busy with work and everything. I can’t believe it’s been over a year since we last met.      Same here! Honestly, I’ve been avoiding calling you because I didn’t want to say the wrong thing. You know how it is—when you haven’t spoken in a while, you’re always worried about catching up on everything.      I know, it’s like you always have something to say but never the right time. Anyway, how have you been? Work still stressful?      Oh, you have no idea. It’s been madness at Pearson. I got promoted last month, which is great, but the hours are insane. I’ve been working late almost every night, and it’s starting to take a toll. I feel like I’m constantly running on fumes.      That’s rough, but at least you’re climbing the ladder. I feel like I’ve been stuck in the same place for ages. I’m still a project co-ordinator, and it’s not like I’m getting any more opportunities.      I know, it’s frustrating. But maybe it’s time to start thinking about moving on. Have you thought about what you want to do next?      Honestly, I’m not sure. I love what I do, but I don’t feel like I’m growing. I’ve been thinking about doing some freelance work on the side, maybe something more creative. I miss the freedom of being able to pick my own projects.      That sounds like a good move. You always had a creative streak. Maybe it’s time to take a risk. I know it’s scary, but sometimes you have to step out of your comfort zone.      Yeah, you’re right. I’ve been so afraid of changing things, but I think I need to stop fearing the unknown. Besides, I’ve got you and the others to keep me grounded.      You know I’m always here for you. And don’t even think about changing your mind about moving to Oxford. You’re staying with me, and we’ll figure it out together.      Deal. But first, let’s order the food. I’m starving, and I can’t remember the last time I had a proper meal.      Agreed. And maybe we can plan a weekend trip to the countryside.

Alright, lass, I’ve been thinkin’ about the internet shopping lately. You know how I’ve been havin’ this thing where I can’t find the right pens for my exams? I mean, I need them for the GCSEs, and I’ve tried every store in York, but they’re just not the same as the ones I used to buy in North Ferriby.      Yeah, I get that. I mean, I’ve been on eBay for a while now. It’s not like the old days when you had to go to the shop and pick things up. Now you can just click and buy. My mates say it’s easier, but I’m not sure. I mean, sometimes you get what you want, and sometimes you don’t.      Exactly. I tried eBay a few times, but it’s a bit confusing. You have to be careful with the descriptions, you know? I once bought a set of pens that were supposed to be red, but they turned out to be green. And I had to send them back. It’s not like the real thing.      That’s a bummer. I’ve had some weird stuff too. I bought a pair of headphones that were supposed to be noise-canceling, but they just made everything louder. Silly me, I didn’t read the reviews. I mean, I was in a rush to get them for my audition. I thought they’d work.      You and your auditions, lad. I remember when I was your age, trying to get into drama school. I used to buy the most ridiculous things, thinking they’d help me. But really, it was just the school uniform that mattered. And even that, I had to order online. I thought I was so clever.      Well, you did pass your exams, didn’t you? I mean, you were a GCSE Maths Examiner. I can’t even do fractions without getting confused.      That’s the thing, though. I know how to read the numbers, but sometimes the actual goin’ on the internet is more of a mystery. I think I need to spend more time on Amazon. I’ve heard they’re better with the returns. You can just click “return” and they take it back.      Yeah, I’ve been using Amazon a lot. It’s faster, and they have better customer service. You just need to make sure you check the ratings.

You know, I was just thinking about how different things were when I was your age. Back in the days when I used to work at the factory, we’d have long shifts, but at least we had a sense of purpose. Now, with things the way they are, I don’t know if people even know what they want anymore.      I guess things have changed a lot. I mean, I’m in a job, and it’s not like I’m struggling to make ends meet. But I do wonder sometimes if the younger generation is too caught up in all the tech and social media stuff. I don’t know, it just feels like they’re missing something.      Yeah, I suppose there’s a lot to be said for the old ways. You know, when you had real conversations, not just texts and emojis. I still remember the days when people would sit down and talk about their day, not just scroll through their phones.      I can see that. I do try to get away from my phone as much as I can, especially when I’m with family. It’s funny, though — I used to be the one who always had my phone out, but now I’m the one trying to put it down.      That’s the life, eh? You never think you’ll be the one doing the old-fashioned thing, but here we are. Still, I’ll say this: even though I’m not working, I do feel like I’ve got more time to enjoy the little things. Like this coffee, or just sitting here and talking with someone I care about.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? No matter where you are in life, it’s the people you surround yourself with that make the difference. I mean, I’ve got a good job, a stable income, but without people like you, I wouldn’t be as happy as I am.      Well, I’m glad to hear that. Alright, so I’ve been thinking—what are we actually doing for Christmas? I mean, I know we’re all staying in, but I feel like we need to make it a little more special. Not like last year, where we just ended up watching  The Office  and eating cheese and biscuits.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking too. You know, I’ve been thinking about this whole accent thing. It’s weird how people from different parts of the country sound so different, even if they’re all from England. So, I was just telling the kids about balanceability. You know, that thing when you’re on a tightrope or a beam and you have to keep your balance? It's like, you can’t just wobble—you have to think about where your center of gravity is.      Yeah, I tried that on the monkey bars at school. I kept falling off because I wasn’t balancing properly. They just said, “That’s okay, you’ll get the hang of it.”      I remember when I was your age. It was all about learning how to balance. I think it's part of growing up. I think it’s supposed to be a place for the kids to relax. I tried to climb up it once, but I slipped and fell into the grass.      You were lucky it was just grass. I can’t imagine what would happen if you fell into the water.      I think I’d drown in the water.      No, you would’ve floated. You’re not that heavy, after all.      Yeah, maybe you’re right. So, I was just telling my cousin about the time I tried to do a HIIT workout and ended up throwing out my ankle.
