I tried to redecorate and ended up with more paint on the ceiling than the walls.      That sounds like a classic. I’ve been trying to get some work done at home, but the cat keeps knocking over my coffee. I told her she was a menace, and she just meowed back.      I feel your pain. I’ve got a dog who thinks he’s a human. He’s constantly trying to eat my shoes. I swear, if he doesn’t stop, I’m going to have to take him to the vet again.      I don’t know what I’d do without mine. He’s a great listener, actually. Spends more time with me than my actual friends. But then again, I’m out all day at work, so he’s my only companion.      You know, I’ve actually been thinking about changing up my diet. I’m trying to get healthier. I’ve been eating more vegetables and cutting down on the takeaways. It’s tough, but I feel better.      I tried that too. I used to eat a lot of fast food, but I’ve been trying to cook more. You know, healthy meals. It’s not easy, but I’ve started making soups and lunches to take to work.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been on a low-carb diet for a while now, and it’s actually helped me lose some weight. I’ve been trying to keep it up, but it’s not always easy when you’re in the mood for something sweet.      I’ll admit, I’ve been a bit of a chocolate addict. I bought a box of chocolates the other day and I’ve been hiding them in the freezer.

So, I’ve been trying to get that TV licence sorted, but it’s like trying to find a needle in a haystack. I mean, I’ve called the number three times, and every time they say “just a moment” and then it’s another hold. It’s so frustrating.      I know the feeling, mate. I tried to renew mine last week, and I got sent a letter saying I had to call a number, which then led me to a website, which said I had to call another number. It’s like a loop. I think the government has forgotten what a TV licence even is these days.      Yeah, I’ve had that too. I even called the helpline and got put on hold for over an hour. I ended up giving up and just not watching the BBC for a month. It was a bit of a shock, but I couldn’t be bothered to argue. They’ve made it so complicated.      I told you about the eclipse last week? It was amazing, really. I mean, it was the first time I’d seen one up close. I had to stay up late and set up the telescope, and the kids were in awe. It reminded me of when I was a kid, watching the sky – it’s one of the few things that still take me back to the good old days.      That sounds lovely. I didn’t get to see it, though. My TV wasn’t working at the time. I’m still trying to sort the licence out. I can’t watch the documentaries about the cosmos anymore. I miss the shows about black holes and the beginnings of space. They used to be so educational.      I remember the Cosmos series. Carl Sagan was brilliant. I still have the DVD. I used to watch it every night. It made me want to study astronomy, but then I got busy with the nursery and never followed through. I think I could still do it, though. I’ve always had a bit of a knack for it.      You know, I’ve been thinking about moving. The house feels a bit too big now. My wife passed away a few years back, and I’ve been alone a lot. Maybe I should go down to the coast. I’ve always wanted to live by the sea. It would be nice to have a garden with a big old tree and some plants.

So, I was just thinking about where we should go for dinner. I know it's late, but I’d love to check out that new Italian place near the cathedral. I’ve heard it’s really good.      Yeah, I’ve heard about it too. The reviews are all over the place, but I think it’s worth a try. But wait, we’re driving, right? You don’t want to be stuck in traffic or anything.      Oh, don’t worry, I’ve got the GPS on. I’ve got it set for the shortest route. But I was thinking—we could also check out that little café near the bus stop. It’s the one that only opens at 5, and the food is supposed to be really local.      Hmm, the bus stop café? I’ve passed it a few times. It’s got that sort of cottage vibe, you know? I mean, it’s not much, but sometimes a bit of simplicity is better. Although, I’m not sure if we’ll have time to get there. I’ve got that meeting tomorrow, and I don’t want to be too tired.      Fair enough. But you know, I’ve been thinking about moving. Maybe we could look for a place closer to the cathedral. I mean, the buses are a bit of a hassle, and it’s not like we’re in a rush anymore. We’ve got time to explore.      That’s true. I mean, I’ve always wanted to live near a cathedral. There’s something about the architecture, the history. You can’t ignore the presence of that kind of place. But I’ve got to be realistic. The housing prices there are insane, even for someone like me with a postgrad degree.      I know, I know. But it’s not just about the price. It’s about the lifestyle. I mean, I’d rather live in a small house near the cathedral than in a big flat with a 30-minute commute. Do you think we could even afford it?      Maybe not right now. But we could save up. I mean, I’m a consultant engineer, so the income is steady. And you’re a corpus administrator—don’t underestimate that. That’s a solid job too. But let’s not get ahead of ourselves. Let’s focus on the present.      Right, right. I’m just getting used to the idea.

Good morning, Mavis. I hope you had a good night’s sleep. I’ve been trying to get up early to hear the birdsong, but I keep getting distracted by the alarm clock. You know how it is—every time I think I’m awake, it goes off again.      Oh, I know all about that! I’ve been up since six this morning, but I’ve got a headache now from all the noise. I think it’s the alarm clock. I tried to get rid of it, but the new one just reminds me of my husband. Still, I made it through, and I’ve been feeding the birds. I’ve got that old bird feeder out by the window. I left some sunflower seeds out, and the sparrows came in droves.      That’s lovely of you. I try to do the same, but I always end up forgetting. I’ve been trying to remember the names of the birds. I think I’ve got the blackbird and the chaffinch down, but I’m not sure if I’ve got the tit right. I keep thinking it’s a different kind of bird.      Oh, they’re so small, aren’t they? I think they’re called the Great Tit. I used to have a book with pictures, but I lost it. I’m trying to remember from memory now. I think they’re the ones with the yellow heads and the red breasts. Oh, and don’t forget to mention the blue tit. They’re quite different.      I’ll try. I think I’ve seen a couple of blue tits too. I’ve been feeding them because I heard about how important it is for the birds to have food in the winter. It’s a bit of a selfish thing, really—I’m doing it more for me than for them, but I do enjoy the company.      I can see that. I’ve been doing it for years. It’s something to look forward to in the morning. I’ve even started getting up early just to watch them. I remember when I was younger, I used to think birds were just little things that sang, but now I see how much they depend on us.      That’s true. I think it’s a shame more people don’t do it. It’s a way to connect with nature, even in the city.

So, it’s been way too long, isn’t it? I can’t believe it’s been almost five years since we last saw each other. How have you been?      Oh, it’s been a whirlwind! Life has thrown so many things my way. But honestly, I’m just glad to be catching up. How are you? Still teaching at that school in Oxford?      Yeah, still there, although I’ve been thinking about making a change. I’ve always admired your journey—moving into social work. It’s such a different path but clearly one you’re passionate about.      Thank you. I love what I do, but it’s not without its challenges. I still remember the first time I had to help a single mother with her IVF journey. It was so emotional and I felt like I had to be there for her every step of the way.      I can only imagine. I’ve been through a lot with my own family, especially with the way social media has changed the way people deal with things like IVF and parenthood. It’s both a blessing and a curse, don’t you think?      Absolutely. On one hand, it gives people a platform to share their stories and find support. On the other, it can be so overwhelming. I’ve seen so many people feel the pressure to present a perfect life, even when they’re going through something really tough.      It feels like the world has changed so much since we were younger. I’ve been thinking about writing a book about my experiences as a teacher, and how the education system is changing. It’s such a complex topic, but I think it’s important to share the real story.      That sounds amazing. Maybe you could also include how people use social media in their personal lives, like how I’ve found a whole community of single parents who are going through similar things. It’s been a huge support.      I’d love to hear more about that. I’ve been trying to incorporate more yoga into my routine as well. It’s been a great way to unwind and stay grounded. I’ve even started reading some books on mindfulness.      That’s so good to hear. Yoga has changed my life in so many ways. I think it’s one of the few things that can really help you feel present, especially when life feels like it’s pulling you in a million directions.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about education. It’s such a big part of people’s lives, isn’t it? Especially for someone like me, teaching language is all about how people learn and how their background affects that.      I couldn’t agree more. I spent most of my life in education, teaching history. Though I’ve been retired now for a few years. It’s funny, isn’t it? You think you know someone’s story just by their job, but once you get to know them, there’s always more to it.      That’s true. I’ve always found people fascinating, especially how they approach learning. I remember when I was teaching in Hitchin, there was this one student who had a really strong accent but was brilliant at picking up languages. It was like he had this raw talent that just needed a little guidance.      That’s the thing about teaching, isn’t it? You get to see so many different ways people learn. I always thought that being a teacher was more about patience than knowledge. You’ve got to be able to explain things in a way that anyone can understand, no matter their background.      Exactly. I often tell my students that understanding where they’re coming from is just as important as the grammar and vocabulary. It builds trust and makes the learning process smoother.      I remember when I was teaching, I had one student who was always talking about crime in Birmingham. He used to say the city was full of stories, but he wasn’t exaggerating. I think he was just trying to impress us with the tales he’d heard growing up.      That sounds like a great story. You should tell it sometime. I bet it’s got more than just local gossip. I’ve heard about some fascinating things happening in Birmingham over the years.      I’ll have to. But I think you’d enjoy it. You’ve always had a good ear for people’s stories.      I think I would. I love hearing how people’s lives intersect with the places they come from. It’s like a puzzle – each piece telling a part of the bigger picture.      To the stories we’ve shared, and the ones we still have yet to tell.      To the stories, and to the conversations that keep us connected. I think that’s one of the best things about being a teacher – you never run out of material.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever miss proper food back home? I mean, I’ve been eating takeaway every night since I moved to Cambridge. It’s all right, but it’s not the same as my mum’s Sunday roast.      I know what you mean. I’ve got this craving for my nan’s homemade pie and mash. It’s not that I can’t get decent food here—Cambridge has some amazing places—but it’s just not the same. You can’t beat the smell of a proper roast in your own kitchen.      Yeah, I get it. I’m from Kent, so we’re used to that kind of food. But I’ve been trying to cook more since I moved here. I reckon I’ve got the skills now. If I can just get my hands on some decent vegetables and a proper roast joint, I could be cooking like a chef.      Sounds like you’re on the right track. I mean, I’m a consultant engineer—so I do a lot of reading, not cooking—but I’ve been experimenting with some recipes. I made this carbonara last week that was pretty decent. It wasn’t perfect, but it was better than the takeout I used to eat.      Really? How’d you manage that? I don’t even know how to boil an egg without burning it.      Let me guess—you’re the type of person who insists on using the same pan for everything, right? I’ve got a whole set of cookware now. It’s all part of the upgrade from being a graduate civil engineer to a proper chef.      I’m not sure I’m ready for that level of commitment. I mean, I’m a graduate civil engineer too, but I’m more of a “get it done and move on” type. I prefer to cook something simple and not worry about it.      That’s the key, really. Cooking doesn’t have to be complicated. Just find what works for you and stick with it. I’ve been listening to some folk music lately too—like that guy from the North East, he’s got this raw, honest sound. It’s different from the pop stuff I used to like.      Yeah, I’ve heard of that. I’ve been into more indie stuff lately. I’ve been trying to find new bands to listen to.

So, I just got back from this weekend trip to the Lake District. It was absolutely beautiful, but honestly, I was so tired from all the hiking. I don’t know how people do it. I mean, I’m an engineer, not a fitness expert. But I swear, I ran up that mountain and I felt like I was going to die.      You were in the Lake District? I’ve always wanted to go. I think I might be doing a solo trip there next summer. I’ve been trying to get my fitness up, too. I’ve started going to the gym more often. It’s not like I’m some kind of athlete, but I feel like it’s helping with my stress levels.      That’s great! I actually got into the gym last month, too. I was so out of shape and I felt like I couldn’t even run for more than a minute without stopping. But now, I’m getting stronger. I’m even starting to like it. It’s weird, but I found some great music to listen to while I work out. I’ve been playing some indie rock, and it actually helps me focus.      Oh, that’s cool. I actually got into music production a while back, and I tried making some beats for the gym. It’s kind of a weird hobby, but I love it. I just started a new project, and I’m trying to get more people to listen to it. I might even take it to a music festival next year.      That sounds awesome. I’ve never really thought about music production, but I do like to DJ at my local bar sometimes. It’s not too serious, but it’s fun. I think I’d like to try making some beats myself. But honestly, I don’t have the time with work and everything else.      I get that. I’ve got my own job as a teacher, and I’m always trying to balance work and personal life. But I think it’s important to have something you really love. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about traveling more. I’ve been planning a trip to Spain for next year. I’ve never been there, and I’ve heard it’s amazing.      That’s a great idea. I’ve been thinking about traveling more too, but I’m not sure where.

Can you believe it? That goal they scored in the 85th minute—what a game! I’ve never seen a more dramatic finish. I swear, if I’d been there, I’d have been jumping up and down like a maniac.      Yeah, I remember when we were kids and we used to pretend we were all footballers on a rainy afternoon. I think I scored a goal too—against a cardboard box. You were the goalkeeper, weren’t you?      Oh, I was the goalkeeper all right. You remember how I used to shout "Save it, save it!" and then just let it in? It was a disaster. But hey, at least we had fun. I think I still have the matchday programme from that day.      Yeah, and you still wear that hoodie with the team logo. I remember you bought it in Sunderland at the market. I always thought you were going to start a team of your own. That would’ve been something.      Please, I’m a Research Manager now. I’ve moved on. Although, I did go to a couple of football matches last year. It was just… a bit too much for me. I mean, the chants, the crowds—exhausting. But I do miss the thrill of the game.      You just need to get back into it. Maybe you could start a local team? It would be good to see you out and about, not just stuck in an office all day. I mean, you  are  a PhD student now, right? Not that I’m not proud of you—but come on, you’re missing out.      I’m not missing out, I’m just… taking it slow. I’m trying to balance work and life. Plus, I’ve been watching more films lately. I think I’ve got a new favorite. I watched  The Grand Budapest Hotel  the other day, and I was completely hooked.      Oh, that one’s a classic. I love it. The set design, the colours, the way the story unfolds—it’s so unique. But I think you’re going to love  The Favourite  next. It’s brutal, but it’s amazing.      I’ve heard it’s really good. I’ve been meaning to watch it. I’m just trying to catch up on some older films too. I’ve been thinking about Easter this year. You know, like the old days, when we would go to the countryside, have a bonfire, and eat chocolate eggs.

You know, I still can’t get over how much they’ve grown since the last time we saw them. They were so tiny back then, just squirming around in that stroller.      Yeah, it’s wild how fast time flies. I remember the day they took their first steps. My brother was so proud, he even took a photo of them both walking side by side.      That’s one of the best photos in the book. I can still hear him shouting, “Come on, little ones, you can do it!” I swear, the sound of his voice still echoes in my head.      Oh, I remember that too. I was in the kitchen, and I heard him shouting from the living room, and I thought he’d lost his mind. But no, he was just trying to capture the moment.      He’s always had a knack for capturing things. He even ran the London Marathon a few years back, didn’t he? I remember seeing the photo of him with his number pinned on his shirt, running through the streets of London.      Yeah, and he did it with a smile on his face the whole way. I remember the weather was terrible, like pouring rain, and he still kept going.      I think he did it for the kids. He said it was for the memory, so the grandkids could see what their dad was capable of. It was pretty inspiring.      I think that’s what makes him so special. He always puts his family first. Speaking of which, I still can’t believe he took the whole family to Iceland last summer. I mean, how does someone plan a trip like that with a toddler?      Oh, he was a different man then. I think he even got a few photos of the Northern Lights. He said it was the best trip they’d ever taken.      Yeah, and he took us all to a cinema too. I think it was that gothic horror film. I was so scared, I almost ran out, but he kept me in there until the end.      You were so scared, you even cried when the monster came out. I remember that. And then, of course, we went to a fun fair. He bought you all cotton candy and stuffed animals. I think he even got a stuffed bear for the baby.      Yeah, and the baby still has it.

So, I've been thinking about the old days, you know? When we used to play with those wooden toys and tin soldiers out in the garden. I still remember the smell of the grass and the feel of the wooden blocks in my hands. It's funny how such simple things can bring back so many memories.      Oh, I remember those days too! My mum used to make us a big lunch every Sunday, and we’d have this big wooden table where we’d all sit and play. I think it was called the “family table,” or something like that. We used to play with those little wooden trains and build little villages. I can still see the toy train track running across the floor.      Oh, I remember those! We had a tiny toy train, and I used to love pushing it around and pretending it was going to somewhere far away. I think it was called the “Blue Bullet,” or something like that. My dad used to make me a cup of tea and sit with me while I played. He said it was the best way to start the day.      That’s sweet. I always thought that was a really special time. It’s funny how, even as adults, we still find joy in those simple things. Speaking of which, I’ve been thinking about food a lot lately. I tried making that really old recipe my mum used to make—something with fried onions and beans. It was a bit of a hit at our last family gathering.      Oh, I’ve been trying to get back into cooking too. I’ve been experimenting with some old recipes my gran used to make. I recently tried making a sort of lasagna, but it ended up being more like a stew. I think the problem was that I didn’t have the exact right ingredients. I need to be more like you and just go with what I have.      Well, you can always borrow my recipes. I’ve got them all neatly written down. Although I have to say, some of them are a bit obscure. Like that “casserole with a twist” that’s supposed to be from the 1960s. I’ve tried it once, and it was  very  strange.      I go for the classics. Nothing too fancy. I think the key is to cook with love, not with perfection.

Alright, I’ve had a right old day today. You know, the weather’s been so miserable, I couldn’t even get out of the house. Stuck inside, watching the rain drum on the windows like it’s trying to get in. Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve been in the same boat, more or less. Sat here, watching the sky turn grey and the wind howl like a dog. I swear, it’s like the world’s holding its breath. I reckon it’s the same old thing, isn’t it? Rainy days, cold winds, and you just can’t do much about it. I was thinking the other day, how used I’ve become to sitting around like this. Used to be, I’d go out, walk the dogs, do a bit of gardening — now, it’s all just… silence. It’s sad, isn’t it? I feel the same way. I used to have that full-time job as a childminder, you know, running the place, chatting with the kids, getting up early, then getting home late. Now, it’s just me, the cat, and the occasional visit from the postman. Aye, and the postman’s been a regular. I’ve got that full letterbox, you know. Letters from the council, bills, and occasionally, some nice letters from old friends. It’s funny, being old — you think you’ve forgotten people, but they still remember you. That’s the thing about being old, isn’t it? You think you’re forgotten, but the world hasn’t forgotten you. Though I suppose it’s not always nice. You get all those letters that just say, “We would like to offer you a service,” or something like that. Aye, and they all seem to think I’ve got a lot of money. They don’t know what I’ve got — a couple of pounds in the wallet, and a few goody bags from the council. Well, that’s the spirit. You know, sometimes I think we’d be better off just living in a hut in the woods and not having to deal with all this paperwork and all that nonsense. I think I’d like that. Just a hut, a little fire, and some good company. You know, like we’ve got now. Aye, and you’re the best company I’ve got. Though I reckon if you ever left, I’d still be here, waiting for you to come back.

Oh, I can’t believe how much has changed since we were last in London. It’s been ages, hasn’t it?      Yeah, it feels like forever. I remember when we used to meet at that little café on Oxford Street. Now I can’t even remember the name of the one we’re in now.      That’s because we’ve moved on from the days of coffee shops with Wi-Fi and actual coffee. These days, it’s all about the baristas and the Instagrammable pastries.      Oh, I still love the little things, like the way the barista made that one special latte for me last time. It’s like you’re part of the family.      Yeah, I suppose that’s the thing about being friends. You get to know the staff better than most people. I even got a free cup of tea from the barista last week just because I mentioned we were catching up.      Speaking of catching up, how’s work going? You’re a teacher now, right?      Yeah, I’m a primary school teacher. It’s so different from when I was a student. I love it, though. The kids are amazing. I mean, they’re not as cute as my golden retriever, but they’ve got that spark.      I can only imagine. I’m still teaching, but I’m with a secondary school. It’s a bit more stressful, but I still love it. We’ve got this new project where we’re trying to introduce more creativity into the curriculum.      That sounds interesting. I know that copywriting is all about creativity, so I can see how the two could overlap. I mean, if you’re trying to make a lesson engaging, it’s almost like it’s a form of storytelling.      Exactly. We had one kid who was obsessed with dinosaurs. I ended up turning the entire week into a dinosaur theme—lessons, art projects, even a little play. He was so into it.      I’d love to see that. I’m still trying to figure out how to make math fun, and I keep failing at it.      You know, I think it’s all about the approach. You don’t have to be a mathematician to make it fun. Maybe a little bit of magic? Or a game?      Or a pet. I mean, I don’t know about you guys, but I think pets are the real teachers.

You know, I’ve lived in Liverpool all my life, but I still find it fascinating how the city has changed. I mean, the old terraces are disappearing, and new developments are popping up everywhere. It’s like the place is constantly evolving.      Yeah, I agree. I’ve been here since I was a kid, and it feels like the rhythm of the city has changed. I used to love walking around the docks, but now it’s more of a tourist spot. Still, there’s something about the community here that never really fades, even with all the changes.      I couldn’t agree more. I moved here from Manchester a few years ago, and I still feel like a stranger sometimes. There’s a certain kind of warmth in the streets, though, you know? Like, people still wave at you and say hello, even if they don’t know you. It’s comforting in a way.      And the food! I mean, the best pizza in the whole country is right here in Liverpool. I used to go to that place on Bold Street all the time. You know, the one with the red and white sign? It’s like a ritual for me. My mum used to take me there when I was a kid – even though I didn’t like pizza then, I still remember the smell.      Bold Street? That’s the place. I used to go there with my mates when I was in uni. We’d grab a pint and talk about everything under the sun – politics, football, even what we were going to do with our lives. It’s funny how those little moments shape your memories.      I remember when the nightlife was so much better. People used to come from all over the country for the clubs. Now it feels like it’s more focused on the tourists. I still go to a few places, though. The ones that have that real Liverpool vibe – no loud music, just a few people enjoying a drink and chatting.      You know, I’ve been reading a lot lately. Mainly fiction, but I picked up a book about the history of Liverpool. It’s amazing how the city has been a melting pot for so many cultures. From the Irish, the Italians, the Germans, even the Africans who settled here in the 19th century. It’s like the city has always been a place of opportunity and struggle.

Well, I've been thinking about our trip to Nepal. I've always wanted to see the mountains and try some local food, but I’m not sure how to plan it properly. I mean, we’ve never gone abroad before, except for that holiday to Spain back in the 80s. It was a bit of a mess, honestly. We got lost in Seville and ended up in a completely different town.      Oh, I remember that! You were so upset, and I couldn’t understand a word the locals were saying. But it was funny in a way. Still, I think Nepal is a great idea. I’ve been meaning to go for years. I’ve actually got a few travel books that might help. Although I must say, I left my last job as a teacher to look after my kids, and I haven’t been abroad since 2008.      I still go to the village shop every week, though. The farmers there always bring in the freshest produce, even if it’s a bit pricey. I actually started going there when I was a school administrator—wanted to support local businesses. I remember once, the shopkeeper had this incredible gluten-free bread, and I tried it. It was so different from the stuff in the supermarket.      Oh, I’m gluten-free now, too. My doctor said I had an intolerance. It’s been a bit of a struggle, especially when my husband is cooking. He’s always trying to make something with flour and never checks the labels. I once had a big argument when he made a gluten-free cake, and it turned out he used normal flour. I still don’t forgive him.      I know what you mean. My daughter is also gluten-free, and I’ve had to be very careful with lunches. I actually coordinated a school display about food allergies once, and it was a bit of a nightmare. There were so many different dietary needs, and it was hard to make sure everything was safe. I think it’s a huge issue now, especially with the new free school meals system.      Yes, it’s changed a lot. I’ve also been thinking about the war-time food. My mother-in-law told me how she had to ration everything back in the 40s, and she had to travel from Siberia to Africa in a convoy.

So, I was just telling Anna about that time I got stuck in a lift at work last week. I had no idea how to get out, and it was like a horror movie! You know how it is, right?      Oh, I remember when I was at my old job, I was in a lift that suddenly stopped between floors. I was so scared I started shouting, but no one heard me. I thought I was going to die in there! What did you do?      That sounds terrifying. I once got stuck in a lift during a storm. The power went out, and the doors wouldn’t open. I was like, “This is not happening.” I ended up shouting for help for like ten minutes until someone came.      I think I was more nervous because I was alone. I kept thinking about all the things that could go wrong. Like, what if the lift fell? What if I couldn’t get out? It was so weird. I mean, I’m not scared of heights normally, but that moment—ah, it was awful.      You’re not the only one. I’ve heard stories from colleagues where they’ve had the same experience. I think it’s just one of those things that happens when you’re not paying attention. But really, it’s all just a bit of a shock when it happens.      Yeah, and it’s funny, because when you’re in that situation, everything seems so dramatic. You’re like, “What’s happening?” But once you get out, it’s just a silly memory. Still, I wouldn’t want to go through it again.      Definitely not. I’m starting to think that maybe I should get a lift card or something. Like, that little badge you can wear that says you’re not in a lift. But I don’t know if that actually works.      I heard about that. I think it was a joke, but maybe it’s real? I should look into it. I mean, if I end up being stuck again, I don’t want to be the one with the most dramatic reaction.      I think the key is to stay calm. If you go in there with panic, you’re more likely to make things worse. I remember in my story, I was just breathing deeply and trying to remember what to do. It helped.      That’s good advice.

So, I just got an email about the local library being up for demolition. They’re proposing to tear it down and build a car park instead. I’m so upset about it. I mean, where are we going to get a community space like that in this area?      I know, it’s ridiculous. I saw the council meeting notes. They’re saying the library is outdated and not used enough. But that’s not true. I’ve seen the numbers—they’ve had a steady number of users, especially for the kids’ programs and the workshops. It doesn’t make sense to axe something that serves the community.      Exactly! I’ve been volunteering there for the past two years, helping with the literacy program. It’s not just about books. It’s about the people. The kids come in, they get help with their homework, and then they have a chance to read, play, and socialize. It’s a safe place.      I agree completely. And I think the council is just being short-sighted. They don’t realize what they’re losing. I was going to suggest we start a petition, but I need your help with that. You’re the one who’s always on top of things like this.      I’m in. Let’s get together later and draft it. I can put my contacts in the local newspaper and maybe some of the community groups. It might take a while, but if we can gather enough signatures, we might be able to convince them to reconsider.      Sounds good. I’ll check with my colleagues at the office—maybe some of them have connections or can help spread the word. Also, I’ve heard that the council is planning to cut funding for other public services too. That’s another issue we could tie into our petition.      Oh, that’s even more worrying. The borough has been making decisions that don’t seem to benefit the people. I was thinking about the work shifts at the bookstore too. I’ve been working late shifts all week, and I’m exhausted. I can’t see how they’re managing with such poor planning.      I know what you mean. I tried to switch shifts last week, but there was no availability. I had to take on extra hours just to keep up with my workload. I think it’s a sign of the bigger issues facing the borough—budget cuts, poor management, and lack of support for staff.

Well, I've been thinking a lot lately, you know, about the village characters. You've got those who're always out and about, and others who've pretty much retired from the whole thing. Not sure if they're happier or not.      Yeah, there’s old Tom from the corner shop who’s always on his bike, even though he’s in his seventies. And then there’s Mrs. Harrow, who’s always complaining about the noise from the new takeaway. It’s like the village doesn’t run on the same clock as her.      Oh, I know her well. She’s always got her complaints about everything. My son used to take her for a walk every Sunday, but he moved to London and now she’s more alone than ever.      It’s sad, isn’t it? I remember when I was a lad, the village used to be full of life. Now it’s just bits and pieces. I was thinking the other day, maybe we should try and do something to bring people together. Like a village fair or something.      I’d love that. It’s been too long since we had any real community spirit. Though I do wonder—is there any point? With the way things are these days, people just don’t care about the village as much as they used to.      I think it’s more about loneliness. People don’t have the time, or the energy, to connect anymore. Also, with all the taxes and the politicians, they’re too busy worrying about that rather than their neighbors.      Exactly. I mean, voting—what’s the point? We’ve got the same politicians running things, and it’s all about the money. I just wish we could put the village first. But then again, what can we do? We’re all just sitting here, stuck in our own little worlds.      I suppose that’s the thing. We’re all long-term unemployed, and it’s hard to find purpose when you’re not working. But I try not to let it get me down. I still go out for walks, and I meet up with old friends.      You know, I’ve been thinking about joining the Jehovah’s Witnesses. It feels like a way to connect with others, to have a sense of structure and purpose. But I’m not sure if I’m ready for that.

I can’t believe it’s already been a month since we got the logs from the antique shop. I’ve been transcribing these files all week, and I still haven’t got through half of them.      That’s true, but I think it’s all worth it if it means we can finally get the log burners up and running. The heating’s been a bit of a problem since we moved in, and the new place is so drafty. I remember when we were in Tokyo, the winters were just as cold, but at least we had proper central heating.      Tokyo? Oh yes, you were there for that long trip! I still remember you coming home with a suitcase full of fudge and a very sad face because the cat had chewed through the label. But you did manage to find a great restaurant near the station. I bet it was better than the one next door?      That’s the one. The new restaurant across the road is a bit of a revelation—somebody finally took the risk and did something different. I only hope the budget doesn’t go through the roof. I’ve been trying to keep track of how much we’re spending on food and utilities. I think we might need to start outsourcing some of the work to India. It’s not like we have enough people here to handle everything.      I hear you. I’ve been thinking about that too. With the log burners and all the other maintenance, it’s getting a bit much. Still, I wouldn’t mind a bit of time off. I’ve been transcribing these logs all week, and I can feel my brain starting to short-circuit.      You should take a break. I’ve been meaning to ask—have you heard about the school academies? They’re making a lot of noise about them. I think it might have something to do with the new policies on education. I’m not sure how that’ll affect things, but it’s one of those topics that keeps coming up in meetings.      You know, I think the real issue is the budget. It’s not just about education or work—it’s about how we’re managing everything in our lives. I’ve been thinking about the cats and dogs we used to have. They made such a difference to the household.

You know, I've been thinkin’ about buyin’ a house again, but with the way things are now, it’s like tryin’ to catch smoke. The prices are up, and the taxes are higher than ever. I can’t even afford a deposit without sellin’ the place I’m in now.      Aye, I know what you mean. I’ve been watchin’ the market, and it’s a real nightmare. The council also started raisin’ the rates again. I reckon they’re gettin’ more money from the government, but it’s all passin’ on to us.      It’s not just the house, though. I’ve been tryin’ to get my pension increased for years. It feels like the government’s tryin’ to get us to retire early and just sit back and wait for death.      Exactly! And then there’s the politics. I don’t know what’s goin’ on, but it feels like every time we get a new party in power, things get worse. I remember when we had more stability.      I remember when people used to talk about real issues – like healthcare, education, and jobs. Now it’s all about privatization and cuttin’ back. It’s like the country’s run by a bunch of people who don’t even live here.      Aye, and the Sat Nav’s been a nightmare too. I had to drive out to a remote village the other day, and the thing told me to go down a dead-end road. I ended up walkin’ for half an hour to get back to the main road.      That’s not the worst. I once went to a farm in the countryside for a meeting, and the GPS said to go through a field. I ended up gettin’ stuck in a ditch for an hour. I had to call a rescue.      You know what’s funny? Even the TV’s not the same. I used to watch the news every night, but now it’s all about celebrities and reality shows. No one talks about real problems anymore.      I know, and the recycling thing? It’s like the council’s tryin’ to make us feel guilty. I’ve been sortin’ my rubbish for years, and I still get fined for not doin’ it right. I think it’s more about money than actually bein’ environmentally friendly.      I think we’re all just tired. We used to be able to rely on each other, but now it’s all about lookin’ out for ourselves.

Okay, I think I know what's wrong with this laptop. The fan's not working properly, and it's getting really hot. I've seen this before with some of the older models we've sold. I bet it's a warranty issue.      Yeah, that’s what I’ve been thinking too. Dad said he’d take it to the shop, but he’s been busy with rugby. We need to get it fixed before the weekend.      I know, I know. I’d help, but I’m still trying to get my head around how to use the laptop properly. I mean, I’ve used it for emails, but not much else.      It’s a basic model, so it shouldn’t be too hard. The warranty should cover the repair, right? I’ll check the terms again.      Wait, isn’t that the one I left in the car yesterday? Did you take it out?      No, I left it here. I thought it was safe, but maybe it got bumped or something.      Maybe he’s the one who knocked it over. He’s been playing with everything lately.      He’s a curious little one. Anyway, let’s not get too worked up. We’ll take it to the shop tomorrow.      Wait, what about the fajitas? I was going to make them for dinner tonight. I found some sauce in the pantry.      That’s a good idea. I’ll help you cook. I’ve been meaning to try a new recipe.      I can help too. I’ve got some extra ingredients in the fridge.      I just need to confirm if the rugby match is still on for tomorrow. I’ll text the team.      I think he’s ready for a nap. You know, he’s been sticky out of his ears all day.      He’s like a little version of you, Speaker_1. Always sticky, always curious.      Yeah, I guess I’m not too different. But at least I don’t have to worry about fixing laptops anymore.      Yeah, but you still have to worry about him.      Time for a nap, little man. Let’s get you out of those sticky ears.      So, we’re fixing the laptop, cooking fajitas, and then maybe swimming later?      Yeah, and if we’re lucky, we might even get a little time to relax.      Come on, let’s get you ready for a nap.      It’s going to be a good evening, I think.

So, I was just telling the kids about the Loch Ness monster, and they were all wide-eyed. I mean, it’s just a legend, right? But you know, it's fun to imagine what it might look like.      Yeah! I think it’s a big, green dragon that lives in the loch. I’ve seen pictures online—it looks like a big, scaly monster!      I think it’s a giant turtle. Wait, no, that’s the one from the sea. I think the Loch Ness monster is like a giant crocodile.      You know, they say it’s a monster, but I think it’s just a really big fish. Or maybe it’s a dinosaur!      Dinosaurs? But they’re all extinct!      Well, maybe it’s a time traveler! It could be from the past, you know. Or maybe it’s just a big, misunderstood creature that’s been living there for centuries.      Or maybe it’s a giant human who just likes to live in the loch.      That’s a possibility. Or maybe it’s not even a creature at all—maybe it’s just a trick of the light and the water.      I think it's real. I saw it once in a dream.      Me too. I dreamt it was wearing party clothes and doing handstands in the water.      Handstands? That’s a funny image. I mean, if it’s a monster, doing handstands is kind of… dramatic.      Yeah! And it’s got a really fancy hat.      You know, I was just talking about making a fairy garden. Maybe we could invite the Loch Ness monster over for tea.      Yeah! We could put out some pizza for it. I love pizza.      I think it would like pizza. I like pizza.      You’re both right. Pizza is one of the best foods ever. I mean, it’s like a blank canvas for any kind of topping.      Can we make a fairy garden with pizza?      Maybe. But first, let’s make sure the Loch Ness monster doesn’t eat the pizza.      We’ll put it in a little box.      And maybe put some basic addition problems on the box.      Oh, that’s a good idea. Maybe the monster will solve them and then befriend us.      I think it’s already our friend.      Yeah, I think it’s real.      Well, I think we’re going to have to start a party. A monster party.

So, I tried to order a  pomfrit  here, but the waiter said it's not on the menu. I thought it was a local specialty or something. What's even a  pomfrit ? I mean, it sounds like a French word for something else, right?      Oh, it's actually a Croatian dish—it’s like a type of potato pancake. But I don’t think they serve it here. They’re more into seafood and fresh vegetables. I asked for a  pašticada  instead, which is a local beef dish, and it was delicious. You should try it.      My teacher said we should learn about local food in our geography class. He showed us pictures of  štruklji  and  friči —which are like dumplings. Wait, does that even count as food technology? I mean, I thought food tech was about robots in kitchens or something.      Food technology is more about how we grow, prepare, and store food. But I think your teacher is mixing it up with food studies. Anyway, let’s talk about the weather—it’s been so hot lately. I didn’t think Croatia would be this warm in August. I thought it would be more like the UK, but no, this is like a summer camp.      Yeah, the heat’s been brutal. I almost skipped flying over here. I had to deal with the airport staff, and I got stuck in a long line because of immigration checks. It was ridiculous. I thought I’d be in a nice, cool place, and I ended up sweating like a pig the whole time.      I know, right? I’ve never felt so uncool in my life. My sister texted me and said, “You look like you’ve been on fire.” I almost replied, “I have been on fire!” But I didn’t. I’m too polite for that.      Wait, are we going to visit more countries? I’ve been thinking about going to Iceland for a trip. I’ve heard it’s so cold and beautiful. But I need to save up for flights. Plus, I think I might have a tic when I’m there. I’ve been twitching my left eye all day. It’s so annoying.      A tic? Is that new? You’ve been okay all week. Maybe it’s the heat. I’ve heard that heat can cause all sorts of things. Are you feeling okay?      I think it’s just stress.

Well, I’ve had enough of that debt collector this week. They came round like it was the Queen’s visit. I told them I’m retired, not a bank clerk, and I’ve got more cash in the garden than in the bank account.      Oh dear, I know the feeling. I had one last week too. They said I owed money from a PPI policy I never knew I had. I don’t even remember signing up for that. It’s all so confusing.      PPI? That was a nightmare for a lot of people. I remember when I was working, we had to sign up for it as part of the mortgage. It was a bit of a scam really. It’s amazing how many people got stuck with that.      It was a complete farce. I still remember when the government had to pay out billions. It was one of those things that went wrong because of poor regulation.      Yeah, and I heard that some people even got compensation for it, but it took ages. I’d rather have kept the money.      It’s not just PPI though. These days, it seems like every time you open your eyes, there’s some kind of debt or financial problem. I think it’s all because of the economy.      It’s true. You know what I found interesting though? I read an article in the magazine about how people are using TV to escape from the real world. It’s like we’re all hiding in our living rooms.      Exactly. I still watch a bit of telly, but most of the time I’m on my computer. I’ve been learning to use it properly. It’s not as hard as you think once you get the hang of it.      I tried, but I’m just not into that. I prefer the old ways. I still remember when the TV was a big box with a knob. You had to change the channel manually. Now it’s all digital and you can’t even find the right channel.      I still do that. My grandchild taught me how to use the remote, but I still end up watching the wrong channel. I think I’m going to give up and just watch the telly that’s on the floor.      You know, I heard about a party coming up in the village. It’s supposed to be a big one.

Good evening, Jean. How was your day at the court? I heard you had a busy session today.      Oh, it was quite a day, Alice. I had to deal with a few cases that were more complicated than usual. I had to sit through a couple of long hearings. It’s not the most exciting work, but it keeps me on my toes.      I can imagine. I always find it fascinating to hear about the cases people bring up. I’ve been teaching English for years, and I still find the way people express themselves in court quite interesting.      That’s true. I’ve noticed that people often say things in court that they wouldn’t say in everyday life. My job requires me to be very attentive to detail. It’s a bit like being a detective, although I don’t get paid as well as I’d like.      I can only imagine. You must be very focused. I’m a bit jealous, though. I’ve always wanted to work in a field where I can make a real difference, but I ended up in education.      I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about whether I should take on more training to move into a better position. But with my age and the kind of work I do, it’s not easy. Plus, I have a family to support.      That’s understandable. I’ve been thinking about climate change quite a bit lately. It’s been on my mind because I’ve been reading a lot about it. Do you think the justice system is doing enough to address environmental issues?      I think there’s more awareness now, but I don’t know if it’s enough. The courts are dealing with so many other issues. I’m not sure how much they can focus on climate change. It’s a global problem, and it requires a lot more than just legal action.      Definitely. I think it’s about changing people’s habits and making the right policies. But I do believe the legal system has a role to play. I hope we’ll see more cases being brought forward in the future.      I hope so too. It’s hard to believe that we’re still dealing with these issues, especially with the technology we have now. I guess that’s why I always say that change takes time.

I think I’ve been feeling really happy lately, haven’t I? It’s been a good few weeks, you know. I’ve had a lot of time to read and just relax. Not too much work, and the children are behaving well. It’s nice.      Yeah, I’m happy too. I like when we all sit together like this. It makes me feel safe. And I think I saw a butterfly outside today. It was so pretty!      I saw a butterfly too! It was flying around the garden. I tried to catch it, but it was too fast. It was a yellow one, like the one on my shirt.      That’s a good one, love. You know, I was thinking the other day – do you think having lots of money makes people happy?      I think it might make people happy, but I don’t know. I mean, if you had a lot of money, you could buy lots of toys. But I think happiness is more about being with people.      Yeah, like when we’re all together. I think being with my family makes me happier than having money. I don’t know what money is, but I think it’s like the thing you use to buy things. Like the coins in the jar.      That’s right, love. Money is what you use to buy things. But I think the more money you have, the more things you can buy. But I don’t think it’s the most important thing. I think happiness is more about feeling safe and being with your family.      But if we had lots of money, we could go on holidays. I’d like to go to the seaside. I heard that there are big waves and surfboards there.      I could ride a surfboard! I could do it like a superhero. I’d be the best surfer in the world.      You’d be a great surfer, I’m sure. But let’s not get too carried away. Let’s just enjoy the moment. I think being with you both makes me feel very happy.      I think you’re the best person in the world. You make me feel safe and happy.      I love you, Mummy. I love you so much.      I love you too, sweeties. And I love being with you both. That’s what makes me happy.      I’m getting tired. Maybe we should go to bed.

So, I was just thinking about what we're going to do after we finish exams. I've been thinking about careers and stuff. Maybe I want to do something with technology? Like, invent something?      Yeah, I heard about this guy who invented a new kind of solar panel that’s way more efficient. He actually got a patent for it. It’s pretty cool. I wonder if that’s something you could do too, like invent something and get a patent.      That would be amazing. But how do you even start? Is it hard to get a patent? I mean, I’ve heard about patents, but I don’t really know much about the process.      From what I remember, you need to come up with something original and useful. Then you go through a process with the patent office, and they check if it’s new and hasn’t been done before. It can be really complicated, but if you’re really into something, it might be worth it.      Yeah, but what kind of inventions are actually useful? I mean, like, I know people have made inventions for things like medical devices or environmentally friendly tech. What about something like AI or robotics?      Definitely! AI is huge right now. I was reading about how companies in China are using AI in everything from transportation to healthcare. It’s really growing there. I mean, not just in terms of tech, but also in the economy and investment.      That's interesting. I guess China is also investing a lot in renewable energy and tech. I remember hearing that they’re leading the way in electric cars and batteries. But is that just because they have a lot of money, or is it because they’re smart about it?      I think it’s a mix of both. They have a lot of capital and government support, but they’re also investing in the right places. For example, they’re not just making cars—they’re building entire ecosystems around them. You know, like charging stations, apps, and infrastructure.      That makes sense. It’s not just about making products, but also about creating a network around them. So, maybe the future is about more than just inventing things—it's about building systems that support those inventions.      Exactly! And I think that’s why investors are looking at China more closely now. They’re not just big on manufacturing; they’re also big on innovation and sustainability.

So, I just got the confirmation for our ski passes. They’re all booked for the whole week, which is fantastic. I thought we’d be stuck with just the basics, but it turns out the hotel has a partnership with the local ski resort. That’s a real bonus.      Oh, that’s great! I was just about to ask about that. I thought maybe we’d have to sort it out ourselves. But I’m glad you got it sorted. So, are we going to start skiing tomorrow or wait a day?      Well, the weather report says it’s going to be a bit chilly today, but mostly clear. I think we’ll start tomorrow morning, just to warm up and get the feel of it. I’ve already packed my gear, and I brought a couple of extra layers in case it gets too cold.      That makes sense. I’ve been looking forward to this trip for ages, and I want to make sure I’m ready. By the way, did you check if the lift passes are included in our room rate?      Let me check my phone… Yes, they are. I think it’s all included as part of the package. The hotel even mentioned that they have a free shuttle service to the slopes in the mornings. So we’ll be set.      Perfect. I was worried about trying to figure out the logistics on my own. It’s so much easier having everything arranged already. I’m just hoping the snow isn’t too bad. I heard it’s been a bit of a dry spell lately.      Yeah, the ski resort said the conditions are good, but they’re expecting a fresh snowfall later this week. So we might get to enjoy some real skiing. I’m really looking forward to it. And I’ve already booked some lessons for tomorrow afternoon. I think I’ll start with the basics to make sure I don’t crash into anything.      That sounds like a solid plan. I’ve never really skied before, so I’m a bit nervous, but I’m ready to give it a try. Maybe I’ll even take a lesson with you? I could use the company.      Absolutely, that’s a great idea. We can learn together and support each other. And if I make a complete mess of it, you can laugh at me and then help me up.

Well, I just wanted to say, I think I’ve figured out a way to prevent those strings from breaking when we’re repairing the badminton rackets. It’s not perfect, but it might work.      Oh, really? I was getting worried that the problem would keep coming up again and again. What’s your idea?      Well, I read something about using a combination of elastic bands and cable ties. I mean, I know cable ties are a bit of a pain to remove, but they hold things in place much better than just relying on the string.      That’s interesting. I’ve used cable ties before, but I never thought of using them in conjunction with elastic bands. What about materials? I mean, are there any specific types of string or cable you recommend?      I think the string should be a bit thicker, like the ones you use for plant supports—those are more durable. And for the cable ties, maybe the ones with the oversized plastic parts, so they don’t slip out too easily. Also, I noticed that positioning the strings closer to the grip area might help with the tension.      That makes sense. I wonder how much that would cost in total—materials, time, and labor. You know, if we were to market this as a product, people might be interested.      Yeah, I was thinking about that too. Maybe we could call it ‘Racket Reinforcement Kit’ or something like that. And we could even include a guide on how to use it properly. I mean, if we’re talking about marketing it, maybe even pitching it on Dragons’ Den?      Haha, I’d love to see that! Although I’m not sure how well it’d go over. But seriously, this could be a great idea. I mean, it’s a niche market, but the demand for racket repairs is steady.      Exactly. And I think it could be a good way to pass the time while we’re both unemployed. I mean, I’ve been reading about how people are starting small businesses from home, especially with the current situation.      That’s true. And it’s not like we’re doing anything else. I mean, we’ve got the time on our hands, and this could be a way to make some money. Plus, I’ve got this new idea for a haircut I’ve been wanting to try.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot about art lately. It’s got me reminiscing about the days when I used to go to the art galleries in Norwich. I remember that one painting with the green hills and the blue sky—it looked so peaceful.      I remember that one too. It was the one that made me feel like I was standing right there in the countryside. I used to take my kids there when they were little. They always got so excited about the colours and the shapes.      That reminds me of the time I visited the Tate Modern in London. It was the first time I saw a large-scale abstract piece. It was so intense, you know? It made me feel like I was part of the artwork itself.      I agree. There’s something about abstract art that doesn’t just sit there—it moves you. I think that’s why I started taking photography classes. It’s like capturing the essence of a moment in a way that words can’t.      You’ve always been the artistic one, haven’t you, Steve? I mean, even when we were at university, you were always sketching in your notebook.      I didn’t think it was that obvious. I just like to see the world through different lenses. Maybe that’s what I’m doing now with my lectures—bringing art into the classroom in a way that makes it accessible.      You know, I’d love to go back to the galleries more often. I used to do that when I was a childminder. I always thought that the kids would benefit from seeing different forms of art. It helped them think more creatively.      That makes sense. Art has a way of sparking imagination. I’ve found that when I teach, encouraging students to express themselves through art helps them engage with the subject more deeply.      I suppose I never really had that chance. I was more of a practical person, you know. But I do miss the feeling of creating something—whether it’s a painting or just a cup of tea.      And that’s what makes art so important. It connects people, even in the most unexpected ways. A cup of tea, a painting, a child’s drawing—they all have their own kind of beauty.      I think that’s what I’ve come to appreciate more as I’ve grown older.

So, I just wanted to say, I am  so  over the whole “girls are always so hard to please” thing. I mean, I’m not saying I don’t have my moments, but I swear, every time I go out, it’s like everyone’s got a different opinion on how I should act, what I should wear, or what I should say. It’s exhausting.      I  know , I know! I had this one guy last week who said I was “too direct” because I told him I was tired of his constant texting during our date. And he was like, “You should be more gentle with your words.” I was like, “Are you serious? You’re the one who texted me 37 times in one hour. I tried to be considerate!”      Oh my god, I feel that. I had this friend who was dating this guy, and he would always say things like, “You need to be more confident” or “You need to be more outgoing.” But then he was the one who wouldn’t even look me in the eye when we were talking. I mean, what even is that?      It’s so frustrating, isn’t it? Like, are we supposed to be perfect in every way just to be liked? I think it’s just a load of nonsense. I mean, sure, we should be ourselves, but not to the point where people are judging us for it.      Exactly. And I just don’t get why people always seem to think that the problem is  us , not them. Like, if you’re a guy and you want a girl to be more approachable, you can just make an effort, you know?      Oh, come on, I get it. I’ve been there. I know that sometimes you’re just trying to be a good partner, but the truth is, if you don’t respect someone’s personality, it doesn’t matter how much effort you put in. You’re just not compatible.      Right. I think the real issue is that people are too focused on how they’re perceived rather than how they  are . But hey, I’m not going to start a debate about that now. I’m too tired. I’ve been procrastinating on cleaning my room all week, and now I have to do it before my parents come over for dinner.      Ugh, me too. I have that big pile of dirty laundry in the corner that I’ve been avoiding for weeks.

You know, I’ve been thinking a lot lately about how different people approach problems. Like, some people just go with what they know, even if it’s not the smartest thing. I mean, I’ve seen it in work—some colleagues who think they’re being clever just because they use jargon, but they’re actually just repeating what they heard somewhere.      Yeah, I’ve seen that too. And it’s not just in work. I remember one time when my aunt was trying to fix her computer, and she kept saying things like, “I think it’s a  software issue ," as if that’s a real thing. It wasn’t a software issue, it was a virus. She got so frustrated because she thought she was being technical.      I think it’s funny, but also kind of sad. Like, if you’re not educated enough to understand something basic, you just assume it’s a more complicated problem. It’s like, you don’t have the tools to solve it, so you just throw bigger words around.      Exactly. And I think that’s where a lot of the misunderstanding comes from—between people, between cultures, even between men and women. Like, when people talk about feminism, they sometimes think it’s about women being angry and demanding, but it’s really about equality and respect. It’s not just about what you  think  it is, it’s about what it  actually is .      I get that. I think part of the problem is that people don’t take the time to listen or understand. It’s like, if you don’t have the intelligence or the knowledge, you just dismiss it. I mean, I know I can be guilty of that too. Sometimes I think I know something because I read it somewhere, and it turns out I didn’t understand it at all.      That’s the thing, isn’t it? I remember when I first started working as an IT consultant. I thought I knew everything about computers because I could use them, but then I realized how little I actually knew. It’s like, you think you’re smart because you do something, but there’s always more to learn.      Yeah, and that goes for everything. I think some people think they’re smart because they have a degree, but it’s not about the degree—it’s about what you do with it.

So, we’re off to the farm today? I can’t wait to see the animals. I’ve been meaning to take the kids somewhere peaceful for a bit. The past few weeks have been so hectic with school drop-offs and the like.      Yeah, it sounds like a nice change of pace. I’ve been really looking forward to it. I think the kids might be excited too. They’ve been talking about cows and sheep all week.      Me too! I want to ride a horse! I saw a picture of one in the magazine. I think it’s called a pony, right?      That’s a good question, love. I think it’s called a pony if it’s smaller, but horses can be bigger. Either way, you’ll get to see them at the farm. Now, I just need to make sure we bring some snacks for the trip. The kids usually get hungry so quickly.      Good idea. I’ll bring some sandwiches and maybe some fruit. I think we should also check if there are any educational activities at the farm. It might be a good way to make the trip more fun and learning-focused.      Can we see baby animals too? I think there was a baby cow in the photo.      I’m sure we’ll see plenty of baby animals. Farms are full of life, especially in the spring. But just a heads-up—don’t get too close to the ones that are still young. They can be a bit skittish.      I know, but I’m sure the farm staff will keep an eye on things. Speaking of which, are we going to be late for the school drop-off? I don’t want to make the kids wait.      No, we’ve got time. The farm is just a short drive from here. I’ll make sure we stick to the schedule. Oh, and I’ve been thinking about the DVDs we watched last night. I thought the kids might be a bit tired after school, so maybe we can play a movie tonight to wind down.      What movie? I liked the one about the dragons. It was really cool.      I know, I think we can watch that one again. It’s always a hit with the kids. But I’ll also bring some snacks for after the movie—maybe some popcorn and juice. It’s going to be a nice, relaxing evening.

You know, I’ve been thinking about starting to knit again. It’s been a while since I last picked up needles, but I’ve been meaning to get back into it. I remember my grandmother used to knit all the time—she made the most beautiful scarves and mittens.      That’s nice. I’ve actually been trying to learn how to knit myself. I got a book from the library, but honestly, I’m still struggling with the basic stitches. It’s not like the Olympics, where you just need to keep up with the pace. Knitting is more about patience, right?      Oh, you’re telling me. I remember my first attempt—it looked more like a tangled mess than a scarf. But I kept at it and eventually got the hang of it. It’s actually quite meditative, isn’t it? You get lost in the rhythm of the stitches.      Yeah, I agree. I think that’s why I like it so much—there’s something calming about it. I’ve also been thinking about how much I miss the arts in general. I mean, with everything that’s going on in the world, it’s easy to forget how important creativity is. Especially for people like us, who are in academia or research.      Definitely. It’s easy to get lost in the grind of work, especially with a postgrad degree and all the deadlines. But I think things like knitting or even just reading a good book can help reset your mind. Speaking of which, I’ve been meaning to catch up on some art. I’ve been meaning to visit the Tate Modern again—maybe this weekend?      That sounds like a good idea. I love the Tate. I remember seeing a really incredible exhibition last year with some modern sculptures. It was so different from anything I’d seen before. I think that’s the beauty of art—it challenges you to see things in a new way.      Exactly. And I’ve been thinking about the Olympics recently too. Watching the athletes push their limits is inspiring. I mean, they have to be so disciplined, so focused. It’s not just about winning—it’s about personal achievement.      And that’s what I love about it. You don’t have to be a professional to appreciate the spirit of the Olympics. Even just watching the opening ceremony with all the flags and the music—it’s a celebration of humanity.

So, I was just thinking, do you remember the last time we went to that 3D cinema in London? That one with the dinosaurs? I swear, the seats were so uncomfortable, I nearly fell asleep mid-film.      Oh yeah, I remember that! I mean, the movie was fine, but the 3D glasses were like a piece of plastic with a hole in the middle. I kept looking at the screen like, “Is this worth it?” And then we had to queue for ages just to get in, and the queue was outside the cinema, not even inside. I mean, what’s the point?      My point exactly! I’ve been meaning to visit the Imperial War Museum again, but I keep putting it off. I was thinking maybe we could go this week? It’s been a while since we last went, and I’ve been curious about their new exhibit on the Cold War.      Oh, I’d love that. I actually heard they’ve got some really cool interactive displays—like, you can try out different kinds of weapons or something. But I’ve been meaning to go for ages too. I just haven’t had the time. And then there’s the public transport thing – buses are a nightmare these days, and the tube is always packed like sardines.      I know, I know. I’ve been trying to convince myself that the tube is just part of the city’s charm, but honestly, it’s not. I was in the Underground this morning and saw a group of people crowded in one carriage, and one of them was holding a baby. It was like a horror movie! I mean, how do people even survive that?      I know, it’s crazy. Maybe we should take the bus instead for the museum. I mean, if we’re going to London, we could take the bus to the museum and then walk the rest of the way. It’s not that far, and it gives you time to take in the sights along the way.      That’s an interesting idea. Though I do miss the convenience of the Tube sometimes. I mean, it’s not just about the cost or the crowdedness—it’s about the comfort. I remember when I was a student, I used to take the train all the time. It was faster, and the seats were nicer.      Yeah, I used to work in London, so I had to travel a lot.

So, I was just thinking about Christmas. I mean, it’s a bit of a blur since we’re all over the world, but I’ve been trying to make it feel a bit like home. I’ve got a tree up, and I’ve even managed to find some proper decorations. It’s not the same as having family around, but it’s a start.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to replicate that too. I’ve got a few mates coming over for dinner—actually, we’re thinking of doing a proper Christmas dinner. Just the four of us. You know, like we used to do back in Manchester. I’ve even got the turkey in the fridge. It’s like forcing the turkey to be festive, you know?      That’s the spirit! You know, I was just thinking about the old days. Remember that one time we tried to cook Christmas dinner when we were in university? I mean, we ended up burning the turkey and the potatoes turned to charcoal. We ate it anyway, though. Said it was “authentic.”      Oh yes! That was a classic. I remember you tried to make a Christmas cake and it ended up being more like a cake of regret. But we laughed about it for weeks. I think that’s what makes Christmas special—those shared memories, even the bad ones.      Exactly. It’s not just about the food or the presents. It’s about the people. I’ve been thinking about someone I haven’t seen in a while. You know, that old mate from university. He’s in London now, and he’s been meaning to get in touch. Maybe we could plan a Christmas dinner together? I mean, if he’s not too busy.      That sounds brilliant. I’ve been trying to get in touch with some old friends too. You know, the ones who have drifted apart. It’s funny how time flies. I was just watching a movie the other day— The Favourite —and it made me think about how people change. You know, some of my old friends are still around, but others... well, they’ve moved on.      Yeah, it’s weird how life changes. I’ve been meaning to catch up with some of my old mates from the postgrad days. We used to have those long nights in the library, arguing about philosophy and politics.

Alright, I think I’ve had enough of this internet nonsense for one night. I got another terrible review on Twitter about my café. It’s not even true, honestly. Some total stranger said the coffee was “bitter as a week-old cup of tea,” and it was just a regular customer who didn’t like the way the beans were roasted.      Oh, I’ve seen that one too. I’ve had a few people write things about my bakery that are just…  out of context . Like that one guy who said the pastries “taste like cardboard.” He even took a photo of the cake with a weird angle, and now people think it’s a disaster.      Yeah, I know the feeling. You know, I actually used to work in a restaurant in Margate, and I’ve seen how bad reviews can really kill a place. I mean, one negative review can throw off the whole vibe. I remember one time, a customer came in and was just  super  rude, and then left a one-star review about the “poor service,” not even realizing the waiter was new and didn’t know the menu.      That’s the worst. You can’t even defend yourself without sounding like you’re blaming the customer. And then there’s the whole issue of anonymous reviews. You never know who’s writing them. I got one once from someone who said they “couldn’t get a full English breakfast,” but they ordered a toast and a cup of tea. It was so confusing.      I had someone write that my croissants “had a weird texture” and “were like eating a rock.” She even included a photo of the croissant with a crack in it. I think she was just trying to be dramatic. I mean, I’ve had a few baked goods go wrong, but that one was just a total fluke.      I once had a customer who complained about the “lack of design” in my café. I mean, the place is a little run-down, but it’s supposed to be cozy. She said the furniture looked like it was “from the 80s.” I didn’t even know there was a design trend for that.      You know what’s funny? The worst part is that people don’t even know what they’re talking about. I mean, I’m a student, right? I don’t even know what I’m doing with my life half the time.

So, Oisin, what did you do today? I saw you came in like you'd been chased by a giant dog.      I didn’t do anything, Mum. I just rode my bike to the park and then came home. I saw some birds with eggs in the bushes.      Yeah, I saw that too. I think they were robins. I’ve never seen bird eggs up close before. They were so small and yellow. I almost tried to pick one up, but I remembered what the teacher said about not disturbing wildlife.      That’s wise, lad. You’ve got the instincts of a naturalist already. Though I’d be careful about picking up eggs – they’re not for eating, and you don’t want to scare the parent birds off.      I agree. I’ve taken care of a few gerbils before, and they’re very sensitive to sudden movements. I once had a friend who tried to give one a raspberry and it nearly ran away. You have to be gentle with animals, whether they’re in the wild or in a cage.      Wait, you said raspberry? Is that like the fruit or the animal?      Oh, don’t be silly. Raspberry is a fruit, love. The animal is a gerbil. Though, I must say, I’ve also seen some people try to feed birds chocolate ice cream. It’s not good for them, though. They can get sick from the sugar.      I heard that from my geography teacher. She said the birds can’t digest it properly. And I’ve seen some kids at the park trying to give them treats. It’s kind of funny, but I think they’re being irresponsible.      I remember when I was a kid, I used to think it was fun to feed the squirrels. I’d give them bits of chocolate and then they’d come running out of the trees. But my dad always told me to be careful, because squirrels can be territorial, and they might get aggressive if you mess with their food.      That’s right. I once had a squirrel that came up to my garden and barked at me. It was like it was saying, “Don’t mess with me, or I’ll mess with you!” I’m not sure if it was a real threat or just a playful bark, but I learned my lesson.      That sounds kind of dramatic, but I can see how that could happen.

I was just thinking, I need to go food shopping today. I’ve got a couple of meals planned for the weekend, and I’m running low on essentials.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve been meaning to do that too, but I’ve been so busy with the cleaning rounds. I’ve got a backlog of jobs, and I’ve been working extra hours just to make ends meet.      Well, you know what I say—don’t let the cleaning get the best of you. You’ve got to look after yourself too. I still remember when I was your age, I used to push myself too hard. Just like I did with my own kids.      I know, I know. But between work and helping out with my niece and her family, I’m stretched thin. I’ve been thinking about arranging a meal out with my sister. She’s been meaning to see me, and I think it’d be nice to catch up properly.      That sounds lovely. I might have to join you, though. I’ve been meaning to get out more. Between work and watching over my mum, I’ve been pretty much stuck at home.      Oh, don’t worry, dear. You’ll get your time. You’ve always been the one who steps up when it matters. I remember when you used to help me with my eyebrows. I had no idea how to shape them, and you were so patient.      That was a  long  time ago. I think I still have the clip I used back then. I still remember how I had to borrow a mirror from your neighbour to get the right angle.      That’s for sure. I still get asked if I do my own eyebrows. I told them I did, but it was all a lie. I just used a pencil and hoped for the best.      You were the one with the mismatched eyebrows, weren’t you?      Oh, go on, I’ll tell you. It was a complete disaster. I even had to go to the hairdresser’s to get it fixed. And he told me I should be careful with the eyebrow pencil.      You know, I’ve been meaning to get a haircut too. I’ve had the same cut for years, and I think I need something a bit fresher. I’ve been thinking of trying a new style, but I’m not sure what to go for.

Oh, I can’t believe how fast the baby’s growing. It feels like just yesterday she was barely out of the hospital.      Yeah, time does fly. I’ve been thinking about how much I’ve changed since then—well, not physically, but emotionally. It’s been such an incredible journey.      I know, it’s amazing how fast things change. I remember when you first told me you were pregnant. I couldn’t believe it. You were so surprised yourself, weren’t you?      Oh, I was. I still get caught off guard sometimes, especially when she starts doing things that surprise me. Like yesterday, she suddenly started cooing when I put her on the swing. I almost cried.      That’s so sweet. You’ve always been such a gentle person, and it shows with her. I can see how she’s already forming such a bond with you.      Thank you. It means a lot coming from you. I feel like I’ve found my place in life with her. But honestly, it’s also been exhausting.      Of course it has. But it’s all worth it.
