Oh, I know that one. My team had the same issue. Still, it’s amazing how quickly these kids pick up things. I bet you’re getting a lot of help from them.      You could say that. I’m actually thinking about getting some new furniture for the house. The renovation is starting to take shape, and I’d like to make it feel more like a home. Maybe even add a little kitchen bar.

So, I just got this really cute pair of vintage jeans from that little thrift store in Chester. The fit is perfect, and they're so unique. I think I’m going to wear them to the yoga class this weekend. You know how I love the way they feel when I’m moving.      That sounds great! I’ve been meaning to find some vintage pieces too. I actually found this adorable floral dress last week in a charity shop in Camden. I got it for like ten pounds. It’s not the most flattering fit, but it’s so colorful. I’m thinking of wearing it to a picnic with my sister next weekend. Do you want to come?      Oh, that sounds lovely! I’d love to. I’m actually going to try to make a vegan quiche this week for the picnic. It’s a bit of a challenge, but I’m thinking of using some nutritional yeast and a mix of veggies—like spinach, bell peppers, and mushrooms. I’ll need to check the recipe again to make sure I have the right proportions.      That sounds like a great idea! I’ve been meaning to try more vegan cooking too. My friend introduced me to this new plant-based smoothie powder that’s supposed to be really nutritious. I’ve been mixing it with almond milk and some frozen berries. It’s a bit pricey, but I think it’s worth it. Maybe I’ll bring some of that to the picnic?      That sounds delicious. I’d love to try it. I’ve been thinking about traveling more lately. I’m really inspired by that travel magazine I read last week—there was a feature on hiking in the Scottish Highlands. I’ve always wanted to go there, but I’ve been putting it off because of work. Have you thought about any places you’d like to visit?      Honestly, I’ve been thinking about a trip to Cornwall for a while. The beaches are amazing, and there’s so much to do. I even have this idea for a blog post about the best places to stay there. I’m considering writing about it for the magazine I work for. I just need to figure out the logistics.      That sounds amazing. I love the idea of writing about travel. I’ve actually been thinking about starting a small blog about language learning and travel, too.

So, I just got back from my evening class, and I was thinking about how it’s been such a long week. I’m exhausted, but I’m also really looking forward to getting home and seeing you.      Yeah, I can imagine. It’s been one of those weeks where you just want to collapse on the couch and not move for a day. But honestly, I’ve been thinking about how much I miss our usual Friday night routine. We always end up talking for hours, even if it’s just about the most mundane things.      Right, remember when we used to joke about how we could talk about anything—no topic was off-limits. Even things like toe nails. I still remember that one time when we were at the café and you started telling me about how you had this fungus on your big toe, and I couldn’t help but laugh. It was so absurd.      Oh, that was  the  night! You were in your element, I remember. I think you even started comparing it to some kind of social experiment. Or was that just me? Either way, it was one of those conversations that I can still visualize even now. We were so into it.      It was funny, though. We always thought that being lecturers made us too pretentious to talk about such trivial things. But it turns out, we’re just like everyone else. We still have toe nails, we still get bored, and we still talk about our friends.      Exactly. And I’ve been thinking about a few of them lately. I was talking to Sarah the other day, and she mentioned that she’s been trying to get back into the habit of hanging out with people more. She said she’s been so focused on her work that she’s almost forgotten how to be social.      That’s worrying. I mean, we all have busy lives, but it’s important to keep that balance. I remember when we were younger, we used to say that our friends were the reason we kept going. Even if we were stressed or overwhelmed, being with them would always remind us of why we started doing this in the first place.      Yeah, I couldn’t agree more. I think that’s why I started thinking about how much I miss our little group chats. It’s not just about the conversations—we’re not just friends, we’re like a support system.

So, I heard you mentioned you're going to be in Birmingham for the weekend. How’s work been lately? I know you've been juggling a lot with the company.      It's been pretty intense. We’re launching a new project, and it's been like a whirlwind. But I'm getting used to the pace. It's all good, honestly. I’m just glad I don’t have to do all the work myself anymore.      That’s great to hear. You always had a knack for managing people. I remember when we were at university, you were the one organizing the study groups and even helping out with the student radio. How's the radio still going? I miss that.      Oh, it's still going, though it's not the same as it used to be. We’ve had some changes in leadership. It's a bit harder to get the same level of support now. But I still go in once in a while. It’s a small part of me that still loves it.      I can imagine. I was thinking about the old days, like when we would sneak into the studio after classes. Remember that time we got caught by the security guard? It was so funny.      Oh yes! I still remember that. You were so brazen, trying to act like you were just stopping by for a coffee. I still laugh about it every time I think about it.      There’s something about that time in our lives—so full of energy, so full of possibilities. I wonder what we’d do if we had that same energy now. Maybe we’d still be in education, or maybe we’d be doing something else entirely.      I dunno. I think I’d be doing what I’m doing now. I love the challenge, and it keeps me on my toes. But I do miss the simplicity of being in education. Teaching language is such a rewarding job, even if the hours can be long.      I completely agree. You always had a passion for helping people grow. I remember how you used to always encourage me to speak up in class, even when I was too shy. You were a good teacher, even before you were a director.      Aw, you flatter me. But I think you were just in the right place at the right time. You had the talent, and I was just the one to bring it out.

You know, Dad, I’ve always thought that Jamaica Inn would be such a cool place to visit. I mean, the book is so mysterious, and I've heard the movie's pretty scary too. Do you remember when we tried to read it together when I was eight?      Oh, I remember that well. You were so scared of the ending, you wouldn’t even let me finish reading it! I had to promise you it wasn’t real, and you’d be safe at home. Still, it's a great story, don’t you think? It’s like a mix of fairy tales and mystery.      Yeah, it is. I also like how the book talks about the colours of the road. I think it’s more than just the landscape—it's almost like the road itself has a personality. You know, like in  The Wizard of Oz , when the road leads you somewhere special.      Absolutely. And I love how  The Wizard of Oz  showed that even the most ordinary things, like a ruby slippers or a green screen, can lead to something amazing. I remember telling you about the time I read  Sherlock Holmes  when I was a kid and thought I could solve every mystery in the world.      You were so into it! I still remember you pretending to be Holmes, solving a mystery in our kitchen with a magnifying glass and a tape recorder. You were pretty convincing, even if the 'crime' was just knocking over a bowl of cereal.      Oh, yes! And I still have the original  Alice in Wonderland  book from when I was a boy. It’s about time I passed it on to you. You know, it's funny—Lewis Carroll wrote all those fairy tales, and yet he was barely a grown-up. I wonder what he was thinking when he wrote them.      I bet he was thinking about the world he knew as a child. You know, I've been thinking about Morse code lately. I saw a sign on the road that had something to do with a telegraph. Do you think people still use that?      Not as much as before, but it's still used in some places. I remember when I worked in customer services, there was a time we had to deal with a flood of telegrams. People used to send messages through the telegraph instead of phones or emails.

So, I was just thinking about that time I tried to cheat at Monopoly. I got so obsessed with getting that property development, I actually  tried  to build a hotel on a street that wasn’t even owned by me. My mum walked in and said, “You’re not playing Monopoly, you’re playing Russian Roulette.”      I remember that. You were always trying to outsmart the game, weren’t you? It was like you were trying to run the whole thing from the start. Didn’t even want to buy the properties properly — just wanted to skip straight to the big houses.      Yeah, like that one time when you tried to buy the entire board with just one roll of the dice. I still remember your face when you rolled a three and screamed, “I’m gonna win this!”      Oh, I was so sure. I’d even started planning my own little empire in my head. I was going to open a theme park called “Monopolyland” and charge people to play.      You were serious about that, weren’t you? I remember you even tried to sketch a blueprint of it during the dinner break.      Yeah, and I was going to have a roller coaster that would take you from the start to the end in one ride. It was madness.      You were a bit of a dreamer, weren’t you? But hey, that’s what makes life interesting. I mean, I remember when we were kids, we used to play games like that all the time.      I guess you’re right. It’s funny how those little things stick with you. Maybe I should start a blog about my Monopoly adventures.      You’d be the first person to read it. I’d probably be the only one who’d take it seriously.      Well, I think I’ve got a better idea. Why don’t we all set up a board game night? We can all try to cheat at the same time.      That sounds like a plan! I could even bring in some vintage board games from my parents’ attic.      I’ll bring the snacks. I’m not letting you win without a proper snack break.      I’ll bring the drinks. And maybe some stories about my childhood. You all know I have a lot of them.      Alright, let’s plan it. I’ll start by checking out the local store for the games.

Hey Mum, how’s everything going? I’ve just arrived and I’m starved. I think I’ll grab a bite with you before we start sorting through the moving box.      Oh, you’re just in time! I’ve made a roast dinner—just a few minutes away. You’ll be glad to know the roast was marinated overnight and it smells wonderful.      That sounds amazing. I’ve been surviving on takeaway and cereal since I left London. I think it’s time to get back to proper food.      Well, you’ll have to get used to it. I’ve been cooking for you since you were a child. I even made that weird turkey dish you loved when you were seven. Remember?      Oh, I remember! It tasted like a mix between a chicken and a shoe. But I loved it.      You were so excited about it. Anyway, I’ve also been sorting out the list for the new house. I thought we could go through it together. I’ve got the moving box open and everything is laid out.      That’s perfect. I’ve been trying to make a list, but it’s been a little chaotic. I’ve got so much stuff to move, and I’m still figuring out what’s important.      I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about what I might need for the new place too. I think we should also talk about the furniture. I’ve noticed you’ve been spending a lot of time with your friends from university and I want to make sure you have a place to relax.      Yeah, I’ve been trying to figure out what to do with my old stuff. Maybe I could sell some of it or give it to friends.      That’s a good idea. I was thinking about how much time you’ve been spending with your friends. It’s been a while since you’ve talked about your wedding plans. You’re getting married soon, right?      Yeah, next spring. I think it’s going to be a big event. We’re trying to plan a nice venue and make sure everything is set.      That’s great! I think you’re going to have a beautiful wedding. I can’t wait to see it.      I can’t wait either. Although, I’ve been having so much jet lag from my trips to Europe.

So, I was just thinking about that plant we bought last week. You know, the one that’s supposed to thrive in low light? It’s still alive, but it looks like a sad little thing. I feel like it’s judging me.      I know, right? I thought it was going to die the first week. I’ve never been great with plants. I mean, I can keep a cactus alive, but anything more complex? It’s like trying to do a PhD in botany without the proper equipment.      You’re telling me! I’ve got a plant that’s been in my office for three years and it’s basically a walking shrub. I swear it’s starting to develop its own opinion on the state of the world.      It must be. I’ve been trying to get it to bloom, but I think it’s just waiting for me to start a proper garden. You know, with soil, sunlight, and maybe even a few hours of silence.      I think it’s been waiting for the NHS to reform. It’s seen more change than I have. I mean, the NHS is such a big part of our lives – especially with the new A-Level reforms and the petrol crisis making things even more complicated.      Yeah, I can’t shake the feeling that the government’s trying to make everything more expensive and harder to navigate. Like, why are they changing the A-Levels now? It’s not like it’s a secret. It’s like they’re trying to make us all feel unprepared for the future.      And then there’s the petrol crisis. It’s not just about the price anymore. It’s about how it affects everything – transport, travel, even the way we live our lives. I can’t even afford to go on holiday anymore. I feel like I’m stuck in a system that’s designed to make us all feel inadequate.      It’s insane. I keep thinking about the people who have to work 60-hour weeks just to afford basic things. I mean, I’m a PhD student on a stipend, and I’m still struggling. I don’t know how people manage to keep up with everything.      It’s exhausting, isn’t it? But I think we’re both just trying to keep going, one day at a time. Maybe that’s all we can do.

So, I heard you all were talking about the Black Death the other day? I mean, what are we even doing talking about that? We’re all stuck in our flats, trying not to get infected by the new virus. That’s like, way more relevant.      Yeah, I told you, it’s like history repeating itself. Though honestly, I think the only thing worse than the Black Death would be social media. You know, how we all know someone who’s been infected or something, but no one’s actually died yet. It’s like watching a horror film but without the actual death.      I can’t even look at my phone without thinking about how people used to die from the plague. I mean, they had no idea what was causing it. I think it was like a medieval version of a pandemic, and they had no idea it was a bacterium. It’s so strange.      Yeah, but at least now we can do Zoom calls and stay safe. I mean, it’s not like we can just go out and get infected like back then.      Tell me about it. I tried going to the pub last week, got one cup of tea and then had to isolate for three days. My flatmate’s been in a state. I’m telling you, if this gets worse, I’m going to start smoking again. It’s the only thing that can make me feel like I’m not in a bubble.      You don’t say. I mean, it’s not like you’ve had a proper cigarette in months. I’ve been trying to quit for the last year, and now you’re saying you’re going back to it? That’s not helping.      I don’t know. I’ve been thinking about university lately. I mean, I’m supposed to be starting in September, but I’m not sure if I’m ready. I’ve been living at home all this time, and I’m just not sure if I can handle the pressure of living on my own.      I get that. I’ve been thinking about the same thing. Work-wise, it’s not like there are real jobs out there. Everyone’s either working from home or not working at all. I mean, your dad’s a teacher, right? I heard he’s been doing online lessons for months now.

So, I just wanted to say, I think I’ve reached a point where I don’t want to see some of my friends anymore. It’s not that I don’t like them, it’s just that I feel like we’re not on the same wavelength anymore. It’s like we’re all moving in different directions and I just... I don’t know. I feel like I’m losing myself in all the trying to keep up.      That sounds really heavy, honestly. I mean, I get it. Friends can change, and sometimes the friendship just… doesn’t feel the same. But how do you even start phasing out someone without hurting their feelings? I mean, you don’t want to come off as rude or like you don’t care anymore, right?      Exactly! I’m terrified of that. It’s like, I don’t want to be the one who just disappears, you know? But I also don’t want to keep pretending that everything’s fine. It’s so complicated. I mean, we used to have these deep conversations about life, work, everything. Now it’s just… small talk and random texts that never get answered.      I’ve been there too. I think it’s just a natural part of life, you know? People grow, places change, and relationships evolve. Sometimes they just fade out, and that’s okay. But the trick is how you handle it. You don’t want to burn bridges, but you also don’t want to keep clinging to something that’s not working.      Yeah, I guess that’s the thing. You have to be honest with yourself first. You can’t be honest with someone else if you’re not honest with yourself. I’ve been thinking about it a lot on this journey. It’s like this whole coast trip is a metaphor for life—you know, heading somewhere new, and sometimes you just have to let go of the people who don’t fit anymore.      That’s a really poetic way to put it. I think I’ve been trying to do that with some people too. I don’t know if it’s the same for me, but I’ve been more selective lately. I’ve started to value quality over quantity. I’d rather have a few amazing friends who truly understand me than a whole group that’s just… there.

So, I’ve been meaning to ask you, how did you end up moving to the UK? I mean, I know your family is from Austria, but I’d love to hear more about your background.      Oh, it’s a long story, but let me start from the beginning. I was born in Vienna, in what was then Austria-Hungary. My parents were both musicians—my father played the violin, and my mother sang in opera. Growing up, art was always a part of our lives. But when the war came, things changed. We had to flee, and we ended up in Italy. It was a difficult time, but we made do.      That must have been tough. I can only imagine what it was like to leave everything behind.      It was, but I think that’s where my love for art truly began. When we arrived in Italy, we found a small community of exiles—people from all over Europe. We shared stories, music, and art. I remember one time, I painted a small portrait of my mother, and it made me realize how powerful art could be—it could preserve memory and emotion in a way nothing else could.      That’s beautiful. I’ve always thought art was a way to connect with something bigger than ourselves. You know, I studied art history at university. It’s kind of funny, because I always thought I’d end up working in a gallery, but I ended up studying it more from a theoretical angle.      I bet you’ve got a different perspective now. I always admired how students are so passionate about the subject. I had a few students once who were just like you—full of ideas but not sure where they wanted to go.      Yeah, I guess we’re all just figuring it out as we go. But I think I might be going to an exhibition in London next month. It’s a new one at the National Gallery. I’d love to take you.      That sounds lovely. I’d love to see it. I’ve been meaning to go back to the National Gallery more often. I think I’ve been too busy with my own work lately.      Well, we’ll have to plan it. Maybe we can even bring some of your old paintings with us?      Oh, you know I’d love that. It would be a perfect way to spend an afternoon.

So, I just thought of something. You know, before we go to the gym today, we should grab a proper meal. I’m not sure how much more energy I’ve got left.      Yeah, I feel the same. I mean, it’s been like three hours since we had breakfast, and I’m already thinking about the gym. But I reckon we should stop somewhere near the next town. I remember there’s a café that’s supposed to be pretty good.      That sounds like a plan. Although, I wonder how long we’ll be stuck in traffic. I don’t like driving without a clear idea of when I’ll get where I’m going. Time is such a strange thing, isn’t it? You think you’ve got enough of it, and then suddenly it’s gone.      Time has definitely been playing tricks on me lately. I feel like I’ve been on this road trip for ages, but it’s only been three days. It’s weird how quickly things can pass when you’re driving.      It’s funny, isn’t it? We’re both English, but I feel like we’re not really from the same place. You’re from the North, I’m from the South. We speak the same language, but somehow, there’s this unspoken difference. I almost feel like we’re from different countries.      I know what you mean. I’ve always found that there’s this kind of regional divide in England. I mean, I grew up in Bury, and I’ve never been to Cambridge. But you know, I think it’s more about the way people speak and the way they carry themselves.      Yeah, and I think there’s also the whole gender thing. I mean, I’ve always found that there are certain expectations around what women should do, even in the workplace. I teach part-time, and I’ve noticed that even though I’m qualified, people sometimes question me more than they do a man.      That’s so unfair. I’ve experienced that too. Like, when I was doing my postgrad, I was told I wasn’t “serious enough” because I was a woman. It’s something I’ve had to deal with all my life.      It’s exhausting, isn’t it? I mean, I’m not even working anymore, but I still feel like I have to prove myself.

Well, I've been thinking about those hand-thrown mugs I bought at the local festival last week. You remember the one with the blue glaze and the little daisy on it? It's just perfect for morning coffee, don’t you think?      Oh, I remember that one very well. I reckon it's the daisy that's the real charm. You know, I still have this old mug from when I was a teacher. It’s got a crack in the handle, but it's been through so much. I used to keep it on my desk, just like a little trophy.      You always did like your mugs, didn’t you? I remember the time you tried to throw one across the room to catch a fly. It broke in half, and you had to clean up the mess for hours. Still, it was funny.      Oh, you wouldn’t believe the stories we could tell about that old kitchen. And I still remember that time the power cut left us all in the dark. We had to use the candles and the old radio. It was like living in the 1950s.      Yes, and remember that time you got a spider in your tea? You were so upset, you nearly threw the whole thing out. I still don’t know what happened to that spider. I hope it found its way out of the window.      Oh, I had a bit of a scare with that. I spent the whole evening being very careful with my tea. And I’ve never been the same about spiders since. I even started putting out the little traps you bought from the shop.      I think you’re more scared of them than they are of you. But I must say, your garden has improved so much. The birds have been coming in more often. You’ve even got the little blackbirds nesting in the bushes.      That’s because I’ve been planting more flowers and keeping the weeds down. I took your advice about the compost heap, and it’s made a world of difference. I go out there every day, even if it’s just for a bit.      You know, I’ve been thinking about the local festival again. The one with the live music and the fair. It’s been a while since we went to that. I feel like I missed out on something.

So, we’re going away for the holiday? That’s so exciting! I’ve been planning this for ages. I’m really looking forward to it.      Yes, we’re going to Cornwall. I’ve been meaning to go there for a while now. I think it’s going to be a nice change of scenery. It’s been a bit dusty here in Hastings lately, and I’ve been craving some fresh air and waves.      Cornwall, eh? That’s a lovely place. I remember when I used to go there in the summer when I was younger. It’s like a different world out there. The beaches, the cliffs, the people… it’s got a real charm.      I love the beaches. I’ve always wanted to go to the seaside. I can’t wait to swim in the sea and maybe even take some pictures. Do you think we’ll get to go to any of the famous places like Land’s End or St Michael’s Mount?      I think we’ll try to make time for some of the famous spots. I’ve heard St Michael’s Mount is amazing. I also think we should check out some of the local festivals. They’ve got some great music and food. I might even take a little souvenir or two.      Festivals are always a good way to meet people and experience the local culture. I used to go to music festivals in the summer when I was younger. It’s always a good time. You know, music and friends—nothing beats that.      I can’t wait to meet up with some of my friends there. I’ve been planning to invite a few of them, but I’m not sure yet. I think I’ll ask them the week before we leave. It’s hard to know for sure.      That sounds like a good idea. Maybe we can have a little get-together before we go. It will be fun to catch up and plan some activities. I’d love to hear what they think about the trip.      Yeah, it’s good to have friends around. I think we should all take some time to relax and enjoy the break. It’s easy to get caught up in the daily grind, so it’s important to step back and really take in the moment.      I couldn’t agree more. It’s been a long year, and I really need a break.

Hey, did you see that movie we watched last night?  10 Things I Hate About You ? I mean, I thought it was okay, but honestly, I was kind of annoyed by the whole Shakespeare reference thing. Like, sure, it’s a modern take, but it felt a bit forced.      I totally agree with you! I mean, it’s not like Shakespeare is  that  hard to understand, but they made it this big deal. And then there’s the whole, like, "Shakespeare’s a romantic" thing. It’s so cheesy, but I guess it’s what made the movie popular.      Yeah, but the dialogue was still so corny. I mean, you know, I liked the chemistry between the two leads, but the rest of the movie felt like it was trying too hard to be dramatic.      Honestly, I think it was just a way to market the movie. They had to make it sound more serious, like it was a real drama or something. But the whole thing was basically just a love story with over-the-top acting.      I mean, maybe that’s why it still works. It’s not too serious, but it’s not too silly either. I guess it’s got that classic teen movie vibe.      Yeah, I guess. But I was more annoyed by the school part. Like, the whole scene with the principal and the strict rules. It felt so unrealistic. I mean, in real life, schools don’t even have that kind of drama.      Right? I mean, I can’t even imagine having a principal like that. My school’s pretty laid-back, honestly. We have a principal who’s more interested in sports than rules.      That’s cool. I wish my school was like that. Mine is super strict. My teacher even said we need to start planning for the future trip to London. I’m so excited about it!      Yeah, London is amazing! I’ve always wanted to visit the Tower of London and the British Museum. But wait, do you think we’ll actually get to do it?      I hope so. My teacher said the trip is still in the planning stages, but if we get enough responses, we might go. It would be so cool to see all the places we’ve studied about in class.      I can’t wait. I’ve been dying to see the Houses of Parliament and maybe even a football match.

You know, I was just looking at Facebook this morning. It's like a time machine, really. You see these old photos of us from when we were kids, and it brings back so many memories. I remember when we used to play in the fields near Costessey. That was before the council built that new housing estate.      Oh yes, I still remember that. We used to run barefoot through the grass, and Mrs. Pritchard would yell at us for getting muddy. Didn’t stop us, though. She’d always say, “You’ll get chicken pox one day, you little rascals.”      Oh, I got chicken pox when I was about eight. It was the worst. I remember lying in bed for weeks, just itching all over. My mum used to put something on me—like a sort of ointment she made herself. I don’t know what it was, but it didn’t help much.      I got it when I was a child too. My mum said it was a blessing in disguise because it made me immune to everything else. Although, I can’t say I appreciated it at the time. I had to miss a whole term of school. I was so pale, and my hair was all matted.      Yeah, I got it when I was about seven. I remember being so sleepy all the time. I used to fall asleep in class, and the teacher would get so frustrated. But hey, at least I didn’t have to worry about socializing with other kids, right? Not that I was ever really into that.      Not really. I think you had to be the most awkward kid in the class. You’d sit in the corner, reading a book or something. No one wanted to sit near you. Though, honestly, I think it was just the way you were.      We were all such strange kids. You know, I also always thought religion was a bit of a joke. My father took us to church every Sunday, but I never really understood the point. It was more about the hymns and the nice smell of the candles.      I was always curious about religion. I used to ask my parents all these questions. Why do we believe in God? Why do we pray? I think I got more answers from the books on the shelf than from them.      Yeah, my mum used to say, “Don’t question too much, love.

So, I was just telling my daughter about the time I tried to teach my cat to fetch the newspaper. It ended up knocking it off the table and into the tea. That was a  real  disaster. You remember that, don’t you, Steve?      Oh, I remember that very well. I was sitting there with a cup of tea myself, and I swear I could hear the cat saying, “What’s wrong with you, Mavis?” You were so proud of yourself, thinking you were training a supercat or something.      Yeah, and then you tried to post the newspaper to the postman with the cat on your shoulder. It looked like you were trying to deliver a message from the sea.      Exactly! I said, “The cat’s got the map, and the cat’s got the breakfast, and the cat’s got the paper.” Haha! It was a  true  British moment.      I think that’s the kind of thing that defines the old days, doesn’t it? I mean, we all had those moments where we tried to be clever with the animals, and they just thought we were mad. I remember trying to teach my dog to do tricks with a tennis ball. He just ended up chewing it and running off with it.      Yeah, I remember that. We used to do those kind of things all the time. It was part of growing up in a small village. You had to be creative with what you had.      Exactly. I still remember the time when my nan tried to teach me how to knit. She said it was “a skill that would take you places.” I ended up making a scarf that looked like a scarf made by a blindfolded elephant. It was the most ridiculous thing I’ve ever seen.      That’s the kind of thing that gives you stories to tell. I still have a little scar on my arm from my first attempt at using a chainsaw. I thought it was a hobby, not a weapon.      I remember that too. You ended up cutting the tree in half instead of just trimming it. It was a real wake-up call. You started off with a chainsaw and ended up with an outdoor sculpture.      It was all in the name of progress, wasn’t it? We were all trying to make the most of what we had. I think that’s part of what makes us so close.

Hey man, how's it going? You've been busy with that restaurant gig, right? I heard you're working on a new project with the kitchen team.      Yeah, things are going alright, thanks. I’ve been pretty swamped with the opening of the new menu, but it’s been rewarding. How about you? Still crushing it with your studies?      Yeah, I’ve been keeping up with the modules, but honestly, I’m feeling a bit stuck. I’ve got this huge project due in a couple of weeks and I’m not even halfway through.      That sounds rough. You ever think about taking a break? Maybe hit up a gig or something? You know how much you love music. It might clear your head.      Honestly, I’ve been thinking about that. I’ve been listening to a lot of new bands lately. There’s this group called  The Midnight Echoes —they’re doing some cool fusion of indie and jazz. Their latest album is really good. I’ve been playing it on repeat.      Oh, I’ve heard of them. They’ve got that sort of vibe. I’ve been trying to get into more live shows too. I’m actually going to a local gig this weekend. You should come. It’s this band from Brighton called  The Rhythm Refrain —they’ve got a killer drummer. I reckon they’re going to be huge.      That sounds awesome. I’d love to come. I’ve been meaning to check out more local scenes. I’ve been a bit out of the loop lately with all the studying.      Definitely come. It’s a good way to unwind and meet people. Speaking of which, did you hear about Alex? He’s doing an internship at that music magazine in London. He’s barely left the house since he started.      Yeah, I heard. He was always the one who was into music the most. I guess it’s a dream come true for him. I wonder if I’ll ever get that kind of opportunity.      You’ll get there. You've got the talent and the drive. Just keep pushing. And hey, you never know—maybe one day you’ll be the one organizing the gigs instead of just attending them.      Thanks, man. I appreciate that. I’ll be there this weekend. You know what? Maybe I’ll even bring my guitar. I’ve been writing some new tunes, and it’d be nice to play them in front of a crowd.

You know, I’ve been meaning to ask you, when are you planning to visit Durham again? It’s been a while since we last went on that little trip with the family.      Honestly, I’ve been meaning to go back, but my schedule’s been a bit all over the place. I’ve got all these exams coming up, and I’m still trying to figure out what I’m going to do after school. It’s a bit overwhelming, to be honest.      That’s understandable. I can’t imagine being in your position. I remember when I was your age, I’d rather have been out playing football than worrying about exams. Still, you’ve got to make the most of it.      Yeah, I know. But I’m trying to keep my head down. I’ve been thinking about this summer holiday, though. Maybe I’ll take the bus to Newcastle and then catch the train to Durham. I’ve been reading up on the rail routes.      Newcastle’s not too far from here. I’ve got a few friends who live there, and they always say it’s the best place to catch a good coffee. You should try the one near the castle. I’ve heard it’s really popular among students.      I might. I’ve been looking for a good spot to hang out with my mates. We’ve been talking about doing a domino drive or something like that. You know, those things where people drive through and get stuff. It’s kind of a fun way to meet people, or at least that’s how I see it.      I can see that. I remember when I was your age, I used to do those drive-throughs with the family. You’d be surprised how much you can get done in an hour. And honestly, they’re a great way to meet people from different places.      Yeah, and you can get some of the best deals if you take advantage of the loyalty promotions. I’ve been trying to save up for a new phone, so I’m always on the lookout for deals.      Just don’t get too distracted. I remember one time I got so caught up in the promotions, I ended up buying a bunch of things I didn’t really need. But hey, that’s part of the fun, isn’t it?

Hey, thanks for coming over. I’ve been dying to catch up. It’s been ages since we last saw each other.      No problem, I’ve been meaning to visit too. It’s great to be back in Sussex, even if it’s just for a few hours.      Yeah, I moved into this new flat just a few months ago. It’s a bit of a project, but I love the location. I mean, it’s only a short walk from the beach, and the view from the window is amazing.      That sounds perfect. I still haven’t managed to move out of my old place, but I’m hoping to get a place in the city soon. Just need to sort out the budget.      You should definitely do that. I know how expensive it is here, but if you’re in a higher professional occupation like you are, you should be able to afford it.      I know, but I keep thinking, “What if I get a flat in the city and then I need to move again?” It’s just this constant cycle of planning and hesitation.      I get that. So, I just got the confirmation that our trip to Lancaster is finally sorted. I can’t believe it—after all the back-and-forth about the train times and the accommodation, it’s all set! Yeah, I couldn’t agree more. I think it’s also about the friends you meet along the way. I mean, we’ve met some of the best people through music. So, I think I just made it through the first round of Pandemic without dying... or at least without losing all my cards.      You’re doing better than me. Alright, let’s make a pact and try not to kill each other. I think that’s the only way we’re going to win this game.

You know, I've been meaning to ask — when's everyone's birthday this year? I want to make sure we don't end up with a clash of celebrations.      My birthday is in July, Mummy. So, I’ve been thinking about moving again. You know how I’ve been working in engineering for the past few years, and it’s starting to feel like I’m stuck in a loop. So, I just got this really cute recipe for a chocolate avocado mousse from my sister-in-law. It’s got this amazing, creamy texture, and it’s actually really healthy. So, you two, I’ve been meaning to tell you about the trip I took with my brother last month. It was to the Lake District, you know, that place with all the beautiful lakes and mountains. I used to go hiking there when I was younger, but I’ve been too busy with work lately. I wish I could take some time off for a trip like that. You should go. It’s good for the mind and the soul. I’ve been retired for a while now, and I’ve actually started taking more trips to different parts of the country.

You know, I’ve been thinking about this new coffee machine we bought last week. I mean, it’s supposed to be the best, but I've had more burnt coffee than anything else. I’ve been in the army for years, and even that, you know, it’s not the same as starting over in a new country. But I reckon if it’s the right job, it’s worth it. Sometimes you have to leave one life behind to find another. I mean, I’m still at the same job, but I’m thinking about maybe getting some training to move up.      That’s a big step, but I can see where you’re coming from. I mean, I’ve been thinking about doing some courses to upgrade my qualifications.

You know, I've been thinking about how we all sound different, even though we're all from England. I mean, I’m from Gillingham, and I can tell when someone's from London just by the way they speak. How could I forget? We were both so determined to find our way, but we ended up relying on a friendly shopkeeper who spoke a little English. He even gave us a souvenir, a little keychain. I still have it.      I still have mine too. It’s funny how little things from those years stick with you. Speaking of which, you mentioned flying lessons the other day. Are you still working on that?      Yes, actually. I’ve got a few more lessons scheduled before my next test. It’s been a bit of a challenge, but it’s also been a lot of fun. I think I might head to New York for a visit later this year. I’ve always wanted to see that city.      That sounds amazing. I’ve been meaning to visit New York for years. I’ve heard it’s a city that never sleeps, and there’s something magical about it.      You should come. We could meet up, and I’ll show you around. It’s been a while since we’ve had a proper trip together.      I’d love that. I’ve been thinking about making a few changes in my routine too. Maybe I’ll take up some social media again, but only if it doesn’t take over my life.      I know what you mean. I’ve been trying to balance my online presence with real life. It’s tricky, but I think it’s important to stay connected without losing yourself.

Alright, I think I’ve got a few moves here. Let me see—what’s the highest-scoring word I can make with these tiles?      You’re always so focused on the game, aren’t you? But honestly, if you’re not careful, you’ll end up with the same score as me again. I’ve been trying to beat you for weeks now.      Oh, don’t be so dramatic, Dave. We all know you’re just holding back. If you really wanted to win, you’d have stopped playing chess with your brother last night and come here earlier.      Yeah, you know, I’ve been meaning to ask—how did you two end up playing Scrabble in the first place? I mean, the last time we all got together, we were arguing about whether breakfast is a meal or just a habit. You two were in the kitchen trying to decide the proper way to scramble eggs.      It was a combination of boredom, a lack of better ideas, and the fact that we all had different opinions on how to spell “supercalifragilisticexpialidocious.” I remember arguing for hours about whether it should be “supercalifragilisticexpialidocious” or “supercalifragilisticexpialidocious.”      Honestly, I just said “It’s spelled with an ‘o’ because it sounds better.” And then we all agreed. That’s how we ended up playing Scrabble. It was like a  Breaking Bad  moment, but with crossword tiles.      You mean like when Walter White decided to cook meth? Yeah, that was the exact same level of drama. Though, in my case, I had to put up with my sister’s obsession with grammar. She once tried to correct me on the spelling of “flour” and ended up spelling it “flour” with a ‘u’ at the end. I think she was trying to make it sound like a French word.      That’s amazing. I remember my best friend trying to go to university on a scholarship, and he kept getting rejected because he made spelling errors in his application. He was like, “Why can’t they just accept what I write?” It was like he was trying to prove that spell check was a crime.      True, but let’s not forget where we all started. We were all just kids, trying to work out what A Levels meant and whether we would ever get to university. I remember my friend trying to explain that “A Level” meant something, and I just thought it was an abbreviation for “Advanced Level of Stress.”

I've been thinking a lot lately, you know. I've had a few years now since I retired, and I feel like I've had time to reflect on things. I mean, I've always been a bit of a person who likes to look back, but lately, it's been like the memories just come flooding back all at once. I know what you mean. I've been feeling that too. I’ve been sitting by the fire, sipping my tea, and just watching the rain fall, and it's like the world has slowed down. You know, sometimes when you're not working, you start to notice things you never did before. Like the way the light changes in the room or how the birds sing at different times of the day. Yeah, it’s strange, isn't it? You used to be so busy with work, with kids, with everything, and now there's just this big, empty space in your head. I remember when I was in my early sixties, I used to say, “I’ll have time to do all this when I’m retired.” But I never really thought about what that meant. Now I’m here, and honestly, I don’t know what to do with myself half the time. I remember when I was younger, I used to think the same thing. “When I’m retired, I’ll travel, I’ll write, I’ll do all these things.” But now, I've got this little garden at the back, and I've started planting flowers. It’s a bit boring, but it's something to do. I think the key is to find something that keeps you busy but doesn’t drain you. Like, you don’t have to make it exciting, just something that keeps your mind off the quiet. That’s a good point. I’ve been trying to learn to fix things around the house. My wife used to do most of it, but now I’ve got her gone, I feel like I have to do it myself. It’s not easy, but it’s a start. I mean, I can fix a light switch, and I can’t even tell you how to change a tire, but I’m learning. That’s admirable. I think it's important to stay active, even if it's just in little ways.

Hey, I’ve been meaning to ask — do you know where I can get some of that real apple pie filling? I’ve been trying to make a proper pie for the holidays, but I can’t seem to find anything that tastes like the stuff my mum used to make.      Oh, you just need to go to the local market. They have these little stalls where they sell all sorts of preserves and jams. It’s like a treasure hunt. I’ve been there a few times, and I always end up with a jar of something I didn’t even know I wanted. Last time I got a pear and ginger jam — it was amazing.      Yeah, and I’ve been meaning to talk to you about the new fitness app I started using. It’s called ‘FitTrack Elite’ — it’s supposed to help you track your workouts and diet. I’ve been using it for a couple of weeks, and it actually works pretty well. It gives you personalized recommendations based on your goals.      I’m not sure I’d trust an app with my fitness. I’ve seen too many people use them and end up watching three episodes of ‘The Crown’ instead of going for a run. But I suppose it’s worth a try, right? I’ve been meaning to start getting back into shape, especially after the holidays.      There’s also this local news update about the train station. They’re finally going to open it next month after years of delays. It’s going to make commuting way easier for people in the area. I heard they’re even planning to add a new bus route to connect with it.      Oh, that’s great to hear! I was thinking about taking the train to Exeter for a weekend trip. Maybe I’ll start planning that. I’ve been feeling like I need a break from the usual routine.      Speaking of routine, have you both seen the new recipe I’ve been trying out? It’s a chocolate and banana cake — it’s got a bit of a twist with some cinnamon and nutmeg. It’s supposed to be healthy, but I’m not sure if I’m going to admit that to anyone.      It’s not healthy if you eat it for breakfast, but it’s definitely worth trying for dessert. I’ll bring some over to the next family gathering, and we can all compare notes.

So, I just got back from this weekend trip to Cardiff. It was one of those weekends where you think you’re going to chill out, but then you end up doing way more than you planned.      Sounds like a stag weekend? Or are you just hanging out with mates?      Definitely more like a stag weekend, but I didn’t tell anyone. It was just me and a few course mates. We got this place in the city centre, booked a table at this new place called  The Grind . I heard it was the hippest spot in town.      Oh, I’ve heard of that. I think they’ve been getting a lot of reviews. Did you try their burgers?      Yeah, they were decent, but I would say the real highlight was the game night. We played a few rounds of  Mario Kart  and then  Dota 2 . I’ve been playing with my mates in the university gaming club, and it’s amazing how competitive we get.      I can imagine. I’ve been trying to get into gaming more, but I always end up getting distracted by the news or politics. It’s like I can’t focus on something fun when the world feels so unstable.      Totally. I think that’s why people like to escape with something like movies or games. Speaking of, have you seen  The Lie  on TV recently?      Yeah, I did. It was one of those British dramas that made me a bit emotional. I mean, the acting was solid, and the plot was really tight. But honestly, I felt like I was in a political debate at times about how people treat each other.      Oh, I get that. I think that’s part of what makes Shakespeare so timeless. You watch a play like  Macbeth  or  Hamlet  and it feels like it could be happening today. I mean, the human condition hasn’t changed, right?      Absolutely. I think that’s why people still study Shakespeare. He’s like a mirror to society.      Exactly. I’ve been studying it for my English course, and it’s like every time I read a play, I get a new perspective. It’s weird how something written 400 years ago still feels relevant.      I can’t wait to see how the course mates react to it. I think we’ll have some serious debates.      Just don’t start a fight over  Macbeth  and  Hamlet —we’ve got a lot of work to do.

So, I finally got my hands on a proper coffee this morning. I was so desperate for it that I had to walk all the way from the train station just to get it here. You know how I feel about coffee—only the real thing will do.      Oh, I get it. You’re like a human espresso machine. I can’t even imagine being without it. Though I have to say, I’ve been trying to cut back a bit. Still, when I’m here, I always end up ordering a cappuccino.      You’re not fooling me. You’ve been telling me for weeks that you’re going to stop drinking it, and yet here you are, still sipping on that creamy thing with a double shot.      Well, you know me—I’m not one to break promises, especially to myself. But seriously, how are you? I heard you were back in Cambridge for a while after that thing with your ex. How’s that going?      Ugh, don’t bring that up. I’m still trying to get over it. He was really nice in the beginning, but as time went on, things started to change. I just feel like I wasted so much time on someone who didn’t really want to be with me.      I know, I know. You were so head over heels for him. But you’re not the same person you were back then. You’ve grown so much. You’re in a good place now.      Yeah, I guess. I’m just not ready to be in a relationship again. Not yet, at least. I’m focusing more on my work and trying to figure out what I want next.      That’s a good idea. You’ve always been pretty focused. I mean, you managed to run that project last month, right?      Yeah, it was tough, but I handled it. I think I’m getting better at managing people and keeping things on track. I’m even thinking about taking on a bigger project next year.      That’s great news! I’ve been thinking about going back to London for a while now. My company wants me to be based there, and I think it’s time I took a real leap.      That’s a big move, but I think you’ve earned it. You’ve worked so hard, and you’re not afraid to take chances.

You know, I’ve been thinking about my nan’s garden ever since I got back from the family trip. She has these amazing plants, like this huge rose bush that’s been in the family for generations. I swear, it looks like it’s been there since the ’50s.      Yeah, I remember seeing photos of that rose bush when I was a kid. It must have been a real family treasure. My mum used to say it was the only thing that survived the war. She always claimed it was a symbol of resilience. You know, like the British spirit or something.      That’s probably the best description of it I’ve ever heard. But I think it’s more about the fact that it’s been there through everything. My nan says she’s been growing it since she was about 16. She doesn’t even remember when it was planted. Just that it was there when she got married.      That’s the kind of thing that becomes part of the family lore, isn’t it? Like, you don’t just grow a plant, you grow a story. I’ve been trying to get my own garden going, but I’m not sure if I have the patience for it. I’m more of a kitchen person, honestly.      Well, you could always combine the two. I’ve been experimenting with herbs in the kitchen. Like, growing basil in pots on the windowsill. It’s a bit of a hobby, but it’s nice to have fresh ingredients. Plus, I feel like I’m contributing to the house’s overall green vibe.      I tried that once. I bought this huge basil plant that was supposed to be easy to grow. Two weeks in, it looked like it was dying. I ended up giving it to my sister. She’s more into plants than I am. She actually has a small greenhouse.      That’s a bit of a shame. I mean, you could’ve just given it to me! I’m not the best gardener, but I’m not completely hopeless. I mean, I can go weeks without killing a plant if I don’t overwater it.      I’ll take that as a compliment. Maybe I’ll try again. I’ve been reading up on indoor gardening. There’s this app that tells you exactly when to water your plants. I feel like I’m doing it the modern way.

Good morning, John. How was your weekend? I saw you had a bit of a schedule with that family event in Cardiff.      It was good, thank you, Alan. A bit long, but we had a nice time. My daughter came back from London, and she brought her new partner. We had a barbecue in the garden, and the kids were running around like mad. It was a bit of a chaos, but fun.      Sounds like a typical weekend for a family. I had a quieter one. My son got married last week, so it was mostly just me and my wife. We had a nice meal at home and watched some old football matches on TV. Still, it was peaceful.      That’s a big deal. Congratulations! I can imagine the hustle and bustle. Speaking of which, have you seen any of the young football players lately? I saw a few on social media—some of them look like they’ve taken up running or cycling, not just football.      Yes, I saw that. It’s fascinating how some of them are diversifying their activities. I think it’s good for them, though. It keeps them active and gives them something to do outside of training and matches. I remember when I was younger, football was everything. Now, it’s more about balance.      True, balance is the key. By the way, have you heard about the new snooker tournament in Manchester? I think they’re allowing some young players to participate. It’s a great way to give them exposure.      I heard about that. It’s a bit strange, though. Snooker is such a quiet sport, and I don’t know if the younger generation is into it. But I suppose it’s part of the tradition. Speaking of sports, I was thinking about gardening the other day. My wife mentioned that the garden needs some serious attention. I’ve been meaning to get back to it.      Oh, gardening is a great way to unwind. I’ve been trying to grow some vegetables in the shed. It’s not much, but it’s satisfying. Do you mark students' work yet this term?      Yes, I’ve been caught up in it. It’s been quite a workload. I’ve had to mark a few essays and some exams. It’s not the most exciting part of the job, but it’s necessary.      I can imagine.

Right, I’ve got the dates for the birthday and the Christening sorted. But I’m still not sure about the venue for the birthday. Do you have any ideas, Lucy?      I don’t know, Mum. Maybe somewhere outside? I want to have a picnic.      Actually, I think a park would be lovely. There’s one near the river that’s really pretty in the spring. The kids love it.      That sounds nice, Elise. I’d like that. But I still need to confirm if the park is available. I’ll call the council tomorrow.      Can I help with that? I’ve got my phone.      Of course, sweetheart. You can look it up for me, or even message the park office. I’m sure they’ll be happy to help.      I’ve got a few ideas for the Christening too. Maybe we can have it at the local church? The one near the school.      That’s a good idea. I’ve been meaning to get back in touch with the Reverend. He’s been very helpful with the last few events.      Can I have a nickname for the baby? Like Mommy or Daddy?      Oh, you’re already thinking about it! I think we’ll have to wait until the baby is born to decide. But you can help pick out the baby’s name when the time comes.      I’d like to be part of that too. I’m not sure if I’m ready to be an aunt, but I’d like to be there for the baby.      You’ll be amazing, Elise. I’ve no doubt about that. You’re already so thoughtful.      I think I know what I want to name the baby. I like the name Lily. It’s like the flowers in the park.      That sounds beautiful. I think Lily is a lovely name.      I think Lily is perfect. It’s a strong name, and it’s so pretty.      Alright, let’s make a list of the things we need to do. The birthday is on the 20th, and the Christening is on the 30th. We need to arrange the venue, send out the invitations, and get the food sorted.      Can we have cake? I really want to have cake!      Of course, you can have cake. We’ll have plenty.      Alright, we’ll start planning the menu tomorrow. I think that’s a good start.      I think I’ll help with the menu too.

Well, I've been thinking about that holiday to New York we've been talking about. It's been a while since we last went on a proper trip, and I think it's time we did something a bit more exciting than just a weekend at the seaside.      I agree. It’s been ages since we had that trip to Cornwall. Remember how we got stuck in a queue for the best fish and chips in the whole town? It was a disaster, but it was also hilarious.      Oh, don’t remind me. I still have that photo of us arguing with the fish and chip shop owner about how we were “ way too posh ” for his place.      Mom, can I go to the park with Dad? It’s nice and sunny today.      Of course, sweetheart. Just be back by 4, okay? And don’t forget your sun hat.      Yeah, I’ll be back before you even finish your cake.      You know, I was just thinking – maybe we should plan the New York trip for the end of August. I’ve got a bit of time off next month, and I think the weather will be better then.      That sounds like a good idea. We could even book a flight and a hotel before the end of the month. I’ve got some friends who’d be happy to join us as well.      That would be great. I’m just a bit nervous about the cost, though. I mean, New York is not exactly cheap.      I know, but I think we can split the costs. And maybe we can look for a place that’s centrally located so we can do a few things without wasting time traveling.      Can I go too? I’ve never been to New York!      You’d be the youngest there, love. But if you’re up for it, I’m sure we can make it work.      I think we should start planning the itinerary soon. Maybe we can talk about where we want to go – the museums, the city tours, even the famous restaurants.      Sounds good. And we can also discuss the weather. I keep hearing it’s going to be hot, so we’ll need to pack accordingly.      I’m going to go and play with my toy cars now.      Do you think we could also go to the wedding of your cousin next month?

Alright, I've got this paperwork for my thesis, and I’m just trying to make sense of it all. I mean, it’s all this jargon and I can't even figure out where to start. I keep thinking, how do they expect us to do this without any clear guidance?      Yeah, I feel you. I was handed this same thing last week and I was like, "What even is this?" I mean, it’s got all these sections but none of them are properly explained. I just hope the supervisor doesn’t mind us asking questions when we get stuck.      Exactly! I've been trying to read through the guidelines and I'm still confused. There's this part about "methodological rigor," and I don't even know what that means in the context of my research. I mean, I know it's about being thorough, but how do I show that in my work?      I think it's more about how you structure your approach. Like, if you're looking at the impact of social media on student mental health, you need to outline clearly how you're collecting data—whether it's through surveys, interviews, or something else. And then you have to justify why that method is the best fit for your research question.      Oh, right, I guess that makes sense. But how do I even start drafting that section? I mean, I can't just wing it. I need to make sure I’m covering all the bases. I remember one of my lecturers saying that the methodology is the backbone of your thesis. Without it, the whole thing falls apart.      Definitely. And it’s not just about what you’re doing—it’s also about what you’re not doing. Like, you need to acknowledge any limitations in your research design. I know it sounds weird, but it shows you’re aware of the boundaries of your study. Plus, it makes your work more credible.      That actually makes sense. I was trying to avoid talking about limitations because I didn’t want to make my research seem weak. But I guess it’s part of the process. I think I need to do a bit of research on methodology examples from previous theses. Maybe I can find some templates or go through some sample chapters.      That sounds like a solid plan. I’m actually going to go through some existing theses this weekend.

So, I was just thinking about my dreams last night. I had the weirdest dream, like I was running through a forest, and there were these giant, glowing mushrooms all around me. I kept trying to find my way out, but every time I thought I saw a path, it just led back to where I started.      Wow, that sounds intense. I had a dream last week where I won the Lottery. I was just sitting in my living room, and the numbers came up on the TV. I couldn’t believe it—at first I thought I was dreaming, but then I woke up and checked my phone, and it was already 6:30 a.m. I had no idea how I felt about it. Was it a dream or did it actually happen?      That’s wild. I can’t imagine winning the Lottery. I mean, I’ve always wanted to, but I think I’d be too scared to spend it all. Maybe I’d just buy a house, get a dog, and then maybe even start a small business? I’ve always thought about that—owning a dog, especially one of those big, fluffy ones that you can’t help but fall in love with.      Dad, can we get a dog? I really want one! I’ve been saving up my pocket money for months!      Yeah, me too! I think I’m going to be the one who takes care of it. I’m strong and I can carry the bags!      You two are a nightmare. But seriously, I think owning a dog would be amazing. It would keep us all busy, and it would give us something to look forward to. I mean, I’ve always wanted a pet, but I was too afraid to get one. I was worried about the responsibility.      I can relate. I used to think about getting a dog too, but then I realized I was too busy with work and my students. Plus, I always thought I’d be too clumsy to take care of one. But now, with the kids around, maybe it’s time to think about it. Although I’m still not sure if I’m ready for the amount of time and money it would take.      But it’s worth it! Imagine having a dog that follows you around all day, and then your dad and mom would be so happy.

You know, I still can’t believe we ended up in A&E like that. I mean, it wasn’t even that bad, was it? Just a little fall on the pavement.      Yeah, yeah, it wasn’t  that  bad. But you know what they said? "You’re lucky it wasn’t worse."      Oh, please. If it had been worse, I’d be in a wheelchair, or worse. You know what I mean? I’ve had worse.      You’ve had worse? My uncle broke his leg jumping off a roof to catch a cat. And I’m not even sure the cat was worth it.      Yeah, but he’s got a cat now. I guess that’s something.      Exactly. But seriously, I was so worried. You were unconscious for like five minutes. I thought you were going to start bleeding out or something.      I know, I know. I was just being stupid. I was rushing to meet you for our date – I thought I could make it in time. But the pavement was wet, the lights were out, and somehow I just slipped.      It’s all in a day’s work. But you need to be more careful. It’s not like you’re the only one who’s ever had a fall.      Oh, come on. I’m not asking for a medal or anything. I just need to remember to look where I’m going.      You’re not going to remember that, are you?      No, not unless I get a reminder from you every time I step outside.      Then I’ll have to start writing you notes. “Step carefully. No running. Watch the pavement.”      Oh no, you’re already goading me. I’m going to start doubting my own abilities.      You’re already doubting your own abilities. You just don’t know it yet.      That’s not fair. I was just trying to be on time.      Yeah, well, next time, maybe you can take the bus. Or wait for me.      You’re not going to let me off that easy, are you?      No. Not a chance.      Okay, okay. I’ll take the bus. Maybe I’ll even wear shoes with grip.      Yes! That’s the spirit. Next time, no more falls. No more A&E. Just a little walk, a little date, and no more drama.      Yeah, yeah. But if I do fall again, I’m blaming you.      That’s fair. You’ve got to hold someone accountable for your own stupidity.

So, John, I’ve been thinking about that business idea we talked about last week. You know, that café and bookshop combo. It’s been on my mind ever since I read that article about the rise in independent cafes in the area. People are looking for places that offer more than just coffee. They want community and culture, right?      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about it too, Phil. It’s actually something I’ve been considering for a while now. The café part is easy—people love a good cup of coffee—and the bookshop could tie into that. But I’m not sure about the logistics. I mean, running a café is one thing, but adding a bookshop on top of that… It could get expensive, especially with the rent and staffing.      I know, it is a bit of a leap, but if you think about it, the two go hand in hand. People who come to the café for a coffee might also want to browse the books. Plus, if you curate the books well—maybe even include some local authors or independent publishers—you could create a real sense of community. I’ve seen it work in a few places around Brighton and Hove.      That does sound promising. I’ve been reading a lot about how small businesses are surviving these days by creating unique experiences. It’s not just about selling things anymore; it’s about engaging people. But I still need to do some research. I might check out some of those independent cafés in the area and see how they’re managing the combined model.      Exactly, and I’d be happy to help with that. You know I’ve got a bit of experience in running small businesses through my teaching career. I can help you with the planning and maybe even some of the marketing. Speaking of which, I saw some interesting international news yesterday about the new trade agreements. It’s going to affect the import of goods, including books.      Oh, right, I heard about that too. It’s a bit concerning for small traders like me who rely on importing books and other materials. If the costs go up, it could really hit the margins. But I suppose that’s just part of the game these days.      It is, but I think it’s also a chance to adapt. Maybe focus more on local publishers or even start a small print-on-demand service.

So, I was just thinking, we need to get some food before the TV show starts. I know it’s not the best choice for dinner, but I’m not hungry for anything else right now. What do you say?      Yeah, I agree. I’ve had a long day at work and just want to relax. Maybe we can grab some snacks from the bar? They’ve got those little fish fingers and chips things, but I’m not too sure if it’s worth it. It’s not like we’re in a fancy restaurant, though.      Well, it’s not like we’re in a fancy restaurant, is it? I mean, we’re in the Guardhouse pub, and honestly, the décor is pretty cool. I love the vintage posters on the walls and the old wooden bar. It gives it that classic English pub vibe.      Definitely. I remember when we first came here, I thought it was a bit too much in terms of style, but now I actually quite like it. It’s got that nostalgic feel, like it’s been around for ages. Plus, the lighting is just right—soft and warm.      Yeah, I think it’s the kind of place that makes you feel like you’re in a film. You know, like the kind of pub you’d see in  Happy Valley —all the drama, all the atmosphere.       Happy Valley ? Oh, I’ve been binge-watching that lately. It’s so gripping, isn’t it? I can’t get enough of it. The characters are so intense, and the settings are so vivid. Even though it’s set in the 80s, it feels like it could be happening right now.      I’ve only seen a few episodes, but I’m planning to catch up with it this week. Maybe we can watch it together sometime. I’ve been meaning to sit down and actually watch something that’s not just a documentary or a show about cats. Speaking of cats, have you seen the little one that’s been hanging around outside?      Oh, you mean the black cat with the white spot on its nose? Yeah, I’ve seen it a few times. It’s such a weird sight in a place like Woolwich. I don’t think it’s a stray, though. It looks like it’s got a home somewhere.      It’s weird, isn’t it?

So, what’s the deal with that weather we had last week, eh? I swear, it was like a giant kid throwing a tantrum in the sky. One minute sunshine, next minute it’s hail and rain and you’re sodden to the bone.      Oh, I remember that one well. I was out taking photos in Leith Walk, and I was just getting some decent shots of the old quayside when it hit. I had my camera wrapped in a towel and was trying to keep it dry. It was a mess. You know what’s even worse? The wind! It felt like a giant hand was trying to rip the camera out of my grip.      Yeah, I know the feeling. I was out in the Pentland Hills the other day trying to take some landscape photos, and the wind was so strong I could barely stand. I had to hold my tripod like it was a lifeline. And then it started to rain. I ended up running back down the hill, camera in one hand and coat over the other. Came back soaked and with half the photos blurred.      That sounds like a tale for the ages. You know, I was thinking the other day about how much I miss travel, especially to places with good weather. I was in York the other week, and the skies were clear and the sun was shining. It was perfect for photography. I took some great shots of the castle and the river. Just wish it had lasted longer.      York? You’re not telling me you’re planning a trip there soon, are you?      Not yet, but I’ve been thinking about it. I’ve got this idea to do a photography tour of some of the lesser-known cities in England. I thought maybe a few weeks in York, then Manchester, then maybe even a quick trip up to Carlisle. I’d love to take some photos of those old stone buildings and the bridges. I could use the change of scenery.      That sounds like a plan. I’ve got a friend who’s into travel and photography too. Maybe we could go together. I’ve been wanting to get out of Edinburgh more. I get so tired of the same old views, even if they’re beautiful.      Yeah, I’d like that. It’s good to mix it up. And with the weather being as fickle as it is here, it’s better to get out before the next storm hits.

So, I was just thinking, do you remember the last time we actually had a proper weekend together without some kind of chaos? It feels like it was ages ago.      You’re not the only one who feels that way. Honestly, I’ve been so caught up with nursery drop-offs, parent meetings, and trying to keep my head above water that I haven’t even had time to think about what I want to do with my own time. It’s like the days just keep sliding by.      I know what you mean. I’ve been thinking about the plans for the week, honestly. I was hoping we could do something, you know, just us. Maybe a little getaway, even if it’s just for a day. I’ve been meaning to take you to that new café in Birmingham. I heard they have the most amazing coffee.      That does sound nice. I’d love that. But I’m not sure if I’ll have time. I’ve got a parent meeting tomorrow about the nursery’s new playgroup, and then I’m supposed to help organise a birthday party for one of the kids next week.      I understand, but you need to take a break. You’re working so hard, and I don’t want you to burn out. We could plan something small, like just a picnic in the park. Would you like that?      I’d love that. It’s been ages since we did something like that. But I’m also thinking about the baby—do you think we should start thinking about what we’re going to do with her next? I’ve been reading a lot about education and childcare, and it’s making me wonder if we’re ready for the next step.      I’ve been thinking about that too. The nursery is doing well, and the staff are really good, but I do feel like we’re just getting into the rhythm of things. Maybe we can start looking into other options. Do you think you’d be comfortable with a different type of setting? Like a playgroup or maybe even a Montessori school?      I’m open to anything, as long as it’s good for her. I just don’t want to rush into something we’re not ready for. I think it’s more about what feels right for us as a family.

So, I’ve been thinking about what I’m going to wear for the conference next week. I’m not sure if I should go with the smart casual thing or just stick with my usual jeans and a hoodie. You know, the one with the dinosaur print.      You’re going to a conference, not a park! You need to look presentable. I’ve been in meetings where people were wearing too much denim, and it just makes you look lazy.      Yeah, I agree with Speaker_2. You can’t just turn up in a hoodie, even if it’s a conference. You need to show that you’re professional. But honestly, I’ve been in that situation too. I once tried to wear jeans to a client meeting, and they thought I was joking. They said I looked like I was about to start a band.      Haha, I don’t want to look like I’m trying too hard, though. I mean, I’m not going to wear a suit, but maybe a nice top and some smart trousers?      That sounds better. Maybe you can go for something like a blazer? I saw a few people in the office wear that. It’s not too formal, but it shows you care.      You know, I was in a similar position last month. I had to attend a meeting with a client in London, and I ended up wearing a smart dress. I had a lot of flirty comments, but I just smiled and said it was my way of showing I was taking it seriously.      Oh, I can imagine. You’re going to be the only girl in the room with a scarf and a jacket. You’ll be the hero.      Yeah, I had a friend once who wore a blazer to a job interview and got the job. I think it just made him look more confident.      Speaking of appearances, have you seen the new clothes line that came out last week? I think it’s got some nice jackets. I might pick one up for the conference.      Really? What’s the brand? I might need to check it out.      It’s called  Urban Threads . I saw someone in the café wearing one, and it looked really good. I think it’s a bit more affordable than the usual business wear.      I’ve been thinking about my own wardrobe too. I need to update my clothes.

You know, I’ve been thinking about how different the tea is now compared to when I was a lad. Back in Costessey, we used to brew it strong, like it was a medicine. You’d have to add milk and sugar, but it was all about getting the warmth and comfort out of it.      Oh yes, I remember that. When I was a girl, my mum always made it with a pot on the stove, and she’d keep it going all day. It was like the whole household was connected by that cup of tea. Now, I guess people just grab a packet and pour it in the kettle, no thinking about it.      I think it’s the same everywhere, really. I still make it the old way—boil the water, pour it into the pot, and let it steep. I’ve been doing that since I was a teacher, and I don’t see the point in changing. It’s not just about the tea, it’s about the ritual, the tradition.      I agree. There’s something about sitting down with a proper cup of tea that brings people together. It’s not just a drink; it’s a conversation starter. I remember when I was teaching, I’d always have tea with the students after class. It was a way of building trust, you know?      And now, with all this technology and everything, people are always on their phones. I can’t imagine going through a whole day without a cup of tea. It’s like the anchor of the day for me.      I know, I know. I used to take it with me everywhere—on buses, in the park, even to the doctor’s. People used to think I was mad, but I’d say, “I need my tea, or I’ll go mad myself.”      To tea, then. May it always be a part of our lives, even when the world changes around us.      To tea. Even if we’re retired, we still have our rituals. It’s part of who we are.      I think that’s what keeps us going. The small things—like a warm cup of tea—make all the difference. Especially when the day feels long and uncertain.      Exactly. And with the way things are, we might as well hold on to what we know. The tea, the conversations, the comfort of familiar things.

So, I was just telling my sister about the time I tried to cook a Sunday roast and ended up setting the kitchen on fire. It was  absolutely  not the first time, and I don’t think it will be the last.      That sounds like  my  story. I tried to make a chicken cacciatore once, and I ended up burning the entire kitchen down. My parents were so upset; they even had to call the fire brigade.      You know, I think the only time I’ve burned anything was when I made a cup of tea. But I’ve still got a scar from that. My mum said I was too distracted by my phone.      I feel like we’re all just cursed with cooking accidents. I once tried to make a proper Sunday breakfast, and I ended up with a pancake that looked like a UFO. It was the most bizarre thing I’ve ever seen.      Speaking of weird things, I still can’t get over the time we went to that protest in London. You know, the one where they were protesting about the CRB checks? I didn’t even know what a CRB check was.      Yeah, that was  so  confusing. I didn’t understand why people were so upset about it. I mean, aren’t CRB checks just a form of background check?      It’s not just about the check, it’s about the process. I think some people feel like they’re being treated like criminals.      Exactly. I think there’s a bigger issue about how we’re being monitored. It’s like we’re not trusted to be responsible.      Right, but I do think there’s a lot of good in that. I mean, if you’re working with children or the elderly, you probably need those checks.      True. I just think the system is a bit too strict.      Speaking of strict, do you remember the time you tried to drive around with your dad and he got pulled over for speeding? I still can’t believe he was fined for going 15 over the limit.
