Hey, thanks for coming over. I’ve been dying to catch up. You know how it is when you haven’t seen someone in a while—your mind starts filling up with all the things you want to talk about.      No worries, I’ve been thinking about you too. I’ve had a bit of a rough week with the patients, but I needed to get out of the hospital bubble for a bit. Speaking of which, have you seen the new film that came out? The one with that guy from  Shame ? I thought it was pretty good, though I don’t know if I’d call it a classic.      I haven’t seen it yet, but I’ve heard mixed reviews. My friend Lucy said it was too slow, but I’m not sure if I’m the right audience for it. I’m more of a  Britannia  fan, to be honest. Although, I did go to that cinema in town last weekend and saw  The Power of the Dog —it was intense, to say the least.      Oh, I saw that one too. I had to take a break after the first half. It’s one of those films that makes you think about everything, you know? But I can’t stop thinking about that scene where he burns the scarf. So intense.      Yeah, that was pretty haunting. Anyway, I wanted to ask you—have you seen the new  Harry Potter  movie? I heard it’s kind of a reboot, but I’m not sure if I want to watch it. I mean, I loved the original series, but I don’t think I want to relive those days.      Honestly, I’ve been avoiding it. I think I’m just not in the mood for fantasy vibes anymore. But I did hear that it’s got some new actors and it’s a bit more modern. I might give it a try just to see what’s up. Although, I’m not sure if I’m ready to see any more wizards.      I can understand that. I think I’m just going to stick to the classics. Although, I do miss the days when we used to go to the cinema every weekend with our old school friends. Remember when we used to get so excited about the latest release? We’d argue over which one was better, and then we’d go out and eat pizza afterwards.

Hey, you know what I just saw on the TV? That ad for that new coffee shop in the city center. It was like, "Wake up, Britain, we’ve got the best beans in the world!" I don’t know, it just felt a bit forced. You ever notice how all the ads these days seem to be trying too hard to be cool?      Yeah, I totally get that. I mean, I remember when ads were just straightforward. Like, “Buy this product, it’s good.” Now it’s all about the lifestyle. You know what’s funny is, even the coffee shops are trying to sell you the idea of being a cool, woke, environmentally conscious person. It’s like they’re trying to sell you the vibe more than the coffee itself.      I know, right? But then again, it’s not just ads. I mean, even the TV shows these days are like... I don’t know. It’s like they’re all trying to be edgy. I mean, why did we even watch this episode? It was about a guy who runs a car boot sale and gets into a crime ring. It was like  Mission: Impossible , but with second-hand vinyl records.      Yeah, I remember that one. I mean, it was kind of ridiculous, but it was fun to watch. It reminded me of when we first moved in together. We had this big car boot sale in the park, and I found this old NLP manual. You remember? It was like a literal book on neuro-linguistic programming. I tried to read it, but it felt like I was trying to understand a different language.      Oh, I remember! You were like, “This is changing my life.” And then you just sat there for an hour trying to figure out what “anchoring” meant. I thought you were going to start talking to the plants.      I was! I was trying to teach them to respond to my voice. My plants are now obsessed with me. They literally jump out of their pots when I walk in the room.      Okay, that’s  not  a thing. Well, I've been thinking about the old days, you know. When we first moved into the area in the 1960s, it was completely different. I remember how we had to search and search for somewhere to live. Well, I’ve just finished a cup of tea, and I think I’m going to take a walk around the park later. It’s been a while since I’ve had a chance to do that. So, we’re almost back in London, huh? I can’t believe it’s already been a whole month since I left for Cambridge. Time flies, doesn’t it?      Yeah, it’s funny how quickly the days pass. So, I heard you’re both working in language research. What’s it like being in such a niche field? So, I just saw this viral video of a bunch of kids in London doing this crazy dance challenge. It's like,  what even is that?  But it's gone wild! They’re educated, but also hyper-connected.      Yeah, I mean, I’m a graduate, and I’ve got a degree in business. But I still feel like I’m behind the curve when it comes to what’s trending online. I think it’s a bit of an education gap, actually.      That’s not just you. I still can’t figure out how TikTok works. My cousin is into that stuff, and I’m like, “Wait, how do you do that?”      Hey, I have a kid who’s into TikTok. He posts videos of him trying to make sourdough bread. I mean, I was in university and there was this whole thing about being a “digital native,” but I had to learn how to use all these apps.

So, what do you think about the new tax changes? I’ve been trying to figure out how they’ll affect our finances, and honestly, I’m not sure if it’s going to help or hurt us.      I know, it’s been on my mind too. I mean, the government keeps talking about cutting taxes for the middle class, but with inflation rising and everything, I don’t know if it’s actually helping. You know, I still remember the time we used to visit my aunt in Stamford when I was a kid. She had this amazing garden, full of roses and peonies. I used to help her plant them in the spring. I know, it’s funny how time flies. I’m starting to feel the same way. I recently took a break from work to travel to Cornwall for a few weeks. The landscapes there are so different from what I’m used to. It was like a whole new world.      That sounds like a great trip. I’ve always wanted to go to Cornwall. It’s always nice to take time out and do something you enjoy. I’ve been reading about some new films coming out, but I haven’t had much time to go to the cinema lately. I’m thinking of going to see one of those historical dramas.      I go to the cinema every week if I can. I love the newer sci-fi films. They’re so imaginative. I think the latest one about space exploration is really good.

So, I was just telling my wife about the game my nephew was playing with his soft toys last night. It was something like "I’m a footballer, you’re the goalkeeper," and it went on for ages. Yeah, I think it’s about that age where they’re just exploring their imagination and not really concerned with the rules. My wife says it’s good for developing creativity, but I think she’s just trying to justify why the kid is still playing with the same teddy bear from when he was two.      I can see that. My toddler was obsessed with his stuffed elephant for months—until he decided it was a dinosaur. Now he’s convinced it can fly. It’s like he’s trying to tell me something, but I just don’t understand.      Exactly. My brother-in-law used to say that kids at that age are just trying to make the world make sense. You can imagine being a superhero or a king, and it feels like you can control everything. I think that’s why they get so invested in their games.      Maybe that’s part of it. Every toy is a friend, and every imaginary scenario is a way to cope with the reality of being a small person in a big world.      That’s a pretty profound take. I always thought it was just a game, but now I’m starting to see it as something deeper. I wonder if that’s why the kid is still so attached to his toys. Maybe he’s not just playing—he’s learning how to navigate the world.      I can see that.

So, I was just telling my wife about the last time we tried to cook Christmas dinner. You know, when I thought I was being clever and tried to cook the Turkey in a bag? Yeah, but it was a classic case of putting the cart before the horse. Or, in this case, the paint before the face!

Okay, I’ve got this for your birthday. I couldn’t decide what to get you, so I just bought this whole box of stuff.      Oh, you’ve gone all out. What’s in there?      Is it something clever? You’re both worrying about the wrong things. I mean, I found the book for you, and I even got the chocolates. What more do you want?      Actually, I was thinking about going to that new café in town. The one with the indoor garden? I heard the coffee’s amazing.      Yeah, I’ve heard about that. I go there sometimes on my lunch break. Well, if that’s what you like, then that’s what we’ll do.      So, are we all set then?      I think so. It’s a good idea. I’ll even bring my book.      Perfect. So, I was just telling my wife about the time I tried to cook a roast dinner without the electric oven working. You know, that whole  life without power  thing. It's like living in the Stone Age! No fridge, no microwave, just a gas hob and a boiling kettle.      Oh, I remember that! You tried to boil a kettle and forgot it was on, and then the whole house got cold. And the kids were like, “Dad, why do we have to eat cold food?” I said, “Well, that’s what you get for not living in a modern house!”      I’d say you’re living in a very modern house if you’re still having to explain things like that. I know, but you don’t get that luxury when you’re on the dole, you know? And let’s be honest, someone’s gotta pay for the lights.      That’s true. I was just talking to my sister about how we all used to go out to the pub every Friday. But now, most of us are too old to go out much. I had a  Big Brother  moment when I set up a get-together and ended up watching the whole thing like it was a reality show. It was hilarious – and terrifying.      You know, I’ve been thinking about getting a dog. I mean, I’ve always wanted one, but with the heating not working and the power going out every now and then, I was worried.

So, I was just thinking about that film we watched last night,  The Favourite . You remember, the one with the queen and the ladies-in-waiting? It was so intense, wasn’t it?      Oh yeah, it was wild. I mean, I didn’t expect the queen to be so… ruthless. I thought she’d be a bit more… regal. But the way she played it, it was like she was a chess player, calculating every move.      Exactly! And then there was Abigail, right? She was like the glue that held everything together. It’s like, who’s really pulling the strings?      Yeah, I mean, that’s what makes it so interesting. It’s not just about royalty; it’s about power dynamics – how people play roles and how they navigate those roles. It’s like a political drama, but with more drama.      To the drama, then!      To the drama!      You know, I was thinking about my family the other day. My mum and dad are both retired, and they’re always bickering about who did what during our childhood. Like, “Didn’t you water the plants?” or “You were the one who forgot to pay the council tax!”      Oh, I know that feeling. My gran would always say, “You were the one who broke the vase, not me!” And I swear, she was right. I did break it. But she’d always take the blame for it.      I think it’s just how families work. You can go your whole life thinking you know your parents, and then one day, you realize they’re just as human as you are.      Exactly. And sometimes, it’s the little things that bring you back to earth, like family gatherings or holidays. I mean, I’ve been over to my dad’s place for Christmas, and it’s like stepping back in time. Same decorations, same smells, same arguments about the football.      It’s like living in a sitcom, isn’t it? But I love it. It’s messy, but it’s also home.

Well, I've been thinking a lot about the referendum lately. You know, the one about Scotland becoming independent. It's such a big deal, isn't it? Not just for Scotland, but for the whole country.      Yeah, I've heard a lot about it. My geography teacher at school was talking about it last week. He said that a lot of people in Scotland really want independence. But I don't know much about it. I mean, what's the point, really? Why would they want to leave the UK?      Good question. I think it's about identity, you know? Like, being Scottish and not having to be British. I remember when I was a kid, the whole idea of the UK was just something you learned in school. But now, it feels like people are more divided than ever. Some people want to stay, others want to go.      But what about the economy? I mean, if Scotland becomes independent, how would that affect things like oil? I heard there's a lot of oil in the North Sea. Doesn't that make Scotland rich?      That's one of the arguments for independence. The oil and gas sector is a big part of the Scottish economy. But there are also a lot of people who are worried about the uncertainty. What if the referendum doesn't go the way people hope? What if they can't run their own country properly?      I guess it's also about being able to make their own decisions. Like, maybe they can have their own laws, their own health system, the way the education system is run. It might be more tailored to what they want.      Exactly. And I think that's part of the appeal. People in Scotland are proud of their culture, their history. They want to preserve that. But it's not just about pride, it's also about power. Being able to control their own destiny.      I can see why some people would want that. But I still don't get it. The UK is a good place. I mean, if you're not Scottish, you're still part of the UK. Why leave?      Maybe it's not about leaving the UK, but about being part of something bigger. Being part of a country that represents them, not just a larger country where they're one of many. It's about belonging.

Oh, I can't believe how thick that bloke sounds on Jeremy Kyle. I swear, he’s like a giant boulder with a microphone.      Yeah, I know, right? Can you believe it? That goal they scored in the 85th minute—what a game! I swear, if I had a pound for every time I've seen that exact type of play, I'd be able to buy a house in Sunderland.      Yeah, I remember that one. It was one of those moments where you're like, “Oh no, not again,” and then suddenly it’s a goal. But you know what’s even better? Spain, France, Germany—all those teams, they’re all really strong.      Maybe. But if we win the group, we’ll be in the semifinals, right? And if we get past that, who knows? So, I just watched  The Bee Movie  again with the kids, and I’m still trying to wrap my head around the whole “bee as a king” thing. It’s so weird, right? I mean, bees are such busy little things, but they’re also so organized. I guess that’s why the movie made me think about royalty and all.      Yeah, I remember that part! The queen bee, right? She’s like the ruler of the hive. But you know what’s funny? I once read that in real life, the queen bee is actually not as powerful as she seems. She’s just a big, fat, lazy bee who lays eggs all day. The worker bees are the ones who do all the work—like building the hive, foraging, and even defending it.      Wait, doesn’t the queen bee have to be fed by the workers? Like, she’s not allowed to leave the hive, right?      Exactly! So maybe the movie got it a little wrong. But still, it’s a cute idea. Oh, you’re talking about the British royal family again? I mean, they’re not exactly known for being the most politically savvy. So, like, what happens if the country becomes a republic? Would they just disappear?      That’s a good question. I think if the UK became a republic, the queen would probably retire gracefully, like a queen bee. Or maybe she’d start a reality TV show. We could call it  Queen of the Hive  or something.      I’d watch that. But you know, I’ve always wanted to be a politician. Or at least a royal. If I could choose, I’d rather be a royal. I mean, living in a palace, eating all the royal fruits, and getting free vitamins. It sounds like the dream life.      Yeah, but I’ve heard the royal family has to pay for their own food and drinks now. I guess the crown’s not as generous as it used to be.

You know, I just love the way the light comes through the windows here in the morning. It’s like the café breathes with the sun. I think I’ll be coming here every day now, even though the coffee isn’t bad either.      You’re not the only one, Mavis. I’ve been coming here for years. It turned out like a Jackson Pollock painting. I had to get a decorator in the end, and I never even painted the walls again.      Maybe you should start a blog about it. I mean, it’s kind of interesting to see how people handle their lives. I mean, I’m just here for my coffee and my phone, but it’s still something to write about.      You know, I actually wrote a short story about someone whose life is full of clutter and confusion. They tried to move house, but every time they thought they were getting somewhere, it just ended up worse. It’s funny, but it’s also a bit sad.      That sounds like something I’d read. I’ve always thought about writing, but I’m afraid I’d just end up like the characters in your story. I’m too busy remembering things to move forward.

Right, so I’ve been thinking about this museum in Chester that I wanted to visit. I remember reading about it online—some kind of Roman site or something. But I’m not sure how to get there. Should I take the train or a bus?      Oh, you mean the Roman remains at the museum? Yeah, I think you can take the train to Northwich and then a bus to Chester. But let me check the route. Wait, actually, there’s a direct bus from Liverpool to Chester, but the last one is at 5:30. Are you planning to go later tonight?      Yeah, I was hoping to go after work. I’ve got the day off, so I thought maybe we could go this weekend. But I don’t know if you’d want to. I mean, it’s not exactly a big attraction, but it’s a bit of a local thing, you know? You can park there for about £5, right? That might be cheaper than taking the train.      Yeah, I think that’s right. Although I’m not a big fan of parking. I always end up circling the block like a lost puppy. But I guess it’s worth it for the experience.      I know what you mean. I once spent 20 minutes searching for a parking spot in Liverpool, and I finally had to park on the street and got a ticket. Not fun. So, if we decide to go, maybe we can go on Sunday. Not really, unless you want to bring a camera. The site is really interesting, and you can take photos. Just don’t go into the restricted areas. Also, maybe we can check if there’s anything on at the museum. I think they sometimes have special exhibits.      Sounds good. I’ll check the website tomorrow. Oh, by the way, I was thinking about applying for a Masters in Education.

Oh my god, I just saw this video of this guy doing a freestyle rap in the park. He’s so good, like, I can’t even believe it. It's like he's got this natural flow. Have you seen anything like that?      Yeah, I saw that! He’s got this vibe, like he’s not even trying. I mean, he’s got that kind of raw talent. But honestly, I think it’s just because he’s been grinding for so long. Like, do you think he’s even a real artist or just someone who’s trying to go viral?      I think it’s the latter, honestly. I think it’s made it harder for real artists to get noticed because everything is so fast-paced.      I agree, but I also think it’s given a lot of new people a platform to express themselves. Like, I know some of my friends who are into music and they just started posting their music online. It’s not like they had a record label or anything. It’s kind of inspiring, honestly.      Yeah, I guess it is. I mean, I still think there’s a difference between being popular online and actually being successful. But I guess that’s the thing with the internet—it’s all about the numbers. You could be the most popular person, but nobody knows who you are in real life.      Exactly. I told my mate the other day, I think we’re all just performance artists now. We live our lives like we’re on a show. Except we don’t get a paycheck.      Oh, I’m not so sure. I think we might be getting paid in likes and followers. It’s a different kind of currency.      Yeah, I guess you could say that. But you know what? I’m still going to keep posting my pizza photos. It’s all I’ve got.      That’s the spirit. Now, I’m gonna go get a slice before it’s gone.

So, I was just thinking about that game we were playing last night with the new Pokémon update. I finally caught that Celebi, and it was like a dream come true. I feel like I've unlocked some serious power here.      I can’t even tell you how proud I am of you, sweetie. You’ve come so far with that game. I’ve been trying to get that Celebi too, but every time I get close, it just slips away. Maybe I need to upgrade my gear?      Mamma, I want to catch a Pokémon too! Can I play with you? I know how to press the buttons!      Of course, Oisin! You're a pro at this game. I think you’ve got the reflexes of a pro gamer. Now, with Oisin, it's hard to find the time. I’m not even sure if I should be on my phone so much.      I get it. With a toddler, you have to be careful. But being with him is so rewarding. We’ve been talking about going to that new ramen place downtown. I think the owner has a great taste in food. Do you think we could go this weekend?      Maybe. I have to check if I can manage the time. But if I can, I would love to. I’ve been craving Japanese food for ages. Oh, and I saw some skinny jeans at the store the other day. They were so cute. Do you think they’re in style?      I think you’re still in style with anything you wear, Mummy. But seriously, I think skinny jeans are back in. Just don’t wear them to the café with that toddler. He’s already got enough trouble with the slippers.      Mamma, my slippers are so soft! I like them better than your shoes!      I know, Oisin. I know. But I think you’re going to love the ramen. It's always so good, and you’ll get to try new things.

You know, I was just thinking—the other day, I found this old tin box down here. I’m not sure if it’s from when we were kids or not, but I remember something about a ‘gardening set’ we used to play with. Do you remember that?      Oh yes! That was one of the best toys we had. I think it was this little plastic set with tiny tools and a small patch of dirt you could dig in. We used to pretend we were working in our own garden, even though we had no actual garden.      True, but it was like we had our own little world. I still remember the way we would water the pretend plants with the little watering can, and then I’d get the little ‘Bako’ building set out and start constructing something.      Oh, the Bako! That was the real deal. I think it was this big plastic box with lots of colorful pieces, and we used to build the most amazing things. I remember one time we built a whole village out of it. It had houses, a school, even a little shop.      I think we even had a ‘postman’ who delivered letters to the shop. It was so detailed. I wonder if those toys still exist. It’s amazing how much fun we had with such simple things.      It’s funny, isn’t it? We had a lot of imagination. I think the Bako was the one that really sparked my interest in building things. Even as an adult, I’ve always liked creating and making things.      It’s just sad how much of that has gone. I mean, now we’re both retired, we have all this time, but we’re still struggling to keep up with the house. There’s so much clutter, and the cupboard is just one of those places where we haven’t really been able to tidy properly.      I know. It’s always been one of those tasks that feels too big. I keep telling myself I’ll get to it, but then another day passes, and the dust bunnies get bigger. I think we need to start with the smallest things. Maybe the cupboard is a good place to begin.      Yeah, I agree. I think if we start with the cupboard, we can tackle the rest step by step. And who knows—maybe we’ll find some more old toys or memories hidden in there.

You know, I swear the mosquitoes around here are getting worse. I’ve been trying to keep the baby covered up, but it’s like they’re all after us. I don’t even remember the last time I saw a cloud without them buzzing around.      Yeah, I know what you mean. I’ve had to use more repellent than I ever have before. I mean, I used to be able to walk into a park without getting bitten. Now, it’s like the entire neighborhood is hosting a party and we’re the main attraction.      I swear, the baby’s getting more bites than I do. My poor little one, I feel awful. I keep telling myself it’s just a phase, but I can’t shake the feeling that the world is trying to take us out one by one.      Well, at least we’re not the only ones. I saw a couple of kids down the street the other day, and they were all covered in bites too. I thought maybe it was a new strain or something. But then again, maybe it’s just summer. You know, the time of year when everything seems to come alive, including the bugs.      I guess you’re right. Though I can’t help but think about the music gig we were supposed to go to last weekend. We had everything planned—tickets, food, even a picnic blanket. But then the mosquitoes hit, and we ended up just staying home.      I know. I was really looking forward to it. The band was supposed to be amazing. I mean, I’ve heard some of their tracks, and they’re really good. But you know what? Maybe that was fate. Maybe the mosquitoes were trying to tell us to stay in.      Or maybe they were just trying to stop us from getting too comfortable. Do you think we’ll go next week?      I’m hoping to. I’ve got a few buddies who said they can get us in for half price. But I’m not sure how I’ll explain the bites to the band. I mean, I don’t want to risk getting them all wrong.      You could always say it’s the London traffic. I mean, have you seen the congestion down there? I think the mosquitoes are just the tip of the iceberg.      Yeah, and the traffic’s only getting worse.

Hey, you're just in from work? I’ve been trying to get this internet connection working properly. It’s been giving me the runs all day. I tried to watch a movie, and it just froze mid-scene. I tried to send a message to my cousin earlier, and it just kept bouncing back. I swear, I’ve had enough of these damn tech issues. It’s like the universe doesn’t want me to get anything done. You know what’s even worse? I couldn’t even finish my post about the theatre review I wrote last night. It’s still sitting on my phone, and I’m worried I’m going to lose it.      Aww, don’t worry. I bet you can just retype it. I mean, I’ve been doing that more and more since I started my career in golf. You’d be surprised how many times I’ve had to redo a training plan or a match strategy because I lost it in the middle of a phone call or something. Sometimes I think I’ve got a ghost in the Wi-Fi. Like, it’s got a life of its own.      You’re not the only one who feels that way. I’ve even started thinking that maybe the Wi-Fi is haunted. I mean, every time I try to phone my mum, it just goes straight to voicemail, and then it feels like someone’s knocking on the door. Like, maybe a ghost just wants to say hello. It’s ridiculous, but it’s getting to me.      That’s your new coping mechanism? Ghosts? I mean, I get it. I’ve had days where I just feel like I’m being watched. Maybe it’s the golf training. I mean, every time I run, I feel like someone’s chasing me. Sometimes I think it’s just my imagination. But I have to be careful. If I start thinking too much about ghosts, I might lose my focus on the game.      Yeah, but you’re also always trying to find the best route to the next match. I bet you’ve got a GPS in your head. I, on the other hand, go out of my way to avoid the bus stop.

Alright, mate, I think we’ve got the table set, and the kid’s got the dinner song down pat. You’d think with all that energy, he’d be able to eat without throwing a tantrum.      He’s got the voice of an angel, if you ask me. I swear, if he keeps that up, we’ll be running a kid band before we know it.      Oh, don’t get me started. I’ve heard him sing “Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star” with such intensity, I thought the ceiling was going to come down. Still, it’s kinda cute, in a way.      Yeah, he’s got that Cork accent, doesn’t he? D’you know, I think he’s got a better chance of making it as a singer than I ever did.      Aye, and I’m the one who hides the chips in the fridge. You’re the one who’s still trying to find the remote control, and now you’re talking about the kid’s musical talent. What’s next, you’re going to start calling him a prodigy?      I’m not denying it. I just think he’s got potential. Anyway, I’ve got the dinner sorted. It’s that chicken and leek casserole I found in the back of the fridge—well, what’s left of it.      You mean the one you said was going to be a “masterpiece” last week?      I said I’d try to make it look good. Not that it’s actually going to taste good.      Well, at least it’s not the standard ‘leftover baked beans’ that we usually serve.      You know, I was thinking, maybe we should try to get him into some kind of music class. You know, to channel that energy.      I’m not sure he’d be able to sit still for a lesson. The kid’s got the attention span of a goldfish.      Aye, that’s true. But maybe we can start with something simple. Like, you know, singing along to a few nursery rhymes.      Yeah, and maybe we could get him to sing the “Cloud Song” like we used to when we were kids.      I don’t know, I think we’re already pushing our luck. I’m just trying to survive this dinner without getting a head injury.      You’ll be fine. Just remember, it’s not about perfection—it’s about family. And if the kid’s got the voice of a real angel, then we’re all set.

So, I just saw ANON this morning, and he was still sleeping in his pants. I thought he’d got up and left, but no, he was still in bed, legs crossed, just like a little kid.      Oh no, what? Was he like that all night? I mean, I thought he’d finally grown out of that phase. I mean, he’s almost 15 now. A lot of kids outgrow that, don’t they?      Yeah, but it’s not just him. I think it’s the whole family, honestly. Mummy’s still in her pajamas, even though it’s 10am. And the twins are still in their pyjamas, even though they’re supposed to be getting ready for school. I think we’re all just getting used to the idea of being in our pajamas all day.      Oh, I know, it’s so much easier. No need to get up, no need to change, just lie there, daydream, and pretend the weekend never ended. I mean, I’ve been thinking about the house extension, though. I’ve got these crazy ideas about a big garden room and a cinema.      A cinema? You can’t have a cinema in a house. What about the noise?      Well, I know, but imagine it. You could have a projector, a big screen, and a popcorn machine. And we could all get together, watch movies, and someone could even bring a blanket. It would be like a little movie theater.      Yeah, but what about the kids? They’d be running around like mad things. I mean, ANON might even make his own popcorn.      Exactly! We could have themed nights. Like, “Classic Film Night” or “Silent Film Night.” And we could even have a concession stand. It would be like a guest house, but for movies.      You know, I was thinking about it the other day. Maybe we could even add a small studio. You know, for taking photos of the garden or the house. It would be perfect for capturing the light, the seasons, the way things change.      That’s a brilliant idea. We could even make it a little gallery. You know, for when we have friends over. It would be like a little art space in our own house.      Yeah, and we could even have a section for the kids to draw or paint. It would be a creative space. I think we’re all starting to think about this house like a little haven.

Good morning, John. Did you bring the coffee? I’m beginning to think you’ve been working in the lab all morning instead of coming to the office.      Good morning, Roger. I did bring it. I only had a quick cup in the lab before coming over. I was trying to get some ideas for my research on the Hadron Collider. But honestly, I’m more interested in the coffee than the collider right now.      That’s a shame. The Hadron Collider’s fascinating, but I’ve been thinking about my own research lately. I was just talking with a colleague about funding. It’s getting harder to get grants these days, isn’t it?      You’re not the only one. I’ve been applying for a few projects myself. I was just wondering if you’ve had any luck with the funding applications for your home decorating study?      Not yet. I’ve been putting it off. I’m actually trying to finalize the design for my new house in the countryside. I’m redoing the whole place. It’s going to be a combination of traditional English and some modern touches. I’ve been looking at Italian design a lot—especially from Florence. It’s beautiful, but expensive.      Italy, you say? That’s interesting. I remember when I was in Tredegar, we used to talk about the Italian Renaissance and how it influenced architecture and art. I always thought it was fascinating how Italian aesthetics blend with the principles of form and function.      Yes, it’s a great mix. I’ve been thinking about what you said about water companies. I was reading an article about how some of the older water systems are failing, and I was wondering if there’s a connection to the way we design our homes now—especially with water conservation in mind.      That’s a good point. I think we’re all starting to see the consequences of poor planning. It’s not just about the technology, it’s about the infrastructure. I was actually thinking about how the Hadron Collider is a huge investment, but so is maintaining our water systems. Maybe we should be talking to the local water company about new ideas?      Absolutely. I think there’s a lot of potential for innovation there. I’ve been meaning to get in touch with a few local officials. But until then, I’ll just stick to my coffee and my decorating plans.

Well, I think it's time we got the Lego sorted out properly. I’m so tired of finding a few bricks missing from each box. I don’t know who’s been taking them, but it's getting ridiculous.      Is it really? I didn’t notice anything missing. I just put all my bricks back after building the Turtle Shell. Maybe it's the Easter chocolate? I was eating a piece when I was playing, and I might’ve accidentally dropped a brick.      Yeah, that’s what I think. I saw you drop one last night. But I think I found the missing bricks in the couch cushions. I was trying to find my lost slime toy, and there they were.      Oh, you found them? Good. I was about to tell you I found the same ones in the top drawer. I guess we just need to get a better system. Maybe we can assign each box to someone and keep track.      That sounds like a good idea. I mean, it’s not like we’re going to build the entire Hogwarts castle with just one box. But it would be nice to know where everything is. It’s not just Legos, though. You know, the one from  The Simpsons Movie . I thought it was just a random poster, but it was actually a hidden Harry Potter one.      Wait, really? You found a hidden poster? That’s awesome. I thought we were going to go to the cinema this weekend. I was planning to take the kids to see  Teenage Mutant Ninja Turtles: Mutant Mayhem  again. It’s been a while since we’ve seen it.      That sounds fun! I want to see it again. I love the way the turtles fight the Foot Clan. But I also wanted to see  The Simpsons  one more time. Is it showing again soon? She said she’s going to make the kitchen look like Hogwarts.      Oh, she’s been talking about that for ages.

Hey, thanks for coming over! I’ve been dying to catch up since you were away. How was your holiday? You didn’t tell me where you went.      It was amazing, honestly. I went to Cornwall with my sister. We stayed in a little cottage by the sea, and it was just the two of us. It felt like we were on holiday, even though it was just a weekend.      That sounds so peaceful. I’ve been feeling a bit stuck in my routine lately. Work’s been pretty hectic, and I haven’t had much time to myself. You know how I get when I’m overworked.      I know, I’ve been there too. But you’ve got to take time for yourself. I think I’m going to start doing some yoga again. It helps me clear my head. Do you want to come with me? There’s a class starting up next week.      Seriously? That’d be great. I’d love to try it. I’ve always wanted to give it a go. I just never had the time before.      Perfect. I’ll send you the details. Oh, by the way, did you hear about the football match on Saturday? I was so excited to watch it, but I ended up helping my mum with some stuff. I almost missed it.      Yeah, I saw the highlights. It was a tight game. I think my team won in the last minute. Honestly, I couldn’t have been more excited. I even got my dad to watch it with me. He’s been talking about football non-stop since.      That’s so cool. I miss watching matches with people I care about. I think I’ve been too busy lately to really enjoy it. Maybe I should start going to some games with friends again. I feel like I’m losing touch with that part of my life.      You should. I think you’d love it. And don’t worry, I’ll be there to help you get your enthusiasm back. Speaking of which, did you ever figure out what happened with your ex-boyfriend? I’ve been dying to hear the full story.      Oh, that’s a long one. Let’s see… He moved out of the country a few months ago, and then he started dating someone else. It was really hard because we were so close. I still think about him sometimes, but I’m trying to move on.

Right, I need to get some more flour and sugar before the weekend. I’m starting to run out, and I know how much the grandkids love baking.      Yeah, especially when it comes to your famous Yorkshire puddings. I still remember the time you tried to make them for the family dinner and ended up with a mess in the oven.      Oh, that was a disaster! I think the cat even tried to help, or maybe it was just curious. Either way, it ended up with a whole mess of flour on the floor, and we had to clean up for hours.      And I still have the photo of it, too. I think it’s in the attic with all the other old family photos. You know, I was thinking earlier about going through some of those boxes. Maybe we could find some old letters or something from the war years.      That sounds like a good idea. I’ve been meaning to get around to that. But I should probably wait until the weather’s a bit better—this damp is making it hard to open some of the older boxes.      You know, I’ve been meaning to ask—what exactly are you planning to do with all those old things? Are you going to put them in a museum or something?      No, no, no. We’re just keeping them as family heirlooms. I think it’s important to remember where we come from, even if it’s a bit dusty.      Exactly. My father used to tell stories about the old days, and I think it’s good for the kids to hear them. Especially now that they’re getting older.      You know, I was talking to the grandkids about that the other day. They said they’d like to hear more of the old tales. Maybe we could do a sort of family history night?      That’s a great idea! I could help with that. I’ve been wanting to work on some of my old stories, and I think they’d go down well with the younger generation.      I’d be happy to help too. I’ve got some old photos from when I was a kid, and maybe some stories about the time I tried to ride a bicycle for the first time.      Oh, that was a real doozy! I remember you fell into the river and had to be rescued by the local constable.

You know, I've been thinking about the Peter Pan stories again. I've always loved the way the characters run away from growing up, but I wonder what the real message was behind it all.      I think it's about never wanting to grow up, right? But I also remember reading somewhere that it's more about the idea of childhood being magical and pure. Like, the place where you can be whoever you want to be.      But what about the film versions? I remember watching the Disney one when I was little. It was so pretty, but I also thought the characters were kind of boring. Like, why did Tinker Bell get so angry all the time?      Oh, she’s just a bit dramatic, I think. And the movie definitely softened a lot of the original story. J.M. Barrie’s book was more complicated, with darker themes. I remember reading that he had a real connection to Great Ormond Street—his father was a doctor there.      Wasn't Great Ormond Street the place where Peter Pan was inspired by? I think the hospital was where he first wrote the story. I remember reading that it was based on real children he met there.      Exactly. And the original story wasn’t just about never growing up—it was about the emotional impact of losing someone. The story of Peter Pan was inspired by the loss of his brother, and the idea of childhood as a way to escape pain.      But why did he never grow up? I mean, isn’t that kind of sad? If you never grow up, you can’t be an adult and have a family or do all the things that grown-ups do.      That’s a really good point. I think it’s about the duality of childhood—how it’s both wonderful and limiting. Peter Pan is stuck in a sort of limbo, and that’s why he’s always flying and always trying to find his way back to Neverland.      But what about the movie with the pirates? I didn’t really like that part. It felt so scary, and I didn’t like the pirate characters at all. Why were they so mean?      The pirates were part of the adventure, I think. They represented the darker side of life, the things you have to face as you grow up. But in the story, Peter always manages to outwit them, which shows that he’s still childlike, even in a dangerous world.

It’s strange, isn’t it? I remember driving from Southend to Taunton when I was working. I used to do that every week, long before I retired. Back then, I was always rushing—get up at 5 a.m., rush to the station, catch the train, then the bus. Now, it’s just me in this car, with no particular rush, but still, the distance feels the same.      It’s funny, isn’t it? I used to drive from Exeter to Taunton too when I was teaching at the college. I’d always think, “How long will this journey take?” but I never really got it right. Ten minutes, twenty minutes, thirty—always too long. I think it’s just the way you feel when you’ve got something to do.      I remember when I first moved to Wellington. I used to drive back to Taunton for visits, and it was like a second home. I’d always say, “I’ll be back in a week,” but it would be a month before I felt like leaving.      That’s the way it is with family. You get so used to the place, it feels like home. I remember my mother used to say that when I was a kid, I’d never want to leave Southend, even though I was only five. But now, I don’t even know if I’d want to live there again.      I still miss Taunton, though. The coffee shops, the old school—there’s something about the place that’s hard to forget. And I suppose that’s why I still teach. I like the routine, the structure, even if it’s just a few hours every day.      I think we all need that structure. I’ve been trying to get back into teaching, but I keep getting pulled in other directions. I’m still in the system, but not with the same energy.      Speaking of structure, have you thought about the Christmas plans? I was hoping we could all come together. I’ve got a little place in Exeter, and I was thinking of throwing a house-warming party. It’d be nice to have everyone together, even if it’s just for a few hours.      That sounds great. I’d love to come. I’ve been meaning to visit you all for ages. It’s been too long since we’ve all been in one place, even if it’s just for a few days.

Well, I suppose we're both taking a break from the track work, aren't we? It's a bit of a relief, isn't it? Though I can't say I've ever been too fond of the physicality of it. Got a bit of a stiff back from the last one.      Aye, I know what you mean. I used to be an accommodation manager, so I was always pulling shifts, managing people, and now I'm just here, working the track. Funny how things turn out, isn't it?      Funny, indeed. You know, I used to run an antique gallery back in Somerset. Had a bit of a passion for the old days, the stories, the history. But then the market went south, and I found myself unemployed for years. It's strange how life throws you a curveball.      Yeah, I can relate. I was in a building society for most of my life, and then when they changed the way they ran things, I found myself with no job. It was a real shock. But I suppose we’ve both got to make the best of it, in our own way.      It’s funny, though. Now that I’m not working, I find myself thinking more about things I never had time for before. Like, someone mentioned the ME event next year. Do you know anything about it?      Not much, honestly. But I heard it’s going to be a big deal, especially with the focus on women’s involvement. I suppose the terminology around it is quite progressive. It’s all about equality, isn’t it?      Yes, and that’s a good thing. Female equality has come a long way, but there’s still a lot to do. My wife always said that women should have the same opportunities as men, but I used to think she was being too idealistic. Now, I’m not so sure.      That’s a common sentiment, isn’t it? Especially among older generations. But I think it’s getting better. You know, I had a niece in nursery education, and she’s making a big impact on the kids. It’s inspiring to see.      That’s beautiful, really. You know, I’ve been thinking about going to a Swedish massage. I’ve heard it’s good for the body and the mind. Maybe I’ll try it next week.      Swedish massage?

So, what do you think about going to the coast for our holiday? I've been thinking about it for ages. You know how much you love the sea, and it's been a while since we've had a proper beach day.      Oh, I’d love that, darling. It’s been so long since we’ve had a proper break. I was just thinking the same thing. The weather’s supposed to be nice, and it’ll be a change of scenery. Plus, you know how much I love the fresh air and walking along the shore. You could even bring your little ones if you want—though I know you’re not ready for that yet.      I know. I’d love to take them, but I think I need a bit more time. I’m still adjusting to the teaching job, and I’ve been working quite late. But maybe next year? I mean, with the summer coming up, it’s the perfect time for a little getaway.      I was just thinking about the trip we took to Cornwall last year. I remember we got stuck in the rain for hours, but we still had a great time. You always find a way to make the best of things. I think the coast is a wonderful place to be, especially with the sea breeze and the sound of the waves. It’s so calming.      Yeah, it’s the perfect way to relax. I’ve also been reading a few travel blogs about places near the coast. There’s this little village called Bude, and I thought it might be nice. It’s not too far, and it has a great little beach. I think you’d really enjoy the scenery there.      Bude sounds lovely. I remember it from a trip I took with some friends a few years back. The beach was so clean, and there were these little cafes with the best pastries. You know, I think we could even take a walk to the nearby cliffs. I’ve always wanted to go there.      That sounds perfect. I’ll do some more research and see what options there are. I was also thinking about renting a cottage—small, cozy, with a garden. That way, we could have some space, and maybe even cook a few meals ourselves.      Oh, I’d love that. I think I’ll start looking for a place too.

Hey man, I just got my hands on a new phone, man. I was out in town with the lads last weekend and saw this new model on display at the shop. I thought, "I gotta get this one," so I went ahead and bought it. It's a bit pricey, but I figured it's worth it for the specs. Oh yeah? You always go for the latest and greatest, don’t you? I remember when you were still using that old Nokia you got from your nan. You said it was "reliable." Yeah, I know, man. But I’ve been meaning to upgrade for ages. Plus, I’ve been getting into some serious gaming lately. That phone’s got the best graphics and processing power I’ve seen. I’ve been playing this new FIFA game, and it’s next-level. I think it’s called FIFA 24, or something like that. FIFA? I thought you were still into football in general, not just the games. You used to follow the Premier League back when you were in university, right? Yeah, I still do, man. I’ve been keeping up with the transfers. Manchester City and Liverpool are both having a good season. I even got a ticket to see West Ham play last week. It was a proper match, with all the fans and everything. I had a great time. That sounds cool. I wish I was there. I’ve been busy with work, and I’ve been trying to get back into the groove of things. I’m a manager at a small firm, so I’ve been dealing with a lot of admin and meetings. It’s been a bit of a grind lately, but I’m trying to stay positive. I can imagine. You’re in a higher professional role, so you know that stuff comes with the territory. But you’re still in that position, right? I heard you were promoted last year. Yeah, I was. It was a big deal, but it also meant I had to take on more responsibility. I’ve been working late a lot, but I’m learning a lot from it. I guess that’s what you do when you’re in that bracket. You're doing well, man. I go to university on a scholarship, so I’m not in the same boat, but I appreciate what you're doing.

Right, I was just thinking about that globe we had when I was a boy. I remember it was a real big one, covered in stickers, and we’d try to find countries and see how far we could go. It was such a treat, especially after a long day at work.      Oh, I remember that too. My dad used to bring it out every Friday evening. We’d all gather round, and he’d tell us about the places we’d visited. It was like a mini-travel show in our living room. I still have a little globe in my sitting room now, though it’s not as big as the one we had.      You know, I still have the one I had at school. It was a bit of a prize for the history project. It was a plastic one, but it had all the continents and oceans marked. I remember using it for hours when I was trying to memorize the countries.      You were always the clever one, weren’t you? I’d rather be out in the garden with the dogs than sit and look at a globe. Although, I’ve always wanted to go to Yorkshire. I hear it’s got beautiful countryside. My brother-in-law used to take us there every summer.      It’s got that famous moors and dales. I think you can even see the Pennines from some of the hills. But I’m not sure why people go there just for the scenery. You can get a better view from a bus window in the city!      Well, I did a school project once about the underground system in London. We had to draw a map of the Tube. It was such a mess! I ended up with a map that looked like a spiderweb. But I got an A, so I guess it was worth it.      I had a different kind of project. I once had to write an essay about the importance of gardens. I didn’t even have a garden, so I had to write about someone else’s. I think I ended up writing about my neighbor’s garden, which was full of roses and peacocks.      Peacocks? You don’t say. I had a bad leg once, and I couldn’t even take a walk to the park. I think I ended up spending more time on the sofa than I ever did in my life.

So, I just got a text from my sister saying her new flatmate has a parrot that’s learned to say “I’m not a fan of your cooking.”      Oh no, that’s not even the worst. My cousin’s cat started meowing at 3 a.m. every night like it was on a mission. I thought it was a ghost at first.      Oh, I’ve had worse. When I was living in Leeds, I got a roommate who called me “babe” every time he saw me. I didn’t even know him that well.      You’re telling me. I’ve got a friend who once left a banana peel on the stairs to play a prank. It took me three days to get the smell out.      Yeah, but then I had a cat who once ran out of the flat, got stuck in a tree, and then showed up at my work the next morning with a bunch of leaves in its fur. I had to explain it to the boss.      That’s wild. I feel like we’re all just trying to survive our living situations.      Yeah, but it’s all part of the adventure, right? It’s not like we’re living in a hotel.      True. Though I still can’t believe I paid over £1,000 a month for a room in London. I thought I was getting a flat, not a cage.      I know. I mean, I can’t afford a flat in Doncaster either, but at least I can cook. I think I’ve got a stove.      Oh no, you can cook? Does that mean you have a fridge as well?      Yeah, I’ve got a fridge. And a microwave. And a kettle. I think that’s all I’ve ever needed.      Well, I’m happy for you. I’ve been living on takeaway for weeks now. My flatmate’s a vegan and won’t cook anything.      Well, I’ve got some recipes you could try. I made this amazing lentil and rice dish the other night.      Oh, I’d love to try that. Maybe I can bring some of my takeaway leftovers over and we can swap.      That sounds great. I’ll bring the lentils and you bring the curry.      Deal. I think I’ve had enough of being a foodie tourist.      Yeah, let’s make it a real meal this time.      Speaking of which, have you sorted the flights yet for the trip?

Well, I've been reading about the cost of living, and it's just gone through the roof. I mean, even petrol prices are up, and I've got to take the bus to work. Not to mention the cost of groceries—some things are like double what they were five years ago.      I know, I've been feeling that too. I’ve been trying to save up for a new laptop, but every time I think I’ve got a bit of money saved, something comes up. You know, like when the internet provider sends a bill for a new service or when I have to replace my phone. It's like the prices are always going up and up.      I can’t even afford to take the bus now, let alone the train. The only reason I go to Birmingham is for the job. I have to get up at 5 a.m. just to make sure I catch the first bus. And then when I get there, the station is so crowded. I'm just glad I don’t have to do that every day, like some of the people I know.      Yeah, I’ve been thinking about how the cost of living has gone up so much. I remember when I was your age, I could buy a whole week’s worth of groceries for what you can now buy for one day. It’s just not fair, especially for people like us, who are in intermediate occupations. We’re not rich, but we’re not the poorest either. It’s a tight spot.      I’ve been thinking about whether I should switch my mobile phone provider. I’m tired of the same old company charging me extra for data. I’ve been doing some research online, and there are a few other providers that offer better rates. I just don’t know if I can trust them or not. I mean, what if they just give me a worse deal later on?      I’ve been there. I switched my provider a few years back, and it turned out to be a good move. They had better customer service, and the price was more reasonable. But I had to be careful not to sign up for anything I didn’t need. It’s easy to get caught up in the promotions.      Yeah, I’ve had some issues with customer service before.

So, I was just thinking about my holidays last year. I went to Cornwall for a week with my family. It was so peaceful, you know? Just the sea, the cliffs, and we had this little cottage with a garden. We cooked a lot of fish and chips and fresh veggies from the market. Got me thinking about holidays again.      Oh, that sounds lovely! I actually went to the Lake District last year. It’s so beautiful there. I loved hiking and just being surrounded by nature. But it got a bit chilly, so I had to pack a lot of layers. Still, the views were worth it. Did you go anywhere else besides Cornwall?      I went to the Cliffs of Moher in Ireland. It was absolutely breathtaking. The views from the top, the sea crashing against the rocks, it was like something out of a movie. But I was a bit nervous at first, climbing up those stairs. I had a picnic with a friend, and we ate some soda bread and cheese. It was a real treat.      I’ve never been to the Cliffs of Moher, but I’ve been to Snowdonia in Wales. It’s got those amazing mountains and lakes. I went on a hike up the mountain and it was such a rush. I brought a picnic with me too, just some sandwiches and fruit. It was a bit cold, but the view was worth it.      I actually went to the Yorkshire Dales. There are these really cute little villages and some great walking trails. I stayed in a cottage and cooked a lot of homemade soup and stew. I also went to a local market and bought some cheeses and fresh bread. It was a great way to relax.      That’s such a cool place. I’ve always wanted to visit the Yorkshire Dales. I think I’d love it there. Speaking of food, do you all like to cook?      I do, actually. I’m trying to become more of a home cook. I love experimenting with different recipes. I recently tried making homemade pasta, and it was so satisfying. I’ve also been learning how to make proper soups and stews.      I’m more of a takeout kind of gal, but I do go out of my way to cook sometimes. I love trying new things, especially with the different ingredients I can get from the local markets.

So, I was just thinking about what’s going to happen when we’re old. I mean, like, when we’re, like, 70 and all.      Oh, I bet you’re already planning your retirement party. What’s the plan? Are we going to live in a cabin in the woods, eating scones and reading poetry?      Maybe. I was just watching this documentary about people who live to be 100. They all said the secret was just to keep doing things you love—like painting or playing music or something.      Yeah, I like that. I mean, I’ve been thinking about starting an art project. Maybe I could do something with the university’s art department.      That sounds cool. What kind of art? I mean, I’ve been trying to work on my essays, but they’re just… not clicking. I keep thinking about the same ideas over and over.      I get that. Sometimes I feel like my essays are just… stuck. I’ve been reading this book about how to write better, though. It’s called  The Elements of Style .      Oh, I know that book. My English teacher used to quote it all the time. You know what I hate about it? It says to avoid contractions. Who even talks like that?      I know, right? It’s so outdated. But maybe it’s good to read it anyway. You never know, it might make your essays sound more formal.      I’m just worried about the future. Like, what if I don’t get into grad school? What if I have to go into a job I hate?      I get it. But you have to think about what you really want. I mean, I’m doing this art course, and it’s not the easiest, but it’s what I love. If I’m not good at it, I’ll just keep trying.      Yeah, I guess that makes sense. I just feel like I’m stuck in this loop of essays and exams. I need a break. Maybe I should try playing some computer games. I’ve been meaning to get into something like  The Last of Us  or  Elden Ring .      Oh my god,  Elden Ring  is so amazing. I’ve been playing it for weeks, and I still haven’t finished the main story. It’s like a dream.      I can’t even get through the tutorial. I’m so bad at fighting.

So, I’ve been thinking about making a big batch of spaghetti bolognese this week. I’ve got all the ingredients, and I’m really in the mood for something hearty. What do you think?      That sounds amazing! I love bolognese. It’s one of those dishes that feels like comfort food. I’ve been craving it all week. Do you have everything you need?      Yeah, I’ve got the tomatoes, the ground beef, the onion, garlic, and the herbs. Oh, and I found this new jar of marinara sauce that’s really good. I think it’ll make the sauce extra rich.      Oh, that sounds great! I’m glad you found something new. I’ve been using the same brand for years, but I guess it’s time to mix it up. Do you have any plans for the rest of the week? I mean, aside from cooking?      Haha, not really. I’ve been pretty busy with work, but I’m trying to make time for my friends. I’ve got a girls’ night out planned for this weekend—some of the people from my work. We’re going to a new café that just opened downtown. It’s supposed to have really good pastries.      Oh, that sounds fun! I’d love to come, but I’ve got a shift on Saturday. Maybe next weekend? I have a feeling I’ll be busy with a few things, but I’m hoping to make some time for my friends too. I’ve been feeling a bit isolated lately, you know?      I get that. Between work and everything else, it’s easy to feel like you’re not connecting with people. I’ve been trying to reach out more, but sometimes it’s hard to find the right time. I’m trying to be more proactive, though.      That’s really admirable. I think it’s important to make time for people, even if it’s just a quick call or a coffee. I’ve been trying to set up a regular meet-up with my closest friends. I’m going to ask them to meet up this week. It’ll be casual, just to catch up.      That’s a great idea. I think it’s so important to have those little moments of connection. Maybe we can plan something together? Like, maybe a weekend trip or something?      Yeah, that could be nice.

Right, so we’ve got the consent forms to go through. I think we should make sure everyone’s on board with the seminar structure before we finalise the details. It’s a bit of a big project, and we don’t want to end up with conflicting expectations.      Absolutely. I was just thinking the same thing. I’ve got the draft outline here. Let me just run through the main points. We’re focusing on international business communication, right? So it’s going to cover cultural differences, language barriers, and maybe some case studies.      Yeah, that sounds good. I think the case studies could really bring it to life. I was thinking of including some examples from the Middle East and East Asia, to show the diversity in approaches. But I need to check the data first—do we have enough material on those regions?      I think we do, thanks to the research we did last year. But maybe we could also include some regional variations within Europe? I know the North and South have different business cultures, and I think that’s a good point to highlight.      That’s a good idea. I’ll make a note to include that in the slides. Also, I was wondering—should we have a section on non-verbal communication? I think that’s a critical part of international business, especially in cross-cultural settings.      Definitely. Non-verbal cues can be so misunderstood. For example, eye contact in some cultures is seen as a sign of confidence, while in others it can be rude. I think it’s important to address that to avoid misinterpretation.      Yes, and that ties into the consent forms. We need to make sure that participants are aware of the content and that they’re comfortable with the discussions around cultural sensitivity. I think we should include a brief disclaimer at the beginning.      I’ve drafted that already. It’s pretty straightforward—just a statement about the seminar content and the participants’ right to withdraw. I think it’s covered.      I’m really excited about this. It’s a great opportunity to share knowledge and help the participants understand the complexities of working internationally. I think the structure is solid, but maybe we could have a Q&A session at the end to address any specific concerns.      That’s a good point. I’ll add that to the agenda. We’ll also need to make sure we have enough time for each of our segments.

So, I just got back from my lecture today, and I was thinking—do you ever feel like we're working so hard, but we're not even close to being done? I mean, I had a student who asked me about the implications of the latest research paper on quantum mechanics, and I was like, “Wait, are we even in the same class?”      I know, right? I’ve been up all night grading essays, and now I’m walking home with a migraine. It’s not just the workload—it’s the  expectations . Like, we’re supposed to be experts now, but we’re still learning. It’s so contradictory.      Exactly! And don’t even get me started on our university’s new housing policy. I got an email this morning saying we need to apply for a housing unit by the end of the month. But how are we supposed to do that when we’re barely managing to survive on our stipends?      Ugh, you’re not wrong. I mean, I’ve been thinking about buying a place, but it’s so expensive here. Even a tiny flat in London is out of our reach. I keep telling myself, “Maybe when we get tenure, we’ll have more money,” but I don’t know, sometimes I wonder if we’re just chasing something that’s never going to happen.      I totally get that. It’s not just the cost—it’s the  location . I mean, we’re both from the South, but here in China, it’s like trying to live in a completely different world. I miss the familiarity of walking through Norwich, or even just the bus routes I know so well.      Yeah, I miss London too. I mean, I know it’s different, but there’s something about being in your own city. I was thinking the other day—what if we moved back to the UK? You said you’d like to be closer to family, and I’ve been thinking about starting a business. Maybe something related to education.      That’s actually an interesting idea. I mean, we could do something together. But wait—what about the students? They’re used to us being here. I don’t want to leave them hanging.      I get that. I think it would be a tough decision, but maybe we could do it in stages. Like, we could start working on the business plan while still teaching.

So, I just wanted to bring up something I’ve been thinking about a lot lately—the food waste in our grandparents’ house. You know how they always had more than enough, but somehow ended up throwing out a lot of it? It’s crazy, right? I mean, they used to grow their own vegetables and make everything from scratch, yet they still wasted food.      Yeah, I remember that. They always said it was because they were so busy and didn’t have time to use everything. But honestly, it felt like they didn’t care much about waste. Do you think that’s how it was back then? Like, people just didn’t worry about it as much?      Maybe, but now that I think about it, even with all the food we have access to, I still hear about people struggling with food insecurity. I think there’s a huge disconnect between how much food we waste and how many people go hungry. It’s so frustrating. I’ve been trying to make more of an effort at home to not waste food, but it’s hard. What about you?      I’ve been reading a lot about urban farming initiatives lately. There’s a new show on TV that’s really got me thinking. It follows a group of people who are trying to grow food in cities. It’s amazing how much you can do with small spaces, right? Maybe that’s something we could try in our place? We’ve got that little yard, and I’m sure we could grow some vegetables.      That sounds great. I’d love to get into that. I’ve always wanted to try something like that. But then again, I’ve also been curious about robots in the kitchen. I mean, I’ve seen those gadgets that can chop vegetables or even cook meals. Are we heading toward a future where we don’t need to cook at all?      Honestly, I don’t know. I think robots will definitely change how we do things, especially in bigger kitchens or restaurants. But I’d miss the personal touch. Plus, I think there’s something about cooking that’s part of our culture, like how our grandparents used to cook everything from scratch. It’s not just about food—it’s about tradition, family, and connection.      That’s true. I go back to my parents’ house sometimes and it’s so different from how my grandparents used to do things.

I’ve been thinking a lot lately about how time just slips away. It’s like, one day you’re in your 20s, and the next thing you know, you’re in your 30s, and you haven’t even had a chance to really settle down.      I know, I feel the same. But honestly, I found it a bit too slow at times. Like, I got lost in the details and didn't really connect with the main character.      That’s what I thought too. The pacing was a bit off for me.
