I’m more into horror, honestly.  Hereditary  is my go-to for that. It’s so intense, and the way it builds suspense is unbeatable. I couldn’t stop thinking about it for days.      Oh my gosh, I just watched that! I was so scared, I had to turn off the lights halfway through. But honestly, it was so good. It made me think about family and how much we take for granted.      I’m more of a comedy fan, but I absolutely loved  The Office  . It’s such a cult classic, and the way they portrayed the workplace is so real. I mean, I still watch it all the time.      That’s true, but I think the  Office  is better in some ways. The humor is more slapstick, but it’s still brilliant. I’ve been trying to get my roommate to watch the UK version, but she keeps saying she’s too busy.      I think the UK version is more realistic, to be honest. The way they depict the office hierarchy is so much closer to how it actually is. But the US version has some great moments too.      You know, I think the key is that  The Office  is a show that people can relate to no matter where you are. It’s about the small, awkward moments in the workplace. Plus, the cast is so talented.      Definitely. And it’s one of those shows you can just binge without getting bored. I’ve watched it multiple times, and I still find something new each time.      I agree! I think that’s what makes it so special. It’s not just about the humor, it’s about the characters and how they grow.

You know, I still can’t believe we managed to get through Paris without getting lost once. I mean, I’m not exactly a fan of navigating through a foreign city with a map that keeps changing every five minutes.      You were on your phone the whole time, weren’t you? I swear, you were more focused on making sure your Instagram story was perfect than actually paying attention to where you were walking.      Yeah, and then you ended up in this tiny little café that only took cash. You had to ask three different people for the address because your phone kept dying. I thought I’d never see you again.      Oh, it’s a miracle I made it back. I was so focused on getting my photos just right that I didn’t even notice the time. By the time we got back to the hotel, it was like midnight.      I remember you getting so excited about the croissants. You took three pictures of them before you even sat down.      I think you even tried to eat one with your hands like it was a sandwich.      Okay, maybe I was a little dramatic. But I swear, the croissants were  worth  it. You should’ve seen the size of those things. I think I could have eaten a whole bag by myself.      Honestly, I think you were just trying to avoid the cheese board. I saw you eyeing it like it was the last meal you’d ever have.      That’s not fair. I was just being polite. I mean, I didn’t even get to the cheese board. We were too busy arguing over what to do next.      I mean, it wasn’t even that bad. We found this amazing little jazz bar in Montmartre. The owner was so friendly, he even gave us free drinks. It was like the whole city was smiling at us.      You did say you were going to take a holiday to relax, not to become the star of a stranger’s YouTube video. But I have to admit, it was kind of endearing.      Yeah, I think you’re going to have to rethink your travel goals. Maybe next time, just enjoy your croissants and leave the camera in the bag.      Maybe. But I think I’ve already made plans for next year. I’m going to France again. I’m not going to let a little thing like getting lost stop me.

Hey, Sarah! Nice to see you before class. How’s your weekend going?      Oh, hey James! It went pretty well, thanks. I actually stayed in most of it because of the weather. Not the best weekend for going out, but I managed to catch up with my mum on Facetime. How about you?      Honestly, it was pretty chill. I went to Chichester with some friends. The town has this amazing theatre, and we saw a musical. It was one of those shows that makes you feel like you’re right in the story.      That sounds amazing! I’ve always wanted to see a real live musical. I know you’re into theatre, right? You even did a bit of creative writing in your undergrad, didn’t you?      Yeah, I did. I’m actually working on a novel now. It’s still in the early stages, but it’s a bit of a passion project. I think it’s going to be a drama set in the 1980s.      That’s cool! I’ve always been into stories, even if I didn’t go into writing. I’ve been thinking about going back to school for a master’s in linguistics. You know, maybe even something related to the British National Corpus.      Oh, that sounds interesting. I did my graduate work in English Language Teaching, and I’ve always loved the way language works. I mean, have you ever thought about how dialects like the Malaysian one compare to British English? It’s something I’ve been curious about.      Definitely! I think it’s fascinating how different accents and dialects shape the way people communicate. I remember once watching an episode of  Judge Judy  where someone used a very strong regional accent and it really affected how the judge interpreted their case.      That’s a good point. I think dialects and accents can be a huge part of identity, especially in the UK. I mean, I was born in Bedford, and my accent is pretty different from someone from Croydon. Do you ever notice the differences in your own speech?      Oh, I do! Sometimes I’ll catch myself using a more formal tone when I’m at work, even though I’m from a pretty casual background. I think it’s just part of the job. Speaking of work, you know I’m planning to take some time off for a bit.      Yeah, I heard you were thinking about that.

So, I tried to cook rice for the first time today, and it ended up like a lump of concrete. I don't know what I did wrong.      Oh, I know exactly what you did! You probably didn’t let it rest after boiling. You know, the rice needs to sit for about 10 minutes so the moisture can absorb.      Yeah, that sounds familiar. I was so excited to make rice and curry for dinner. We’ve been trying to eat out less, so I thought I’d make a meal at home. But I guess even simple things can be tricky.      That’s true. Being a parent, I’ve learned that cooking at home is actually easier than eating out, especially if you’re using vouchers. I used to go out all the time, but now, with the toddler, it’s just too much.      Haha, I can imagine. I’ve been thinking about getting some food vouchers for the weekend. Maybe I can treat myself to a nice meal without spending too much.      That’s a good idea. But you should remember to be mindful of the salt and fats. I’ve been trying to cut back, especially since I’ve been reading a lot about health stuff. Sometimes, even the food you think is healthy can be packed with hidden salt.      Oh, I’ve heard that! I made a curry the other day, and I added jalapenos because I wanted it a bit spicy. But it ended up being hotter than I expected.      Jalapenos can be tricky. If you’re not used to spicy food, even a little bit can make the difference. You might want to start with a small amount and add more later.      Yeah, I guess I’ll have to be careful with that. I also heard about someone having a facial deformity from eating too much spicy food. Is that real?      I think it’s just a myth, but I’ve heard of people getting mouth ulcers from overdoing it. But I’ve never seen anyone with a real facial deformity from it.      Okay, that’s reassuring. I was getting a bit worried. But I’m still going to try making that curry. Maybe with a bit more caution.      That’s the spirit! And don’t forget, if the meat starts to go off, you should throw it away. I saw a documentary once where they showed food that had gone bad, and it was really gross.      Ugh, yuck!

Alright, so I was thinking, do you know what's the real deal with uni? I mean, I've got a degree, and I'm still unemployed. What's the point? I don't even know what I want to do. It's like I'm just stuck in this loop.      I know, right? I'm still at sixth form. I'm not even sure if I want to go to uni. My mates are all talking about it like it's the only way to get ahead. But honestly, I don't even know what I want to study. Maybe I'll just do something practical, like nursing or something?      Yeah, I hear you. I left school early, and I've been working odd jobs, but it's not enough. I mean, I'm not even sure about uni. I think it's expensive, and if I do go, I'm not sure if it'll help me get a job. I mean, I've seen so many people graduate and still end up in the same place.      It's not just the cost, it's also the system. You get a degree, but it doesn't guarantee you a job. My brother did a degree in IT, and now he's stuck doing admin work. I mean, maybe it's not the same as working in the field. But then again, maybe he just needs to find someone who will hire him.      I mean, I did a degree in law, and now I can't even get an interview. I had to take a job as a barista just to pay the bills. I feel like I've been sold a lie. I thought getting a degree would open doors, but all it's done is close them.      I guess that's the thing. A lot of people think uni is the only way to be successful. But I'm not sure. I mean, some people are really good at self-employment or doing something creative. Maybe I should just try and start a small business or do something like that instead of chasing a degree.      I think I might try something like that too. Maybe I can learn some skills through online courses or something. I don't know, it's just hard to figure out what to do when you're not sure where you want to go.

So, I was just thinking, do you ever miss working, even though you’re retired? I mean, I can’t imagine not having a job, you know? I’d probably go mad.      Honestly, I wouldn’t say I miss it. I mean, I liked the freedom, the not having to get up at 7 in the morning for a meeting. But I do miss the routine, a bit. You know, having something to look forward to every day. Especially when the weather’s nice and you can’t just go out and cycle or something.      I get that. I’m always trying to find time to exercise, but work’s just so busy. I’m thinking of starting a group for people in the office who want to get fit. Maybe even do some yoga or something. It’d be great for team bonding too.      That sounds cool. I’ve always been into exercise, but I didn’t have the time when I was working. I used to cycle a lot when I was younger, but now I just walk around the park with the dog. It’s not the same, though.      I tried walking with a dog once. It was okay, but I got lost in the woods, and I had to find my way back. I didn’t want to admit it, but I called a friend to come and pick me up. It was a bit of an embarrassment.      That’s not bad. I once got stuck in a bus that broke down in the middle of nowhere. I had to wait for over an hour before someone came to help. I was so hungry, I just ate my sandwich and waited.      You’re telling me! I’m trying to be more independent, but I think I need someone to look after me. Maybe I should find a friend to go exercise with. You know, someone to keep me on track.      That could work. I could join you. Although, I might not be as fit as you. But I do like the idea of getting out more and being active. It’s just that the weather has been so bad lately, right?      Yeah, it’s been really gloomy. I’ve been trying to get out more, but it’s just too cold. I’ve been reading about the benefits of exercise, though. It’s not just about looking good, it’s about mental health too.

So, lads, I think we’ve cleared up enough for one night. We’ve got to make sure the kitchen’s spotless before the weekend, right? I can’t have you two running around like you own the place.      Yeah, but I just wiped the counter. What’s the big deal?      You wiped the counter? That’s not clearing up! You need to clean the fridge, take out the trash, maybe do the laundry. You’re both supposed to help out when you come home.      I’ll tell you what, I used to do that when I was your age. My mum would make me do the whole house. She’d say, “You’re not just here to play games, you’re here to help.”      Yeah, I guess. But I just want to watch a bit of tennis. It’s the World Cup finals, right?      Yeah, and I was just thinking, if I had a girlfriend, maybe I’d take her to see it. But I don’t even have a girlfriend. I’ve got a crush on someone, though.      Oh, you do? Who’s the lucky girl?      It’s… it’s someone from school. She’s cool, and she’s into tennis. I mean, she doesn’t even follow it, but she’s okay.      Well, whatever floats your boat. But you know, I used to be in a band. Not a very good one, but I had a girlfriend then. She was into Instagram, so I had to start using it too. I was like, “What is this thing?” But now I have 200 followers and a whole bunch of photos of my cats.      That’s not bad. I tried using Instagram a little, but I just post my dog and then I delete it. It’s not like I’ve got a life or anything.      That’s the problem, lads. You’re too young to really get the life you want. If you don’t start now, you’ll be out of luck. I remember when I was your age, I used to think I could just take over the world. Thought I was going to be a famous writer or something.      Yeah, and now you’re just a self-employed marketing guy with facial hair.      Touché. But it’s not all bad. I’ve got a nice flat, a good job, and I’ve got you two to help me out.

So, do you think we’ll get the new sofa by the weekend? I’m really starting to feel like my old one is going to fall apart on me any day now.      Honestly, I’m beginning to think we should just take the one from the tip. You know, the one that’s a bit worn but still usable. I saw one this morning that looked like it had been used by a couple of kids. It’s nothing fancy, but it’s solid.      Oh, right. I remember when we used to go to the tip all the time. It was like a treasure hunt, really. I still remember the time we found that old armchair that was covered in dust, but once we cleaned it, it looked brand new.      You were so excited about that chair, weren’t you? I remember you told me it felt like finding gold.      I did! And it was pretty much the same with the old table we got from the tip. It was old, but it was good. I think we’re all getting a bit attached to the idea of recycling stuff.      I mean, I did hear about this whole new building that’s going up near the old town. There’s even a shop that sells second-hand furniture. Maybe we can check that out instead.      Oh, I’d be happy to see that. I used to go there when I was about your age, Anna. It was such a good place to meet people. There was a whole group of us who used to go there every weekend.      You mean like the ones who started the beaver scout group? I remember that. They used to have a Christmas party every year, and it was always full of stories.      Yeah, and I remember one of the boys from primary school ended up joining the scouts. Still remember that time he got into a fight with the network scouts over a chocolate bar.      Oh, that was brutal. I think he ended up getting a lecture from all of them. It was like a mini war.      And then there was the time one of ANON’s friends got dementia and had to move in with the family. It was really hard on everyone, but they were so supportive.      Yeah, and it made me realize how important family is. Even when things get tough, we’re always there for each other.      Exactly.

Hey Mum, how’s everything going? I’ve been meaning to catch up with you for ages.      Oh, I’m good, love! Just been busy with the school term and trying to get my head around this new project at work. You know how it is — always something on the go.      Yeah, totally. I’ve been feeling the same. I’ve been thinking about redundancy at the office too. I mean, the company’s been going through a bit of a rough patch, and I heard they might be cutting some roles.      Oh no, really? That’s not good. Have you spoken to your manager yet?      Not yet, I’m just trying to figure out the best way to approach it. I don’t want to come across as negative, but I’m worried about the stability.      I get that. I’m actually in the same boat. I’ve been getting a lot of emails about possible redundancies in our department. It’s really stressful. I was thinking maybe I should start looking for other opportunities, just in case.      That’s a smart move. I was thinking about going to the gym more too, but I haven’t had much time. I’m trying to stay active and keep my mind off things.      Oh, you should! You know what my grandad always says — if you don’t take care of yourself, no one else will. I’ve been trying to get back into the habit too, but I’m not very consistent.      He’s right. I’ve been meaning to ask about your house extension. I heard you mentioned it last week — is it going ahead?      Yes, we’re hoping to get the planning approved soon. It’s going to be a bit of a hassle, but I think it’ll make a big difference in the long run. I was also thinking about going shopping next weekend — you up for joining me? We could run errands and maybe grab a bite to eat.      That sounds like a plan! I’ve been craving some good food lately. I’ve been eating a lot of takeaway, which I know isn’t the healthiest, but I just haven’t had the energy to cook.      Well, we can make a day of it — get some healthy stuff, maybe even check out that new café near the market. It’s got some really good reviews.

So, what do you think we should do today, little man? The sun’s shining, and the holidays are here. I’m feeling like we should do something fun.      Me? I wanna swim! Swim like a fish!      Yeah, swimming’s a great idea. But let’s not forget about your dad. He’s been trying to practice his guitar, and he says he needs a break from that.      You know, I actually think it would be nice to take a walk around the village today. The summer sun is perfect for that. And maybe we could also check out the local library. I heard they have some new books for kids.      Library? I like books. I like stories.      Yeah, and he’s got the attention span of a gnat, but he still likes the stories. So, what do you think, Mr. Toddler? Library or swimming?      Sun!      He’s got a point. The sun is shining bright, and it’s warm enough for the pool. But I was also thinking about Mick. You know, the kids’ program. I think we could tune in to that today. It’s always fun.      Mick’s a good show. It’s got all those silly characters and the songs. But wait, what if we  actually  do something? Like, maybe we could try to figure out what ANON is saying. I keep hearing that from my friend, and I can’t understand a word.      ANON? That’s the anonymous person on the internet, right? They just say things without telling who they are. It’s kind of weird, but I suppose it’s a way to speak out without being judged.      Yeah, but I don’t get it. Why would someone want to be anonymous? You know, I sometimes think about Japan. I’ve heard that their culture is completely different.      Japan? That’s a big country. I’ve never been there, but I’ve heard they have amazing gardens and temples. Maybe next year, after the holidays, we could plan to go on a trip or something.      Yeah! We could even go to Tokyo! I’ve heard they have the best ramen.      Guitar?      Yeah, your dad’s been working on it. He says it's getting better every day. Maybe after we take a walk or swim, he could play you a tune.      That’s a good idea. I think he’s been working too hard on it.

So, I just watched that film we were talking about last week,  The Dentist . You were like, “That’s the one with the guy who becomes a dentist and starts getting weird vibes?” Yeah, I couldn’t stop thinking about it after. It’s so weird how the whole thing just kind of  stops  at the end, right? Like, you’re all in this horror situation with that guy, and then suddenly, it’s just a routine dental check-up. It was so jarring.      Didn’t it just mess with your head? I mean, I was like, “Wait, is this a metaphor for something? Or is it just a boring dentist ad?” Honestly, I think they did it on purpose. It’s like a commentary on how we’re always expecting the worst, but in reality, life just goes on in the most mundane way. It’s a bit of a mind-fuck.      Yeah, and I was also thinking about that thing you mentioned about accents. You said that people from Liverpool don’t like being called “Livvies” or whatever. I’ve always thought that was a bit rude. I mean, I live in Leicester, so I know what it’s like to have a regional identity. We get called “Leicsters” too, but I think it’s kind of a joke. Although, I have to say, I don’t think I’d ever call someone a “Leicester” in a derogatory way.      That’s the thing, man. I think it’s all about context. If it’s a joke between friends, it’s fine. But if it’s someone trying to mock you about where you’re from, it’s not cool. I mean, I had this guy in my class last year who was like, “Oh, you’re from Birkenhead? That’s just a ‘Livvie’.” And I was like, “Yeah, that’s my accent. You want to try it?” He was like, “No way.” So, yeah, it’s not really a big deal if you’re in the right space.      I guess I’ve never thought about it like that. I mean, I’ve heard some people say that Liverpool accents go hand in hand with a certain attitude or something. But I think it’s just about pride. I mean, we’ve got a lot of history, and people here are proud of it. I think it’s the same with Leicester.

Oh, I've been meaning to talk to you about our Easter plans. With the Christening coming up, I thought maybe we could all get together and do something special. You know, make some traditional Easter cakes and spend the day with the kids.      That sounds lovely, Mum. I was actually just thinking about that myself. I’ve been looking forward to the Christening, but I also wanted to make sure I had some time to relax and get ready. I’ve got a few things to wrap up at the school before the holiday.      Right, I know you've been busy. I heard you got the new job at the primary school. How are you settling in?      Oh, it’s been a bit of a rollercoaster. I love the kids, but I’m still getting used to the pace. I’ve been trying to figure out how to balance teaching with my own time, especially with Easter coming up.      Well, that’s to be expected. You’ve got a lot on your plate, and I know you’re doing a great job. I’ve been meaning to ask—what exactly is it you’re teaching?      I’m teaching Year 2. It’s a bit of a challenge, but I think I’m getting the hang of it. The kids are so full of energy, and it’s been a real joy to see them grow and learn. I just wish I had more time to prepare for the Easter activities. It’s such a busy time of year.      I can imagine. Between the Easter holidays and the Christening, it’s bound to be hectic. I’m thinking about making some traditional Easter eggs and maybe even some of those lovely sponges and simnel cakes that we used to make when I was a kid.      That sounds like a great idea. I’d love to help. I’ve been trying to get my baking skills back up to speed. I even tried making some cupcakes the other day, but they didn’t turn out too well. I think the kids would have preferred chocolate sauce over the frosting.      Oh, I can imagine. You’ve always had a flair for the dramatic. Well, maybe we can make a few batches, and then you can take some to the school for the kids. It would be a nice touch for the Easter celebrations.

So, how’s life treating you, Ann? I haven’t seen you in ages. It’s been like... forever since we last met. You’ve been busy?      Oh, you know me, Lucy. Always running around. I’ve been trying to balance work and family, which isn’t always easy. But I’ve been keeping busy with my teaching and helping out with the kids. How about you?      Honestly, it’s been a whirlwind. I’ve started teaching English abroad, actually. A few months ago I got a job in Budapest teaching at a language school. It’s been fantastic, but it’s also been a bit of a culture shock at times. I miss the familiarity of Hitchin, you know?      Oh, Hungary? That’s a lovely place. You must be getting some interesting stories. Do you have any students you’ve really connected with? I still remember when I was teaching in London, there was this one boy who used to bring me homemade cookies every week. He was adorable.      Oh, I’ve had some really interesting students. One of them is a young girl whose parents are both from different countries. We’ve been learning about different cultures in class, and she’s been teaching me so much. I think it’s been a mutual learning experience.      That sounds wonderful. I always thought learning a language was about more than just grammar and vocabulary—it’s about people and stories. Speaking of which, have you heard anything from your sister? She mentioned she’s thinking of starting a business selling handmade beauty products.      Oh, she’s been talking about it for ages. I think she’s finally taken the plunge. She’s got a small shop in Stratford-upon-Avon now, and she’s doing really well. I’ve been helping her with the copywriting and branding. It’s amazing how much she’s grown since she first started out.      That’s great. I think it’s so inspiring to see people follow their dreams, even if it’s not exactly what you planned. I’ve been meaning to start something too. Maybe a blog or something related to education. I’ve been thinking about how to help other teachers in the same situation as I was.      That sounds like a really good idea. I’d love to help you with that. We could even collaborate on some ideas. And don’t forget—what’s the latest with your dog?

So, I’ve been trying to get my sister to let me cook the Passover meal, and she keeps saying, “You can’t cook a Seder without knowing the first thing about Jewish food.” I don’t even know what I’m supposed to be cooking!      You’ve got to start somewhere, mate. I mean, I’ve only been baking for a few years, and I still mess up the matzo ball soup. But honestly, it’s worth it. You can’t beat the smell of a proper Passover meal, especially with all those herbs and spices.      That’s the beauty of it, really. It’s not just about the food—it’s about the traditions, the stories, the history. I think the most important part is passing the story of the Exodus down through the generations. It’s about remembering and honoring our ancestors.      Yeah, I agree. I remember when I was a kid, my Grandpa would always tell the story of the Exodus, like it was the most important thing in the world. He’d make it sound like a dramatic movie. I still remember the way he’d say, “And they left Egypt with nothing but the clothes on their backs and a burning bush in the desert!”      That’s the spirit! He was a legend. But seriously, I was thinking—do we even know how to properly make the food this year? I mean, I’m not a novice, but I’ve never been to a proper Passover meal before. I’ve seen the ingredients and everything, but I don’t know which ones are kosher.      Oh, don’t worry. I’ve been preparing for this all week. I’ve got the matzo, the maror, the charoset. And I baked the hamantaschen last night. It was a total disaster, but the kids loved them. They think I’m some kind of Jewish baker!      You’re doing great. And if you ever want help, I’ve got a few recipes from my grandmother. She used to make a stunning Passover brisket that would take the whole family days to eat. It was like a festival in itself.      That sounds amazing. I can already picture it. But wait—do we have any ideas for special dishes this year? I was thinking of maybe making some Italian-inspired Passover food. You know, like a Jewish-Italian fusion or something.      That’s a brilliant idea!

So, I've been thinking about the new BBC series that’s been on lately—the one with that actor from  The Crown , you know the one with the dark hair and the brooding look? It's been getting a lot of buzz, and I think it's worth watching, but I haven’t had time yet.      Oh, I tried to watch it last week, but I got bogged down with work. I actually ended up watching a few episodes of  Doctor Who  instead. That’s the one with Jodie Whittaker, right? I’ve always loved that show—it reminds me of my childhood.      I haven’t seen it yet, but I’ve heard that the new series is pretty different from the old ones. It’s supposed to be more grounded, less sci-fi, more of a drama. I’m a bit nervous about it, honestly. I think I’ll wait until the next season starts.      I’d say wait, but I’ve heard the first season is really good. I actually got into it so much I started knitting while watching it—like, I’d be in the middle of a stitch, and then I’d be back to the episode. It’s kind of therapeutic, honestly.      Knitting? I used to do that, but I gave it up when I started working full-time. It’s so much easier to just use a tape measure and a spreadsheet! Though, I have to admit, someone once told me that crocheting is like knitting, but with more creativity. I tried it once and ended up with a scarf that looked like a tangled mess.      That sounds like my experience with knitting. I tried making a baby blanket once, and I had to throw it in the bin. I ended up buying a new one online. But I do enjoy it when I do get it right. Maybe I should start again. I’ve been thinking about getting some new yarn.      I’ve been working on a shawl for my mum. She’s into that kind of thing. She’s also always been a huge book lover. She told me the other day that she prefers physical books because they feel more personal. She said the pages are like memories.      That’s so true. I read a lot, but I’ve started using the Kindle more lately. It’s convenient, and you can carry so many books in your pocket.

Okay, so I've got this new phone. It's a Nokia, right? I thought they were more like... I don't know, old school? But this one looks pretty sleek. I guess the brand still has some clout.      Yeah, I think they’ve actually come a long way. I mean, I used to have a Nokia back in the day—like, a basic one with a clunky keyboard. But now, this one’s got all the modern stuff. You can even download apps, right?      Yeah, I’ve heard about that. My lectures are all online these days, so I need a phone that can handle that. I’m not sure if this one can do it. I mean, I’ve got a tablet, but it’s a bit slow for some things.      Oh, I can help with that. I’m still working on my PhD, so I’ve been juggling a lot of apps and cloud storage. So, what do you think, Lucas? Which one is your favorite? The cat or the dog?      I like the cat! She's soft and purrs when I touch her.      Yeah, my cat, Muffin, is the best. So, I was just thinking about how different Christmas was when I was a kid. I remember my mum always made this traditional Christmas pudding, and we’d have it with brandy. It was like a ritual. You couldn’t even imagine not having it on Christmas Day.      Yeah, I remember that too. But I think my family had more of a modern approach. I always thought it was the most important part of the day. And the way we all sat around the table, singing carols and telling stories—there was something very magical about it.      I can see that. I used to have the same Christmas traditions growing up—turkey, puddings, carols. But I also remember that in my family, we had this tradition of drinking real, proper British beer on Christmas Day. My dad would always say it was part of the holiday spirit.      Yeah, I think that’s something that’s becoming rarer these days. More people are trying to be health-conscious or just not drink as much. But for me, I still enjoy a glass of something on Christmas. Though I’ve started to drink a bit more responsibly now.      I’ve been trying to cut back too. I think I’ve been drinking more responsibly since I started university. It’s funny, though—my friends still think I’m the one who goes out and drinks a lot. Absolutely. I think we’ve all had moments where we felt pressured to drink more. It’s part of the culture, I suppose. But I think it’s important to choose what you want to do.

So, I just got my new Kindle, and I’ve been really into this detective series. I think it’s got to be one of the best ones I’ve seen in a while. The pacing is just right, and the twists are all over the place. You’ve got to admit, it’s addictive.      I’ve been meaning to get one, honestly. But I still prefer paper books for the real reading experience. There’s something about the feel of the pages and the smell of the paper that you just can’t replicate.      Yeah, I get that. I’ve had a few paperbacks in my reading list, but I’ve been leaning more towards e-books lately, especially since I’ve started working from home. It’s just easier to carry around, and I can adjust the lighting and font size. Plus, I’ve been getting a lot of free books from the library’s digital service.      Oh, I should check that out. Well, I’ve been thinking, you know, about all the time we’ve spent together over the years. I mean, we’ve had our ups and downs, sure, but we’ve always managed to find a way through. That’s what makes us a good team, isn’t it?      Yeah, I feel the same. Remember when we first moved into this house? It was a bit of a mess, and I was worried I’d never get used to it. But you made it feel like home.      Oh, I remember. You were so proud of the patchwork quilt you made for the living room. It looked like a jumble of colors, but I loved it. It reminded me of the way we used to patch things up in our lives—slow, steady, and always with a bit of heart.      You two are talking about the old days again. I always find it amusing. That’s the thing, Liza. You and I, we’ve always known that life’s not about having everything perfect. It’s about making the most of what you have, and supporting each other along the way.      And that’s something I think I’ve learned from you both.

So, I've got this idea for a party next week. I was thinking maybe we could do something... offbeat. You know, something that’s not your typical office bash. Maybe a themed event? Hey, have you seen the latest homework from Mrs. Thompson? I swear, it's like she's trying to make us go insane with all these essays and math problems.      Oh no, I know! Like, finish one assignment before doing anything else.

So, I just got the latest update from work, and it’s a bit of a mess. The new system we’re supposed to be using is glitching more than I can handle. Hey, Sue, it's been a while! How have you been? I haven’t seen you in ages, and I’ve been meaning to catch up with you properly.      Oh, I’ve been okay, thanks. Just been busy with work and trying to keep up with the kids. You know how it is with teenagers—always something going on. How are things on your end?      Yeah, I can only imagine. So, how’s the uni work going, then? I know you’re studying English, right? I’m just trying to figure out how you manage to keep up with all that reading and essays. That’s what you think. I’ve got a postgrad in social work, and I’m trying to fit in a bar shift five days a week, plus nights. I barely have time to sleep, let alone study. Unless you’re serving a professor who’s been drinking too much.      Oh, I’ve had that happen. A couple of times. I had this guy who came in all dressed up, talking about philosophy, and then he turned out to be a professor from the university. We’re both in the North, but your accent is way more posh than mine.      Oh, don’t be so harsh. I’ve heard you talk before, and I think you sound like a proper Yorkshire lass.

So, how was your holiday, everyone? I’ve been meaning to ask. I spent mine in the Lake District, actually. It was lovely, but honestly, I think I stared at the same waterfall for three days. I don’t know why I thought it would be different.      Oh, I went to the south coast with my family. We rented a little cottage in Cornwall. It was amazing. The beach was so clean, and the weather was perfect. Oh, and my niece tried to build a sandcastle, and it collapsed like a house of cards. She was so upset. I had to laugh, but it really broke her heart.      Cornwall sounds lovely. I went to the west coast of Ireland with my husband. We stayed in a small village, and the views were incredible. But I have to say, the food was the highlight. I tried a traditional Irish stew, and it was so hearty and warm. I still dream about it.      Ah, Ireland, right? I’ve always wanted to go. I’ve been thinking of doing a road trip there. But I’ve been too busy with work. I’ve been working on this e-learning project, and it’s taking up all my time. I feel like I haven’t got a holiday in years – unless you count a two-day weekend.      You’re not alone on that. I’ve been trying to take a holiday for months, but every time something comes up. I was supposed to go to Scotland with a friend, but she got sick, and I had to cover for her at the library. It’s been a bit frustrating, but at least I had a quiet weekend. Can you believe the way they played that game? I mean, it was like they were trying to score from half-way the pitch. I don’t know, maybe they just had a good game plan. Or maybe they were just trying to keep the crowd entertained.      Or maybe they were just desperate. Look at the scoreline—three-nil to the other team. I mean, if they’re going to lose, they might as well go out with a bang, right?      I guess that’s the thing about football. You can’t always control the outcome. But hey, at least they didn’t have to eat fast food for the entire match.      Yeah, I feel like that’s what we should be doing instead of watching this. It’s the one with the neon lights and the smell that follows you home. I think they call it “The Grub.”      Yeah, that’s the one. I heard the burgers are decent, and the fries are like real fries. Not that soggy, sad mess you get in the café near the uni.      I’d say they’re worth the trip. Although, I’m not sure I’m up for fast food after watching that match. Yeah, yeah, you’re a legend. But I still say the fries go to me.      Fine. But when you’re done, you’re buying the next round.      Deal. You know, Mum, I still remember watching  Doctor Who  on a regular basis when I was a kid. It was the old series with Tom Baker, right?      Oh, I remember that well. That’s what I love about the old programmes. They had more heart, I think. These days, it’s all about the special effects and the CGI. Where’s the soul in that?      I agree. Though, I will say, the modern ones are still good. I mean, I’ve got a daughter who really likes  Doctor Who  now. I’ve made some proper pancakes for Pancake Day. The kids really got excited about it. They’ve been talking about it all week. So, I was just thinking about how different things used to be. I was out in the garden the other day, and I saw this old bicycle that my dad used to ride around the village.
